The quill pen brushed lightly across the page, writing: "Dunn Smith was secretly tainted by the Antigonus family's notebook, and later, after entering Hanass Vincent's dream and seeing the clear image of the 'True Creator,' the corruption Dunn Smith suffered began to gradually spread. The Everni..."
The pale hand quickly lifted the pen. The quill pen had almost written "Evernight Goddess." After all, the quill was just a sealed artifact, and if it involved the Evernight Goddess in the story, it would definitely catch Her attention. Ince Zangwill, who wielded the pen, would surely meet a tragic end in Tingen City.
The pale hand crossed out the word "Evernight" and continued writing: "Klein's ritual was a great success, but due to his spiritual depletion, he didn't have time to inform Dunn Smith about Old Neil's ongoing ritual. Over time, Klein continually forgot to mention it to his colleagues due to various reasons, believing it wasn't that important. By the time he had the chance to explain, it was already too late.
"Old Neil's ongoing ritual would push him to the brink of losing control once again—maybe in three weeks, maybe in four. He would return to the edge of madness. His eventual breakdown was inevitable, as his ritual attracted certain gazes. As long as his ritual continued, the corruption would persist, and so would the risk of losing control.
"His breakdown would deal a psychological blow to Dunn Smith and exacerbate the secret pollution already affecting Dunn, leading him to actions Ince Zangwill anticipated...
"What's puzzling is, how did Klein realize Old Neil was on the verge of losing control? His fate took a strange turn here. Could it be because he obtained..."
The pale hand quickly lifted the pen again. He had a premonition that if he allowed the quill to continue writing, things would spiral out of control.
He quickly closed the notebook. This unexpected story had come to a temporary halt.
Ince sighed as he looked out at the lawn with his one eye. Why is it that the stories in Tingen City are always disrupted by uncontrollable forces? Especially this Klein—why does he keep messing up the carefully crafted stories?
---
On Tuesday morning, Hobert gathered the relevant materials and took the law firm's carriage to visit the client, Mr. Polly, in the western suburbs.
Mr. Polly was a man in his fifties, with thinning hair, wrinkled skin, and a pipe in his mouth, giving him a stern appearance.
"I'm going to ruin the Ailey family! I swear, I'll make them pay!" Mr. Polly muttered through his pipe, "Last night, yes, just last night, the giant dog he keeps in the basement escaped again and made a mess of my flowerbed. But that old scoundrel Ailey still insists he doesn't own a dog, let alone a giant one!"
After listening to Mr. Polly rant for a while, Hobert understood the gist. Mr. Polly and the Ailey family were neighbors, but they did not get along.
The root of their disagreement was religious—Mr. Polly's family worshiped the Evernight Goddess, while the Aileys followed the Lord of Storms. They had been neighbors for over a decade, and they had quarreled for just as long.
Recently, however, Ailey had allegedly been keeping a giant dog in his basement. The dog occasionally escaped and wreaked havoc in Polly's garden, even killing several chickens.
Yet Mr. Ailey adamantly denied ever owning a dog. Frustrated, Mr. Polly reached out to a friend to find a lawyer, and thus, Hobert became involved.
Hobert asked, "Have any neighbors seen this giant dog? Would they be willing to testify for you?"
"They've seen it! The Will family across the street and the Allens on the left both saw it, and they're willing to testify for me," Polly replied. "Go ahead, take Ailey to court, Hobert. Let him see how serious I am."
Hobert smiled and said, "Mr. Polly, I'm just a lawyer, not a judge."
He added, "Before going to the Magistrate's Court, I'll first have a conversation with Mr. Ailey. If he's willing to compensate you for your losses, it will save everyone trouble. But if he insists on going to court, we'll be ready for that as well."
Mr. Polly nodded. "Alright, lawyer, I'll follow your lead."
In truth, he wasn't keen on going to court, as it would be too much hassle.
Hobert asked, "How much compensation are you seeking from Mr. Ailey?"
"100 pounds! Lawyer, I want him to pay me 100 pounds."
"That amount is too high. A judge would never accept it," Hobert replied. "I recommend asking for 10 pounds in compensation and an additional 10 pounds for legal fees."
Twenty pounds was a sum a small landowner could handle. If Ailey had to pay 100 pounds, he would indeed be ruined.
Mr. Polly trembled slightly with his pipe in hand. "Goddess! You're charging 10 pounds for legal fees?"
"Didn't your friend explain our rates?" Hobert smiled. "This is already the lowest fee."
"Alright, alright, as long as Ailey is paying."
After settling the details, the two signed a contract. Hobert then asked Mr. Polly to take him to visit the Will and Allen families. As Polly had said, both families were willing to testify, having also seen the giant dog and been frightened by it.
Finally, Hobert went alone to visit Mr. Ailey. Ailey was at home, and when Hobert explained the reason for his visit, Ailey shouted from the doorway, "I've said it a hundred times! That old fool Polly must be going blind! We've never owned a dog. Fine, fine, if he wants to sue, I'm ready."
His voice was loud enough for Mr. Polly, on the other side of the fence, to hear clearly. "Old fool! We used to argue, but I still thought you were a man. Now you're just a clown refusing to admit the truth!"
Their argument prompted a series of barks, and by the sound of it, the dog wasn't small.
Mr. Polly's words made Ailey flush red. As the two men prepared to escalate the confrontation, Hobert quickly interjected. "Mr. Ailey, may I take a look at your basement? The neighbors have all seen it. The giant dog escaped from your basement."
"Fine, fine," Ailey replied. "Lawyer, I trust you. But let me tell you, representing Polly is going to be the stain on your career."
As he spoke, Ailey led Hobert to the outside door of the basement. The barking grew louder.
But when Ailey opened the door, there was nothing inside—just farming tools and miscellaneous items, with no trace of any animal!
Wait! Hobert felt a familiar, twisted sensation, much like the feeling when using the power of the Lawyer Pathway in the Nation of Disorder!

chapters.title: Chapter 59 - 59: Law of Beyonder Characteristics Convergence
chapters.content:
Join www.patreon.com/KeyofStars for advance chapters
~~~
Hobert's first thought was the "Law of Beyonder Characteristics Convergence." If he was right, this seemingly ordinary case must conceal a mystical item or a Beyonder from the Lawyer Pathway.
When handling Mr. Baron's case earlier, based on what Penny told him about the "Country Lawyer," he was 100% certain that they were a Beyonder from the Lawyer Pathway!
Hobert smiled helplessly: "I should have realized earlier. The Nation of Disorder is a key element for both the Lawyer and Arbiter Pathways to become a Great Old One. It's like a massive magnet, drawing the Beyonder characteristics from these two Pathways toward me."
He then reflected on himself: "Over the past month, I still haven't fully transitioned my mindset from the modern era to the Beyonder world. My past life experiences are useful, but in this extraordinary world, its rules are what truly matter."
Seeing Hobert lost in thought, Airey smiled smugly, "So, Mr. Lawyer, as I said before, we've never owned a dog."
Hobert asked, "Then where did the barking we heard come from?"
"The Henry family, who live behind us, own a dog!" Airey said. "I think their dog must have gotten loose, first coming to my yard, then to that old geezer Polly's yard."
"As for why Polly swore that the dog came from my basement, I believe it's because his old eyes played tricks on him. Plus, he doesn't dare confront the Henrys, so he cowardly pushed the blame onto me."
After leaving the basement, Airey pointed to the predominantly dark-colored house behind his own, "That's the Henrys' house."
The house gave off a deathly atmosphere. The curtains and door drapes were tightly shut, as though it had been uninhabited for a long time.
Airey explained, "It seems one of Henry's children has a rare illness. Their complexion is pale, and they're afraid of sunlight, so their house is always sealed off like this."
"Henry is a fabric merchant, stern-faced, and not easy to get along with. The neighbors don't like dealing with him."
"Oh, and speaking of which, it seems they haven't left their house in a few days."
As Hobert left Airey's backyard and approached the Henry household, sure enough, he heard barking coming from the basement.
Hobert knocked on the garden gate, but no one answered. So, he opened it and knocked on the front door.
After waiting for about half a minute, he finally heard footsteps inside. The person inside seemed to drag their feet across the floor, and a hoarse voice asked, "Who is it?"
Hobert briefly introduced himself and explained his reason for coming, "May I take a look at the dog you're keeping in the basement?"
The hoarse voice responded, "We all have a severe flu. If you don't want to catch it, come back in a few days."
After a moment of thought, Hobert replied, "Alright. I'll return later this week. I hope you all recover soon."
Back at Mr. Polly's house, upon hearing that Airey didn't have a dog but the Henrys did, and that the barking came from their basement, Polly shook his head repeatedly, "Sir, I may be old, but my eyes aren't that bad yet. Besides, I'm not the only one who saw it; everyone saw the big dog coming out of Airey's basement."
Hobert glanced out the window, noting that Airey's and Henry's basements were only separated by a narrow country lane: "Perhaps there's another explanation…"
He smiled, "Let's talk about Mr. Henry, shall we?"
"Oh, Henry's not someone to mess with," Polly said as he filled his pipe. "Last year, a thief snuck into their house, and Henry beat him so badly, he was left only able to mutter 'He's dead, he's dead.'"
"They moved here when I was a kid. I even attended the funeral of old Henry, Mr. Henry's father, young Henry's grandfather."
"They used to be a friendly family, but ever since young Henry fell ill three years ago, they've become strange…"
Listening to Polly's ramblings yielded little useful information.
However, Hobert was certain that the Henrys weren't ordinary fabric merchants. He decided that after receiving compensation from The Hanged Man, he would investigate further.
After informing Mr. Polly that he'd return in a few days, Hobert took his leave.
Upon returning to his law office, Hobert received a letter from the Mercenary Club, informing him that since yesterday evening, The Private had received two packages.
Hobert didn't expect The Hanged Man's package to arrive so quickly, but after thinking it over, he understood. The package must have come back with the mercenaries returning from the Southern Continent, and one of them had delivered it to the club.
After lunch, Hobert headed out again to "visit a client."
He didn't rush to collect the package but instead sat in the club's lounge for a while, sipping the club's provided tea. From the conversations around him, he learned that a group of mercenaries who had ambushed Beyonders from the Feysac Empire in the Southern Continent had returned by airship.
Many people already knew the details of the battle: two Sequence 5s, six Sequence 6s, seventeen Sequence 7s, and several Sequence 8s and 9s were taken down.
It was also said that the spoils included Beyonder characteristics, many mystical items, and even two sealed artifacts.
It was easy to imagine that this weekend's Beyonder gathering would feature several participants selling their spoils.
Hobert calculated his current wealth, which had reached nearly 1,100 pounds. If there was a suitable mystical item, he'd definitely make a move!
After two cups of tea, he finally went to the front desk to retrieve The Private's package.
Instead of leaving immediately, Hobert requested a small meeting room, where, after closing the door, he opened the first package. Inside was 600 pounds in cash.
Hobert happily counted the money, then took out his wallet—wait, his wallet was already full. He had to stuff the cash into his inner pocket.
At that moment, Hobert felt nostalgic for the days of online payments. Money in a phone wouldn't make him a target for thieves or criminals.
The other package contained a dark ring box. Hobert held the ring in his palm and, feeling no discomfort, slipped it onto his index finger.
The moment he put it on, his mind was filled with a dozen techniques for using a cane to attack enemies, as well as how to coordinate his footwork with his strikes and defenses in battle.
Hobert smiled slightly; this was exactly the ability he needed.
He glanced at the packaging on the table. It had to be destroyed to prevent anyone from tracing his identity.
Should he tear it into pieces? No, no, what if someone picks up the pieces and puts them back together?
But how should he destroy it? Fire? What if that starts a fire?
Or... wait, Hobert suddenly realized that his concerns were a side effect of the ring.

chapters.title: Chapter 60 - 60: I'm Asking on Behalf of a Friend
chapters.content:
Join www.patreon.com/KeyofStars for advance chapters
~~~
Hobert first bought a military-grade telescope from the mercenary club, then wrote a letter to Miss Xio, asking if she still wanted to consult him about Beyonder knowledge. Whether she wanted to or not, he requested her to meet him at the law office the next morning.
After sending the letter with the help of a servant, Hobert prepared to head home early to avoid missing dinner in three hours. When he arrived at the club's entrance, he began pondering whether stepping down with his left or right foot would be safer.
As he was choosing a mode of transportation, he worried about whether the hired carriage might overturn or if the coachman could be a psychopathic killer.
Bad rating! Hobert thought to himself after getting into the hired carriage. I should give the Hanged Man a bad review. Is this caution? This is more like paranoia!
However, Hobert had not yet taken off the ring. He wanted to quickly adapt to the negative effects of the ring, ideally being able to distinguish real caution from the ring's side effects as soon as the cautious thoughts arose.
Thus, at dinner, Hobert hesitated whether to pick up the sharp knife. While going up the stairs, he again contemplated which leg to step with first, and when closing the door, he turned back several times to ensure his clothes weren't caught.
Back in his room, physically and mentally exhausted, Hobert sighed: "Indeed, acquiring new abilities always comes with a price."
The next day, Hobert arrived at the law office at seven o'clock, two hours early, to avoid missing his meeting with Xio, which might disrupt his plans for the next few days.
This was an hour earlier than usual, and the office door wasn't even open yet.
Looking at the tightly closed door and having missed breakfast, Hobert felt an urge to return the ring.
However, after sitting on the office steps and reflecting, Hobert suddenly realized that his previous impulse to argue with others had disappeared. After all, arguing often leads to fights, and being cautious means it's better to stay quiet.
Thinking this way, he found that the ring's negative effects weren't entirely useless.
Alright, alright, I'll keep it, he thought, and then came the naming phase.
Hobert suspected that the Beyonder characteristic used to make the ring likely came from a Warrior Pathway Pugilist or a Mystery Pryer Pathway Melee Scholar.
The latter seemed more probable because the ring's negative effect likely originated from the Beyonder characteristic's provider. Typically, Beyonders of the Warrior Pathway weren't this overly cautious.
A comical image appeared in Hobert's mind: a warrior on the battlefield hesitating whether or not to fire his gun. What if the gun backfires? What if I hurt the enemy? What if the bullet damages the plants?
While the warrior hesitates in the trench, the enemy has already taken the position.
This image was absurd just thinking about it.
On the other hand, "Mystery Pryer," who know a lot of ritual magic and knowledge, tend to revere the Beyonder world and often become extremely cautious.
So, the ring's Beyonder characteristic was more likely from a "Melee Scholar."
Hobert thought, Since the ring can make me an expert fighter, I'll just call it the 'Combat Ring'!
Then Hobert wondered if he could use his Beyonder abilities to counteract the ring's negative effects.
More specifically, he thought about twisting the cautious thoughts induced by the ring. Since this was a confrontation with its negative effects, whether the twisting succeeded or not, he could generally tell which cautious thoughts were real and which stemmed from the negative effects.
It was a great idea, so Hobert gathered his spirituality and began resisting the ring.
He soon found this method very effective. He could easily distinguish the negative effects and, with his twist, no longer had to hesitate over trivial things like which leg to step with first.
However, with more complex caution, the effect of the twisting was limited. Hobert's hesitation was still noticeable, but he could now differentiate which thoughts were caused by the "Combat Ring's" negative effects, giving him a clear target in fighting against his overly cautious mindset.
Around nine o'clock, Xio and Fors arrived at the law office, and Hobert received them in a small meeting room.
Hobert dragged his chair a little further from Fors, always feeling like she might stretch out her hand and open a door on him. To be cautious, he thought it was better to keep his distance from her.
Wait, no! That's the Combat Ring's negative effect, he realized, and under Xio and Fors' slightly confused gazes, Hobert awkwardly dragged his chair back to its original position.
Xio asked with some concern, "Hobert, are... are your legs cramping?"
"No, no," Hobert said with a bitter smile. "I just... felt the floor was a bit uneven."
He quickly changed the topic: "Have you decided on what kind of Beyonder knowledge you want from me?
"As I mentioned before, it would be best if we start the operation this afternoon. If you haven't decided yet, you can choose to let me owe you an answer or explanation, or I can pay you a sum of money."
Xio said, "We've decided." She glanced at her friend Fors.
"I have a friend," Fors cleared her throat and said, "Yes, I'm asking on behalf of a friend.
"Well, during the appearance of a blood moon, she hears maddening ravings. Why is that?"
Hobert, of course, knew the backstory and immediately exposed it: "Your friend is a Beyonder of the 'Apprentice' Pathway, right?"
"Uh, uh?" Fors froze for a moment. "Y-yes."
Hobert continued, knowingly, "Does her surname happen to be Abraham?"
"No."
"In the Fourth Epoch, the Abraham family had mastered relatively complete potion formulas for the 'Apprentice' Pathway," Hobert explained. "But ever since their ancestor, Bethel Abraham, disappeared during the War of the Four Emperors, the family's Beyonders have seemed cursed, hearing maddening ravings on blood moon nights.
"I suspect your 'friend' consumed a Beyonder characteristic left behind by an Abraham family member without proper treatment, so even though she isn't a member of the Abraham family, she's still affected by their curse."
Xio quickly asked, "That's right! Your description is just like how our mutual friend described her experience! Is there a solution?"
"There are two solutions," Hobert said.
Xio was thrilled. She hadn't expected that the problem that had been giving them such headaches and left them clueless could be solved by Hobert in two ways!
"But both methods are difficult," Hobert added. "The first is to find a suitable mystical item to extract your friend's Beyonder characteristic, treat it, and then let her consume the characteristic again.
"To my knowledge, the Abraham family used to cultivate many non-family 'Apprentice' Pathway Beyonders. As long as the characteristic is treated and the person isn't a member of the Abraham family, they won't suffer from the family curse."

chapters.title: Chapter 61 - 61: The Beyonder Family
chapters.content:
Join www.patreon.com/KeyofStars for advance chapters
~~~
Hobert's suggestion left Xio and Fors baffled. Lacking sufficient knowledge about the Beyonders, they couldn't quite grasp the feasibility of Hobert's method.
Hobert continued, "From what I know, this method is incredibly painful and carries a high risk of losing control. So, unless absolutely necessary or if you're entirely confident, don't try it."
The reason he mentioned this method first was to showcase his expertise—essentially, he was bluffing. He added, "The second method is to wait and see—rely on your friend's luck!"
"Luck?" Fors asked, "What do you mean?"
Hobert smiled, "Once you become a Beyonder, your fate undergoes a massive transformation. All your problems will eventually be answered by the arrangement of fate.
"Don't think I'm being superstitious. The field of mysticism is inherently filled with complex and obscure matters."
Fors frowned, unsatisfied with this answer.
Xio asked directly, "Could you be a bit more specific?"
"The curse is a cry for help!" Hobert clarified further. "From what I know, a mysterious entity has recently taken an interest in this plea for help.
"This is your friend's opportunity. Don't try to manipulate fate—just let it unfold naturally."
For Hobert, letting events play out according to the original storyline was most advantageous, as it allowed him to maintain his "omniscient perspective."
Hobert's words managed to quiet both Xio and Fors, leaving them deep in thought.
After a dozen seconds of silence, Fors finally asked, "So, you're saying the best course of action is to do nothing?"
Hobert smiled, "Exactly. Pay close attention to everything around you, and you'll eventually find some hints from fate."
For example, Audrey placing The Fool's honorable name in Viscount Glaint's library. And, um, Audrey placing The Fool's honorable name in Viscount Glaint's library again.
Hobert added, "Perhaps, when things seem most uncontrollable, that's when fate is about to shift."
Xio scratched her head, "Hobert, is fate really that magical?"
Hobert shrugged, "The fate of a Beyonder is indeed that magical. Alright, I hope you won't worry too much about fate's arrangement. For us 'low-sequence' Beyonders, we can only accept the arrangement of fate.
"The more you dwell on it, the more fate fluctuates—and it just causes unnecessary trouble."
It was only then that Xio and Fors realized that Hobert seemed to be talking about some advanced mysticism knowledge they had never heard of or thought about before.
However, it felt like Hobert had only described a portion of this mysticism knowledge—they hadn't seen the whole picture.
Hobert asked, "Are you satisfied with my answer?"
"Very satisfied," Fors quickly replied. "This has given our friend a lot of insights. At the very least, she now understands the source of the curse and won't feel so lost and confused anymore."
Hobert nodded, "Now, let's talk about the next steps. Last week, while working on a case, I came across a villager who seemed to be a Beyonder.
"I'm curious where he got his potion formula from, so I want to investigate."
Seeing the puzzled looks on Xio and Fors' faces, Hobert smiled and explained, "Let me give you both some free knowledge.
"The Beyonder characteristics within the three of us can be traced back to the Fourth Epoch. Following the historical threads, the potion formulas for those on Xio's Pathway are primarily held by the royal families of Loen and the Feynapotter Kingdom.
"The potion formulas for Fors' Pathway are mainly controlled by the Theosophy Order and the Abraham family, or Beyonders associated with them.
"I suspect that after the disappearance of Abraham's ancestors in the Fourth Epoch, the family suffered attacks from other factions, causing significant losses without a powerful protector.
"The Theosophy Order, which formed in the early Fifth Epoch, likely obtained the Beyonder characteristics and potion formulas of the 'Apprentice' Pathway from their plunder of the Abraham family.
"As for the Beyonder characteristics of my own Pathway, they should theoretically be in the hands of three or four Beyonder families, but the historical threads became unclear after the War of the Four Emperors.
"Does that make sense?"
Xio nodded repeatedly, but from her expression, it was clear she didn't fully understand.
After some thought, Fors said, "So, if we trace the factions that control most of the Beyonders on our respective Pathways, we could use that as a clue to obtain the next potion formula!"
Her eyes lit up, "Mr. Hobert, the information you've shared is incredibly valuable to us! Is this really free?"
She had been unable to find the Trickmaster potion formula at the Beyonder gatherings and was almost ready to give up. But Hobert's words today gave her new hope.
Hobert smiled, "Of course it's free. Do you think I was joking when I said that, by forming the 'Justice League,' we're here to support each other?"
Wake up, girl. Free things are often the most expensive. Now that you know where to find the potion formula, won't you want to know more about the Theosophy Order? Will you need to take action? Can you and Xio obtain the formula on your own?
And if not, will you seek help?
Heh, Hobert realized today that he was quite the marketing genius.
Xio, finally understanding, let out a belated "Oh."
Hobert continued, "The villager I mentioned, who seems to be a Beyonder, appears to be on the same Sequence as me, so I'm curious about the source of his potion formula."
Xio asked, "When do we take action?"
Hobert glanced at his pocket watch, "It's not even 9:30 yet. Let's each make preparations, and how about we meet at Backlund Bridge at 1 p.m.?"
"Sounds good."
After seeing Xio and Fors off, Hobert returned to his rented room and summoned the "Spirit Medium Necklace" from the Nation of Disorder.
This time, Hobert held the initiative, unlike the previous investigation, where the clues vanished quickly, leaving no time to prepare. Now that he had time, he was determined to bring his best equipment, just in case there was a need for spiritual communication.
After putting on the necklace, Hobert activated Spirit Vision, and the world before him changed entirely. Everything became a misty gray, with only the living beings outside on the street still colored.
He envied those with high spiritual intuition, as they could see a person's health and general emotional state just by using Spirit Vision.
Shutting off Spirit Vision, Hobert gave in to his cautious side, deciding to leave early so as not to be late for the agreed meeting time. After having lunch at his law office, he took a carriage to Backlund Bridge.
As expected, Fors had managed to pull herself out of the embrace of her armchair to join her friend for the action.
Thus, the three young people took a rented carriage and headed to the outskirts of Backlund.

chapters.title: Chapter 62 - 62: The Door to the Spirit World
chapters.content:
Join www.patreon.com/KeyofStars for advance chapters
~~~
To avoid drawing attention, Hobert, Xio, and Fors got off the carriage early and left the main road, walking through the fields until they reached the countryside villa of Upton.
Xio found a good vantage point for surveillance. The three hid near their observation post, with Hobert using binoculars to look at the villa.
In the yard, a man in his forties was chopping wood, likely Upton's butler. Through the window, they could see shadows moving in a room on the second floor, which should be Upton himself.
However, despite watching for a long time, Upton did not come out.
Hobert checked his pocket watch. It was only around 4 p.m., and he whispered, "We'll move after dark."
Fors took the binoculars from Hobert, keeping watch over the distant farmyard. "Life here seems so peaceful. I dream of living like this. If only…"
If only it weren't for the whispers under the full moon, she would have saved up to buy such a small estate and spend every summer in peace.
Hobert smiled and said, "Dreams are only valuable when they remain dreams."
Fors sighed. "Emperor Roselle may have said something wise, but that's because all his dreams came true. I wouldn't know what it feels like to have my dreams fulfilled."
Hobert chuckled. "Alright, alright, all the famous quotes come from Emperor Roselle."
As the three of them chatted, the sun gradually set, and night descended.
At around 7 p.m., after having a simple meal in the wilderness, Hobert handed masks to Xio and Fors. "Don't reveal your voice, habitual movements, or anything else that could give you away. Upton might have ties with some secret Beyonder organizations."
After preparing, the three approached Upton's farm under the cover of darkness.
Though this place still belonged to Backlund, it was in a very remote area, with no nightlife to speak of. The nearby village had long since gone dark, leaving only one light shining on the second floor of Upton's villa.
Standing before the yard's wall, Fors kept watch outside while Hobert and Xio agilely jumped over the wall and into the yard.
Earlier that afternoon, Hobert had mentioned he had acquired a Beyonder item that made him more agile.
As partners, it was essential to inform one another about such things to avoid misunderstandings during operations.
However, Hobert hadn't told Xio about the "Spirit Necklace." While he trusted her, one always needed a few trump cards.
The two of them swiftly climbed up to the second-floor window, where the light was on. Inside, the dim light illuminated only half of the room, and they saw the figure of Upton lying in bed, as if he'd forgotten to blow out the oil lamp before falling asleep.
Hobert signaled Xio with his eyes, and they pushed the window open together and jumped inside.
According to the intel Hobert had gathered, Upton was likely a Lawyer or, at most, a Barbarian.
Even if they couldn't subdue him, both Hobert and Xio were confident they could easily escape, so Hobert suppressed many cautious thoughts and chose to take the most direct approach to get the information he needed.
As soon as they entered the room, Hobert sensed something off. The air was unnaturally cold. While it was late August in Backlund and the evenings could be cool, it shouldn't have been this cold.
Xio also realized something was wrong and didn't recklessly advance. She stayed by the window, guarding their escape route.
Though she might not always be the sharpest thinker, Xio was extremely reliable in action.
Suddenly, Hobert's spirituality was stirred. He quickly activated his Spirit Vision and saw a figure with an unnaturally long face and disheveled hair standing not far from them.
Hobert took a step back and immediately realized that the figure was a spirit. Though not aggressive, its appearance was certainly terrifying.
The Spirit Necklace gave him the ability to identify a spirit's weaknesses. Combined with his Lawyer ability to detect vulnerabilities, Hobert instantly realized that this spirit was afraid of fire, which was why it stayed in the farthest corner from the oil lamp.
Hobert stepped forward, grabbed the oil lamp, and hurled it at the spirit.
Crash!
The oil lamp shattered, and flames spread along the spilled oil, igniting the floor.
Whoosh!
With a howl, the spirit swiftly fled the room.
At the moment the oil lamp hit the floor, a figure rushed out from the dark corner. In the firelight, they could see it was a young man with evident nervousness on his face.
He swung a fist toward Hobert's head, but Hobert easily dodged.
After activating Spirit Vision earlier, Hobert had glanced at the bed and hadn't detected any living aura there. Instead, he sensed a person's aura in the darkness of the room, and he had guessed that Upton was hiding there. Thus, he had been prepared for Upton's ambush.
But Hobert found it odd that Upton was so guarded.
When Upton's punch missed, he followed up with a series of attacks, each blow carrying tremendous force.
However, Hobert skillfully used his cane to counter Upton's strikes, holding his own in the fight. It was as if he instinctively knew how to attack his opponent and how to dodge each blow, moving like a natural-born fighter.
At the same time, Hobert realized that Upton had consumed the Barbarian potion. His strength was astonishing, and several times, Hobert's cane was nearly knocked from his hands. The Lawyer pathway wasn't supposed to be this strong.
However, Hobert soon noticed that, while Upton's attacks were powerful, they were somewhat slow.
At this moment, Xio joined the fight, and Upton lost the ability to retaliate.
Yet, he sneered, "Did the Tamara family really send two nobodies like you to kill me? How naive!"
Upton's face suddenly turned pale, and Hobert abruptly saw that the door to the room had opened.
But beyond the door was a strange, indescribable world—a place of chaos without up or down, filled with vast amounts of information. One could see every detail of that world, with nothing obstructing their view.
Hobert and Xio both felt a wave of dizziness and nausea as they stared.
The Spirit World!
Hobert realized what he was seeing—the Spirit World!
While low-sequence Beyonders could sense the Spirit World and some with heightened spirituality could even receive revelations from it, they could not yet directly touch or enter it.
As the door to the Spirit World opened, a humanoid monster emerged, with long arms and a tongue, lacking eyes and ears.
Hobert and Xio's spirituality immediately screamed of the incoming danger.

chapters.title: Chapter 63 - 63: The Suicide-Type Sealed Artifact
chapters.content:
Join www.patreon.com/KeyofStars for advance chapters
~~~
The spirit with long arms and tongue moved incredibly fast, and Hobert realized there was no time to escape.
However, the Spirit Necklace and the Lawyer abilities quickly revealed that this spirit had a weakness—fear of water.
Water!
There was water on the table over there!
But it was too late; the spirit had already raised its long arm, which transformed into a scythe, resembling the Grim Reaper ready to claim a life.
Ho-phuu~
In a panic, Hobert spat at the spirit.
What happened next was a rather comical sight through Hobert's spiritual vision: the terrifying spirit carefully avoided the spit on the ground.
It looked as if it were cautiously avoiding a landmine.
Although Xio and Upton couldn't see this through their spiritual vision, their instincts told them that the threat had suddenly paused.
Upton, in disbelief, exclaimed, "Damn, this is the first time I've seen holy water like this."
By this point, the spirit had circled around Hobert's spit, and Hobert hurriedly spat again. The spirit circled around once more, and Hobert spat again.
Thus, what had been a dangerous battle turned into a bizarre scene of Xio and Upton watching Hobert continuously spitting on the ground.
Soon, Hobert's mouth was dry, and he shouted to Xio, "Spit towards two o'clock!"
Xio quickly realized that the spit could repel this invisible threat. However, although she was usually quite bold, she was still a young woman with some sense of decorum.
Hobert, out of options, gathered the last bit of saliva and spat towards the "long-armed spirit," once again halting its advance. "Hurry! I'm out!"
Finally, Xio spat in the two o'clock direction, and Hobert took the opportunity to rush over, grab the glass of water on the table, and splash the remaining water at the "long-armed spirit."
Whoosh~
With a shrill howl, the "long-armed spirit" vanished.
Upton, gathering the last of his spirituality, said, "It's not over yet!"
Freed from the battle, Hobert finally had the chance to pull out his gun and point it at Upton, dry-mouthed and hoarse as he shouted, "We're not from the damn Tamara family. If you use another sealed or mystical item, I'll shoot you dead!"
Upton, having expended a lot of spirituality, was even paler than before, gasping for breath. He asked, "Then who are you?"
Hobert commanded, "Raise your hands!"
Not wanting to die, Upton quickly complied.
Xio, in sync with Hobert, began searching Upton and found a strand of glowing hair on his arm.
It was a sealed artifact. Hobert handed Xio a pair of gloves he had prepared in advance. "Don't touch the hair directly."
Xio nodded, put on the gloves, and carefully removed the glowing strand of hair, placing it on the table.
Hobert, once again holding a gun in one hand while rummaging through his coat pockets for vials with the other, asked, "Have you ever heard of spirit communication?"
"Y-yes," Upton replied, sensing something bad.
"Apologies," Hobert said sincerely. "Interrogating you is too troublesome, and I'd have to figure out whether you're telling the truth or not. So, I'll use spirit communication to get the answers I need.
"But you're still a living being, and spirit communication will completely mess up your thoughts and logic. After I get the answers, you'll have the intelligence of a two- or three-year-old."
"For that, I deeply apologize."
Upton turned deathly pale. "W-wait, wait! You haven't even asked me anything yet. How do you know I won't tell the truth?"
From Upton's reaction, it seemed he wasn't a very experienced Beyonder, because if he had known about spirit communication or had been properly informed, he would've realized that Hobert's words were only half true.
Given Hobert's current spirituality and mental strength, he wouldn't dare use spirit communication on a living person, as the overwhelming amount of information from the other person's spirituality would severely impact his mental state.
The result would likely be two new lunatics in the world.
"Alright then," Hobert said. "I'll ask the first question. Where did you get your potion formula and the main ingredients?
"You saw earlier that I can communicate with the spirit world to defeat the spirit you summoned. I can also use divination, and if you lie, I'll immediately resort to spirit communication."
Upton hurriedly replied, "My potion formula and the main ingredients come from the Tamara family! I swear I'm telling the truth."
Hobert hadn't tried using the Spirit Necklace for divination before, but theoretically, since the necklace enhanced the wearer's spiritual intuition, it could also assist with basic divination.
Of course, Hobert couldn't perform complex divination like a Seer, but he could manage simple yes-no answers.
He closed his eyes and silently repeated in his mind, "Upton is lying.
"Upton is lying.
"…"
After repeating this seven times, Hobert stood his cane upright and lightly let go. If the cane fell forward, Upton was lying; if it fell backward, Upton was telling the truth.
Hobert saw the cane fall backward and smiled. "Very good. Let's hope you continue to tell the truth. Second question, what are the abilities of the sealed artifact you just used? What are its negative effects? And where did it come from?"
Having been frightened by Hobert's divination, Upton gave up on lying entirely. "This sealed artifact is called the Astrologer's Hair. My father said it came from a runaway Astrologer.
"It has two abilities. One is a vague sense of danger that will happen within six hours. The other is opening a door to the spirit world. Behind that door, there might be nothing, but more often, a mysterious spirit with unknown abilities and intent appears, attacking both allies and enemies indiscriminately.
"The negative effects are that the wearer is easily noticed by certain entities in the spirit world. After using it for more than an hour, the wearer will merge into the spirit world and never return to the real world."
Hobert thought to himself: No wonder he knew we were coming to attack him. It's due to this sealed artifact's ability. But its abilities and negative effects sound like it's practically a suicide-type sealed artifact!
A spirit that attacks everyone; attention from certain entities in the spirit world; never being able to return to reality.
Both the abilities and the negative effects are terrifying.
Upton continued, "This sealed artifact was taken by my father from the Tamara family."
Hobert was taken aback. "What's your family's relationship with the Tamara family?"
It seemed like they were both enemies and capable of taking sealed artifacts from them?
Upton smiled bitterly. "I am part of the Tamara family, but ever since I was a child, my father has been trying to sever ties with them."
"Why sever ties?"
"My father said that the 'high-Sequence' members of the family seemed to be affected by some kind of mysterious corruption."

chapters.title: Chapter 64 - 64: Upton's Request
chapters.content:
Join www.patreon.com/KeyofStars for advance chapters
~~~
Hobert suddenly recalled that the Tamara family was one of the five great families that supported Tudor in founding his empire, with a long and storied history.
It seemed they possessed the potion formulas for the Lawyer and Arbiter Pathways. Due to a past marriage alliance with the Abraham family, they also held part of the Apprentice Pathway's potion formulas and Beyonder characteristics.
However, after the fall of the Tudor Empire, members of this family rarely appeared in the public eye.
Even Hobert, who had thoroughly studied the original work, only vaguely remembered the general situation of this family and could not recall the specifics.
This indicated that the family had indeed appeared very infrequently.
In Hobert's impression, if one traced the Lawyer Pathway's Beyonder characteristics back to the Fourth Epoch, they were essentially held by three families: the Solomon family, the Tudor family, and the Trunsoest family.
The Tamara family never produced a "Black Emperor" or "Justiciar," suggesting that at most, they only possessed Sequence 2 Beyonder characteristics during the Fourth Epoch.
However, after the fall of the Blood Emperor and the Night Emperor, things became unclear. Most Beyonder families gained Sequence 1 characteristics through the downfall of their former "masters."
For instance, Blood Emperor Tudor and Night Emperor Trunsoest obtained the Sequence 1 characteristics of the "Black Emperor" Pathway after assisting the Seven Gods in defeating Solomon, thus ushering in the era of dual governance.
To Hobert, the Tamara family was shrouded in fog—its strength and stance unknown.
Moreover, had their "High-Sequence" Beyonders been secretly contaminated?
Hobert asked, "What kind of contamination?"
Upton replied, "I don't know. My father didn't tell me. Maybe he didn't know either.
"In any case, my father always said that the Tamara family had become unrecognizable and that I should rather die than return to it."
Hobert's spirituality suddenly issued a warning, indicating that the topic should not be pursued or discussed further.
He quickly changed the subject: "You don't seem to be in great shape." This was apparent from the other's aura.
Upton smiled bitterly: "Yes, ever since I took the Barbarian potion last year, my condition has been poor.
"My mother told me that it's because I hadn't fully controlled the 'Lawyer' Beyonder abilities before forcing my promotion."
He added sorrowfully, "My mother died after failing to forcibly advance to the rank of Astrologer."
Clearly, their family had no understanding of the concepts of "acting" and "digesting." Hobert was puzzled: "You've already left the Tamara family? Why take such a risk to forcibly advance?"
Upton sighed: "My father's plan to leave the family was discovered early. Fortunately, his prior preparations allowed us to escape the pursuit of the family members.
"But my father said that the preparations he made would only hide us for ten years. After that, since we carry the blood of the Tamara family, the family members skilled in divination would immediately find us.
"My father tried to seek refuge with other factions to avoid the family's pursuit, but they were more interested in obtaining the sealed artifact and information about the Tamara family that my father possessed, leading to even greater disasters.
"My father lost the immensely powerful sealed artifact, was gravely injured, and after shaking off the pursuers with my mother and me, he soon passed away.
"My mother and I didn't dare contact any other factions. We could only try to enhance our power through promotion, but it was too late. My father died, my mother died, and I'm barely able to control the 'Barbarian' potion. If I try to advance again, I'll immediately lose control."
As Upton spoke, his eyes reddened: "It's been ten years now. Maybe next week, maybe next month, but family members will certainly come for me."
Having also lost his father at a young age, Xio felt some sympathy for Upton: "Don't think about advancing anymore—just run."
Hobert also said, "My companion is right. Staying here is a dead end."
"I'm unwilling!" Upton's eyes burned with fire: "We only wanted to live a free life. Ever since I was a child, I dreamed of becoming a merchant, traveling while doing business and seeing the world.
"Why? Why do I have to live so miserably, like a fugitive?"
Hobert holstered his gun and said, "How many people in this world can truly control their own fate?"
He gestured to Xio, and the two began to retreat toward the window, ready to leave.
Suddenly, Upton called out to them: "Wait! Can you help me escape the family's pursuit?"
Hobert chuckled: "It's just the two of us. Do you really expect us to take on the entire Tamara family?"
"No, no," Upton said. "My father once said that, based on the family's usual methods, the pursuers would likely consist of one Sequence 6, two Sequence 7s, maybe two Sequence 8s, and a sealed artifact.
"If you can defeat them, I can use the method my father taught me to hide myself for another ten years."
Hobert twitched his lips: "Do we look like we can handle a Sequence 6?"
Upton replied, "You both are likely Sequence 9 or Sequence 8, but you have sealed artifacts or magical items on you. I suspect you belong to some organization. I'd like to ask your organization for help!
"I can give you the 'Astrologer's Hair!'"
Hobert shook his head: "Keep it for yourself. I'd like to live a few more years!"
Having learned the source of Upton's potion formulas and the current state of the Tamara family, Hobert's goal had already been achieved. As for the "Astrologer's Hair," carrying such a dangerous sealed artifact was courting death!
"I can also give you the potion formulas for 'Lawyer,' 'Barbarian,' and 'Briber'!" Upton quickly added. "As well as those for 'Apprentice,' 'Trickmaster,' and 'Astrologer'!"
His father's previous experiences had made him extra cautious: "But I've hidden these formulas using a special method. Even if you use spirit channeling on me, you'd only get the formulas for 'Lawyer' and 'Barbarian.'"
Hearing the mention of "Trickmaster," Xio's eyes lit up. This was exactly the potion formula that a friend of hers had been searching for!
Meanwhile, Hobert marveled at how deep the foundations of a Beyonder family ran. Even a down-and-out family member still had a sealed artifact and so many potion formulas.
He calculated in his mind: if he could get Christian to take action, it would be relatively easy to deal with a Sequence 6. That way, he could obtain the potion formula for "Briber" and also likely acquire its Beyonder characteristic.
Thinking of this, Hobert finally said, "If my superior is willing to help you, I'll come back to visit you!"
With that, Hobert and Xio jumped out of the window.
Upton sat weakly on a chair, repeatedly "chewing" on one word: "Superior! Superior?…"

chapters.title: Chapter 65 - 65: Using the Rules
chapters.content:
Join www.patreon.com/KeyofStars for advance chapters
~~~
Before Hobert left, he intentionally said those words for Upton to hear.
It was to intimidate Upton, as well as to deter any future members of the Tamara family who might kill Upton and attempt mediumship.
Of course, it was also a way to convey a message to Upton: "You guessed it right, I do have an organization backing me, one that can solve your problems."
Hobert met up with Xio and Fors, who had been waiting outside, and the three of them returned to the fields. Once they confirmed no one was following them, Xio whispered excitedly, "Fors, we actually found a clue to the 'Trickmaster' potion formula!"
They found a hidden place to rest, and Xio recounted their recent encounter.
In the darkness, Fors glanced at Hobert. He was more powerful, mysterious, and strange than she had imagined. "Could this be the turning point of fate you mentioned?"
Hobert smiled helplessly, "Maybe!"
Miss, this is a clue that wasn't in the original story; even I don't know what will happen next.
He paused for a few seconds and then said to Xio, "After all, this means going against a Beyonder family, and I can't make that decision alone. But if we decide to help Upton, I'll let you know."
Xio nodded. "I understand."
After resting for a few more minutes, they walked several kilometers and finally found a rental carriage.
As they entered the southern district of Backlund, the area became brightly lit once again, reflecting the vibrant nightlife of this metropolis.
When they were about a kilometer away from their rental home, Xio and Fors got off the carriage. Hobert returned home by carriage, arriving past 10 p.m.
He had left a note in the morning, saying he might return late, so only the butler was waiting for him. Everyone else had gone to bed.
Hobert drank three glasses of water before heading to his room.
He first removed his "Spirit Necklace" and "Combat Ring." Carrying both magical items had drained a lot of his spirituality.
Lying on his bed, Hobert didn't fall asleep immediately. Instead, he began reflecting on the day's events.
It was only when he saw the entrance to the spirit world and that "long-armed spirit" that Hobert realized his actions had been somewhat reckless.
The main reason was that he had underestimated his opponent. When he learned Upton was alone on the farm, he assumed he was dealing with a wild Beyonder who had stumbled upon a stroke of luck.
If Upton had been a member of a Beyonder family, it would've been highly risky for him to live alone in such a place. Typically, if only one family member remained, they would likely seek refuge with relatives or have relatives come live with them.
This not only helps prevent losing control but also protects against threats from hostile families or enemies.
Although no one could have anticipated Upton's unique situation, Hobert still felt that his actions were rash. In the future, he vowed to gather more information before acting in similar situations.
He then thought of the Henry family they had met through the door yesterday. They likely had close ties to the Lawyer Pathway.
This was inevitable due to the "Law of Beyonder Characteristics Convergence." People or objects aligned with the Lawyer Pathway would naturally gravitate toward Hobert, who held the Nation of Disorder.
Fortunately, Hobert was still only Sequence 9, and the power that the Nation of Disorder could project through him was extremely limited. Most of the entities gravitating toward him were of low Sequence.
Of course, there was also the chance of encountering mid or high Sequence Beyonders or Sealed Artifacts. These powerful entities generally wouldn't pay much attention to a Sequence 9.
After all, Hobert did have "backing," and being the "eldest son of the commander" provided him with a lot of protection.
Moreover, up until now, the powerful individuals couldn't sense the Sefirah-level aura of the Nation of Disorder from Hobert.
At this point, Hobert realized that constantly viewing the Law of Convergence in a negative light wasn't productive. This law had brought him many benefits.
For example, Fors had been searching for the "Trickmaster" potion formula for years, but Hobert had stumbled upon a clue to the "Briber" potion formula while working on his third case.
This made the test set by his biological father much less difficult.
Of course, this was contingent on Christian's willingness to help, which would make things significantly easier.
In this light, the Law of Convergence was a positive force, providing Hobert with more opportunities to obtain potion formulas and corresponding Beyonder characteristics.
Although this did imply some level of danger, as long as he acted cautiously, most risks could be mitigated. The Beyonder world was inherently dangerous, and some threats were unavoidable, no matter how much one tried to avoid them.
With the "Combat Ring" and "Spirit Necklace," Hobert believed he had the ability to contend with some Sequence 8 Beyonders and escape from Sequence 7 enemies.
As for facing higher Sequence Beyonders, there was no shame in admitting defeat or relying on his background when necessary.
Finally, Hobert concluded in his mind: Don't let laws and rules become a burden, but actively use them to your advantage.
Suddenly, that familiar, exhilarating feeling surged through him again. Hobert realized that he had somehow digested almost a third of his potion!
So, this is what it means to be a Lawyer?
To work with the rules, and to know how to actively exploit them!
This must be a core part of the "acting method." Hobert recalled how, during his previous digestion, it had been a clash of contracts between spirits. Adhering to the spirit of contracts was only the most basic requirement for a Lawyer.
The essence of a Lawyer lies in manipulating the law—in other words, the rules.
The rapid digestion of his potion excited Hobert so much that he couldn't sleep for half the night. Only in the early hours did he finally calm his emotions and drift off to sleep.
...
In a small town on the Southern Continent.
The town boasted a scenic little hill, where the Balk family's council hall and the patriarch's residence were situated halfway up.
As the first rays of sunlight hit the hill, eight elders of the family gathered in the council hall.
Today, they were set to discuss a crucial issue regarding the Balk family's future direction. As the local power in General Anthony's territory, they had already learned about the Feysac Empire Beyonders being ambushed by a group of mercenaries.
This had created a power vacuum within General Anthony's territory. If the Balk family wished to continue supporting the Feysac Empire's rule here, they had the opportunity to fill part of that vacuum.
The eight elders took their seats amid polite small talk, though there were actually nine chairs in the hall. The patriarch's seat had been empty for the past year.
This wasn't because the Balk family lacked a patriarch; rather, the patriarch's condition had worsened. He was constantly battling madness and a curse, leaving most of the day-to-day affairs to the eight elders.

chapters.title: Chapter 66 - 66: Opportunities and Risks Coexist
chapters.content:
Join www.patreon.com/KeyofStars for advance chapters
~~~
Typically, for a warlord like General Anthony, the colonizers or backers behind him would send a demigod and five or six Sequence 5 Beyonders to protect their colonial interests. The demigod serves more as a deterrent, while Sequence 5 and Sequence 6 Beyonders handle the actual affairs of the colony. However, the ambush on the Feysac Empire caused the loss of two Sequence 5 Beyonders and several Sequence 6, which led to a disruption in the colonial administration system.
In every nation, Sequence 5 Beyonders usually hold positions of real power. As a result, the Feysac Empire and the Church of the God of Combat could only dispatch one Sequence 5 to the Southern Continent for the time being.
The Balk family, being the local power, was already aware of this information.
This presented an opportunity—if the Balk family could send a Sequence 5 Beyonder to help the Feysac Empire maintain control, they could gain some colonial benefits in return.
It was a favorable trade, with both sides getting what they needed. After all, no one wanted to permanently rely on the profits from the assassination business.
But the risks were also substantial. While the Feysac Empire might welcome the Balk family's help now, once they had sufficient manpower, they might try to reclaim the lost benefits.
During the meeting in the council hall, five of the elders opposed joining the Feysac Empire in sharing the benefits. They believed the family's Beyonder characteristics were too precious to risk any loss. Leaving their current stronghold in the Nonexistent Town would mean facing immense danger, and risking the loss of their Beyonder characteristics.
They believed the current mode of operation, which the family had been following, was much safer.
Before calling for a final vote, Elder Calvin spoke up, "Before we make a final decision, I have something to share. There's a young man named Elliott in our family…"
He briefly recounted Elliott's recent experiences. Elder Bowen, who was in his thirties, responded, "Such abnormal luck surely indicates something is wrong. We should immediately detain Elliott and interrogate him thoroughly."
However, Chester, an elder in his forties and a demigod, disagreed, "That may result in us discovering nothing at all."
"I agree," Calvin added. "We should quietly observe Elliott for now, and, if an opportunity arises, test him. But we must not interrogate him rashly without being certain."
Calvin shifted the conversation: "The reason I mentioned Elliott is to remind everyone that the Balk family might be facing a new test. Just like how Elliott unexpectedly brought back a 'Barbarian' Beyonder characteristic, could this be a test for us?
"We can't use old methods of thinking to solve today's problems. Moreover, by utilizing Rex's methods to combat the curse, our strength has significantly increased over the past two decades.
"We've grown from five Sequence 5 Beyonders to now having three Saints, including the family head, who is Sequence 3, along with seventeen Sequence 5s. With such strength, we could easily control two warlords in the Southern Continent.
"It's time to show the world our strength. Once the Feysac royal family realizes we are a demigod family, they wouldn't dare turn against us lightly.
"Let me quote Roselle: 'Opportunities always come with risks.' It's time we abandoned some of our conservative strategies."
After these words, the elders fell into deep contemplation.
…
In the rented apartment in Backlund, Xio and Fors.
Early in the morning, Fors was lounging in an armchair. "Are you sure? Hobert really mentioned his 'elder'?"
Xio, eating breakfast, replied, "I'm sure! Fors, this is the third time you've asked!"
"This is important," Fors said seriously. "Didn't your investigation show he's the general's son? It's not surprising if his father is a Beyonder.
"But he didn't say 'father'; he said 'elder.' This means his family has more than one Beyonder! We guessed right—he's from a Beyonder family!"
Xio nodded. "Otherwise, he wouldn't know so much about the Beyonder fworld."
"Xio, you're missing the point," Fors's eyes suddenly gleamed with wisdom as she lit a cigarette. "He drove away a spirit from the spirit world! Such an act requires strong intuition and corresponding Beyonder abilities.
"If I'm not mistaken, he must possess another magical item he hasn't told us about!"
She sighed, "Being born into a Beyonder family really has its perks. For us, getting hold of one magical item is nearly impossible, but he has two!"
Finishing her breakfast, Xio suddenly added, "Maybe he acquired those items himself."
"Why would you think that?"
"I just feel… he doesn't seem like the type who likes to rely on others."
"Think whatever you like." Through her interactions with Hobert, Fors had noticed that Xio and Hobert had a friendship more like that of comrades-in-arms. She trusted Hobert now and no longer worried about him "playing with girls' feelings" or anything like that.
She concluded, "In any case, having a friend like him will certainly bring us many opportunities."
For example, she had searched for years without finding the formula for the Trickmaster's potion. Yet on her first outing with Hobert, they found clues to a potion formula.
…
Later that morning, Hobert took a hired carriage and headed back to the western suburbs. He intended to visit the Henry family again.
He knew this visit carried some risk, but after thinking it over, he concluded the risk was manageable.
The Henry family had lived in the town for years, and they wouldn't expose themselves unless it was absolutely necessary.
So Hobert believed that as long as he wasn't reckless enough to try to seize their Sealed Artifact, he wouldn't be in any danger.
More importantly, Hobert had decided the night before that, since the Henry family had been drawn to him by the Law of Beyonder Characteristics Convergence, there must be a reason for it.
Actively approaching them and turning the risk into an opportunity was a way to use the law to his advantage and a part of his role-playing.
If he ignored the potential risk, it might eventually escalate into a greater danger because of the Law of Beyonder Characteristics Convergence.
Since he couldn't avoid it, he might as well face it head-on. Opportunities and risks often come hand in hand.
At this thought, Hobert grew curious, wondering if Emperor Roselle had ever said something similar.
Hobert first visited Mr. Polly's house. After a brief conversation, he left through the back yard and went to visit Mr. Henry.
Polly and Ailey watched from their backyard as this bold young man entered the Henry family's yard.
Hobert's entry immediately triggered barking dogs. Even Polly began to wonder if he had been mistaken about the intruder—it seemed more likely that the barking was coming from the Henry family's dog.
But then he shook his head. Many had seen the massive dog emerge from Ailey's basement.
Hobert was about to knock on the door when he suddenly felt a strong sense of death and decay. Using his spiritual vision, he saw that there were no living beings inside the house.
Had the Henry family died of a plague?
Call the authorities?
Or explore first?
Hobert quickly made up his mind, kicked the door open, and found two heavily decomposed corpses in the living room.
The sight made Hobert's scalp tingle. Judging by the state of the bodies, they had been dead for over a week.
So the question remained—who had spoken to him through the door two days ago?

chapters.title: Chapter 67 - 67: The Contaminated Giant Dog
chapters.content:
Join www.patreon.com/KeyofStars for advance chapters
~~~
Polly and Ailey were startled by Hobert's sudden action. Without knocking, he had kicked down the door to Henry's house!
Hobert forced himself to suppress the fear rising inside. As he scanned the room, he saw two corpses lying nearby, alongside candles, inverted triangles, occult symbols, mystical materials, and books. He roughly understood what had happened.
It seemed that Henry and his wife had performed some kind of occult ritual days ago. Since they held a ritual, they must have needed a "wall of spirituality."
But it wasn't clear whether the problem lay in the ritual process or the ritual itself. In any case, the couple had perished during the ritual.
Thanks to the presence of the "wall of spirituality," their spirituality hadn't dispersed immediately. So, when Hobert knocked on their door previously, they had still been able to respond.
Of course, it was also possible that the ritual had left them in a strange state—perhaps they hadn't even realized they were dead. Their rotting corpses had continued to "function" within the wall of spirituality, even using "influenza" as an excuse to drive away strangers who might interrupt the ritual.
However, once the wall of spirituality began to dissipate, the couple's spirituality also gradually faded away, leading to the scene Hobert now faced.
Oddly enough, there were no traces of Beyonder characteristics near the two bodies. This suggested that the couple weren't Beyonders themselves.
Initially, Hobert had intended to enter the house for a brief inspection. But given the increasingly complicated situation, rushing in blindly didn't seem like the best idea. Reporting it to the authorities seemed like the more prudent choice, and after all, this was a specialty of the Tarot Club.
He turned to Polly and Ailey, who were standing in their backyard, and said, "Quick, report this to the authorities. Tell them that Henry's family has died under mysterious circumstances. Be sure to emphasize 'mysterious.'"
The two farmers were visibly shocked. Polly was the first to snap out of it. "Okay, okay, I'll go right away!"
"Wait." Hobert pulled out some paper and a pen from his briefcase, saying, "Please send a telegram for me as well."
On the paper, he wrote: Polly's neighbor family has mysteriously died. I may undergo some special interrogation.
On the back of the paper, he wrote: No. 112, Baiminlan Street, Jolwood District. To: Lawyer Barton.
"The reverse side has the recipient's address and name," Hobert added, handing Polly a 2 soli note. "Please send the telegram first, then report it to the authorities."
A telegram would reach Lawyer Barton within two or three hours, while sending a letter—even within the same city—would take at least until the next day.
He chose to inform Barton rather than contacting Christian directly because there was no guarantee that a civilian telegram would reach her. It was more reliable to have Barton notify her.
Polly nodded repeatedly. Sending a telegram wouldn't cost anywhere near 2 soli, and the sight of the note ensured he'd follow Hobert's instructions to the letter.
From the basement, the dog likely sensed an intruder on its master's property. Its barking grew more intense, accompanied by the sound of claws scratching at the basement door, as if the beast were ready to break through at any moment.
Fortunately, Henry's basement door was sturdy enough to withstand the dog's efforts for now.
As the nearby farmers' children began to curiously peek towards the house, Hobert turned to Ailey and said, "Mr. Ailey, please keep watch at the gate and make sure no one comes inside.
"Trust me, if the children see what's in there, they will be terrified."
Since it wasn't harvest season yet, the children didn't need to help in the fields, which meant that many were just playing around the village.
"Alright, alright!" Ailey began to move from his backyard but, suddenly, the sounds from Henry's basement stopped.
The world seemed to fall into an eerie silence. In that moment, Hobert's spiritual sense picked up a surge of "distortion."
Crash!
Ailely's basement door was violently smashed open by an immense force. Ailey's basement didn't house any animals, so it hadn't been reinforced, and the door broke instantly.
A gigantic dog, the size of a donkey, charged out from the basement.
The beast's fur was riddled with tumor-like growths, some of which had already burst open, oozing brown pus.
The tumors distorted the dog's face, making it look grotesque, terrifying, and pained all at once.
Hobert's sudden intrusion had clearly enraged the creature. Its eyes, now clouded and devoid of reason, locked onto Ailey, the closest target, and it charged at him.
"Get down!" Hobert shouted as he rushed towards Ailey's home, gun in hand.
Ailey, upon seeing the monstrous dog, was frozen in place. Hobert's shout, along with the sight of the gun, jolted him into action, and almost instinctively, he threw himself to the ground.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Hobert fired three shots. The first missed the giant dog, but the second hit its shoulder, and the third struck its head.
After the third shot, the dog collapsed to the ground. Both Hobert and Ailey breathed sighs of relief.
The giant dog hadn't died immediately, though. Its gaze, no longer clouded, seemed to regain clarity in its final moments. It let out a mournful howl towards Henry's house.
Hobert, gazing at the dying dog, said softly, "Your master is waiting for you up ahead. You're finally free now."
It seemed the dog understood his words. It stopped howling and passed away peacefully.
The dog's immense size, along with its disfigured condition, indicated that it had been contaminated by some Beyonder characteristic or sealed artifact.
This kind of contamination was irreversible. Hobert hadn't lied; death was indeed a release for the creature.
As for how the dog had ended up in Ailey's basement, it was likely due to the effects of the sealed artifact in Henry's home, which had the power to distort space, connecting the two basements that weren't far apart.
With Henry and his wife dead, no one was left to continue sealing the artifact, allowing it to contaminate their dog while occasionally displaying its abilities.
Given the nature of the distortion power, the artifact was likely related to the Lawyer Pathway. Though, it could also belong to the Apprentice Pathway, though according to the Law of Beyonder Characteristics Convergence, the former was more probable.
Hobert helped Ely to his feet. Ailey, still shaken from the encounter, looked at the dog's corpse and muttered, "Storm above! What kind of monster is this? And how did it end up in my basement?"
"Please, keep watch over Henry's gate," Hobert said, choosing not to explain. Better to let the official Beyonders deal with it.
He then asked, "What faith did Henry's family follow?"
"The Evernight Goddess," Ely replied as Hobert helped him to the gate.
Hobert nodded. That meant the Nighthawks would handle this case.
Ailey leaned against the gatepost, shouting at the children who had gathered to watch, "Go home, all of you!"
With Ailey guarding the gate, Hobert felt at ease as he approached the basement door. He kicked it open, and was immediately hit by the stench of dog excrement and urine. Inside, it was pitch black, as if the sunlight from outside couldn't penetrate the space.
All signs pointed to the fact that the sealed artifact was still "active."
Hobert returned to the front door of the house. Among the scattered books near the corpses, some appeared to be journals, while others were more formal texts. There was a good chance that the journals contained information about the artifact's effects or how it had been sealed.
Stepping inside, Hobert first inspected the bodies to ensure that Henry and his wife were indeed dead. Only then did he squat down to search for any useful notes.
Thump! Thump!
Suddenly, there came a loud banging sound from the second floor.

chapters.title: Chapter 68 - 68: The Solomon Family
chapters.content:
Join www.patreon.com/KeyofStars for advance chapters
~~~
Thud, thud...
Hobert drew his gun once again, cautiously looking upstairs.
The banging sound on the door continued for a few moments before stopping. Hobert, however, had no intention of investigating it like a typical horror movie protagonist would.
He hurriedly grabbed a notebook and retreated to the yard to flip through its pages.
Upon opening the notebook, he saw an abstract design of a scepter and a sword on the title page. It resembled a family crest.
As for which family it belonged to, Hobert wasn't sure, but he soon found the answer within the notebook: it was the crest of the Solomon family. It turned out that the Henry family were descendants of the Solomon lineage.
Hobert smiled as though he had expected this all along—it was indeed the family of a Lawyer pathway Beyonder.
After the fall of the Ancient Sun God, Solomon, with the support of the True Creator and Rose Redemption, became the ruler of the Northern Continent, ushering in the era of the Solomon Empire.
Later, the Six Gods reached an agreement to jointly eliminate the True Creator. Under their combined assault, the True Creator was forced to retreat to the Forsaken Land along with a portion of his followers.
The Black Emperor Solomon, too, became a casualty in this struggle. From that point onward, the Solomon family was hunted down by all the Churches of the Orthodox Gods.
A large family like the Solomons naturally had survivors, and Solomon himself had even revived once, founding the Second Solomon Empire, which revitalized this Beyonder family.
During the War of the Four Emperors, Solomon fell once more. The Six Gods supported the reign of families such as the Augustus and Castiya, ensuring that no true god ruled over human secular powers anymore. Thus began the history of the Fifth Epoch.
The Solomon family went into hiding again, awaiting Solomon's eventual return. However, in the last few centuries, there had been no word of any descendants of the Solomon family. Presumably, over the long passage of time, their strength had greatly diminished.
More than a hundred years ago, Emperor Roselle forcefully jumped to non-adjacent sequences, becoming the new Black Emperor, signaling Solomon's complete demise. This must have been another heavy blow to the Solomon family.
The contents of the notebook corroborated what Hobert already knew. In the early Fifth Epoch, in order to escape the persecution of the Orthodox Churches, the surviving members of the Solomon family scattered across the Northern Continent, organizing themselves into smaller family units.
The Henry family was a descendant of one such scattered family. According to the notebook, the last contact with other family members was over two hundred years ago, when a young member of the family sought to bring everyone back together to form a secret Beyonder organization, hoping to restore their ancestors' glory.
However, due to long periods of separation, the Solomon family had become fragmented. While it wasn't clear how other families had responded, the Henry family chose to refuse.
And so, they lived peacefully for over two centuries until the present day, where only the three members of the Henry family remained.
Aside from the family's history, the notebook also contained much Beyonder knowledge. For a wild Beyonder, this knowledge was invaluable, showcasing the depth of experience held by a Beyonder family.
The notebook also mentioned that the family possessed a Sealed Artifact from the Solomon family, though unfortunately, it did not detail how to seal it.
Hobert also noticed some new handwriting in the blank sections under descriptions of certain rituals from the "Death" domain. Coupled with the fact that the occult symbols used in the Henry couple's ritual included an inverted triangle, it was almost certain that the ritual that led to the Henry couple's deaths was from the "Death" domain.
Such boldness!
Hobert marveled at their recklessness. Without a proper response from the Death God or enough mysticism knowledge, they had dared to attempt a "Death" domain ritual.
At that moment, two policemen arrived at the Henry house, accompanied by Mr. Polly. Upon seeing the scene inside, the middle-aged officer immediately instructed the younger one, "Go send a telegram, say there's a case here we can't handle, and request special support from headquarters."
It seemed the officer was somewhat familiar with the process of dealing with Beyonder cases. Instead of going inside, he began questioning Hobert and Ailey to understand the situation.
Hobert's account was clear and logical. The officer smiled and said, "If every witness could explain things as clearly as you, our workload would be halved."
He then introduced himself, "You can call me Officer Daniel. Mr. Hobert, until police reinforcements arrive, I'll need your help guarding the scene."
Since Hobert was the one who made the report, they couldn't let him leave just yet.
Hobert was well aware of this and replied, "I'd be happy to help."
Upon seeing the giant dog's corpse in Ailey's backyard, Polly tried to complain to Officer Daniel, "Look, officer, that dog, it..."
But Daniel waved him off. "I don't have time for your trivial matters right now."
Having heard Hobert's account, the officer had already realized that this was a case involving supernatural elements. He had no intention of speaking carelessly before the "special support" arrived.
Polly shrank back, saying nothing further.
Daniel approached the door to the Henry house, pulling out a handkerchief to cover his nose as he asked Hobert, "Has anyone been inside?"
Hobert raised the notebook in his hand and said, "Only me. I went in and grabbed this notebook to take a look."
Thud, thud, thud...
Suddenly, the sound of the door banging upstairs rang out again.
Hobert was filled with curiosity. He knew that the sound might signify danger, but he still found it hard to suppress his curiosity.
Daniel took a step back in surprise, then recalled something: "Didn't the Henry family have a seriously ill child? He should still be upstairs.
"If we let young Henry cry for help inside while we ignore him, that would be a shameful failure on my part."
Moreover, with his superior and the special department personnel arriving soon, he couldn't afford to do nothing.
"I'll go with you," Hobert said, realizing that his curiosity might be linked to the Sealed Artifact's influence.
It wouldn't be a bad idea to see the Sealed Artifact's effects firsthand before the official Beyonders arrived.
Considering how the Sealed Artifact seemed to be drawing him in, Hobert surmised it was likely from the Lawyer or Arbiter pathways. Such Sealed Artifacts typically involved rules or laws, which was Hobert's area of expertise. There shouldn't be too much danger.
"You're quite the helpful young man," Daniel remarked.
The two of them checked their weapons and headed upstairs together.

chapters.title: Chapter 69 - 69: Official Beyonders
chapters.content:
Join www.patreon.com/KeyofStars for advance chapters
~~~
Somewhat comically, Hobart had drawn his gun on the stairs, while Daniel only had a baton.
Bang, bang, bang...
Little Henry seemed to hear someone coming upstairs, and the door-pounding increased in frequency.
Daniel had thought about calling out Henry's name to calm him down, but for some reason, in this eerie atmosphere, he found himself unable to speak.
Bang, bang, bang...
The sound was like a death knell. Daniel regretted coming upstairs, but they had already arrived at the bedroom door, where the pounding was coming from.
Using the Spirit Vision provided by his "Spirit Necklace," Hobart confirmed that no living person remained in the room. He raised his cane in one hand, holding his gun in the other, and kicked the door open.
This was the third door he'd kicked in today, and he was getting better at it.
The door flew open, and Hobart and Daniel immediately saw a seven or eight-year-old boy with a pale face, cloudy eyes, and long fangs.
It was obvious that this was little Henry. When he saw the two living people at the door, he let out a sound that was somewhere between a cry and a night owl's screech, then rushed toward Daniel.
Hobart, seeing it was just an ordinary zombie, relaxed and smiled at Daniel, saying, "He just wants a hug."
Daniel also realized something was wrong and quickly dodged, but the little zombie was already struck by Hobart's cane, smashing into the wall.
The blow was hard. The little zombie hit the wall like a clump of mud and didn't move.
Daniel's mouth gaped open, "You—you killed him!"
But just then, the little zombie twitched its neck, slid off the wall, and lunged at Hobart.
