chapters.title: Chapter 114 - 114: Experiment to Shatter Beyonder Characteristics
chapters.content:
Hobert remembered that Sequence 2 Angels had enough power to shatter Beyonder characteristics, after which the characteristics would reassemble, thereby removing some contamination or curse from them.
Hobert was about to obtain the Briber Beyonder characteristic, and he had already obtained the Baron of Corruption Beyonder characteristic. Each of them contained a lower Sequence Beyonder characteristic.
Of course, consuming such Beyonder characteristics would enhance the corresponding abilities, but this would also put pressure on Hobert's spirituality.
Hobert had previously considered that if the Briber Beyonder characteristic only included the main material of the Briber, that would be best, since Sequence 7 was a crucial barrier.
Once past Sequence 7, consuming the Baron of Corruption Beyonder characteristic with its extra Beyonder characteristics wouldn't be as hard to accept.
On the contrary, it could even be a way to become stronger.
Hobert had once envisioned two solutions: one was to find an Unshadowed or an equivalent sealed artifact to separate out the Beyonder characteristics one by one according to their Sequences.
The other solution was to use a High Sequence sealed artifact or request an Angel to shatter the Beyonder characteristics.
But the Unshadowed are demigods, and Angels are Sequence 2. Even if Hobert knew where to find them, it wasn't likely they'd help someone at Sequence 8, especially a stranger.
Both solutions were hard to realize, and Hobert gave up on the idea after some thought.
However, after seeing this piece of information today, Hobert had a flash of insight.
The Nation of Disorder represents the "Shadow of Order," and unconventional actions are its basic operating principle.
Perhaps he could attempt to use the Disorder power within the higher position of the Nation of Disorder to shatter the Beyonder characteristic, and then influence it to reassemble according to its Sequence.
With this in mind, Hobert immediately took a cab to 192 Blanca Street.
Although the mercenary club had rooms available, many of the Beyonders there followed the Arbiter pathway, and Hobert worried they might notice when he entered the Nation of Disorder.
Returning to his bedroom, Hobert drew the curtains and entered the Nation of Disorder right away.
Seated on the Iron Throne, Hobert looked at the stone platform beside him and finally selected a Barbarian Beyonder characteristic for his experiment.
When Hobert had received those two Barbarian Beyonder characteristics from the Nighthawks, he had used a sacrificial method to bring them into the Nation of Disorder.
At the same time, he stored the Teleporting Statue in the Nation of Disorder when not in use. Since it was a sealed artifact and not a mystical item, carrying it all the time could exhaust his spirituality, and he might miss the moment he needed to use it.
With a wave of his hand, a Barbarian Beyonder characteristic appeared in Hobert's hand. He then began manipulating the Disorder power of the Nation of Disorder, attempting to turn the Beyonder characteristic into a chaotic state.
The Beyonder characteristic wrapped in the Disorder power immediately started trembling.
There's a reaction!
Hobert quickly gathered more Disorder power into his hand, causing the tremors of the Beyonder characteristic to increase in frequency. Finally, when he reached the limit of the Disorder power he could manipulate, cracks appeared on the Beyonder characteristic, and it transformed into a sticky, chaotic state.
Sweating profusely, Hobert didn't have time to celebrate. He carefully divided the chaotic mass into two portions and placed them on the left and right sides of the Iron Throne.
Hobert let out a sigh of relief, having experienced the limits of power within the Nation of Disorder for the first time.
It wasn't the limit of the Nation of Disorder itself, but rather the limit of what he could achieve as a Sequence 8. Shattering a Beyonder characteristic was already the most he could do using the power of the Nation of Disorder.
Of course, Hobert wasn't naive enough to think he had gained the strength of an Angel. It was his extensive knowledge of mysticism, combined with the special properties of the Nation of Disorder that allowed a Sequence 8 like him to wield such power.
Other Sefirah domains likely couldn't achieve this as easily.
Just as the Nation of Disorder couldn't grant him an ability like "Angel's Embrace," it had its limits.
Hobert turned his attention back to the two portions of the "chaotic state" Beyonder characteristic, noticing that the chaos was gradually dissipating. Soon, the Beyonder characteristic would reassemble into one Barbarian characteristic and one Lawyer characteristic.
Hobert's gaze then shifted to the Teleporting Statue. Since he had time, he decided to try using the Nation of Disorder to strengthen its power.
With another wave of his hand, the Teleporting Statue flew into Hobert's grasp, and he began channeling the power of the Nation of Disorder to surround the statue.
Hobert noticed that part of the power seemed to be absorbed by the statue.
The statue visibly changed, becoming darker in color, almost to the point of shining black.
After withdrawing the power of the Nation of Disorder and examining the statue again, he found its abilities had increased by about half. Originally able to manipulate space within a 10-meter range, it could now affect a 15-meter radius.
A 15-meter range was enough to launch a sneak attack, such as hiding behind a wall and suddenly burying the enemy underground.
The enemy would likely be completely bewildered: "What just happened? Why did it suddenly go dark? Who turned off the lights? I was enjoying my hotpot and singing, and now I can't see anything!"
Heh heh heh, just thinking about it was amusing.
The negative side effects had also lessened somewhat. Every twenty minutes, his soul and body would still be distorted, but the first distortion wouldn't cause irreversible damage anymore. It would just lead to some temporary confusion in his thoughts, or cause his body to act out of sync with his mind.
After finishing all of this, Hobert felt utterly exhausted. He placed the Teleporting Statue back on the stone platform and left the Nation of Disorder.
When he returned to the real world, night had already fallen. After a brief rest, Hobert went downstairs, intending to make dinner in the kitchen.
However, when passing by the armchair, Hobert suddenly felt the "Lazy God" within him awaken. He looked at the kitchen, then at the armchair, and in the end, he chose the armchair.
At that moment, he thought again of the convenience of takeout: if only there were takeout service, he could lie in his armchair and have food delivered to him. Alas, there was no such service.
After lying there for a while, Hobert finally made up his mind. He put on his coat and headed to the nearby "Flavor of Desi Restaurant" to solve his dinner problem.
---
The middle-aged man with shoulder-length, more or less greasy hair smoked a cigar while looking at the material in front of him, and finally he heavily slapped the material on the table, "I spent 200 pounds, and this is all I've found out about this trivial stuff?"
On the side, a man in his thirties with a bowler hat said, "Alva, we have too few clues."
He was Boris, the assistant of the greasy middle-aged man.
Cigar in hand, Alva spread out the material again and pointed to a spot, "What does it mean here that the suspected Nighthawk was involved?"
"After a visit by two detective assistants," Boris explained, "the residents of Moonflower Street seemed to have invariably fallen into a deep sleep on the night of the accident, so the investigators believe that there was a Nighthawk involved."
It was because of this speculation that the other party immediately abandoned further investigation.
"Bullshit!" Boris said, "We've never messed with the Nighthawks, why would they kill our people?"

chapters.title: Chapter 115 - 115: The Appearance of The Sun
chapters.content:
The Tamara Family Council had already prepared to send someone to investigate the recent incident. After all, two Sequence 6 individuals died under mysterious circumstances, and such a matter certainly required investigation.
Moreover, one of the two Sequence 6 victims, a Judge, had been a promising junior in the eyes of a council member, and the father of the Baron of Corruption also held some influence within the family.
Initially, they had assigned them this simple task to help them gain experience, but they ended up dead in Backlund.
This put a lot of pressure on Alva. There was no way he could avoid the council's responsibility inquiry. He could only hope to uncover the truth before the investigators arrived, which might lead to a more lenient outcome.
But what he had discovered so far left him wondering how he would explain it to the higher-ups. Was he supposed to tell them that their people were killed by the Nighthawks?
Even if this were true, the higher-ups would never believe it.
What else could he say? After all, they were dealing with a church where a True God existed, and the Tamara Family was merely a family of Beyonders that had been hidden in the shadows of history for over a thousand years.
Alva took a deep drag on his cigar and reviewed the information again. "So, the location where they were killed was on Rosette Street, correct?"
Boris responded, "That's the assumption. However…"
He continued, "However, the other party seems to have strong anti-divination abilities. We couldn't find a single clue."
Alva found this curious. "I'm just wondering, how did that family traitor named Apton manage to find so many powerful helpers?"
To silently eliminate two Sequence 6 individuals would require at least three to four Sequence 6 individuals, or one Sequence 5 individual. Otherwise, no matter how powerful the opponent's Sealed Artifacts were, it would be impossible for no one to survive.
Boris speculated, "Perhaps Apton has already joined some Beyonder organization."
"Maybe it's the Loen Royal Family!" Alva thought this was a reasonable explanation. To avoid drawing attention from the Loen Royal Family, the family's influence in Backlund didn't include any Mid-Sequence Arbiter Pathway Beyonders.
But in this recent operation, a Judge had shown up!
That explained it. For such a decisive victory in this Beyonder battle, the other side must have had a powerful Mid-Sequence Beyonder holding the line.
And Backlund was the Loen Royal Family's home turf.
Alva and Boris exchanged glances, agreeing that this theory could be reported.
---
On Monday morning, Hobert arrived at the law firm and reported to Barton about Mr. Stan's case.
He also had the driver deliver the jerky and wild vegetables he had previously received to Barton.
Barton smiled, "Another 'tip' from a client?"
Hobert nodded, "It's a token of appreciation for my work."
Barton handed Hobert a more complex case. "I'll let you handle this one."
Hobert took a look at it—it was a business dispute. Such cases were usually straightforward and didn't interest him much. He was about to refuse when he noticed something. "This is a case in Tingen City?"
"Yes," Barton replied. "The trial is some time away, and it doesn't conflict with the two cases you're currently working on. However, you should prepare for a business trip. I recommend you head to Tingen City by next Wednesday."
Hobert put away the file. "Alright."
He wondered if this was fate pushing him to go to Tingen City. Otherwise, why would a reason to go there fall into his lap like this?
Hobert chuckled. Even without this case, he would have made a trip to Tingen City; otherwise, it would have been a regret.
The entire morning, Hobert went into "slack mode," sitting at his desk, "diligently" reading through files.
By noon, Hobert reflected that occasional slacking off was beneficial to mental health.
In the afternoon, as usual for a Monday, he went to "visit clients" and participated in the Tarot Club at exactly three o'clock.
Upon arriving at the grand hall once again, Hobert suddenly realized there was a new figure seated in his row!
The Sun had joined the Tarot Club!
Indeed, "The Fool" Klein introduced him: "This is the new member, The Sun. This is Miss Justice, this is Mr. Hanged Man, and this is Mr. Emperor."
Derrick Berg, The Sun, nodded slightly to everyone, acknowledging the introductions.
"Justice" Audrey had already activated her Spectator abilities, carefully observing this new member.
Alger "The Hanged Man" was speculating what made this new member special. Ever since The Emperor had joined the Tarot Club, Alger no longer questioned The Fool's motives or judgment in selecting members.
Since The Fool valued The Emperor's knowledge, what did He see in The Sun?
Only Hobert remained calm, wondering if he should flatter The Fool and make it appear as if he already knew that The Sun was from the Forsaken Territory of the Gods.
That would make it easier to establish trade in Beyonder materials, buying from The Sun and selling them through Gal, thus creating a streamlined service.
Unfortunately, The Fool's Express Delivery hadn't been established yet, and The Sun didn't use gold pounds. What would they use to measure their transactions?
As for revealing that he knew something about the Forsaken Territory of the Gods, if this were any other gathering, not even in the Justice League, Hobert wouldn't expose his wealth of knowledge. But since he understood The Fool, he wasn't worried about being "cleaned up."
After introducing the new member, the gathering officially began.
Audrey had found two pages of Roselle's diary and hoped to trade them for information on the Telepathist potion formula.
Derrick, clueless as usual, asked, "The Telepathist potion formula? Does it lead to Psyche Analyst?"
Audrey looked at him in confusion. "You know?"
At the same time, her instincts as a Spectator picked up on something odd: Derrick had used the ancient term for Sequence 7—Psyche Analyst—instead of the more modern Psychiatrist!
That's strange... Audrey scrutinized The Sun's every move once more.
Derrick, unaware that he had said anything unusual, replied earnestly, "I can get that formula for you!"
After saying that, he felt guilty because he couldn't provide it immediately and hurriedly explained, "This Sequence originates from the Dragon Race, and our City of Silver was once ruled by the Giant King's Court.
"You know, giants and dragons are mortal enemies, so the formulas for Sequences 9, 8, and 7 are available in the City of Silver. I have a way to get them."
Hobert smiled faintly. In the end, The Sun was still an inexperienced youth who hadn't faced the "hard knocks of society." His words had revealed a lot of information.
Giant King's Court? Dragon Race? City of Silver?
Audrey was completely bewildered. She glanced at The Hanged Man, noticing that he was equally shocked and confused.
Then she looked at The Emperor, who remained as composed as ever.
Mr. Emperor knows about the City of Silver!
That was Audrey and Alger's shared conclusion.
But Audrey didn't know how to broach the subject with Mr. Emperor, so she instead asked The Sun, "City of Silver? I've never heard of this place… Where is it?"
Now it was Derrick's turn to be surprised. "You... You're not from the City of Silver? Which city-state are you from?"
The hall fell into a brief silence.
After a few seconds, Hobert finally spoke. "I've read about a Kingdom of Silver in books. If I'm not mistaken, are you from a land abandoned by the gods?"
The hall plunged into an even more eerie silence.
~~~

chapters.title: Chapter 116 - 116: "Vice Admiral Hurricane" Qilangos + Announcement
chapters.content:
Announcements at the end!!
~~~
Klein thought: The Emperor even knows about the "Forsaken Land of the Gods"? Well, of course, he knows about the elves of the Second Epoch, so how could he not know about it?
Alger carefully pondered each word the Emperor spoke: Forsaken by the gods? Could it be the "Forsaken Land of the Gods"?
He exhaled, recalling how, at the previous gathering, he had just probed Mr. Fool about the Forsaken Land of the Gods. And now, only a few weeks later, Mr. Fool had pulled in a member from there.
He mused internally: I knew it, I knew it! Mr. Fool must have had a special reason for choosing this new member. Furthermore, the Emperor seems to know quite a lot about the Forsaken Land of the Gods. His knowledge is terrifyingly vast.
Audrey, on the other hand, was shocked by the phrase "forsaken by the gods": Oh my, gods? What does that mean? How could gods forsake people? Isn't a god supposed to be a lofty, supreme existence? Why would the City of Silver, or the Kingdom of Silver, be forsaken by the gods? Goddess, where exactly does "The Sun" come from?
Derrick's expression turned somber after hearing Hobert's words. "No, Mr. Emperor, the omnipotent and omniscient god has not forsaken their people. They have merely abandoned this land!"
Alger leaned back in his chair: He really is from the Forsaken Land of the Gods!
Audrey's heart was filled with shock: The gods have abandoned that land? What are they talking about? I understand their words, but I can't grasp the meaning behind them.
Hobert first bowed to Klein: "Please accept my respect. I never imagined I would meet someone from the legendary Forsaken Land of the Gods in my lifetime."
Klein maintained a calm exterior, but internally he breathed a sigh of relief. Sometimes, he worried about exposing himself in front of the knowledgeable Emperor.
There were even moments when he wondered if he should find an excuse to keep the Emperor away from the gatherings for a while.
However, the Emperor's display of respect made Klein abandon this thought. He sighed inwardly: Only those who know about the Forsaken Land of the Gods can truly appreciate the significance of The Sun's participation in these gatherings. And the Emperor clearly recognizes this. The power I displayed today should be enough to shock him.
Hobert, of course, was unaware of the great Mr. Fool's internal musings. His earlier display was merely a case of mutual flattery.
He then turned to Derrick and said, "Seven new gods have provided protection to the people of the Northern and Southern Continents."
Alger's eyes narrowed: Seven new gods! New gods!
Audrey thought: Protection for the people of the Northern and Southern Continents? Of course, we are under the protection of the gods. Oh, Goddess! Does this mean The Sun isn't from either the Northern or Southern Continent?
Derrick was first excited—new gods providing protection for the human world? But then he felt dejected: Why hasn't the omniscient and omnipotent god protected us?
The hall fell silent once again. This was the third time today's gathering had been enveloped in silence.
Whether it was Audrey, Alger, or Derrick, today's gathering shattered many of their prior beliefs.
After a while, Hobert broke the silence: "Apologies for interrupting your transaction. You can now receive the Telepathist potion formula, correct?"
Derrick nodded.
Hobert continued, "What would you like in exchange?"
"I want to exchange it for the initial Sequence of the Sun Pathway."
Klein then initiated a three-way transaction: he would provide Derrick with the Bard potion formula, and Derrick would give Audrey the Telepathist potion formula.
He said, "In terms of an equivalent exchange, The Sun is at a disadvantage here. Once Miss Justice obtains the Telepathist formula, we'll figure out how to compensate him. Alternatively, I'll compensate him myself, while Miss Justice provides money to one of my Favored. He has something he needs to do soon.
"Heh, this is because The Sun cannot receive Miss Justice's cash or material compensation."
These words confirmed that Mr. Fool had acknowledged The Sun as being from the Forsaken Land of the Gods. Otherwise, why wouldn't he be able to receive cash or compensation?
Other than Hobert, no one noticed the key point in Mr. Fool's statement: "Miss Justice provides money to one of my Favored." Hobert immediately felt as if the wheels of fate were set in motion.
When Klein eventually used the funds Audrey provided, it would be the moment his life and fate would take a dramatic turn!
After completing the three-way transaction, Klein began reading the diary provided by Audrey.
Today's diary described something related to "adjacent Pathways." Klein recalled the "Law of Similar Sequence Beyonder Characteristics Conservation" mentioned by the Emperor at the last gathering. Suddenly, it all became clear to him: the conservation of Beyonder characteristics also extends to adjacent Pathways.
In other words, Beyonders from adjacent Pathways see each other as mortal enemies.
If he thought deeper, the fact that the Evernight Goddess Church and the God of Combat Church are sworn enemies might imply that these two Pathways are adjacent to each other.
At that moment, many pieces of the puzzle clicked into place for him.
After Mr. Fool finished reading the diary, Hobert asked Alger, "Any new progress in your explorations?"
Alger replied, "I'm currently dealing with another matter."
He then turned to Hobert and Audrey: "I have something I hope you can assist with."
Audrey asked curiously, "What kind of help?"
Hobert thought to himself: Is Qilangos already entering the scene?
As expected, Alger said, "I've received intelligence that the infamous pirate known as 'Vice Admiral Hurricane' Qilangos has secretly come ashore in Backlund. His intentions are unknown, and I hope you can help me track him down. As for what happens afterward, you won't need to take any risks."
"Vice Admiral Qilangos? One of the Seven Pirate Admirals?" Audrey said, a little excited. As a Beyonder, what could be more thrilling than encountering someone who had previously only existed in noble legends?
Alger introduced solemnly, "Yes, he is a Sequence 6 of the Sailor Pathway and possesses a mystical artifact. He's extremely cunning and ruthless. Don't try to confront him."
He glanced at the Emperor, but the Emperor seemed disinterested.
Hobert, of course, wasn't interested. Even though he had several mystical items and one sealed artifact, he understood the gap between himself and a Sequence 6.
It wasn't just two Sequences apart; there was also the difference between "low Sequence" and "middle Sequence." Plus, Qilangos had the Shepherd's glove.
Only after reaching Sequence 7 did Hobert have confidence in challenging a Sequence 6.
Alger then turned to Klein and asked, "Mr. Fool, may I request that one of your Favored provide assistance at a critical moment? I am willing to offer something of interest to you in return."
It was only then that Hobert remembered that Mr. Fool's Favored, Mr. Azik, was currently in Backlund.

chapters.title: Chapter 117 - 117: Battle of the Mid-Sequence+New Fanfic
chapters.content:
Hobert also thought that it might not be wise to approach Mr. Azik rashly. He decided to leave it to fate—if they met, it meant they were destined to, and if they didn't, there wouldn't be any loss.
Derrick, likely due to his inexperience attending such gatherings for the first time, had shared information about the "Shepherd" without much thought, allowing Alger to gain valuable intelligence without spending a penny.
At this point, everyone had formed an impression of this new member: simple and somewhat reckless.
After finishing the exchange of information about Qilangos, the Tarot Club meeting concluded.
Back in the real world, Hobert estimated the time and realized there were about two weeks left before the Nighthawks team in Tingen City would be attacked.
He aimed to reach Tingen City by the end of this week and make some preparations in advance.
Stretching his body, Hobert returned to the law office to prepare for Bob's trial.
Logically, the defense attorney should have reached out to the plaintiff's lawyer by now to discuss the case, but so far, there had been no contact, indicating that the other side had no intention of negotiating.
"Fine," thought Hobert, "whether we communicate or not, this trial will be a tough battle."
...
Southern Continent, Crowell City.
Late at night, Elliot and his roommate were awakened by a servant and informed that Elder Calvin had requested their presence in the living room.
General Anthony had arranged their accommodations in the suburbs of Crowell City.
It was quiet at this time of night; the sounds of wild beasts in the distant forest and the seemingly nearby chirping of nocturnal insects could be heard.
On the way to the living room, Elliot met his companions from other rooms, and together they made their way to the living room.
Is there a mission tonight? Elliot quickly prepared himself for action.
Not long after arriving in the spacious living room, the other companions gradually gathered, all standing silently on either side of the hall.
"The negotiations have reached their final stage," Calvin began. "No matter the negotiation, strength is always the most important bargaining chip."
He continued, "Tonight is the time to showcase our strength. When we first arrived in Crowell City, I deliberately exposed that we were representatives of the Balk family."
"The 'Rose School of Thought' has been conducting reconnaissance over the past few days. They believe they have figured out our strength and have sent a demigod to eliminate all members of the delegation."
Everyone knew that Calvin was currently Sequence 5, and even with a Sealed Artifact in hand, it would be difficult for him to contend with a demigod who had undergone a fundamental transformation.
However, no one panicked, as Calvin had clearly planned for this in advance.
"Of course, we've made some preparations as well," Calvin continued. "In a moment, I will act as bait and leave the inn immediately. You are not to engage in prolonged battle. Retreat quickly, and once our reinforcements flank the enemy from behind, you will launch a counterattack at the right moment."
"Yes!" everyone responded in unison.
"Alright, return to your rooms."
As they walked back, the group quietly planned their escape routes and discussed fleeing together with companions they had a good rapport with, to avoid being left alone.
Elliot also made plans with a few companions to escape together before returning to his room to wait for the enemy's arrival.
Sitting in his chair, Elliot felt a bit nervous. He had fought members of the "Rose School of Thought" several times, but those were all low-sequence enemies.
Having just become a "Briber," this was his first time participating in a mid-sequence battle, and there was even a demigod involved.
At that moment, he noticed his bedsheet moving as if it had come to life, wrapping itself around the pillow on his bed.
His roommate, sitting on the edge of the bed, was also caught by his bedsheet. Despite struggling, he couldn't break free, and the sheet only tightened further.
Elliot quickly used the dagger in his hand to cut the sheet trapping his companion. He was grateful he hadn't been lying on the bed, or he too would have been ensnared.
He first cut the sheet around his companion's neck to prevent him from suffocating. As he continued cutting, the sheet wriggled like an octopus or jellyfish, extending "tentacles" to grab at Elliot's hands.
Elliot immediately stepped back, but then the coat rack by the door came to life and charged straight at him, as if intent on knocking him over.
Tables, chairs, curtains—everything seemed to have come to life and launched an attack on Elliot.
The worst part was that Elliot could feel his own clothes trying to restrain his movements.
If it had been an ordinary person facing such a scene, they would have passed out in fear, seeing everyday objects spring to life.
But Elliot and his companions had been trained as assassins from a young age. The stranger the situation, the calmer they became.
Elliot dodged the desk's assault and grabbed a cup from the table, throwing it at the animated coat rack to complete the act of "bribery."
"Weaken!"
The objects' movements immediately slowed down, especially the clothes that had been tightening around him—they were now looser.
Next, Elliot entered a "berserk state," kicking away the chair that charged at him.
His companion, now freed from the sheet's weakened grip, tore it apart using his Barbarian strength.
Run!
That was the only thought in Elliot's mind. He grabbed the struggling coat rack, using it to smash through the window.
Unexpectedly, the shattered glass seemed to come to life as well, flying straight at him.
Elliot dodged the rampaging table and crouched behind it, but the glass seemed to have a mind of its own, curving around the table and heading for him.
Elliot raised his arms to protect his face, bracing himself for the incoming shards.
"Disorder!"
Suddenly, Calvin's voice echoed from the direction of the living room.
The glass spun aimlessly in midair like a swarm of insects, as if it had lost its target.
Standing up, Elliot saw Calvin swiftly leaving the inn, with something following him—or perhaps, nothing at all.
Inside the room, the glass fell to the floor, and the furniture that had been struggling moments before was now motionless.
If not for the broken window and the mess everywhere, Elliot might have thought it was all just a bad dream.
So this is a demigod? Without even seeing his figure, we were already exhausted by his abilities.
Sounds of fighting from the courtyard snapped Elliot out of his thoughts and back into battle mode. Members of the "Rose School of Thought," trailing behind the demigod, had launched an attack on the inn.
Elliot and his companions immediately followed the escape route they had planned earlier. They defeated the enemies blocking their way and fled into the forest.
The pursuers were close behind, and Elliot's group, seemingly terrified by the sudden attack, had no thoughts of counterattacking and focused only on fleeing.
After a few minutes of running, a long horn sounded from behind them, and the pursuers immediately halted. This wasn't their first encounter, and they knew well that this was the Balk family's attack signal.
A gust of wind swept through, shaking the trees violently. The Zombies and Werewolves quickly turned to flee.
But they were a step too late. The wind carried a deadly force, cutting off the limbs of the undead and leaving fatal wounds, no matter how tough their bodies were.
This was the Balk family's Sealed Artifact, "Wind Blade."

chapters.title: Chapter 118 - 118: Calvin's Temptation
chapters.content:
"Wind Blade" did not kill all the pursuers in front of Elliot. Two lucky ones evaded the attack of "Wind Blade," and several quick-reacting individuals did not suffer fatal injuries.
For members of the "Rose School of Thought," being able to continue fighting without fatal injuries was expected.
Thus, a Beyonder battle was inevitable.
Elliot felt for the first time how insignificant his power was. In this long-planned Beyonder battle by the family, his Sequence 7 status made his abilities and strength negligible.
All he knew was that he had to fight desperately and be constantly vigilant against the enemy's fatal attacks.
But soon reinforcements arrived, and members of the Bark Family quickly gained the upper hand.
What followed was encirclement, breakout, counter-breakout, and finally pursuit. However, the pursuers and the survivors of the "Rose School of Thought" had already changed positions, with the surviving members of the "Rose School of Thought" running ahead and Elliot's group chasing from behind.
It wasn't until the overall commander of the battle blew the horn to stop the pursuit that Elliot and his companions stopped.
Members of the Bark Family began to converge towards the direction of the horn. Low Sequence members responsible for cleaning up the battlefield placed the enemy's bodies together, totaling more than twenty.
Gradually, smiles appeared on Elliot and others' faces. This was a great victory; in one battle, more than twenty members of the "Rose School of Thought" were killed!
Seeing the results, everyone felt that the fierce battle just now was worthwhile.
"Elliot! Come over here!" Calvin waved from not far away.
Elliot hurried over, and Calvin patted his shoulder. "How are you? Any injuries?"
"No."
As they walked, Calvin said, "We just killed an important figure of the 'Rose School of Thought.'"
The two walked out of the crowd, and Calvin said, "I need you to perform spirit channeling with him."
Following behind, Elliot was puzzled. "Uncle Calvin, I've heard from the elders that when we first opposed members of the 'Rose School of Thought,' we tried to channel their spirits using Sealed Artifacts, but every time there were terrible consequences! Besides, I don't know how to!"
Calvin looked at Elliot. "But he carries crucial information about our family's curse."
At this point, the two arrived in front of a corpse, and Elliot looked at the body in silence.
"If I guess correctly, this information could overturn your understanding," Calvin said. "Think of a way. I'll create a space for you without interference."
"Of course, you can also choose not to channel his spirit, but it will be a long time before you have another chance to access this information."
With that, Calvin left.
Elliot hesitated for a few seconds before praying to the "Creator," interested in the curse of the Bark Family. He hoped the "Creator" could give him some guidance:
"Great 'Creator,' according to Elder Calvin, this body carries crucial information about our family's curse. He wants me to perform spirit channeling with the body."
"But as far as I know, family members have tried to with members of the 'Rose School of Thought' before, and without exception, they all died tragically during the process, with many terrible things happening afterwards."
"Elder Calvin also said that if I don't..."
Finally, he said, "Great 'Creator,' I seek your guidance. May I ask if I can invoke your power to commune? If so, how can I avoid the terrible consequences?"
He prayed several times but received no response from the "Creator." Just as he thought the "Creator" did not advise him to commune, the great figure sitting on the "Iron Throne" appeared in his mind:
"Pay attention to Calvin's wording: 'about,' 'your.'"
The reason Hobert waited so long to respond was that the "Great Creator" had just awakened from a deep sleep and was disturbed by Elliot's prayer, immediately realizing it was Calvin's temptation.
And "the bystander sees clearly." According to Elliot's description, it seemed like the Bark Family needed to channel the spirit of this body of a member of the "Rose School of Thought" to understand crucial information.
But upon closer inspection, Calvin's words carried a completely different meaning.
Elliot immediately recalled where these two words appeared in the sentence: "He carries crucial information about our family's curse," and "If I guess correctly, that information may overturn 'your' understanding."
It was "about" information regarding the family curse, not that "he may have" or "should have" information about the family curse.
It was to overturn "your" understanding, not that "this information will definitely overturn our understanding."
Elliot was not stupid. Prompted by the "Creator," he immediately understood: "Elder Calvin has long known what information can be obtained during mediumship. He just wants to use this mediumship to let me know this information and also..."
He was testing him.
Elliot said somewhat anxiously, "Great 'Creator,' I have never voluntarily disclosed any information about you. This is... an accident."
The "Creator" sat quietly there, making Elliot even more flustered.
After a few seconds, the "Creator" said, "You are ready to undertake my power's ceremony."
Elliot finally breathed a sigh of relief. As he prepared the ceremony, he also felt that his previous thoughts were ridiculous; the "Creator" must have known that he had not disclosed any information about Him.
He further thought that the "Creator" was willing to help him commune, which was a direct response to Uncle Calvin's test!
This... doesn't this mean that the "Creator" is willing to let more members of the Bark Family know about His existence?
This excited Elliot somewhat, thinking that this was an important step for the "Creator" to intervene and lift the curse.
As for the ability of the "Creator" to channel the spirit, this did not seem surprising, after all, He was a mysterious and great existence.
Soon, the setup for the ceremony was completed.
Elliot began to recite the name of the "Creator":
"Creator in the Shadow of Order;
"..."
"I seek your gaze and favor;
"I seek your power to allow me to spiritually communicate with the member of the 'Rose School of Thought' before me."
"..."
Elliot's eyes turned completely black, seemingly losing their pupils. Without anyone's guidance, he grasped the remnants of the spiritual presence of the member of the "Rose School of Thought" in front of him, silently chanting in his mind: "About the secrets of the Bark Family's curse."
"About the secrets of the Bark Family's curse."
"..."
After silently chanting seven times, the haze in his line of sight changed, revealing vague buildings and indistinct figures.
In the Nation of Disorder, Hobert, like last time, took an interest in this "film."
The face of the person in front of him was blurred, indicating that his level was very high. At the level of this communion, the face of the person could not be seen.
"Professor Zatwen, are you saying that the curse of the Balk Family has nothing to do with us?"
The blurred face of Zatwen replied, "Exactly, the curse of the Balk Family resides in their bloodlines, not in a literal curse."
"Why have they always claimed that we cursed them?"
Zatwen said, "They need an enemy!"
Suddenly, from behind Zatwen, a hand stretched out, covered with eyes and a tongue with sharp teeth.
The communion process abruptly stopped. The angel of the "Rose School of Thought," or even the "Abomination" itself, may have projected its power through the spirituality of the member of the "Rose School of Thought."

chapters.title: Chapter 119 - 119: Do Not Test God
chapters.content:
The scene before Elliot left him utterly astonished.
At the moment the mediumship was interrupted, he saw the corpse before the makeshift altar sit up. Its eyes remained shut, one hand covered its face, while the other reached toward Elliot.
In the palm of the outstretched hand, an eye covered in blood vessels slowly opened.
Elliot immediately felt his spirit tremble, as if warning him that the eye before him was extremely dangerous.
From the corpse's wrist, a tongue with sharp fangs grew, and an ominous power filled with countless curses quietly descended upon the land.
At this moment, Elliot was like a lamb awaiting slaughter, his body rigid, unable to resist at all.
From its arm, an ear with bone spikes sprouted, and an overwhelmingly evil and insane power began to spread through the surroundings.
Elliot felt his soul about to separate from his body, ready to die miserably before the altar.
...
Two kilometers away on a hill, Jonas, a demigod sent by the Feysac Empire, and General Anthony, the nominal ruler of this land, leisurely observed the distant battle between demigods.
Jonas smiled, "I didn't expect the elusive Balk family to have two demigods! No, at least two demigods. The 'Rose School of Thought' will definitely suffer this time."
He continued, "With such strength, they indeed qualify to work with us."
Anthony stood slightly behind Jonas, "The problem is whether their ambitions will grow in the future, beyond our control."
Jonas smiled, "Do you think the royal family lacks angels? Or that the Church of the God of Combat has no angels?
"In the presence of an angel, a demigod is as fragile as a baby."
Anthony bowed slightly, "Yes, yes, I was being careless."
"No matter what, drawing in such a powerful family is beneficial to us," Jonas smiled. "Especially a family with mortal enemies on the southern continent; they are the perfect partners."
Just as Anthony was about to offer more flattery, he suddenly sensed a terrifying power descending upon the battlefield.
Jonas's expression darkened slightly, "What kind of terrifying existence have they provoked?"
...
Roughly one kilometer from Elliot, the three demigods who were locked in fierce combat abruptly halted all movements and looked in Elliot's direction.
Chester and another Balk family demigod exchanged glances. This was unexpected—was this the test Calvin had mentioned earlier?
This is reckless. Such a test could drive everyone in the nearby Crowell City into madness.
The Rose School of Thought demigod, however, looked delighted. If the leader has intervened, none of the Balk family members will leave here alive.
...
Calvin, who was commanding the battlefield cleanup, sensed the arrival of that evil and insane power. Everyone turned toward Elliot's direction, their spiritual instincts warning them: a terrifying force was descending.
Calvin said, "Attention! The demigods are still fighting. Leave all spoils behind and retreat immediately!"
The retreat commenced in an orderly manner, but everyone was puzzled. Could a demigod really possess such terrifying power?
...
Elliot had completely given up hope, not expecting such a painful death.
The faces of his deranged sister and close friend appeared before him, as if bidding him farewell.
At that moment, Hobert, in the Nation of Disorder, seized the opportunity, covering the corpse before the altar with the surging power of Order.
Logically speaking, even with the Nation of Disorder's blessing, Hobert was no match for the entity projecting power onto the altar.
But the abilities of the Nation of Disorder never operated "logically."
Hobert, of course, did not choose to face the entity head-on. Instead, he simply restored "order" to the corpse.
The order for the corpse was naturally death and the dissipation of its spirituality.
In this way, Hobert severed the connection between the corpse and the entity projecting power onto it.
This method of exploiting loopholes was the true essence of the Nation of Disorder's abilities.
It was with absolute confidence in this that Hobert had allowed Elliot to conduct the mediumship.
Before the altar, the eye, tongue, and ear on the corpse's arm quickly withered and turned black, as if a strange dark sore had formed.
Thud.
The corpse fell to the ground, black viscous liquid oozing from its eyes, nose, mouth, and ears, completely devoid of life.
Elliot, drenched in sweat, felt as though he had just returned from the brink of death.
He smiled faintly. What had he been thinking earlier? With the Creator's protection, how could he possibly die?
...
Two kilometers away, on the hill, Jonas and Anthony, who were preparing to leave, stopped and looked back.
Anthony, puzzled, said, "It's gone? The Balk family actually defeated that terrifying power?"
Just moments ago, both he and Jonas were ready to abandon Crowell City.
Jonas folded his arms, "The Balk family's strength is far more profound than we imagined."
...
The Rose School of Thought demigod sensed the leader's power suddenly stop and, without a second thought, fled immediately.
That was the leader! That was a divine offspring! To interrupt His power projection required at least an angel-level figure, or a sealing object of that level.
If they didn't leave now, they wouldn't be able to escape.
Generally speaking, a demigod cannot stop another demigod intent on fleeing, especially one like the Rose School's demigod, whose resilience was notorious.
In the end, the Rose School of Thought demigod sacrificed an arm to escape, marking the official end of the battle.
...
Elliot flexed his limbs and cleaned up the altar. As he stood up, Calvin hurried over.
Seeing that Elliot, aside from looking a bit pale, was otherwise unharmed, Calvin asked, "You... you completed the mediumship?"
Before Elliot could respond, a mysterious figure surrounded by swords appeared above him, radiating dark holy light even in the night.
Calvin immediately felt a suppression from the figure's aura, instinctively wanting to kneel.
Hobert, seated on the Iron Throne, cast a sliver of "disorder" toward Calvin, who instantly felt a pain ten times worse than the family curse.
Writhing in agony, Calvin collapsed to the ground, showing signs of losing control.
After about ten seconds, Calvin's uncontrollable state reached its peak. Just as he was about to lose his mind, the excruciating pain vanished. His body was bathed in seemingly endless "Order," and the signs of losing control disappeared completely.
Elliot came over to support the tear- and snot-covered Calvin, who was gasping for air. "Uncle Calvin, do not test God!"
Calvin stiffened and was about to kneel and beg forgiveness from the great being among the swords, but the divine figure had already vanished.
~~~

chapters.title: Chapter 120 - 120: Possession of the "Red Angel"
chapters.content:
After punishing Calvin, Hobert didn't immediately leave the Nation of Disorder. He decided to wait a bit longer to observe Calvin's reaction.
He mocked himself inwardly: Why does this feel a bit like a "client follow-up," checking to see if the "client" fell for my trick?
Feeling bored, he recalled the results of the earlier mediumship.
Although the séance was interrupted, Elliott already had the answer he sought: the Balk family curse had absolutely nothing to do with the "Rose School of Thought." The curse indeed stemmed from the family's bloodline.
This shattered the last bit of Hobert's wishful thinking, as he had always believed there was some intricate connection between the Heller family and the Balk family.
These two families were likely cursed for the same reasons, burdened by something within their bloodline.
If this curse had truly come from a high-level Beyonder on the Prisoner Pathway, the solution would have been straightforward—just kill the one who cast the curse, and it would naturally disappear.
Though this would be difficult, it was something within Hobert's realm of knowledge. All he had to do was become stronger, then defeat the curse caster.
However, tonight's mediumship showed that the curse had nothing to do with the "Rose School of Thought."
Everything returned to square one—the curse was shrouded in mystery, and the investigation would have to begin with the Heller and Balk families.
Unfortunately, these two families were relatively obscure, making an effective investigation challenging for Hobert.
Right now, he had two leads: first, Rex. He decided to visit Dicks sometime soon.
The second lead was the Balk family's council of elders. They must know some secrets about the Balk family, which strengthened Hobert's resolve to support Elliott.
With this in mind, Hobert once again observed Calvin through Elliott's stars. Calvin appeared a bit fearful and much more respectful toward Elliott.
Hobert sighed: Mission accomplished.
Just as he was about to leave the Nation of Disorder, Hobert noticed that the star representing Raft was entwined with something resembling a red thread.
Hobert was startled. He had been busy lately and hadn't checked on Raft in a while. Could something have happened to him?
Hobert spread his spiritual senses toward the star representing Raft. At that moment, Raft was running wildly down a deserted street, clearly engaged in some secretive activity tonight.
On his back, there seemed to be a shadow.
Hobert adjusted his "True Vision" and saw a blurry, dark figure clinging to Raft's back.
Yet Raft appeared unaware.
This... this looks like a crude form of possession!
Could it be the "Red Angel" Medici, and some kind of evil spirit merged with two of his enemies?
Hobert stroked his chin—this was the only plausible explanation.
Unexpectedly, Raft had already been possessed. Any later investigations or divinations by Klein regarding Raft must have been influenced by this evil spirit.
Hobert tried to recall Raft's role in the story, but he was such a minor character that Hobert hadn't paid much attention to him while reading.
He then thought: Possessed or not, it doesn't matter. I'm not planning to help Raft break free for now.
I'll assist him only when he proves useful.
With this thought, Hobert submerged the star representing Raft into the pond, preventing the "Red Angel" from tracking back to the "Nation of Disorder" through his "True Vision."
Dealing with a "King of Angels" level being required utmost caution.
…
In the nighttime streets of Backlund, Raft didn't hail a cab until he was several blocks away from where he had been digging up the ruins.
As he boarded the carriage, the Red Angel possessing him for the first time suddenly looked up into the sky, saying, Solomon?
Another voice from the evil spirit chuckled, "A thousand years underground has rotted your brain!"
A third voice added, "Indeed. When we invaded this Tudor descendant's mind earlier, didn't you notice? Over a hundred years ago, a new 'Black Emperor' arose, and Solomon truly fell."
"Two fools. Have you forgotten Solomon's gaze?"
The second voice retorted, "Unlike you, we don't willingly act as Solomon's dogs."
The third voice said, "Of course you remember Solomon's gaze—that's the loyalty of a hunting dog to its master!"
Medici sneered, "You don't even qualify to be dogs."
"…"
Even after a thousand years, there was no peace among them.
Naturally, neither Raft nor the coachman could hear their argument.
…
After leaving the Nation of Disorder, Hobert lay in the darkness, staring at the black ceiling, listening to the occasional sounds of hooves and horses outside, while imagining the rdinary battle outside Crowell City, far away.
From tonight onward, he would officially intervene in the Balk family as the "Creator."
If executed well, this demigod family could become a significant force in the future.
For example, in the future, if the "Creator" sent one of his Chosen to the Southern Continent for training, it wouldn't be unreasonable to demand control over a small town from the Balk family (since they secretly ruled many villages and towns within General Anthony's territory) to help digest the "Baron of Corruption" potion, would it?
Even if something went wrong, at most, the Southern Continent's channels would be lost. No one would connect the "Creator" to a young man from Loen in the Northern Continent.
As his thoughts swirled, Hobert began to feel sleepy again.
He smiled bitterly to himself. Since he had shown his face before the Balk family's elders, it seemed that the great "Creator" would be forced into action often, even at night.
…
The next morning, Hobert yawned as he arrived at the law firm, made a brief appearance, then left to "visit clients." Around 8:50 AM, he arrived at Viscount Glaint's mansion.
Xio and Fors had just arrived as well, and after greeting each other, Audrey arrived.
After everyone complimented Audrey on her beauty, they headed together to Viscount Glaint's study.
A long table and five chairs were already prepared. Instead of drinks and fruit, there was a simple and rustic astrolabe on the table.
Audrey smiled, "The astrolabe really gives this study a mystical atmosphere."
Viscount Glaint chuckled, clearly pleased with Audrey's compliment.
Hobert also inwardly sighed: Looks pretty convincing!
The group tacitly left the head seat for Hobert, and he took it without hesitation. Audrey and Glaint sat to his left, with Xio and Fors to his right.
Thus, the first meeting of the "Justice League" officially began.
~~~

chapters.title: Chapter 121 - 121: The "Justice League" Meeting
chapters.content:
"First, let's discuss the issue of recruiting new members," Hobert said. "I've thought of a development plan. Hear me out first."
He continued, "As the five founders of the 'Justice League,' we should always have the highest authority, including the 'right to initiate' and the 'veto power.'
"For example, the action I'm proposing now, the recruitment of new members, falls under the 'right to initiate.' If anyone feels this initiative is inappropriate or doesn't align with their interests, they can use their veto power.
"If my proposal is vetoed, it will not be implemented within the 'Justice League,' and we will need to discuss it again and come up with a new initiative.
"This will be a power exclusive to the five of us. Future members will be 'official members' and 'prospective members.' They will have 'the right to speak' but not the 'right to initiate.'"
Audrey asked, "Does that mean future members can only trade or exchange information at the meetings, but won't have the right to suggest the development direction of the 'Justice League'?"
Hobert smiled and said, "Exactly. The 'helm' of the 'Justice League' should only be in the hands of the five of us."
Naturally, everyone agreed with this proposal, which strengthened their own authority.
Hobert continued, "I suggest that in the future, whoever recruits a new member will have them sit behind them at meetings.
"At the same time, the person who introduces the new member to the meeting will be responsible for their behavior.
"If more than three founders deem that a new member threatens the 'Justice League,' we can bypass the introducer, expel them, and erase all their memories of the 'Justice League.'"
Everyone paused, gradually getting into the right mindset, seriously considering the issue of recruiting new members.
Xio raised her hand. "As a mystical organization, if we can erase the memories of those who leave, that would be ideal. But how do we achieve that?"
"Once Miss Audrey advances to the mid-sequence of the 'Spectator' pathway, she will easily be able to do that," Hobert had already thought this through.
"Before that, I have a way to erase someone's memories, provided their Sequence isn't higher than mine. The process is somewhat complicated, but I can manage."
He wouldn't easily reveal that he possessed a mystical items related to this; his explanation was intended to steer the conversation towards ritual magic.
Xio and Fors believed him completely. They knew Hobert had a wealth of mystical knowledge, so this seemed unsurprising.
Audrey and Viscount Glaint lacked sufficient knowledge, but Hobert's previous reliability made them trust his words as well.
Hobert's proposal to recruit new members received unanimous support, marking the approval of the 'Justice League's' first initiative.
Before this meeting, Audrey had merely found the gatherings entertaining, while Xio and Fors hadn't taken the 'Justice League' too seriously either.
However, Hobert's proposal had brought more structure to the 'Justice League,' causing the three ladies to start taking it more seriously.
Hobert then smiled and said, "It's been a while since we've all sat together and chatted. We can now exchange information freely. What might seem insignificant to one person could be crucial to another.
"We can also make trades, like in any other Beyonder gathering."
He said, "I'll start. I'd like to ask Viscount Glaint, who is now an 'Apothecary,' if you can concoct potions that nourish spirituality. I think both Miss Xio and Miss Fors would also need such potions."
Fors immediately realized, "Are you saying that in last week's battle, our spirituality was damaged?"
Last week's battle? As a 'Spectator,' Audrey quickly caught on. She first gave Hobert a hopeful look, wishing he would elaborate, and then she became concerned about the state of their spirituality.
"That's right," Hobert confirmed. "I've already healed the permanent damage to my spirit body, but I still want to nourish my spirituality. You two were farther away at the time, so your damage should be minimal, or you would have noticed it by now."
He could sense Audrey's curiosity, so he briefly explained, "Last week, I, along with Miss Xio and Miss Fors, participated in a battle between Beyonders."
Audrey excitedly said, "I wonder when I'll be able to take part in one of the 'Justice League's' Beyonder battles?"
Girl, that's a bit self-centered! Hobert thought helplessly. Who said this battle was initiated by the 'Justice League'? Don't immerse yourself too deeply!
He smiled and said, "That wasn't exactly a pleasant experience. Besides, you—well, I mean, with your future abilities as a 'Spectator,' you wouldn't be well-suited for direct combat."
At this point, Audrey was still officially searching for traces of the 'Psychology Alchemists,' seeking a way to become a 'Spectator.'
Xio and Fors, hearing Hobert's words, looked concernedly at Viscount Glaint.
Viscount Glaint smiled bitterly. "I don't have any such potion in my memory."
Hobert nodded. "That's alright."
He then said to Xio and Fors, "If I find a recipe for such a potion from other sources, I'll share it with you."
Fors sighed in relief. "Thank you."
"Oh, by the way," Hobert added, "I have a lead on the main ingredient for the 'Trickmaster' potion. If you need it, Fors, I can sell it to you at a discount."
Fors immediately responded, "Of course I need it!"
Audrey was slightly surprised. She remembered that Fors had once mentioned that the 'Trickmaster' potion formula was hard to find. Had she found it now? Did she also get the formula from Hobert?
Hobert nodded. "Once I have it, I'll send you a letter."
Audrey then gave Xio the task of finding "Vice Admiral Hurricane" Qilangos. Seeing everyone's surprised expressions, Audrey felt a little proud. Though Hobert's expression of surprise seemed fake—could it be that he already knew Qilangos was in Backlund?
Xio was the biggest beneficiary of this meeting because Hobert also gave her the task of finding two cultists, with each one having a bounty of 200 pounds.
Xio was greatly interested, as she rarely encountered such a generous bounty.
Audrey, perhaps afraid that her commission wouldn't be taken seriously, quickly added, "My commission will also give you a satisfying reward."
Xio nodded repeatedly. To her, the two tasks did not conflict.
Hobert handed over information about the cultists to Xio and analyzed it for her. "Based on the descriptions in the data, one of the Beyonders is a 'Prisoner,' and the other is an 'Apothecary.'
"As far as I know, there are quite a few 'Apothecaries' in Backlund, but not many 'Prisoners.' This pathway is relatively easy to track down, as the initial Sequence potions give them far more madness and desires than ordinary people.
"I suspect these cultists won't restrain their madness and desires too much, which makes for a good breakthrough."
He added, "If you find them but aren't confident in capturing them, you can call on me for help."
Xio nodded. "I'll let you know if I need it."
The conversation afterward became more casual. Hobert said, "Tomorrow I have a case to defend, one where I'm destined to lose, but I have to fight to the end."
Everyone was curious and decided to attend the hearing together tomorrow.

chapters.title: Chapter 122 - 122: Fragile Prosperity
chapters.content:
After the gathering, Hobert returned to his law office and focused all his energy on preparing for tomorrow's case.
After work, he took a carriage back to his home in Empress Borough and enjoyed a pleasant dinner with his family.
During the post-dinner conversation, Christian asked Hobert, "I heard you're fighting for better compensation for a worker injured on the job?"
Hobert nodded, "Yes."
"Do you need me to step in and help with the negotiations?"
"I want to try to solve it myself," Hobert smiled. "If I can't handle it or if we need more influence, I'll ask you to step in."
Christian smiled and nodded.
Donna, curious, asked, "Isn't it normal for someone to get compensated for a work injury? Why does it sound like it's difficult to get compensation?"
"You can get compensated, but the amount is too small," Hobert smiled. "I won't go into the details, but some things aren't better to know too early."
Christian nodded in agreement.
Hobert then mentioned that he had to travel to Tingen City next week for business. Christian said, "Tingen City, huh? My former deputy from the Southern Continent is now in Tingen City. You can stay at his place when you're there."
Hobert was momentarily surprised but then replied, "I'd rather stay at a hotel and not bother him."
"The hotel's conditions are terrible," Christian smiled. "Besides, you can deliver a personal letter for me."
Hobert had no choice but to agree. "Alright."
Back in his room, Hobert slept soundly. The next morning, he took a hired carriage and went to pick up Bob from the almshouse.
To his surprise, Daly was also there.
As the carriage resumed its journey, Hobert joked, "Ms. Daly, you don't seem too busy today."
Daly smiled, "Occasionally, I also need to check on the status of my informants."
They exchanged knowing smiles, though Bob looked a bit nervous.
After a few seconds, Daly added, "Recently, the church has also started paying attention to the issue of work injury compensation. Mr. Bob's case is quite representative, so the captain asked me to attend as an observer."
Hobert nodded and began discussing the case with Bob, reviewing the materials, and making final preparations.
Around 8:10, the three arrived at the courthouse.
Unexpectedly, quite a few people had already arrived in the gallery. Bob's coworkers sat in the front row.
On the left side of the corner were Xio, Audrey, and others. Daly was slightly surprised to see Audrey, knowing she was the devout daughter of Count Hall, a faithful believer in the Evernight Goddess. But she hadn't expected Audrey to attend.
Then, seeing who was sitting in the right-side corner, Daly was even more surprised and sat down next to him. "Ikanser? Why are you here?"
With his chiseled features and messy brown hair, Ikanser smiled. "This case has stirred quite a bit of discussion among the followers of the God of Steam and Machinery. The Archbishop sent me to observe."
This was none other than Ikanser Bernard, the captain of the Heart of Machinery in Backlund, who oversaw the mystical mirror, Arrodes.
Only then did Daly realize that this case had garnered far more attention than she initially thought.
Hobert, after escorting Bob to sit with his coworkers, waved to Audrey and her group. Then, he knocked on a girl's head beside him. "Donna, why are you here?"
Donna grinned mischievously. "Tyron and I skipped class to cheer you on."
Hobert smiled helplessly. "Don't make it a habit."
Donna nodded repeatedly, then continued, "Hobert, how do you know that angelic-looking lady?"
She was referring to Audrey.
Hobert replied, "She's one of my clients."
"You're lying! She doesn't look twenty yet. How could she be your client?"
"Believe it or not," Hobert said, glancing at his pocket watch before calling Bob to the plaintiff's bench.
The defendant, Arnold, and the judge took their places, and at 8:30, the trial officially began.
As the plaintiff's lawyer, Hobert first outlined the case: Arnold's negligence had caused Bob's disability, so they were accusing Arnold of intentional harm.
From the gallery, Ikanser quietly asked Daly, "You seem familiar with the plaintiff's lawyer?"
"He's one of our unofficial personnel," Daly didn't hide the fact.
"His defense strategy is creative," Ikansel said. "Perhaps this case really can be won."
"Let's hope so."
Then it was the defendant's lawyer's turn to speak. "Your Honor, the plaintiff's claim is clearly unfounded."
This lawyer wasn't the one from the last hearing in the Magistrate's Court. He appeared to be in his thirties, mature and steady, and was likely a well-known but not top-tier lawyer in Backlund.
He pointed to the gallery. "There are no 'safety first' signs posted in this courtroom. If someone in the gallery were to accidentally fall and injure themselves, would that be the fault of the court and the judge?"
Hobert responded, "The defendant's example is quite different from Bob's situation. Bob was under Arnold's employment and was injured while working for him.
"Are the people in the gallery employed by the judge?"
Bob's coworkers immediately started cheering and clapping. Right from the start, the two lawyers engaged in an intense debate.
After two or three rounds of back-and-forth, the defendant's lawyer realized that his eloquence was not gaining him any ground. He switched tactics: "Your Honor, everyone knows that the real issue here is not Mr. Arnold's alleged intentional harm but the compensation for Bob.
"I hope the court will adhere to legal precedents and not be swayed by the plaintiff lawyer's arguments. I believe the outcome of this case will impact future compensation cases between employers and workers.
"Everyone, the current compensation practices have maintained Backlund's stability and peace. To ensure this stability and peace continue, we shouldn't set a precedent that disrupts it."
Hobert silently acknowledged the opposing lawyer's skill. This lawyer was far superior to the one in the Magistrate's Court. He was quicker on his feet and knew how to tie his argument to something Hobert would find hard to refute.
Would Hobert, an ordinary lawyer, argue against the stability and peace of Backlund?
Fortunately, Hobert had prepared well. "Your Honor, everyone, of course, we want to see a more prosperous and stable Backlund! But times are changing, and society is evolving. The old laws and regulations won't always apply."
He passionately continued, "Of course, we want to see a more prosperous Backlund, but the prosperity of the 'Territory of Hope' shouldn't be built on the blood and tears of workers, on the exploitation and oppression of the working class!
"Without adaptation, prosperity is nothing but an illusion!"

chapters.title: Chapter 123 - 123: This Is the Barbarian
chapters.content:
Hobert's debate once again won applause from everyone, but the debate did not end there. Next, the defense lawyer, following old precedents which were more beneficial to Backlund's interests, argued against Hobert, who advocated for adapting to the current era's trends. They engaged in a heated argument back and forth.
After several rounds, the judge lightly tapped his gavel: "Please refrain from debating matters unrelated to the case in this court."
The debate between the two lawyers temporarily ceased.
Next, Hobert challenged again, continuing to argue about Arnold's inaction and Bob's disability causation.
However, the defense lawyer suddenly attacked Hobert and Bob from a moral standpoint, accusing Hobert of prioritizing personal gain and alleging he was here for fame, while claiming Bob was too greedy and his demands exceeded industry norms, among other criticisms.
Hobert countered, "I don't know by what standard the defense lawyer judges me to prioritize personal gain. Whatever the standard, Mr. Arnold sitting in the defendant's seat adheres more strictly to the principle of 'personal gain' than I do, otherwise, he wouldn't be wealthy. As for me, who supposedly prioritizes personal gain, I am just an ordinary lawyer till now."
"Furthermore," Hobert continued, "though the defense lawyer's words just now were carefully worded and did not constitute defamation, your method of defense is despicable, attempting to unsettle my client through moral attacks."
"Ladies and gentlemen, if we are to discuss moral judgments, is my client's remaining life worth only 150 pounds?"
"When did life become so cheap? When did human life become so cheap?"
These words plunged everyone present into a brief contemplation, except for the defense lawyer, who looked coldly at Hobert, not expecting this relatively unknown lawyer to be the strongest opponent he had faced since starting out.
The judge again struck the gavel lightly: "This is a court of law. Please refrain from moral debates."
He asked, "Defense lawyer, do you have anything else to say?"
The defense lawyer and Arnold both sensed that the judge was already leaning towards the plaintiff. If Arnold's charge of intentional injury was upheld, it would mean a victory for the plaintiff.
After careful consideration, the defense lawyer said, "Your Honor, I request a recess."
The judge was slightly taken aback, but it was within the defense lawyer's rights. "Granted, a ten-minute recess!"
After a brief conversation with Arnold, the defense lawyer and Arnold came to the plaintiff's side.
The defense lawyer first glanced at Hobert, then said, "How about 500 pounds? Let's settle this case out of court."
Supporting Bob to stand up, Hobert faced Arnold and the defense lawyer, saying, "Gentlemen, what are you so proud of? This is compensation, not your benevolent charity."
He added, "500 pounds may be acceptable, but we cannot accept the attitude of your compensation. Mr. Arnold, publicly apologize to Bob."
"Our patience has limits."
"Exactly the same words!"
Arnold suddenly said, "Young man, do you know your behavior now will ruin your life? Do you know who you are opposing?"
"You are challenging the entire upper class of Backlund. Let me tell you, I cannot lose this lawsuit! Because from today onwards, the entire upper class of Backlund will stand on my side."
"Hobert, are you really not considering your own future? Do you really want to challenge the survival rules set by the gentlemen of Backlund?"
A smile flickered across Hobert's face. "That's exactly what I'm pursuing!"
He immediately felt the clear feedback from the potion he had taken earlier. Challenging the so-called 'rules of civilization' was what a barbarian would do!
Arnold shook his head incredulously. He gestured to the defense lawyer, and both returned to the defendant's seat.
Supporting Bob to sit down, Hobert asked, "Are you not regretting the lack of reconciliation?"
Bob smiled, "Although I seem to have lost much dignity, your words just now made me suddenly realize that my remaining dignity is more valuable than 500 pounds."
Hobert nodded with a smile.
As soon as the ten minutes passed, the judge announced, "Court resumes! Please let the plaintiff's and defense's attorneys make their final statements."
As Hobert stood up, he sensed a spiritual warning. He scanned everyone and finally looked at the defense lawyer.
The defense lawyer was a true 'lawyer' who was now using his Beyonder abilities to distort Hobert's thoughts.
This indicated that Arnold was prepared to use despicable means to resolve the issue.
Hobert sneered inwardly: Trying to distort the thoughts of a 'Barbarian'?
He injected mana into the 'Psychological Spoon' hidden in his lining: "Psychological cue!"
The defense lawyer immediately stood up. "I-I-I was just using my Beyonder power to attack Hobert because I knew a secret rule of the court. As long as Beyonder powers are involved, the judgment of this court is invalid. The judge will immediately adjourn and, after sternly warning those using Beyonder abilities, schedule a new trial date."
"Regardless of success, I can achieve my goal, as long as this court does not render a final judgment, Hobert's demands will temporarily fail."
He covered his mouth with his hands in horror, but his voice was still clearly heard by everyone: "I-I-I previously used similarly despicable methods to turn the tide, including one week ago..."
"Prohibited!" The judge suddenly spoke with authority. He was a true 'judge'.
The psychological cue that Hobert hastily planted earlier immediately dissolved. Then Hobert burst into laughter suddenly, seemingly laughing at the defense lawyer's despicableness, and also at the defense lawyer for voicing his scheming thoughts.
Audrey sitting in the corner watched the 'vanguard of justice' laughing heartily, saw the stern yet somewhat helpless judge, and saw the defense lawyer in unease.
She planned to paint this scene immediately after returning, which would be extremely ironic.
Xio and Fors exchanged a glance. They were experienced Beyonders and could tell at a glance that in the recent Beyonder ability confrontation, Hobert had won decisively.
On the other side, Daly and Ikanser gradually became serious. They realized that this case might receive more attention in the future. Daly even worried whether Hobert could withstand the pressure.
In the courtroom, Hobert finally restrained his laughter.
The judge waved to the defense lawyer and Hobert separately.
As the two lawyers approached the judge's bench, he said solemnly, "Today, your performances will be recorded by me. Trust me, you have only this one chance. If you use any power outside of the law in this courtroom again, I will immediately send you to a special court!"
Hobert said, "Your Honor, as you saw just now, it was he who used Beyonder powers first. I only responded effectively."
The judge looked coldly at the defense lawyer. "He will certainly undergo some special investigation!"
The defense lawyer involuntarily took a step back. Several cases he had handled before could not withstand investigation. He was likely to be sent to a special court for trial.
While the defense lawyer was uneasy, the judge turned to Hobert again. "Your defense was brilliant."
But in the end, he sighed helplessly. "Court adjourned!"

chapters.title: Chapter 124 - 124: Captain Ikanser Who Likes Red Underpants
chapters.content:
"Hobert, this was undoubtedly the most brilliant defense I've ever witnessed," Audrey spared no praise, "You are not just competent, but what you're doing now far exceeds what any lawyer should do!"
She continued, "I will do everything in my power to support your cause for justice!"
Audrey emphasized the word 'justice' and winked at Hobert.
Facing her playful remark, Hobert smiled and replied, "Thank you for your support."
Viscount Glaint also made a similar commitment before leaving with Audrey in their carriage.
Next, Bob's coworkers approached, saying, "Mr. Lawyer, I will definitely tell every coworker I meet about your brilliant defense today."
Some even had tears in their eyes as they said, "You spoke so well for us, no one has ever fought for our interests before!"
"Steam above, Bob, it must be the great God of Steam and Machinery who heard your prayers and led you to find such a good lawyer!"
"Did you all hear what the defense attorney said? That scum!"
...
After the chorus of praises, one by one, Bob's coworkers left.
Donna came over and said, "Hobert, today I realized how amazing you really are."
"Although the judge had to adjourn for reasons unknown, I could tell you won! You shined brightly in court."
Tyron chimed in, "It won't be long before you become a great lawyer!"
"Hope your flattery will make your teacher feel pleased," Hobert smiled, "so he won't punish you for skipping class!"
Donna laughed, "Punishment or not, I feel like I've earned today by attending."
Hobert shook his head, hailed a carriage, paid the fare for Donna and Tyron, and sent them back to school.
When he returned to the courthouse's entrance, he saw Daly with a man whose messy brown hair caught his attention. Daly introduced him, "This is Captain Isengard from the Church of Steam and Machinery."
Hobert paused slightly, "I remember now, the guy who..."
The guy who likes red underwear! Why wield anything other than a seal? Why not take the mirror!
He smiled, "Captain Ikanser."
Ikanser hesitated, "Have we met before?"
"No, I've heard about you from others."
"Oh. Can we talk privately?"
They left the crowd and went to a corner.
Ikanser said, "Since you've heard of me, I won't introduce myself."
"You should know that most of our church's followers are workers, so we take this case very seriously."
"I think Arnold should try some despicable means in the future. If you need help, you can come to the Church and we'll shelter you."
"Thank you for your kindness," Hobert smiled, "if needed, I'll definitely visit the Church."
"We should be thanking you," Ikanser said, "actually, we should."
Suddenly, something occurred to Hobert, "If you really want to thank me, send me a few tickets to the Roselle Memorial Exhibition. I've been studying the mysterious symbols left by Emperor Roselle."
"How did you know we were planning a memorial exhibition?"
"I heard it from a friend."
"Alright, leave me your address, and when the exhibition starts, I'll send you the tickets." The Roselle Memorial Exhibition was already in the preparation stage, and Isengard didn't find anything wrong with Hobert getting the news early.
Hobert breathed a sigh of relief; just now, his mind was full of the Cards of Blasphemy and he didn't seriously think about when the Roselle Memorial Exhibition would begin.
After seeing off Ikanser, only Bob, Daly, Xio, and Fors were left at the courthouse entrance.
Xio stepped forward, "Hobert, I'd like to ask for your help."
Hobert nodded, "Let's talk in the carriage."
They got into the carriage, first sending Bob back to the almshouse, then Daly.
Before Daly got off, Hobert made an appointment to meet her at the Obsidian Bar at 3 o'clock in the afternoon.
In the carriage were only Hobert, Xio, and Fors.
Xio said, "Hobert, I hope you can accompany us to Mr. A's gathering. I want to make contact with the person who sells the 'Sheriff' potion formula."
This was a suggestion Hobert had made earlier, subtly reminding Xio that only the Sheriff recognized by the royal family was a legitimate "Sheriff."
While Mr. A's gatherings had always had good reputation and guarantees, Xio was still afraid of encountering risks.
"No problem," Hobert asked, "when does Mr. A's gathering start?"
"At 12:30."
Hobert checked his pocket watch, "It's not even 10 o'clock now. Let's first go to the Harvest Church; I have an appointment there."
"Okay."
Arriving at Rose Street, Hobert carefully surveyed the street and didn't see anyone trailing them.
Even if the Tamara family knew that the five family members had trouble on Rose Street, they didn't dare to conduct a thorough investigation or send someone to tail them.
Because their Beyonder influence in Backlund was too weak; without the backing of a demigod, anything they did would risk being investigated by their opponents.
And Hobert could tell that among the Beyonders in the spirit channeling, the man with long hair who liked smoking cigars was not a demigod.
Arriving at the entrance of the Harvest Church, Hobert asked Xio and Fors to wait in the carriage and instructed the coachman to wait here as well. He put on his mask and got off the carriage.
The coachman was happy to wait, as he charged by the hour.
Entering the church, besides Bishop Utravsky sitting in the front row, only Upton sat in the corner.
Upton visibly relaxed upon seeing Hobert; Hobert wasn't sure if he was worried that Hobert wouldn't come or if he couldn't stand the oppressive atmosphere in the church.
Hobert first greeted Utravsky, "Father."
"The Giant" Bishop nodded slowly in response.
Hobert sat next to Upton, "How's your recovery?"
"Almost there," Upton handed Hobert a wooden box.
Hobert opened a corner of the box and saw a diamond the size of an eye inside, even in the box lacking light, it reflected seven-colored light.
Inside the "diamond" was half a palm-sized black crystal ball emitting a charming aura, which made people feel a strong affinity. This is the Beyonder charatceristic of the "Briber."
Hobert closed the wooden box, "Have you been hearing indescribable murmurs lately?"
"I can hear it," Upton smiled bitterly, "and it's getting worse."
"I do have some ways here that can help you eliminate these murmurs."
Upton listened attentively.
"For example, you could try to be a real 'Barbarian.'"
Upton took two or three seconds to understand, "Does the name of the potion imply a way to eliminate murmurs?"
Hobert smiled and nodded, "Pretty clever."
