chapters.title: Chapter 136 - 136: Selena's Cultic Constitution
chapters.content:
Archer glanced at the two strangers behind Selena. Selena quickly introduced them, "They are my friends."
Archer paused on Hobert for a second or two, then withdrew his gaze, "I need her hair, blood, nails, or something she often uses."
Selena was prepared and took out a headdress, "This was given to me by Elizabeth last week. She wore it for a while before I had the chance."
Archer nodded, took out a crystal ball, and placed the headdress beneath it.
Then he began to theatrically chant, as if entering a frenzied state.
Selena and even Melissa were stunned, while Hobert coldly observed from the side. He knew such divinations didn't require any nonsense chants, and he also guessed that the Archer before him should be a Secrets Supplicant.
The ample spirituality of a Secrets Supplicant was enough for them to use some tools to perform divination-like operations.
However, Archer should be a Sequence 7 or Sequence 8, and all the abilities of a Secrets Supplicant should be enhanced.
After a series of operations, Archer took a deep breath and recovered from his frenzied state. He touched the crystal ball and said, "Your friend is in the outskirts to the east, in an abandoned villa."
"Hurry! The criminals are preparing to leave there. If you're late, you won't find them."
"Thank you, Mr. Archer," Selena said, getting up to leave.
However, Hobert asked, "What is the cost of this divination?"
Archer glanced at Hobert, "Selena's divination is free."
Selena smiled proudly.
"No," Hobert said, "I believe every gift from fate has a price."
He continued, "Besides, this is about respect for you and the divination."
Archer stared at Hobert for a second or two before saying, "5 soli."
Hobert handed over 5 soli and then said, "Please return the headdress to me."
He spread out a handkerchief in his palm and held it out to Archer.
Archer took the money, placed the damaged headdress on the handkerchief.
Both movements were slow, as if they were making a transaction more dangerous than high explosives.
Finally, Hobert put away the handkerchief, and the atmosphere in the room immediately eased.
Selena thanked Mr. Archer again, and the three left the dim room one after another.
After getting on the carriage, Hobert instructed the coachman to head east towards the abandoned villa.
Inside the carriage, Melissa was somewhat surprised, "Mr. Lawyer, you don't really believe in the divination just now, do you?"
"Why not?" Selena smiled.
Hobert said seriously, "Miss Selena, please remember the principle of equivalent exchange when dealing with enthusiasts of these mysteries in the future.
"If anyone is willing to provide you with some mysterious services for free, it's because they have greater ambitions."
Selena was first startled, then smiled, "Mr. Lawyer, are you also an enthusiast of mysticism?"
"Also," Hobert continued seriously, "Do not leave your blood, hair, nails, or things you often carry with you to others for yourself, your family, or friends."
He handed over his handkerchief, "These things can be used to find people or to curse."
The smile on Selena's face disappeared, and she took the handkerchief, "I remember."
Then Hobert answered Melissa's question, "Let's trust that divination for now, or we have no other clues."
As for Archer's divination results, Hobert estimated they should be correct. After all, Archer had to maintain his charlatan image in front of Selena.
Melissa nodded and said no more.
Hobert asked again, "Miss Selena, how did you meet Archer?"
"After my teacher, Hanass Vincent, who taught me divination, passed away, I went to mourn him." Selena replied, "I met Mr. Archer who had the same purpose in the cemetery."
Hobert nodded. The exposure and sudden death of Hanass must have attracted the attention and investigation of the Aurora Order.
And this Archer was probably sent by the Aurora Order to investigate the cause of Hanass's death and exposure, as well as to establish contact with Hanass's students.
But he was also really arrogant, appearing openly at Hanass's grave, wasn't he afraid of the surveillance that might exist among the official Beyonders?
Then Hobert was relieved, these were madmen, they couldn't be reasoned with by common sense.
Hobert continued, "Today is Wednesday, aren't you going to class? Why did you have to mourn Hanass today?"
"I've been dreaming about my teacher a lot recently." Selena smiled bitterly, "And the contents of the dreams are almost the same, urging me to mourn him as soon as possible."
She had just finished speaking when she saw Mr. Lawyer close his eyes. She wasn't sure if it was her illusion. When Mr. Lawyer opened his eyes again, his eyes seemed even deeper.
This was certainly not her illusion. Hobert opened his spirit vision because of the blessing of the "Spirit Necklace," and his spirit vision could see all undead creatures.
But he found nothing, "Since when did the same dream start appearing?"
"From..." Selena thought for a moment, then was surprised, "Since I met Mr. Archer."
"Then never go to mourn Hanass," Hobert said seriously, "I don't know what's going on, but I know that as long as you appear at Hanass's grave, you will definitely be harmed."
Selena was somewhat frightened and somewhat at a loss.
"Then go to the confessional at the church and tell the priest about this. I believe Hanass will not appear in your dreams again." Hobert said, "And for the sake of your safety and that of your family, don't contact Archer again!"
Selena seemed to understand something, but also seemed to understand nothing, "Okay, okay..."
Then she reluctantly smiled, "Mr. Lawyer, you know so much!"
Hobert did not respond to Selena's praise, but continued to admonish, "Unless there is a trustworthy guide to be your guide, do not follow teachers in mysterious fields at random."
To be honest, this was the first time he had seen someone with a "cultic constitution."
At this point, the coachman said, "Sir, there really is an abandoned villa!"
They had arrived in the suburbs by the time they spoke, and Hobert told the coachman, "Don't slow down, just drive past."
Through the carriage window, the three saw an abandoned villa overgrown with weeds in the yard.
Thinking back to the divination just now, Melissa was somewhat surprised, but she immediately thought that there seemed to be many abandoned villas in the outskirts.
Hobert smiled, "Looks like this is it! Whatever happens later, don't get out of the carriage."
Melissa and Selena immediately understood that Mr. Lawyer intended to rescue people alone!

chapters.title: Chapter 137 - 137: Rescuing Elizabeth
chapters.content:
Hobert noticed the trampled and flattened weeds in the courtyard and the faint silhouette behind a tree. He deduced that this was the location mentioned in Archer's divination.
Reporting to the police would take too much time, and if the criminals decided to take Elizabeth away, it would be even harder to track them. So Hobert decided to rescue her immediately.
Besides, he didn't take a group of kidnappers too seriously.
Selena excitedly asked, "Mr. Lawyer, are you going to rescue Elizabeth alone?"
Melissa, on the other hand, calmly reminded him, "There might be more than a few of them, and they could have other weapons."
Hobert smiled, "Don't worry, I won't take unnecessary risks, nor will I charge in recklessly."
"Melissa, doesn't this seem like a grand adventure from a storybook?" Selena said, "And we are part of it too!"
Melissa replied, "The main character of the adventure is Mr. Hobert, and we are merely spectators."
Hobert chuckled: This girl is way too calm for her age; she doesn't act like a typical teenager.
The carriage traveled for about three more minutes before Hobert asked the driver to wait.
The driver offered help, but Hobert declined, stating that having him around would be a hindrance.
After stepping out, Hobert briskly walked towards the abandoned villa.
In the courtyard, two criminals were discussing the appearance of the kidnapped girl, maliciously laughing about finding ways to "enjoy" her.
Hobert, as if he were entering his own home, walked straight in and even closed the gate behind him.
Yes, this was his plan all along: to act boldly, not recklessly, like a true "Barbarian."
The two criminals were completely dumbfounded. A companion? Someone they hadn't met? The villa's owner? But hadn't the owner died from illness?
Hobert smiled, "I know this will hurt, but you brought it upon yourselves."
As he spoke, he broke one criminal's nose with a punch, knocking him out. Then, with a swift kick, he shattered the other's arm.
With the strength of at least three grown men, Hobert's attacks against ordinary people caused immediate fractures.
He kicked open the decaying door, just as another criminal rushed at him with an axe.
Hobert dodged nimbly, and seeing the right moment, tackled the criminal, knocking him out with a powerful kick.
Suddenly, Hobert's intuition kicked in, warning him of danger. He instinctively ducked.
Bang!
A gunshot rang out, but because of Hobert's sudden movement, the bullet missed its mark.
The shooter was hiding behind a half-broken wooden door.
"How rude! Shooting from hiding!" Hobert picked up the axe, swinging it toward the door.
Crash! Bang!
The door shattered under the force of the axe, and the head of the criminal behind it exploded.
Two more criminals rushed in from the back door, brandishing knives. But before they could attack, Hobert, like a charging battering ram, knocked one out and smacked the other unconscious with his cane.
The villa fell silent.
Remaining cautious of further ambushes, Hobert searched for Elizabeth.
He heard movement on the second floor, so he carefully ascended the decaying staircase. In the left room, he spotted Elizabeth, tied to a chair with a gag in her mouth.
She frantically shook her head as soon as she saw Hobert.
Hobert quickly assessed the room and guessed there was an ambush waiting for him, but he still walked in unhurriedly.
As soon as he entered, he heard a heavy object being moved on the left. With a glance, he saw a thick wooden beam hurtling toward him, with a gunman hiding behind it.
Such a heavy beam would have severely injured or killed an ordinary person, but Hobert caught it with one hand, effortlessly.
Both the criminal and Elizabeth were stunned.
Hobert pushed the beam back, slamming the gunman against the wall.
Crash!
The villa's entire wall collapsed from the impact, and the criminal fell into the backyard, his condition unknown.
Hobert removed the gag from Elizabeth's mouth and untied her.
"H-Hobert, what... what just happened?" Elizabeth asked in disbelief.
Hobert smiled, "I've always been strong. And as a lawyer, fighting is one of my skills. When words fail, we resort to 'physical persuasion.'"
Elizabeth rubbed her numb wrists, contemplating what "physical persuasion" truly meant.
"You're a 'Barbarian'!"
Suddenly, a cold voice echoed in the room.
It was Archer's voice!
Hobert immediately stood up, raising his cane with one hand and reaching into his pouch for the "Teleportation Statue."
His ability to detect weaknesses kicked in, and he quickly sensed Archer hiding in the shadows of the corner, though the shadows appeared no different from others in the room.
"I didn't expect you to act in broad daylight," Hobert said.
The two had clashed before, but it was more of a battle of wills rather than an actual fight.
Though Hobert's Sequence was lower than Archer's, he was not to be underestimated.
Archer hadn't been prepared at the time and couldn't find a clear opening, so he refrained from attacking.
Hobert thought Archer would flee or wait for the official Beyonders to arrive, preparing to fight them instead. He hadn't expected Archer to use his divination to arrive here in advance, laying an ambush.
"If it were anyone else, I'd choose to stay hidden," Archer said, "But you're different."
He continued, "Heyman from Backlund recently hid at my place. From his 'memories,' I saw your face. I know you've disrupted our organization's plans."
"So, I came here early to kill you!"
Archer had been observing Hobert and, after confirming that he was a Sequence 8 "Barbarian," decided to act.
Without hesitation, Hobert pulled out the Teleportation Statue and first teleported Elizabeth outside the villa.
But a shadow in the corner rose like a black cloth, extending a hand toward Elizabeth, making a choking motion.
Elizabeth immediately felt as if invisible hands were gripping her throat. Panicked, she clutched at her pale neck.
However, there was nothing there—just a red mark appearing on her skin.
Hobert swiftly brought Elizabeth back to his side.
Elizabeth, sitting in the chair, was utterly confused. What just happened? She felt like she had been outside on the lawn, and then suddenly, she was back on the second floor again.

chapters.title: Chapter 138 - 138 Confronting Sequence 7
chapters.content:
Hobert did not rush to take action; he was observing Archer's abilities.
He knew the abilities of the "Secret Supplicant" Sequence 5 "Shepherd," and had a general idea about the abilities of "Rose Bishop," but he only had a vague concept of the abilities of "Shadow Ascetic" and "Listener."
Additionally, Hobert realized that Archer's abilities seemed to somewhat counteract the abilities of the "Barbarian." For Hobert's current abilities, all he could rely on was his physical strength.
But no matter how great his strength was, it seemed futile to strike Archer hiding in the shadows.
If it were any other Sequence 8, encountering such an enemy would almost certainly mean being at their mercy.
However, Hobert was not afraid at all. He had an artifact on him, three mystical items, and one disposable mystical item. Even if he couldn't win, there would be no problem in ensuring his own survival.
Elizabeth still didn't understand what had just happened, but she could sense that there was tremendous danger lurking in this room.
The figure standing in front of her blocked the danger.
In the shadows, Archer did not expect that Hobert actually possessed a sealed artifact that could instantly move positions. Nevertheless, since he had already started, he naturally couldn't stop halfway.
He reached out towards Hobert, who immediately felt suffocated.
Just now, when Archer went to choke Elizabeth, Hobert hadn't quite understood what was happening. Now that Archer was trying to choke him, he probably understood what was going on.
Turning his head slightly, Hobert indeed saw the shadow of his own neck being gripped by a hand from within the shadow.
He exerted force on his neck, and two veins bulged. Archer immediately couldn't move his hand anymore.
Hobert smiled. Could this be "might makes right"?
He had a rough idea of Archer's main abilities now. Although Archer could hide in the shadows and use shadows to affect his enemies, his offensive power was not strong. Faced with a Beyonder like Hobert, who was tough and resilient, his attacks would not be effective for the time being.
Thinking of this, Hobert decided to counterattack. He took large strides forward, intending to knock down the wall near the window, which already showed signs of collapse, to reduce the shadow area in the room.
However, it seemed like his feet were stuck to the ground. Every step he took, the shadows on the ground wrestled with him.
Hobert even had the illusion that each time he lifted his leg, there was a person hanging onto it.
After taking three or four steps, the shadows in the corner of the wall flickered as if breathing heavily.
It was at this moment that Archer realized Hobert was deliberately wrestling with him!
Strength was Hobert's forte, so naturally, he would use his strengths to deplete Archer's stamina.
Identifying weaknesses in an enemy's abilities and leveraging one's own strengths were basic operations for "Lawyers."
Archer now realized that the young man in front of him was not as reckless as he had shown earlier.
He jumped out of the shadows and stood in front of Hobert.
Hobert immediately recognized this as his physical presence and raised his cane to strike.
Swish~
The cane swung by Hobert was caught by a hand covered in thick black fur. In almost an instant, Archer underwent a noticeable transformation. It seemed like he was draped in a black curtain of hair. The sunlight was receding further from the room, and it seemed like the room had suddenly elongated, with the window and door getting farther and farther from Hobert.
Endless darkness swept over, and Archer's power rapidly expanded.
The hand with dense fur pushed forward.
Thump thump~
Hobert hurriedly stepped back two steps, nearly losing his grip on the cane.
Archer's transformation continued. His face grew longer, and two golden antlers sprouted from his head.
Hobert sensed extreme danger and quickly continued to retreat.
In just one or two seconds, Archer's face was covered in black fur, and his head resembled that of a bull, but with golden antlers.
He was draped in a black cloak that touched the ground, with red light shimmering in his eyes.
Just standing there, the surroundings were filled with maddening whispers.
This was a power Archer gained when he was still a "Listener," allowing him to temporarily borrow some of the power of the True Creator's creatures.
It was precisely because of establishing such a connection that he hadn't gone mad or died, making him Mr. Z of the Aurora Order!
Hobert quickly turned away, but he felt that his spirit had already been corrupted. The power of all the corruption in his spirit body and all the madness in his spirit were churning, as if he could lose his sanity at any moment.
This was bad!
Elizabeth!
Looking back at Elizabeth, the chubby-faced girl was staring fixedly at the "monster" in front of her. On her head, two golden horns were slowly growing.
Hobert dropped the cane and hurriedly covered her eyes.
And with the "Teleportation Statue" in his hand, forcibly knocked down the two "golden horns."
Then Hobert quickly used the ability of the "Teleportation Statue" to envelop the surrounding seven to eight meters in darkness created by the statues and deprived Archer of his sight.
There were still indescribable whispers in his ears, but without the visual impact, the mental burden was greatly reduced.
Elizabeth's eyes gradually began to regain their luster, and her mutation from earlier was slowly receding.
Looking at Archer again, he could only stand in the corner of the wall.

chapters.title: Chapter 139 - 139: Klein's Opponent
chapters.content:
Hobert wanted to continue pursuit, but tears had completely obscured his vision, a profound sorrow welling up in his heart.
Perhaps due to using the "Psychological Spoon" twice consecutively, even "Distortion" couldn't completely negate its negative effects this time.
After Archer entered the shadows, his speed increased dramatically. Dragging his visibly uncontrollable body, he swiftly disappeared from Hobert's view.
Half a minute later, the sadness in Hobert's heart gradually faded.
Elizabeth seemed to awaken from a nightmare. "Mr. Lawyer, just now... why were you crying so sadly?"
"It's nothing," Hobert said. "I just remembered some sad things."
He glanced helplessly at Elizabeth and employed his "Hypnosis" ability. "You better forget what just happened."
Elizabeth forgot the memories after Archer appeared, and Hobert soothed her somewhat chaotic mind.
Using the "Psychological Spoon" three times in a row left Hobert somewhat tired. At this moment, Elizabeth couldn't help bursting into laughter.
Hobert quickly twisted her smile.
Elizabeth smiled gently. "Mr. Lawyer, you're really strong. You lifted that thick log with just one hand."
Her memory returned to when Hobert had just untied her.
Hobert sighed. "I'm naturally strong. Your two good friends are outside; let them take you back first."
Elizabeth nodded obediently. She tried to get up but sat back down on the chair. "Mr. Lawyer, I... my legs have no strength."
The creature Archer had transformed into just now had put tremendous pressure on the ordinary Elizabeth, mentally and physically exhausted being a normal phenomenon.
But now time was of the essence, so Hobert had to carry Elizabeth and quickly descend the stairs.
After a slight surprise, Elizabeth unexpectedly found security in Hobert's embrace, which made her feel shy, instinctively moving away to the side.
Melissa and Selina's carriage was nearby. After hearing the gunshot, the coachman drove the carriage over, ready to help Hobert escape if his rescue failed.
Everyone breathed a sigh of relief when they saw Hobert carrying Elizabeth out.
Then Melissa noticed that Elizabeth, in Mr. Lawyer's arms, didn't resist being in such close contact with him. After Mr. Lawyer put her in the carriage, she seemed noticeably disappointed.
Melissa immediately felt that something was wrong; Klein's opponent had appeared!
The reason Elizabeth reacted like this was because she felt deeply afraid in her heart. She couldn't remember exactly why she was afraid, only feeling safe when she was with Hobert.
"Take the three girls back first," Hobert told the coachman. "Elizabeth needs rest now. Also, report to the police. Say all the kidnappers have been caught."
"Yeah, they shouldn't be able to escape for a while."
Those bandits were either dead or disabled. When he went downstairs just now, those who fell into a coma hadn't woken up yet, and those who didn't were lying on the ground crying, unable to move.
The coachman asked, "Sir, what about you...?"
"I have some other matters to attend to. After you take the three ladies to Dominic's company, wait for me at the Church of the Evernight Goddess." With that said, Hobert quickly walked towards the busier street to find a rental carriage.
Elizabeth watched Hobert's figure in a daze, feeling strangely familiar with his back.
"Elizabeth, are you okay?" Selina asked.
Elizabeth came to her senses. "Praise the Lady! The kidnappers didn't finish writing the ransom note before I was rescued."
As she spoke, tears streamed down uncontrollably. "I... I was so scared when I was kidnapped. I thought..."
At this moment, Elizabeth's fright and grievances surged up, finally having the chance to cry out.
Fortunately, Melissa and Selina, her two good friends, comforted her non-stop.
...
On the other side, after finding a rental carriage, Hobert arrived at the Church of the Evernight Goddess.
He instructed the carriage to circle around the street behind the church. After searching for a few minutes, he finally found the Blackthorn Security Company.
It must be said that their signboard was really inconspicuous, and he nearly missed it.
After paying the fare, Hobert climbed the steps and entered the security company.
There was a brown-haired, fair-faced girl at the front desk, seemingly absorbed in reading the newspaper.
"Hello!" Hobert greeted.
Whoosh~ The girl covered the newspaper on the table, but due to the hurried cover-up, something under the newspaper was still exposed: a bestselling book.
Hobert was momentarily puzzled. What's the difference between reading the newspaper at work and reading a novel? Why cover up a novel with a newspaper?
"Sir, how can I help you?" The girl smiled, trying to conceal her previous fluster.
Hobert took out his freelance personnel identification. "I need to see your captain."
The girl behind the front desk, naturally, was Rozanne.
Although she hadn't seen this kind of identification before, she recognized the emblem of the Church of the Evernight Goddess. "Please follow me."
Leading the way, Roselle said, "Sir, you don't sound like a local?"
"Yeah." Hobert followed behind. "I'm from Backlund."
Rozanne glanced back at Hobert. "The City of Hope, right? Is the smog as severe as the newspapers say?"
"We usually don't read newspapers," Hobert said, "because the fog is too thick to see the letters on the newspaper in front of us."
Rozanne chuckled, covering her mouth. "You're quite humorous."
They reached the captain's office, where Dunn, who had heard Rozanne's voice earlier, was already looking towards the door.
"Captain, this gentleman from Backlund has something to see you about." In front of Dunn, Rozanne finally showed her professionalism, inviting Hobert in and closing the door behind her.
Dunn looked at Hobert. "Who are you..."
Hobert looked at the man with gray eyes, high hairline, and a low, gentle voice. "Hello, here are my credentials."
The captain's appearance was slightly more rugged than he had imagined.
Dunn glanced at the credentials. "Welcome, Mr. Hobert." As he spoke, he gestured for Hobert to sit down.
Sitting opposite Dunn, Hobert said, "While resolving a dispute case, I encountered a member of the Aurora Order..."
Hobert briefly recounted the kidnapping case and his encounter with Archer, concluding, "Archer was already showing signs of losing control. According to the characteristics of the 'Secret Supplicant' pathway, he is easily prone to complete loss of control. Even if he doesn't completely lose control, it will take a long time to suppress the signs of his control."
"I think we should find him before he loses control and restrain him! Or seize him while he's licking his wounds!"
"Well, does your team have a 'Seer'? I left clues on him for divination."

chapters.title: Chapter 140 - 140 Action of the Protagonist Team
chapters.content:
In the carriage, Hobert sized up the three team members besides Dunn. One had black hair and brown eyes, with a scholarly air about him—Klein Moretti. Another had black hair and green eyes, unkempt and carrying a poet's aura—Leonard Mitchell. The last one had a prominent nose, an icy and gloomy demeanor, with a pallor that resembled more a corpse than a living person—Frye.
Captain Dunn mobilized three team members at once, partly due to the seriousness of a Sequence 7 enemy and, of course, to watch out for Hobert.
Even after confirming Hobert's identity through a telegram to Backlund, Dunn remained cautious.
That was normal; after all, they hadn't fought together and lacked trust.
"So, Mr. Hobert," Dunn said, "about what you mentioned earlier—what clues do we have for divination?"
Hobert took out his wallet and carefully pulled out a corner of a banknote. "I saw him put this banknote into his pocket with my own eyes. After that, he rushed ahead to the ambush site before me. He wouldn't have had time to take it out after things went haywire."
"So I think that banknote is likely still on him."
The banknote in question was the 5 Soli divination fee Hobert had paid to Archer. As he took it out of his wallet earlier, he had discreetly torn off a small corner.
Klein examined the tiny piece in his palm, using it to find the rest of the banknote. It wasn't too difficult to do.
Leonard smiled and asked, "What if—oh, I mean, what if he didn't have the banknote on him?"
"Then I'll take you to the rented house where he had his divination," Hobert said. "If we find clues there, we'll continue investigating. If not, then it's closed, and I'm out of it."
"I love hearing the word 'closed'," Leonard said with a smile.
"Alright, let's get going," Dunn interrupted their increasingly off-topic conversation.
Klein began directing the coachman using a method called 'Dowsing Rod Divination'.
Hobert, now with some idle time, looked at the people in the carriage and suddenly felt a bit surreal, as if he had suddenly joined the adventure of the protagonist team.
The carriage gradually left the city and arrived at a rural village on the outskirts, finally stopping in front of a farmhouse with a water wheel.
The people in the carriage immediately sensed a dangerous atmosphere inside the farmhouse. The horses pulling the carriage were restless; without the coachman's control, they would have left long ago.
Hobert sighed. With a 'Seer' on their team, finding people or things was indeed convenient!
He took out his gun and reminded them, "Be careful. It seems like the enemy can transform into a kind of creature that exudes madness and corruption. If you see signs of transformation, don't make eye contact."
Everyone nodded and quickly approached the farmhouse. Soon, they discovered dead dogs and several chickens inside. If there were people in the farmhouse, their situation was likely grim.
Klein divined, "The opponent is inside the farmhouse, posing some danger, but within acceptable limits."
After a brief inspection, Dunn said, "I'll pull him into a dream. Wait a dozen seconds before entering."
"No, I can 'bring him out'," Hobert said, pulling out the 'Teleportation Statue'.
Dunn nodded. His earlier suspicion of Hobert stemmed from doubting whether a Sequence 8 could severely injure a Sequence 7. Seeing this Sealed Artifact and Hobert's previous words made Dunn more inclined to trust him.
Then, leaning against a tree outside the courtyard wall, Dunn lowered his head, seemingly entering sleep. Soon, a tranquil aura enveloped him completely.
"Ah..."
A pained cry came from inside the farmhouse, followed by the sound of things being knocked over. But soon, everything quieted down.
Hobert held the 'Teleportation Statue'. "Ready!"
Klein and Leonard glanced at each other, ready for what?
Hobert began using the 'Teleportation Statue'. Within a 15-meter radius, everything, including people and objects, fell under his control. He then moved Archer from the farmhouse into the courtyard.
At this point, Archer hadn't completely lost control; some semblance of reason still remained.
But his entire body had swelled to twice its size, covered with black growths that resembled tumors. Within these growths, some emitted black mist while others oozed murky liquid. Particularly on his back, it seemed to have turned into a thick liquid, emitting an aura of dirt and corruption.
Several people raised their guns and aimed at Archer's transforming head.
Hobert sighed again. Having teammates who could 'control' was really helpful! If he had faced such a monster alone, a fierce battle would have been inevitable. No, he would more likely have fled and then reported it.
After a volley, they realized something was wrong. Where Archer's head had been hit, thick black fur was exposed.
Dunn suddenly looked up. "Bad news. An evil creature is using Archer's body to manifest."
Earlier, Archer had been resisting the manifestation of this evil creature. By pulling Archer into a dream, Dunn inadvertently accelerated the creature's descent.
At this point, golden deer antlers sprouted from Archer's head. Hobert immediately understood—they were the creatures Archer had summoned earlier.
After Archer began to lose control, he became the vessel for their descent.
In the 'Nation of Disorder', this problem would be easily solved—just cut off the path of descent. But in reality, Hobert lacked this ability.
At this point, Dunn also drew his pistol. "Kill Archer!"
Hobert, shooting along with them, marveled, "Captain Dunn's reaction is so fast, immediately understanding the situation and quickly coming up with a countermeasure."
Archer was now the medium for the descent; killing him would also end the descent process.
Archer didn't dodge the bullets but suddenly lay down, writhing and rubbing his back.
When he got up again, the thick slime on his back had been wiped away, revealing thick black fur inside, along with human flesh and bones.
The human flesh and bones were gradually being replaced by the thick black fur.
Dunn buried his head again. Archer's movements immediately slowed down, and Dunn shook his body, struggling against the opponent.
Leonard assisted from the side, chanting, "If life deceives you, don't be sad or troubled. Stay calm on gloomy days."
Everything around them became calm again, and Archer's movements slowed once more. Hobert and Klein almost lost their desire to attack.
Hobert, who had been searching for Archer's weakness, finally found it. There was a piece of human flesh on Archer's back that hadn't grown thick black fur.
He fired two shots, overturning that piece of flesh, revealing black ribs inside. Most of Archer's Beyonder characteristics were concentrated in this black rib, crucial to this descent!
"Cover me!" Hobert said, jumping into the courtyard.

chapters.title: Chapter 141 - 141: The Death of Mr. Z
chapters.content:
Archer seemed to sense Hobert's intentions and struggled harder. The thick black fur covering its human flesh accelerated.
Leonard chanted again, "Then you will know why, in your prime, you lie in your grave."
Archer's movements slowed once more.
Hobert, crossing the courtyard wall, retracted the "Teleportation Statue" and approached Archer. Immediately, he felt discomfort, as if he heard indescribable murmurs again and saw the world's most filthy and depraved things.
He resisted with his own spirituality, using his cane as a lever to pry open part of Archer's flesh and blood. The black rib was fully exposed before him.
Archer slowly opened his mouth, now resembling a bovine's maw!
Oh no!
This guy was about to spit out something fragrant!
[T/N: meaning that he will excessively say flowery language]
It was too late to stop it. Hobert prepared to use the "Teleporting Statue" to move Archer further away, reducing the harm from the "language of foulness."
At that moment, a figure leaped past Hobert.
It was Klein!
He agilely avoided Archer, precisely throwing a stone into Archer's mouth and swiftly kicking, completely sealing Archer's tongue.
Who said he was timid? At critical moments, not at all!
Hobert whistled softly, feeling reassured with an experienced teammate by his side.
He tore a piece of cloth from his overcoat and used it to grab the black rib.
Though separated by a layer of cloth, Hobert still felt immense pressure. He exerted force and prised the black rib from Archer's body.
At that moment of separation, Hobert seemed suddenly transported to a golden grassland, vaguely seeing colossal figures swaying in the distance.
Surroundings turned pitch-black, seeming to harbor unspeakable dangers.
A lightning bolt struck, revealing towering giants around him, draped in massive black hoods, hands resting on giant swords before them.
As if sensing something, the giants turned their heads together, staring at Hobert.
Hobert felt deeply fascinated by the immense power of these giants, but his will ultimately overcame his obsession with power. He turned away, consciousness returning to the farmhouse on the outskirts of Tingen City.
Archer's flesh had already turned into black liquid, leaving only a white skeleton in the yard. The upper half of the skeleton had partially transformed into non-human bones.
Especially the head, resembling that of a bull, but with two golden deer horns.
Hobert tossed the rib outside the yard. The immense spiritual pressure disappeared, along with the sensation of constantly entering another world.
He breathed a sigh of relief. After Archer's loss of control and the arrival of "bullhead and deer horns," the rib would serve as a significant seal of negative effects.
Outside the courtyard wall, Dunn asked, "How do you feel?"
"A bit tired," Hobert said. "It's best to clamp the rib with a clip to avoid direct contact."
Seeing Hobert's normal state, Dunn turned to Frye. "Go check inside the farmhouse."
Hobert looked at his torn overcoat and asked Dunn, "Can this be reimbursed?"
Everyone turned to Klein.
Klein paused. Why did everyone look at him when reimbursement was mentioned?
Hobert sensed something amiss in the atmosphere and cleared his throat. "According to the cooperation model between me and the Nighthawks squad of Backlund, I have the right to share the spoils.
"And in discovering and fighting Archer, I made a significant contribution, so I have the priority to choose the spoils.
"Of course, if the rules in Tingen City are different, we can discuss it again."
The last sentence was purely to leave himself a way out, given the strength of the Nighthawks squad in Tingen City.
"Let's go with your agreement with Backlund," Dunn smiled. "But since you picked up the spoils, we won't reimburse you for the overcoat."
Hobert smiled. "No problem."
The main spoils of this battle were two things: the black rib and the two golden deer horns.
Previously, the bullhead and deer horns had already gained much power. Interrupted in the process, all the previous power concentrated entirely on the two golden deer horns.
The black rib might possess strange abilities, but it was now completely unusable, or the cost of using it was too great.
Although it could be shattered and sold for Beyonder characteristics, considering Dunn and the others were present, a normal Beyonder would not choose the rib.
So Hobert took off his own overcoat and wrapped up the skull and deer horns together.
At this moment, Frye came out of the farmhouse. "There are two broken bodies inside, along with some torn clothing."
Frye took out the clothing, and among them, they found a wallet and a letter. The wallet was messily filled with several bills, including one with a corner torn off by Hobert, a 5 soli note.
According to the contents of the letter, everyone learned that the "monster" who had just died was Mr. Z from the Aurora Order!
"This is a major victory in the fight against the Aurora Order!" Dunn exclaimed.
Hobert smiled. "To celebrate this victory, I invite everyone to a restaurant tonight. Would you all honor me with your presence?"
"If there's a big meal, count me in," Leonard said first.
Dunn smiled. "There's no reason to let guests pay. We'll use the squad's funds to treat everyone tonight.
"Ah, I'll report back to Backlund when I get home. I believe everyone who participated in today's battle will receive a bonus.
"But Mr. Hobert's bonus will be distributed in a way that you contact Backlund's Nighthawks squad after you return."
And so the evening meal was decided happily.
Next was to clean up the battlefield. Not needing so many people, Dunn sent Klein back to call the police to handle the two bodies in the farmhouse.
Hobert followed Klein back in the carriage. During the ride, Klein chatted casually with Hobert while seriously scrutinizing the young lawyer.
He felt that the lawyer seemed somewhat familiar, but couldn't recall where he had seen him.
As a "Seer," his judgment on intuition didn't make Klein think it was his imagination. Instead, it made him pay more attention to every move Hobert made.
Just before getting off the carriage, Hobert smiled at Klein and said, "Thanks to you for sealing its mouth in time. If you ever come to Backlund, remember to visit me at Aslan-Barton Law Firm. I'll host you well.
"And if you encounter any difficulties in Backlund, come find me. I have some connections there."
Klein smiled back. "You're brave, that's impressive. If you hadn't jumped into the yard first, I wouldn't have gone in."
Hobert replied with a double entendre, "I'm a 'Barbarian,' after all."
Klein was taken aback.
After saying this, Hobert naturally opened the door and got out of the carriage without it stopping.
Klein hurried to the carriage door and saw Hobert already standing on the street, waving at him.
He muttered, "Do Barbarians not care about how others see them?"

chapters.title: Chapter 142 - 142 Chameleon
chapters.content:
Hobert got off here because he saw the carriage Ulysses sent to him not far from the Church of the Evernight Goddess.
The coachman, seeing Hobert, said, "Sir, Sheriff Jared and Mr. Dominic hope you can come over."
Jared asked the coachman about Hobert's whereabouts, who professionally claimed ignorance, or Jared would have come over himself.
"Let's go back to the mansion first," Hobert sighed. "I haven't had lunch yet!"
The coachman nodded and took Hobert back to the mansion. While the kitchen prepared lunch, Hobert returned to his room, instructing the male servant outside to guard the door and allow no one in.
After locking the door, Hobert used his own sacrificial method to send the "Golden Stag Antlers" into the Nation of Disorder.
Although he still didn't know the use of the "Golden Stag Antlers," theoretically, these two antlers should be rare Beyonder materials. He decided to leave them in the Nation of Disorder for now and figure out how to cash them out after the heat died down.
Hobert then comfortably took a bath, changed clothes, and finally went to the dining room to enjoy his belated lunch.
While eating, Hobert reflected that he seemed to enjoy these days where everything was served to him on a platter.
Perhaps when playing the "Baron of Corruption," he could indulge himself appropriately.
However, there must be a limit. Otherwise, once the evil in human nature was unleashed, even he might not be able to control himself.
After finishing lunch, Hobert asked the coachman to take him to Mr. Dominic's company again.
Naturally, Dominic was very grateful to Hobert. By then, he had been negotiating the details of a security contract with Awwa Security, and Elizabeth had already been rescued.
Dominic then said, "Sheriff Jared has been waiting for you in the living room. Although the deaths of two thugs have caused some trouble, rest assured, I will hire the best lawyer to help clear your name."
"In addition, when you explain that you are a friend of Ulysses, even if Jared wants to arrest you, he'll have to treat you with respect."
Hobert smiled, "Mr. Dominic, I have no intention of reporting to jail because I have plans tonight."
Dominic was momentarily puzzled. "Because you have plans tonight, you don't intend to cooperate with the investigation?"
"Please take me to Sheriff Jared," Hobert said as he walked out, asking, "How is Elizabeth?"
"Thank goodness, she was just a little scared."
The two of them arrived at the living room while talking. Jared had already consumed two pots of coffee. However, he had to wait here because earlier in the morning, Hobert had caused two deaths and several injuries, making this a major case.
"I'm going to arrest you immediately, Hobert!" Jared shouted loudly as soon as he saw Hobert. "At noon, you killed two citizens of Tingen City!"
"Sheriff Jared, aren't those Tingen City citizens kidnappers?" Hobert put one hand in his pocket and questioned, "Are you protecting the rights of law-abiding citizens or the interests of kidnappers?"
Jared was suddenly stunned. Faced with Hobert's questioning, he actually didn't know how to respond.
"I stopped an ongoing crime!" Hobert said, "Those two dead kidnappers were planning to murder me at the time. This also constitutes an ongoing crime. My actions were in self-defense and not excessive."
"But lives were lost," Jared's momentum immediately weakened.
"Sheriff, I understand criminal law better than you. Cooperating with your investigation is my duty, but you currently have no right to arrest or interrogate me." This was actually another loophole in the law.
Hobert remembered that in similar cases in the era of AD, he would have been locked up awaiting investigation results. However, the Criminal Law of Loen Kingdom did not clearly stipulate whether persons involved in legitimate self-defense should be temporarily detained.
Dominic intervened to smooth things over and revealed Hobert's background as Ulysses' friend. Jared could only take Hobert's statement here.
After recording the statement, Jared wanted an address where he could find Hobert at any time, and the atmosphere gradually became more cordial. When Jared left, he bid farewell to Hobert and Dominic like old friends.
This reminded Hobert of a "Chameleon."
After seeing off Jared, Dominic sneered, "When my daughter was kidnapped, you didn't take it seriously, but now you're coming to question us for a few dead kidnappers."
Meanwhile, Hobert lamented that in this kingdom of unequal personalities, such dramas might unfold every day.
If he were an ordinary person without legal knowledge, he would have been taken away by Jared. Who knew what would happen during the interrogation? Perhaps he would be heavily extorted for bail money if he said the wrong thing.
Dominic invited Hobert to dinner at his home to express their family's gratitude, but Hobert had plans both tonight and tomorrow night, so he postponed the invitation.
Around half past five in the evening, Hobert arrived at the dining room for the gathering. In addition to those who participated in today's operation, three other team members also attended, but none of the administrative staff were present.
Leonard smiled, "Old Neil probably didn't expect his leave today would make him miss such a feast?"
"Leave?" Hobert instinctively felt something was wrong. He didn't know if Klein had reminded Dunn that Neil was conducting a ritual involving an evil god. If they didn't completely disrupt Neil's ritual, he could still potentially lose control.
Klein seemed to want to remind the captain of something crucial but couldn't remember exactly what it was.
Just as he was about to use the spiritual insights of a "Seer" to help him remember, Captain Dunn suddenly brought up the topic of the mental hospital. Because this action was scheduled for tonight, he listened particularly carefully, setting aside his previous thoughts.
Meanwhile, Leonard explained to Hobert, "Old Neil is also a member of our small team, but he's been feeling a bit unwell these days."
Hobert nodded and began to discuss other topics.
When everyone learned that Daly, who had once been a Nighthawk team member in Tingen City, was Hobert's superior, they became closer to Hobert again.
Halfway through dinner, Hobert noticed that Klein first froze, then went to the restroom.
He couldn't help but chuckle, "Lord of the Bathrooms," that's how it goes!
As Hobert chatted with the more opportunistic Leonard, his mind wandered as he pondered who might be looking for Klein.
After some recollection, he remembered that tonight seemed to be the death anniversary of the Great Pirate Qilangos.

chapters.title: Chapter 143 - 143 The Death of Qilangos
chapters.content:
"I met someone who appeared to be Qilangos at Duke Negan's ball. He disguised himself as Baron Gramir, his intentions unclear..."
Miss Justice's prayer, Klein sat on the ancient high-backed chair, speculating about Qilangos' intentions based on the information Miss Justice provided. He responded to Miss Justice first, "Understood."
Then, he materialized the images and voices Miss Justice had just prayed for, projecting them onto the deep red star symbolizing "The Hanged Man."
"Tonight will surely be an extraordinary night for Backlund!" Klein sighed, pondering what changes his recent actions might bring.
But soon, Klein stopped speculating. He returned to the washroom and wrote a letter to Mr. Azik with his portable pen, informing him of Qilangos' appearance at the ball and summoning a large bone messenger with a brass whistle to deliver the message.
After completing all this, Klein suddenly remembered he had only eaten half of his steak and wondered if his visit to the washroom would affect his appetite.
...
Backlund, Holy Wind Cathedral.
Upon receiving Audrey's message, Alger was initially pleasantly surprised, unconsciously pressing his chest with his hand, praising Mr. Fool.
Then Alger's pupils contracted slightly as he once again felt the power of "The Fool"!
This is the Holy Wind Cathedral! Once the headquarters of the Church, and still one of its sanctuaries today. Yet, Mr. Fool silently "descended," responding nonetheless.
Silent for more than ten seconds, Alger finally regained control of his emotions. He turned and left to report this critical information upwards.
...
Audrey, upon discovering traces that might be Qilangos and informing Mr. Fool through prayer, did not passively wait. Instead, she delicately informed her father, Viscount Hall, of this matter.
Thus, Qilangos' assassination attempt predictably failed. Instead of entangling further, he chose to flee immediately, swiftly evading pursuit with the abilities of the Wind-Blessed.
At this moment, Qilangos had time to speculate on where things went wrong and why Duke Negan had been on guard.
Suddenly, he remembered the large tree he encountered a few days ago in East Backlund and the three people hiding behind it.
It must be them! Qilangos realized that the man recognized him then, but intentionally pretended to mistake him, causing Qilangos to relax his vigilance! He refrained from risking killing witnesses.
It was because of these three individuals that cautious Qilangos advanced his assassination plan.
He decided to find these three. An evil smile crept onto Qilangos' lips; they could not always be protected by Duke Negan or official Beyonders.
Once they lost protection, he would surely retaliate against their betrayal in the cruelest manner!
Just then, Qilangos' vision suddenly blurred, and he saw various colors in the darkness intensify. In the high sky obscured by the Crimson Moon, countless indescribable forms appeared, radiating mysterious knowledge.
Oh no, Qilangos realized he had fallen into another ambush, and the strength of these ambushers was undoubtedly high.
Before he could react, he saw one after another giant skeleton with sockets burning with pitch-black flames appear before him, more than a hundred in total!
And below, the dark water surface rose higher and higher, pale and unreal hands emerging, constantly waving upwards, grasping at Qilangos' ankles.
Qilangos hadn't found any escape route yet when he was caught in the dark water. He struggled desperately, but despaired as he saw those huge skeletons approaching him.
In almost an instant, Qilangos realized his vitality was rapidly disappearing.
...
The first batch of Alger, who arrived at the scene, was stunned by the sight before him. Qilangos had already lost all vitality by the time they got closer.
When they approached, Qilangos' face rapidly decayed, oozing yellow-green pus, chunks of flesh falling off one after another.
With a crackling sound, Qilangos completely fell apart, leaving only a pile of gleaming white bones.
Qilangos, one of the seven Admirals, died mysteriously before Alger's eyes.
At this moment, the Spellsinger of God, Ace Snake, asked with his magnetic voice, "Did you tell anyone else this information?"
Alger regained his composure immediately. "I just received the intelligence and reported it to Your Excellency, the Archbishop."
Ace turned away, continuing his search for clues.
However, Alger suddenly shuddered, realizing a possibility: The assailant was likely a follower of Mr. Fool!
Only members and affiliates of the Tarot Club could have known the intelligence so quickly! And Mr. Fool's followers happened to be in Backlund, so they "coincidentally" lent a helping hand!
...
Inside Duke Negan's mansion, Audrey, upon learning that Qilangos had been killed by a clandestine organization, immediately guessed that Mr. Fool's followers had dealt with this Vice Admiral.
Next, Audrey had another surprise awaiting her: she received Qilangos' bounty and a gift from Duke Negan as a token of gratitude, totaling about forty thousand pounds.
Unfortunately, this money couldn't be used directly. Otherwise, Audrey would prepare to trade the twenty thousand pounds' worth of information with Emperor Mr. at the next Tarot Club meeting.
...
Around nine in the evening, after finishing dinner, Hobert and others bid farewell to each other. At the banquet, Hobert and Leonard grew more intimate in conversation and exchanged contact addresses upon parting.
By the time they returned to the villa, it was past ten at night. Despite being mentally and physically tired from dinner, Hobert found himself somewhat sleepless. It was a strange phenomenon; sometimes, the more tired he was, the harder it was to fall asleep.
Since he couldn't sleep, Hobert began his usual introspection.
Firstly, in today's battle, he felt the effectiveness of the "Hypnosis" Beyonder ability, thanks to Dunn and Leonard. The fight at noon in the farm ended rather uneventfully because of them.
Of course, Dunn and Leonard had a fierce struggle in their use of Beyonder abilities against Archer, though much of it was invisible, making it appear less intense.
Hobert's "Psychological Spoon" ability, which he possessed, had a form of "hypnosis", but it was a mystical item, not a sealed artifact..
Although mystical items and sealed artifacts were similar, their methods of use differed.
The negative effects of mystical items were minimal, generally not very active, requiring spiritual infusion to unleash their abilities.
Sealed artifacts, on the other hand, were more active; even without spirituality, they exerted influence on any creature near them at any time.
Through the use of the "Spirit Necklace" and "Psychological Spoon," Hobert had summarized some experience in using mystical items: the power of mystical items was closely related to the holder's sequence and the level of the mystical item itself.
For example, Hobert, a Sequence 8, could unleash almost all the power of the "Spirit Necklace." When he was Sequence 9 before, he struggled with the use of the "Spirit Necklace" for spiritual communication.
Certainly, the higher the sequence, the more powerful the mystical items's ability. The upper limit of mystical items was determined by their own level. For example, the "Spirit Necklace" could only reach Sequence 7 at most, and the "Psychological Spoon" could only reach Sequence 6 at most.
However, Hobert currently could not fully unleash the power of the "Psychological Spoon." He believed that after becoming Sequence 7, he could fully control enemies to a certain extent with the "Hypnosis" of the "Psychological Spoon"! Rather than the current situation where he could not fully unleash the true power of "Frenzy" and "Hypnosis."
This increased Hobert's enthusiasm for advancing to Sequence 7.

chapters.title: Chapter 144 - 144: Proactive Contact
chapters.content:
Hobert allowed his thoughts to wander as he began to reflect on his earlier battle with Qilangos.
He suddenly realized that, despite possessing sealed artifacts and three mystical items, he lacked one crucial thing—a mystical item that could help him escape!
Hobert mused that if he had a sealed artifact or mystical item with the ability to "travel," he could have happily grabbed Xio and Fors, and they would have "traveled" away together. Who would stay and fight Qilangos in a life-or-death struggle?
However, possessing a mystical item with "traveling" capabilities was equivalent to Sequence 5.
The key issue was that Sequence 5 of the "Apprentice" Pathway was notoriously hard to kill, and acquiring such an item would likely cost more than ten thousand pounds, far beyond his reach.
Hobert sighed. Just recently, he thought he was no longer short of money, but now he realized that the nine hundred pounds he had, which might be considered wealthy for an ordinary person, was far from enough for a Beyonder.
As a result, Hobert felt a renewed drive to earn money. He planned to frequently check the bulletin board at the mercenary club for suitable commissions once he returned to Backlund.
As these thoughts swirled, sleepiness gradually overtook him, and Hobert finally fell asleep, although his battle with Archer had left his mind strained, causing him to dream all night.
---
In the Southern Continent, in the Nonexistent Town.
The morning sunlight pierced through the mist, casting a warm glow in the council chamber halfway up the mountain.
The chieftain and several family elders sat as still as wooden statues in their seats.
The demigod elder Chester broke the silence. "So, you're saying that this mysterious being possesses at least the power of an angel?"
Calvin responded, "It seems so. The mysterious being interrupted the descending power of the enemy's angel."
Elder Bowen speculated, "Could it be that Elliot found some kind of loophole...?"
As he spoke, he realized it was unlikely. Even if a loophole were found during the enemy's descent, without a sufficiently high level of existence, it would still be impossible to force back the angelic power.
"No." Calvin corrected. "The mysterious being appeared before me and punished me.
"Elliot said: 'Do not test God!'"
The council chamber fell into silence once again. If they had an angel or even a god-level figure backing them, they wouldn't need to keep hiding in the Nonexistent Town.
Years ago, due to insufficient intelligence, the family had provoked the "Rose School of Thought," only to later learn that the organization was backed by an angel-level figure.
But at the same time, such power could also represent an existential disaster. Even if they combined all the family's strength, they might not be able to stand against this mysterious being.
Several seconds later, Calvin spoke again. "The mysterious being didn't allow me to completely lose control, and he enabled Elliot to complete the spirit channeling process. This clearly shows a response to our probing, and the gesture was filled with goodwill."
"Regardless of our choice, the mysterious being has already taken notice of us," the chieftain croaked. "In that case, why not attempt to contact this mysterious being?"
There was another silence, but this one was different from the earlier tension, as everyone tacitly agreed with the chieftain's suggestion.
"How should we contact the mysterious being?" Bowen asked.
Calvin, having prepared for this, replied, "For example, we could offer Elliot a seat among the elders."
---
Hobert yawned and got up to wash. Despite dreaming all night, his spirituality and energy had been well-restored.
While enjoying breakfast, he glanced at the morning paper, where the front-page headline reported Qilangos's death.
So, last night was indeed the day Qilangos met his end, and Audrey had quite a haul.
Hobert skimmed the rest of the newspaper but found nothing particularly noteworthy, so he focused on his meal.
After breakfast, Hobert went once again to Dominic's company.
Dominic greeted him with a broad smile. "Lawyer Hobert, I was just about to send for you."
It turned out that one of the kidnappers Hobert had injured yesterday had inadvertently let slip during interrogation that there was a mastermind behind the abduction. The police followed this lead and found out the mastermind was none other than Mr. Claude.
This morning, Claude had already been arrested and jailed. Dominic had just received the news that Claude confessed to orchestrating the kidnapping.
As a result, Dominic and Claude's lawsuit was no longer necessary, as the prosecution would take over the case against Claude.
Naturally, Hobert's services were no longer needed.
However, Dominic was generous, paying Hobert a legal fee of 150 pounds and even adding a 30-pound tip to express his gratitude for saving Elizabeth.
Hobert hadn't expected the case to resolve itself so neatly.
Dominic smiled. "I'll also be attending the welcome banquet Mr. Ulysses is hosting for you tonight. Elizabeth will be there too—she's been saying she wants to thank you in person."
"You're too kind," Hobert smiled back. "It's my honor that you'll be attending the banquet tonight."
---
That morning, the Blackthorn Security Company received a new commission: to follow Lady Sharon and uncover evidence of her crimes.
Captain Dunn handed the case over to Klein. Under Leonard's guidance, Klein went to the Hound Bar and found a gang leader, paying five pounds to have his men take turns tailing Lady Sharon and documenting her daily activities.
Fortunately, this expense could be reimbursed.
As Klein left the Hound Bar, reflecting on the situation, he suddenly remembered that Old Neil's house wasn't far from there, and Old Neil had been off sick for two days. Today, he was supposed to visit the doctor.
Klein checked his pocket watch—it was nearly eleven. He wondered if Old Neil had returned from the hospital.
Since he was already nearby, Klein decided to visit Old Neil.
After a twenty-minute walk, he arrived outside Old Neil's house. Klein's spirituality immediately sensed something was off. The sun was high in the sky, yet Old Neil's curtains and door drapes were still drawn.
Could Old Neil's condition have worsened?
Klein hurried to the door and knocked. There was no response.
But inside, it sounded like someone was whispering.
"Old Neil!" Klein called out, but still received no answer, though the whispering continued.
Could Old Neil's condition have deteriorated so badly that he couldn't even get up to answer the door?
Klein took out a piece of paper he carried, flicked his wrist, and the paper instantly became as hard as steel. Using the "steel paper," he slid it through the door to unlatch the lock.
As he pushed the door open, he immediately saw Old Neil pacing in the dark.
Klein didn't approach right away because he noticed that Old Neil seemed to be circling around a small altar.
Thud—
The door suddenly shut on its own, and the candles on the altar next to Old Neil flared up like torches.
In the bright flames, Klein saw Old Neil clearly. Two eyes devoid of any emotion had appeared on his cheeks.
Klein instantly realized that Old Neil was once again on the verge of losing control, and this time, it was far more severe than before.

chapters.title: Chapter 145 - 145: Neil's Uncontrolled Outburst Again
chapters.content:
Apart from those two emotionless eyes, Neil's face was lined with wrinkles, his hair sparse, as if he had aged ten years in an instant. His nails were long, seemingly untrimmed for years, making him look like a zombie clawing out of a grave.
Neil didn't even notice Klein entering. He continued to pace around the altar, muttering words that sounded like some obscure and incomprehensible incantation.
On the altar sat a large basin of blood. In the center was a symbol Klein had never seen before, an eye surrounded by various intricate symbols and polygonal shapes.
Under Neil's chanting, the eye in the center of the altar seemed to come alive, coldly staring at Klein, the intruder.
Klein, no stranger to Beyonder events, forced himself to remain calm. Neil seemed on the verge of complete loss of control. It was crucial not to provoke him further. Calling for the captain's help now would be too late.
The ritual to invoke the power of the Evernight Goddess must commence immediately. This was Neil's last chance.
So Klein approached Neil cautiously, trying not to draw attention. Seeing Neil still absorbed in his chanting, Klein began to arrange the altar.
Everything went smoothly until the altar was prepared. As Klein was about to invoke the Goddess's power, the eyes on Neil's cheeks suddenly moved, seemingly noticing the newly completed altar.
"Little Klein, please don't disturb me," Neil suddenly looked at Klein with a hoarse voice. "I'm about to succeed, I'm going to succeed very soon."
Klein took a deep breath. "Neil, don't be afraid. It won't hurt, it'll be over soon."
"No," Neil's emotions rose, "my research has never harmed anyone else! You haven't lost a loved one, you don't know the pain!"
His tone softened again. "Please, I'm about to succeed, don't stop me."
Klein hesitated, but forced himself to remain resolute. "Neil, don't you know what you're doing?"
"You're hurting yourself, and you'll hurt others."
"Please, Neil, don't resist. This is your last chance."
Neil became agitated again. "You don't understand! You don't know how profound this knowledge is, I stumbled upon it unintentionally, from... from the Hidden Sage!"
Neil's expression turned surprised. "No! That's not it!"
Another eye slowly opened on his forehead.
Klein knew it was now or never. "I pray for the power of the Evernight; I pray..."
Neil lunged forward, intent on destroying Klein's prepared altar.
Klein raised his wand defensively. "I pray for the power of Crimson..."
Neil's strength was overwhelming; he swept his hand, breaking Klein's cane.
If Klein hadn't agilely dodged, Neil's nails would have scratched him.
Neil kicked and destroyed Klein's altar, his last trace of sanity halting his attack. "Leave me alone. Go quickly."
He now realized he had prayed to an Evil God, and something was terribly wrong.
But after saying this, Neil lost his final shred of reason. His skin turned as red as blood, and he roared at Klein like a wild beast.
Klein hurried to the door, but found it wouldn't open.
Neil, now resembling a bloodied figure, charged at him. Klein, using the abilities of the Clown, deftly avoided Neil's attacks.
What to do?
Should he really shoot at Neil?
Klein felt his hand go weak at the thought of reaching for the gun.
No, there's another way! But it's risky!
Glancing at Neil, his tutor in mysticism, Klein knew he had to take this risk now or regret it forever.
After a brief hesitation, Klein recited, "Creator in the Shadows of Order..."
"You are the beginning and end of all order;
You are the lord who governs the clock of order.
I pray for your gaze and favor;"
...
After praying three times and seeing no response, Klein muttered, "Roselle! You great deceiver!"
No, he had to make a final decision. If he continued like this, he would die here!
Just as Klein forced himself to make up his mind, a throne made of swords appeared in midair, with a towering and mysterious figure seated on it.
Then, a surge of power descended. Neil was enveloped by this force, standing still. The abnormalities on his body quickly disappeared, the extra eyes on his face almost simultaneously closed and immediately disappeared.
This power seemed to represent supreme order!
Klein realized something, but restoring Neil's physical order was not enough. His mind was also disturbed.
Just as he thought this, Klein felt another surge of power.
This power made his mind tremble involuntarily, as if a colossal creature stood before him.
It was a Beyonder power of the mind!
Klein breathed a sigh of relief. This "Creator" seemed to offer "full service," even helping to resolve the mental issues of the uncontrollable.
Neil returned to his original state, but he looked much older than a few days ago.
After all this turmoil, he couldn't hold on and collapsed to the ground.
Thunk~
Klein was about to step forward to help when he heard a sound from the altar. Turning his head, he saw that a black eye had appeared in the center of Neil's altar.
It was alive, "jumping" into the basin of blood, though its first attempt failed.

chapters.title: Chapter 146 - 146: Knowledge Itself
chapters.content:
In "Nation of Disorder," Hobert first used the "Power of Order" to restore the order of Old Neil's body. Then, using the power of the "Psychological Spoon," he concealed a portion of the infected spirit body and used "Hypnosis" to make Old Neil forget his ritual and the determination to revive his lover.
As Hobert sighed with relief in "Nation of Disorder," marveling at the success of this "treatment," he suddenly shuddered, as if suddenly being stared at by eyes from an unknown source.
Hobert felt that the gaze could penetrate the "True Sight" and see himself on the Iron Throne in "Nation of Disorder."
Shifting the perspective of the "True Sight," he saw that the symbol representing an eye in the center of the altar suddenly came to life, turning into a real eye.
It was entirely black, with a deep black pupil, making it look like a moving dark paper cutout.
It bounced around, trying to leap into the vat of blood on the altar.
Hobert probably understood what was happening. Old Neil's ritual had indeed attracted some advanced scrutiny, but the entities observing here couldn't project too much power here before Old Neil's ritual was complete.
So the eye hoped to leap into the blood-filled vat to strengthen itself.
Realizing he couldn't let this happen, Hobert realized that if the eye's power grew any stronger, its presence behind it might really see the situation in "Nation of Disorder" through the "True Sight."
So Hobert said to Klein with supreme authority, "Sacrifice it to me."
At the same time, he threw the symbol representing the "Creator" into Klein's stars.
...
Meanwhile, in Klein's room in the suburbs of Tingen City, he felt deeply what it meant to "invite a god easily and send a god difficult." The "Creator" indeed, as Roselle said, cured Neil's loss of control, but it seemed unwilling to leave.
What to do?
Finally, the other party said that the eye that was bouncing around was best, which gave the "Creator" a sacrifice and solved the strange eye.
Klein quickly drew the symbol of the "Creator" near the strange eye, arranged the altar, and then used the knowledge about sacrifice just obtained from "Little Sun" to make the sacrifice.
He saw two huge bronze gates open a crack, and a surging force emerged, followed by a huge suction force that seemed to suck everything in the room into the bronze gates.
When the huge suction force disappeared, the bronze gate disappeared, and the eye bouncing around on the altar disappeared without a trace, and the "Creator" in the air also disappeared.
Klein sighed with relief, thankfully this mysterious existence really had no malice and did not demand unaffordable sacrifices.
As he thought, he tidied up the altar, then went to pull open the curtains, and the dazzling sunlight shone into the room, leaving nothing dark to hide.
...
In a rented house in the suburbs of Tingen City, Ince Zangwill crossed out a passage in his notebook and then wrote quickly: "Klein Moretti was almost killed by the uncontrollable Old Neil. Why didn't he pull out his gun and shoot after the psychological struggle?
"If he shot, Old Neil would become a sacrifice for this ritual. Klein Moretti would immediately lose control due to the hidden gaze of a secret existence and become a pile of flesh and bones.
"But he didn't do that. Not only that, he let Old Neil, who was on the verge of losing control, return to normal. It's incredible, once again making Ince Zangwill feel surprised, even the quill in his hand didn't understand what happened?
"Anyway, Ince Zangwill's plan to kill Klein Moretti failed again, and he was fooled by a Sequence 8 once again, which made him very annoyed..."
Ince Zangwill picked up the pen, a hint of anger flashing in his eyes, not because of Klein, but because he was just mocked by a pen, and that pen was still in his hand.
...
In "Nation of Disorder," Hobert examined the eye in his hand.
It still had the characteristics of being alive, but it looked around as if it had lost its target and didn't know what to do next.
This indicates that "Nation of Disorder" has severed its connection with its original body.
Hobert tried to grasp the eye, and his gaze suddenly extended to an unknown land.
That land seemed to be an endless wilderness, with a tall tower in the calamity, and a fiery eyeball on the top of the tower was staring at this land.
Suddenly, the eyeball seemed to sense Hobert's gaze, and it looked back at Hobert.
Hobert's perspective immediately returned to "Nation of Disorder," and at that moment, he felt that his brain had gained a lot of knowledge.
Snap~
His head seemed to explode like a smashed tomato, and the half-built hall trembled. The pool in front of the "Iron Throne" bubbled like it was boiling.
After about four or five seconds, Hobert's head grew back, and the hall and pool returned to normal.
Hobert smiled bitterly, realizing he had almost died unexpectedly.
Immediately after that, he found a large amount of chaotic knowledge in his mind, and he didn't even understand the meaning of most of it.
But it seems that these things are "knowledge itself," which seems to understand the mysterious world and must be seen to understand.
For example, when he saw the Spirit World, the "knowledge itself" about the Spirit World would emerge, and Hobert would immediately understand the composition of the Spirit World and the principles behind the rules of walking in the Spirit World, and so on.
No wonder the extraordinary people who approach the "Mystery Pryer" are so afraid of being chased into their minds by the "Hidden Sage" to inject knowledge. Is this knowledge useful? Very useful, but generally unnecessary and difficult to understand, and it takes up too much "memory."
If he had grabbed this eye in the real world, Hobert would have already lost control and become a monster.
Hobert manifested a stone box and put the eye that looked around into the box, covering it with the "Power of Order."
Then Hobert began to sort out understandable knowledge: Sequence 9 "Mystery Pryer" potion formula:
"Main Ingredients: A pair of eyeballs from the Nasla Ancient Mountain Giant Ape, 70 grams of Star Crystal.
Auxiliary Ingredients: 80 ml of pure water, 8 drops of Octagonal Gold Tray Flower juice, 7 grams of White Orchid powder, 9 grams of Dragon's Blood Herb."
...
Sequence 9 "Savant" potion formula:
"Main Ingredients: Head of the Brown-backed Firefly, a complete five-colored leaf grass.
Auxiliary Ingredients: ..."
...
Sequence 8 "Melee Scholar" potion formula:
"Main Ingredients: A complete combat beetle, a dried Hanging Orchid flower.
Auxiliary Ingredients: ..."
...
Sequence 7 "Warlock" potion formula:
"Main Ingredients: Complete brain of Pale Giraffe, two fruits of Flying Puff Tree.
Auxiliary Ingredients: ..."
