chapters.title: Chapter 151 - 151 Facing Daly's Interrogation (Bonus 3)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Hobert arrived at the Nation of Disorder and cautiously wrapped Dunn Smith's spirit with the power of order. Then, using the status of the "Nation of Disorder," he accelerated the extraction of Beyonder characteristics.
Finally, he wrapped this characteristic, which had been highly compatible with Dunn's spirit due to being his, together with Dunn's spirit, ensuring that the characteristic could sustain Dunn's spirit for a long time.
After completing all this, under the envelopment of orderly power and nurtured by the characteristics, Dunn's spirit stopped dissipating.
To prevent Dunn's spirit from turning towards malevolence, Hobert took his spirit along with the characteristics and the "Umbilical Cord" to the Nation of Disorder.
Behind the Iron Throne, Hobert manifested a stone coffin and laid Dunn's spirit inside.
At this moment, Dunn's eyes were blank, his consciousness still in a chaotic state.
Hobert could have awakened him with the "Spirit Necklace," but there was no point in doing so now.
Hobert said to Dunn, "I've heard that the 'Classical Alchemists' have a way to craft a normal body. Lie here and wait. Once your body is ready, I'll let you out."
With a wave of his hand, he covered the lid of the coffin, sealing it with another layer of "Order Power" outside to prevent Dunn from becoming an evil spirit.
Next, Hobert manifested a small stone box and placed the "Umbilical Cord" inside, next to the box containing the "Black Eyes."
Feeling his own spirituality depleted, Hobert quickly returned to the real world. He first pulled out a few strands of Dunn's hair, then took out a glass vial from his pocket containing mystical herbs and poured out half a vial of Dunn's now viscous blood.
He then changed the symbol of the "Creator" on the altar to one representing the "Evernight Goddess ."
Just as he finished changing it, waves of exhaustion swept over him. Hobert felt himself about to faint.
Suddenly, he remembered: Oh no, I forgot about the old man inside Leonard!
He called out towards Leonard, "The great 'Creator' says: If you expose the existence of the 'Creator,' He will definitely send you a monocle."
[T/N: every good fanfic needs to threaten Pallez with monocles]
As he spoke, Hobert tried to lean against the wall, but his strength was insufficient to support him crawling over, so he collapsed on the ground and passed out.
Half a minute later, Leonard, pale-faced, woke up. He looked at the reception hall, now resembling ruins, and stared blankly for a second or two.
Then he saw Dunn, with a gentle smile, and Klein, looking incredulous.
Leonard crawled over to check Dunn's and Klein's breath and pulse, muttering, "No..." a word squeezed out of his throat.
He continued to verify, going back and forth between the two, but ultimately had to accept the unchangeable outcome.
Leonard's legs gave way, and he knelt on the spot. His emerald eyes were full of pain, and tears streamed down his face, washing away the blood and dust.
Suddenly, he seemed to grasp at a lifeline: "Old man! Old man! You must have a way, right? You can definitely bring them back to life, right?"
"I'm not a god. Do you think I have the power to resurrect?" A voice that only Leonard could hear said, "Don't bother. Hobert has tried every possible method."
"He said, 'Klein is already dead!'"
Leonard's shoulders slumped, the last hope shattered.
At that moment, the sound of rapid footsteps running upstairs came from outside, the reinforcements from the "Mandated Punishers" and members of the "Machinery Hivemind" rushing to support.
...
When Hobert woke up, he was lying on a cold stone platform. The fiery pain in his back had disappeared, and his spirit and strength had recovered somewhat.
"Old Neil just performed a healing ritual for you." Leonard, sitting on a nearby chair with a pale face, said, "He's also quite old. The deaths of two teammates in a row have aged him a lot."
Hobert sighed with relief, meaning that no one died in this incident, Old Neil didn't die, Klein would come back to life, and as for Dunn, Hobert was also confident that he could bring him back to life.
Hobert had barely achieved the goal he set for himself before.
Next, Hobert sensed that the potion of the "Barbarian" had been digested by most of it. His appearance completely contradicted the script written by "0-08."
The "True Creator" did not wait, but chose to be born with a small part of his power, creating the "Descendant," and Dunn did not die completely in the true sense. The "True Creator" "paid" the reward to Ince Zangweil, picked up by Hobert.
Finally, "0-08" was forced to "invite" a "Frenzied Mage" to create an escape opportunity for Ince.
Because he had been challenging the script written by "0-08" all along, constantly refreshing "0-08's" understanding of Hobert, the potion of the "Barbarian" was well digested.
Hobert asked, "Did you catch Ince?"
Leonard shook his head expressionlessly, "0-08 created too many obstacles for the Archbishop. In the end, Ince escaped with excellent luck."
Hobert nodded. If Ince had been caught, the desire for revenge and the desire to improve his strength would not be so strong for either Klein or Leonard.
He asked, "Has Miss Daly arrived?"
"She should have arrived."
Hobert sighed, "How should I explain to her?"
Leonard was puzzled, not understanding what he meant. At this moment, the stone door of the dim room was opened.
It was Daly. Her eyes were filled with pain. After seeing Hobert, there was some anger left: "Hobert! Didn't you say you could save Dunn?"
She quickly walked over, grabbed Hobert's collar: "I followed your advice and immediately gave the Archbishop a telegram. Why? Why did he die?"
Of course, now is not the time to explain that there is still hope for Dunn to come back to life. Otherwise, the Church of the Evernight Goddess will definitely investigate, which will be a big trouble.
Hobert squeezed out a faint smile, "I'm sorry, Madam. I couldn't save him."
"Madam," Leonard probably understood what was going on. "Hobert did his best. He fainted beside the captain."
As he spoke, he choked up too.
Daly's hand clutching Hobert's collar trembled violently. Finally, she leaned on Hobert's shoulder and sobbed. She didn't cry aloud, just sobbed, but it tore her heart apart.
Hobert patted Daly's back, "He protected Tingen City."
Daly wiped away tears, seeing the blood on Hobert's clothes still not dry, "Sorry, I shouldn't blame you, but, but..."
But her heart was bleeding now, unable to control her emotions.

chapters.title: Chapter 152 - 152 Return to Backlund (Bonus 4)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Daly's emotions gradually calmed down. Hobert could sense that Daly's sorrow was slowly transforming into hatred.
She sat quietly in her chair for a moment, then calmly said to Hobert without expression, "Captain Thomas will see you alone later. Tell him the source of the information was Zachary."
Hobert nodded, "Alright."
Daly slowly got up and walked away step by step. Her departing figure looked desolate and weak.
Watching Daly leave, Leonard looked at Hobert.
Hobert said, "I'm sorry, this involves confidentiality agreements. I can't explain too clearly to you."
It wasn't that he couldn't explain, but rather that he couldn't make it clear at all. For instance, the "0-08" and the information about Ince in Tingen City, Hobert could only fabricate something, but this was the Beyonder world, where lies could easily be exposed.
Saying more might lead to more mistakes than silence.
Leonard realized that Hobert might have known something in advance, but since it involved a confidentiality agreement, he didn't press further.
Hobert changed the subject, "What are your plans for the future?"
"I'm going to take the Red Gloves assessment. No matter where Ince Zangwill escapes to, I'll find him!" There was a glint of hatred in Leonard's eyes too.
Hobert nodded, "If you have any news, let's exchange letters."
"Sure," Leonard grunted.
At that moment, the Scarred Nighthawk Borgia appeared at the door of the stone room, "Hobert, Captain Thomas wants to see you."
Hobert descended from the stone platform and followed Borges to the first floor.
Walking ahead, Borges suddenly said, "We've roughly reconstructed the course of the battle. You both did well!"
Hobert simply replied, "It's what we should do."
The reception hall was indeed severely damaged, but the other rooms were mostly intact.
In the lounge, Hobert saw Thomas standing in front of the window. Borges called out, "Captain."
Thomas turned around, "I want to talk to Hobert alone."
Borges left the room and closed the door.
"Are you feeling better?" Thomas asked.
"Much better, but it may take a few more days to fully recover," Hobert replied.
Thomas nodded, "I heard from Daly that you seemed to have received the news of the arrival of the Evil God in advance?"
"Sort of." After Daly's reminder just now, Hobert had already thought about how to say it in advance, "But at that time, Zachary had already been contaminated, and I saw 'True Creator' from him."
"In such a situation, of course, I had to end the spirit channeling immediately."
Hobert spoke every word truthfully, but guided the conversation to: during the spiritual communication process, he obtained information about Tingen City from Zachary. However, due to the appearance of the 'True Creator,' the information he obtained was fragmented and limited, so it did not attract much attention.
Thomas did not delve deeper into this issue, but asked again, "According to Leonard, did the Evil God ultimately choose to be born as his offspring?"
"Yes."
"How did you kill the Evil God's offspring?"
Hobert was prepared, "Captain Dunn used 'Saint Selena's Ashes' to trap the Evil God's offspring, and Klein used an advanced charm."
This was also true, but they only dealt with Megose, not the Evil God's offspring.
Thomas frowned, "Where did Klein get the advanced spell?"
"I don't know."
Thomas nodded, "Alright, go back and rest well. Oh, by the way, Lord Anthony specifically instructed that from today onwards, you are officially a member of the Backlund Nighthawks team."
"And your actions are still completely free. If the team needs your abilities for any mission, they will find you for help."
"Related documents will be exchanged for you after returning to Backlund."
He smiled, "His Excellency the Archbishop said that your calmness under the mental pressure of a Sequence 3 impressed him."
Hobert then understood why Thomas's inquiries were so succinct; it turned out that the Archbishop had endorsed him long ago, and Thomas was just going through the motions.
"Please thank His Excellency the Archbishop for his guidance," Hobert politely replied.
Leaving Blackthorn Security Company, it was already afternoon. Seeing the sun about to set, Hobert remembered the fierce battle at noon, feeling as if he had crossed into another world.
Strolling aimlessly on the street, Hobert thought of the 'Frenzied Mage' who took away the 'Tree of Order.'
In theory, the 'Tree of Order' could still be used for another two or three minutes. He wondered what the other party would do with it? Would they use it as a clue to find the 'Nation of Disorder'?
This was a considerable hidden danger.
He didn't care much about 0-08 and Ince Zangwill, as he knew their fate.
But the 'Frenzied Mage' was an unexpected participant. If left unchecked, it could be a potential danger. He needed to carefully investigate whether the other party was a friend or foe.
Lost in thought, Hobert saw the coachman who had come to pick him up. The coachman looked surprised and asked, "Sir, are you..."
Hobert then realized that everyone around was looking at him, after all, he was covered in so much blood, "It's okay, it's all over."
His mind had been greatly stimulated today, and he still felt a bit dazed.
He fell asleep in his coat without changing or taking a bath. When he woke up the next morning, it was already dawn.
After breakfast, Hobert asked the butler to convey his thanks to Ulysses and explain that he was preparing to return to Backlund early tomorrow morning.
Hobert spent the whole day resting. He didn't go back to Blackthorn Security Company, but informed Leonard by letter that he would leave Tingen City tomorrow morning.
On Monday morning, Hobert packed his bags and arrived at the door, where he saw Ulysses' carriage parked outside.
Hobert smiled somewhat embarrassedly, "Mr. Ulysses, you didn't have to come and see me off."
"No," Ulysses said, "I have something here that needs you to deliver to Sir Christian."
Hobert was stunned, speculating whether the contents of Sir Christian's handwritten letter were borrowed from Ulysses like this?
Getting into the carriage, Ulysses handed Hobert a box about the length of his forearm, instructing him to personally deliver it to Christian.
Ulysses took Hobert to the station, and after bidding farewell to each other, Hobert bought a ticket for 9:20.
In the afternoon, Hobert saw the city with a thin mist again. Suddenly, he felt close to Backlund.
Not until he got off the train did Hobert realize that he had forgotten to buy gifts for Donna and the others.

chapters.title: Chapter 153 - 153: Turbulence on Nikola Street (Bonus 5)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Coming out of the "Tingen City Specialty Shop," Hobert muttered to himself, "I used to make fun of Christian for buying those laughable gifts, but now I'm worse off—I forgot to buy any gifts at all."
Then Hobert realized a serious issue: could it be that Christian also forgets to buy gifts every time he returns and ends up visiting specialty shops like himself? The more he thought about it during the carriage ride, the more likely it seemed.
Hobert first returned to Blanca Street, where Fors was lounging comfortably in a recliner, flipping through a magazine.
Seeing Hobert enter, Fors lazily got up, saying, "You're back."
"Yeah, where's Xio?"
"She's out doing the task you gave her."
Hobert set down his luggage. "Is there anything to eat at home? I haven't had lunch yet."
"Neither have I."
Hobert blinked. "Have you really been lounging on that recliner since morning?"
"No!" Fors chuckled nervously. "I—I've been brainstorming for a new book!"
Hobert smirked inwardly: What a lie!
Under Hobert's unspoken scrutiny, Fors finally overcame his laziness and got up to order lunch from "Desi Flavor Restaurant" nearby.
After a satisfying meal, Hobert delivered the gifts for Fors and Xio, then said, "I'll be heading home tonight and will come over again tomorrow morning."
With that, he left with his briefcase and many gifts.
Fors responded with an "Oh" and glanced at the dishes on the table: Do I have to wash these too? So annoying, I hate washing plates and bowls.
Hobert walked to the law firm and first briefed Lawyer Barton on Mr. Dominic's case.
"This case is all thanks to you," Barton said. "Let me see... Oh, the commission fee totals 150 pounds. Instead of distributing your compensation according to the firm's 'Commission Fee Distribution Regulations,' the firm will only deduct 50 pounds for intermediary and material fees, leaving you with the remaining 100 pounds. However, your travel expenses for this trip won't be reimbursed."
Hobert joked, smiling, "If I had known this earlier, I would have bought you more expensive gifts."
Barton chuckled and shook his head. "No new cases will be assigned to you recently. Focus on winning the lawsuit you have."
Hobert nodded; he now only had Mr. Bob's case in hand.
Leaving Mr. Barton's office, Hobert distributed gifts to several colleagues he got along well with, then sat down at his desk and quickly calculated the expenses of this trip.
The expenses were minimal: damaged clothes in the battle—a shirt, a trench coat, and trousers—costing less than 2 pounds in total. The shirt was expensive, but it was from home and didn't cost him money.
Then there were round-trip tickets and money spent on gifts, totaling around 6 pounds.
However, his income was 130 pounds: 100 pounds commission and 30 pounds tip. Moreover, he could still use the identification card provided by the Nighthawks to evade taxes, and all 130 pounds was his.
This was the income on the surface; this trip to Tingen City also yielded the horn of the wicked creature, the "black eyes," and the umbilical cord of the offspring of the evil god.
These three things seemed high-level, but for now, they could only be used in the Nation of Disorder and only within the Nation of Disorder.
This made Hobert's methods in the Nation of Disorder more diverse, making him appear more like an evil god.
Because Klein had been lying in the coffin, the Tarot Club for this week was canceled. Regarding this, "Mr. Fool" had already made a prediction on Thursday. I wonder if Klein sensed something at the time?
Hobert stayed at the law firm until closing time and took a taxi carriage home.
His return was welcomed by the whole family, and Melissa had the chef prepare several more dishes.
While dinner hadn't started yet, Hobert handed the box Ulysses gave him to Christian.
Christian nodded with a smile. "Looks like he hasn't forgotten me as his old boss."
He put the box in the study before returning to dinner.
At the dinner table, the family listened to Hobert's stories of his business trip. They found the ending of the kidnapping case he was in charge of more bizarre than the stories in the newspapers.
After dinner, Hobert distributed gifts, and the whole family enjoyed themselves.
On Tuesday morning, Hobert, whose spirit body, spirituality, and physical strength had fully recovered, took the family carriage to work.
He sat in the chair for more than ten minutes before going out to "visit clients." In fact, he went to the rental house on Blanca Street.
With Fors and Xio present, the rental house now seemed lively.
Hobert entered and saw Xio making tea while Fors was on the recliner again. How much does she like the recliner? Hobert really doubted if this girl had spent the night on the recliner?
Xio smiled. "Thank you for the gift; I really like it."
Hobert smiled back. "I'm glad you do."
Fors struggled to get up again, and the three sat around the dining table.
Xio said, "I've found the addresses of the Nikola Shipyard and the Tuma Hotel."
She took out a note with the addresses written on it. Both addresses were on Nikola Street; the shipyard was at 1668, and the hotel was at the other end of Nikola Street, number 35.
Taking the note, Hobert found the address somewhat familiar and searched through his briefcase, finally finding the address Harvey Hayden had given him: Rex's former security guard, Dix, owned a company at 1899 Nikola Street.
Nikola Street was indeed bustling.
After taking a sip of tea, Fors said, "I didn't expect Qilangos to die so quickly; fortunately, we didn't rent a new house, otherwise, we would have wasted rent."
Xio said awkwardly, "Hobert, our rental house has a problem, and we won't be able to move out until the day after tomorrow."
Hobert smiled. "It's okay to stay a few more days; there are three bedrooms anyway."
In Backlund, mixed-gender renting is quite common.
Xio immediately said, "We'll pay you rent! And we promise not to bring any danger back."
"Forget about the rent; it's just a few more days." Hobert said, "While you're here, you're responsible for my three meals a day."
Fors immediately raised her hand. "I'll take care of it!"
Hobert immediately gave up hope for the next few days of dining.
Fors then asked, "Hobert, how much is the rent for a month in this row house?"
"It's usually rented annually." Hobert put away Xio's investigation results. "20 to 25 pounds per month."
Xio stuck out his tongue. "So expensive!"
Fors shook her head too, saying they couldn't afford it right now.
Xio then talked about the mission to find the cultists; she had used her connections to find the hiding places of two cultists, who were not hiding in the East Borough but in a factory by the port.
Xio wanted Hobert and Fors to help her catch these two cultists.

chapters.title: Chapter 154 - 154: Briber (Bonus 6)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Xio had investigated and confirmed that the two cultists had no other accomplices. Their access to the factory was facilitated by the workshop supervisor, who was once a follower of the cult.
Both Sequence 9 individuals lacked emergency escape means, so apprehending them shouldn't be difficult with a solid plan.
Due to Xio's extensive preliminary investigation and the associated information costs, she took the lead in this operation, hence she would receive half of the commission, while Hobert and Fors would split the other half.
If it became necessary to eliminate the cultists during the capture, their characteristics will be distributed according to this model.
Hobert had no objections. He considered the police credentials might have some utility in this operation, so the three split up: Xio and Fors continued scouting and planning the capture, while Hobert took a rental carriage to the Blackthorn Security Company in North Borough to obtain credentials.
Thomas had just returned from Tingen City today, but Hobert wasted no time in finding him.
Thomas instructed Borgia to prepare credentials for Hobert and asked him to wait in his office for a moment before leaving himself.
About fifteen minutes later, Thomas returned with a wooden box and handed it to Hobert. "I received a telegram last week about your success with the Night Hawks team in Tingen City, defeating and eliminating Mr. Z of the Aurora Order."
"We intended to reward you with three-fifths of the Briber's characteristics at that time. However, after the incident with the birth of the Evil God's offspring, due to your outstanding performance in that event, we will give you more rewards."
Thomas continued, "Two of these rewards include the remaining one-fifth of the Briber's characteristics. Along with the one-fifth you previously received, you can now take this portion of the Briber's characteristics."
"The second reward is official membership status. As for the third reward, you may make a request, which we will consider fulfilling immediately or partially."
Hobert opened the wooden box to find a crystal ball emitting a charming aura, confirming it as the Briber's characteristic.
After considering for a moment, Hobert said, "For the third reward, grant me the Judge's characteristic."
Daly had taken a Judge's characteristic during the previous battle to divide the spoils from the ambush of the Tamara family members.
Thomas was taken aback. "What do you need the Judge's characteristic for?"
"I have a friend who needs it," Hobert replied. "I'm short of money lately, so I can sell it to her."
Most importantly, he could soon divide the Judge's characteristic into four parts, turning a sum into a significant amount of money.
Thomas nodded. "Very well, but that's a Sequence 6 characteristic. Its value, I believe, needs no explanation to you. You will receive three-fifths of the Judge's characteristic for your remaining merit."
Hobert had no objections to this. At this moment, Borgia arrived with Hobert's credentials, which included the inspector's badge.
Additionally, Hobert would receive a weekly salary of 6 pounds. In fact, given Hobert's Sequence, he was already considered a "senior member," eligible for a salary ranging from 10 to 12 pounds. However, due to his ability to act independently, he was currently receiving the salary of an ordinary member.
Regardless, the unexpected salary from the Nighthawks team was a pleasant surprise, and Hobert found it sufficient.
Leaving the Blackthorn Security Company with the wooden box, Hobert now possessed two portions of the Briber's characteristic, thinking he could sell one.
Upton would be a good potential customer, though Hobert wasn't sure if he was still vacationing in Desi Bay.
Returning to Blanca Street, Hobert found Xio and Fors still absent. He went back to his room, placing the Briber's characteristic into the Nation of Disorder.
Next, he shattered the Sheriff's characteristic and awaited the aggregation of a Sheriff and an Arbiter's materials in a day or two.
Gazing at the brilliant and colorful characteristics on the stone platform, Hobert had only one thought: to cash in! He needed to do so quickly, preparing to purchase items capable of "traveling" to prevent situations where he might encounter such items without enough money.
Just as he was thinking this, Elliot's star lit up, and Hobert extended his spiritual influence.
Elliot's hands crossed as he lowered his head. "Creator in the Shadow of Order..."
After reciting the title, he continued, "Great 'Creator,' Elder Calvin found me today and said he wanted me to join the family's Elder Council, becoming the tenth elder. Should I go?"
This was obviously the Balk family's attempt to actively approach Elliot behind the scenes of the "Creator," allowing Elliot to become an elder in the council, equivalent to opening the family's decision-making meeting to the "Creator."
Hobert pondered for a moment and felt Elliot's current position in the Elder Council was inappropriate, mainly because Elliot's sequence was too low to gain consensus upon entering the Elder Council.
At that time, he might have to announce himself as the "Creator's" spokesperson to appease other family members' dissatisfaction.
However, no matter what method he used, Elliot would be isolated, which was not beneficial to Hobert's plan to go to the Southern Continent to digest the Baron of Corruption potion.
Since he was the spokesperson for the "Creator," he should be supported rather than isolated.
Thinking of this, Hobert made a decision, using his supreme voice. "Not for now."
...
In the Southern Continent.
Having received a response from the "Creator," Elliot breathed a sigh of relief. Actually, he wasn't very keen on joining the Elder Council now, but he knew more that he couldn't decide on this matter.
Fortunately, the "Creator" is wise and did not require him to join.
Elliot took a deep breath and came out to the living room. Calvin was still waiting for news in the living room.
Seeing Elliot only went in for a few minutes and then came out, Calvin was somewhat surprised. He didn't expect that the mysterious existence would give Elliot an answer so quickly.
This made him curious about what extraordinary encounter Elliot had to gain the trust of that existence so quickly.
Perhaps he couldn't even dream that the reason the "Mysterious Existence" was able to give such a quick response was entirely because he happened to be in his "work position."
Elliot said, "After my careful 'consideration,' I temporarily won't join the Elder Council."
This surprised Calvin again. If Elliot joined the Elder Council now, he would become a simple mouthpiece.
The mysterious existence did not intend to let him join the Elder Council, obviously preparing to cultivate him carefully.
"I respect your choice," Calvin said in his mouth, thinking in his heart: "I need to change my attitude toward Elliot."
Elliot asked again, "Uncle Calvin, I have been trying to act as a Briber recently, but why is my 'Briber' potion digesting so slowly?"
Calvin smiled, "That's because the people you've bribed are all relatives in the family. Even without bribes, they are willing to help, so relatively speaking, digestion will be slow."
"Is there any way?"
"There is. According to the family records, there is currently only one method that you can use."
"What method?"
"Bribe the gods!"

chapters.title: Chapter 155 - 155: Xio's Capture Operation Plan (Bonus 7)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Back in the real world, Hobert waited until two in the afternoon before Xio and Fors returned.
This time they had thoroughly scouted the location. Xio drew a sketch and explained her capture plan.
Two cultists lived in a dormitory building within the factory. Xio planned to attack them from the front entrance, while Hobert and Fors waited in ambush by the windows.
If Xio's surprise attack failed, Hobert and Fors would break through the windows to join the fight.
Given our strength advantage over the enemy, we didn't need overly elaborate tactics. Hobert would handle one cultist alone, while Xio and Fors would deal with the other to end the fight quickly.
Xio usually seemed a bit reckless, but when serious, she was quite competent. Her plan was practical, and her precautions were sufficient to handle most unexpected situations.
However, her stature was a bit short, which somewhat diminished the grandeur of her explanation of the plan.
Lastly, Hobert added a note: If confronted by factory workers during retreat, they could use his inspector's credentials to escape.
Seeing Hobert's credentials, Xio exclaimed, "Where did you get these forged? They look very real."
Hobert didn't reveal the truth and simply smiled, "I borrowed these from a friend."
Xio envied this ability; having such credentials would make many things easier for her.
In the evening, the three had dinner and made final preparations.
Suddenly, the doorbell rang.
"Who is it?" Hobert called loudly from the dining room.
No one answered.
"I'll go and open the door!" Fors immediately got up to avoid washing dishes and went to open the door.
But there was no one outside.
"That's strange." Fors was about to close the door when she noticed a small box outside.
"Wait!" Fors moved to pick it up, but Hobert stopped her. He approached with his cane and nudged the box open. Inside was a pigeon stabbed to death with a dagger.
Fors frowned, "Whose prank is this?" She wasn't afraid of such things.
Hobert chuckled, shaking his head, "These people are so childish!"
Fors noticed, "There seems to be a letter inside."
Without even looking at it, Hobert closed the box decisively and tossed it into a nearby trash can.
After closing the door again, Fors seemed to understand, "Is it because of Bob's case?"
Hobert nodded, "It seems they know I'm back. I suggest you two move out tomorrow; their methods will only get more despicable."
"Now is not the time for us to leave!" Xio said, "With us here, the three of us can take turns resting at night."
Fors agreed, "Yes, if we didn't know, it would be one thing, but now that we do, we can't just walk away."
Hobert smiled, "After you leave, I'll stay at home for a couple of days. Let's see who dares to send such things to a general's house."
Xio and Fors exchanged glances; it seemed like a plan.
"Let's proceed with tonight's operation first," Hobert said. "We'll discuss the rest tomorrow."
By late evening, the three boarded a carriage that often worked with Xio.
Around ten o'clock at night, Hobert and his group arrived at the courtyard wall of a textile factory. Inside the carriage, Xio reiterated the plan they had made during the day.
Then they began their operation: Hobert and Xio climbed over the wall, while Fors "opened" the door directly.
The workshop area was already darkened; after all, this was an era of gas lamps and steam-powered machinery, not yet capable of running 24 hours a day.
Led by Xio, they arrived in front of the dormitory where the cultists resided. There were two dogs here, but Xio had prepared by tossing them some meaty bones. The dogs were too busy with the bones to pay attention to Hobert and the others.
Hobert and Fors lay in ambush outside the window, while Xio agilely climbed into the dormitory from the second floor, reaching the room where one of the cultists lived on the ground floor.
Listening and hearing no movement inside, Xio kicked the door open, only to realize something was wrong. Instead of two people, there were three sitting on the edge of the bed, seemingly engaged in a quiet conversation in the dark.
After Xio kicked open the door, they all turned to look at her.
Scratching her head, Xio said, "Sorry, wrong room!" She politely closed the door on them.
The three inside the room stood stupefied for a second or two, before one of them said, "Catch her!"
They rushed to the door, but just as they were about to open it, the door suddenly swung toward them. Xio hadn't left; she had heard them approach the door and kicked it hard, sending the door panel crashing into the three rushing out.
At the same time, the window side suddenly became ethereal, and Fors crossed through the window into the room.
Immediately afterward, the window was smashed open, and Hobert jumped in with his cane.
Three against three, they engaged in a fierce battle in the not-so-spacious room.
Due to the chaotic scene, Hobert temporarily refrained from using his pistol, afraid of accidentally hitting Xio or Fors.
Hobert's opponent was a skilled fighter, bare-handed against Hobert's cane, and under the blessing of the "Combat Ring," they were evenly matched.
As the fight continued, the opponent seemed to grow stronger.
However, as a "Barbarian," Hobert had greater strength. He quickly adjusted his strategy, using his strength advantage to charge straight in.
The opponent, without a weapon, could only resist Hobert's onslaught with his arms.
Eventually, Hobert slammed him against the wall, kicking up dust and nearly making him cough up blood.
Hobert charged again, and the opponent quickly dodged, not expecting Hobert to use the cane like a sword, leveraging his strength advantage to stab him through and pin him to the wall.
Amid the opponent's screams, Hobert pulled out his pistol.
Bang!
He shot the opponent in close range in the head.
The gunshot in the night was particularly loud, and the earlier sounds of fighting had already awakened many people. But upon hearing the gunshot, the factory workers who had intended to come out and see what was happening quickly retreated and locked the doors again.
Meanwhile, the fight on Xio's side was nearing its end; Fors's opponent was the weakest, and despite Fors not being skilled in combat, she wasn't at a disadvantage.
Hobert went to help Fors, rushing over to kick down her opponent, and then another shot to resolve the situation.
Xio had already slashed her opponent's throat with a dagger; in just a minute or two, they had finished the fight.
Of course, much of this was due to their surprise attack.
Fors breathed a sigh of relief, lit a match, and lit a lamp to examine the faces of the three.
Hobert's opponent was a "Prisoner," although his abilities did not include combat skills, a "Prisoner" was more likely to learn various murder techniques, including combat.
Xio's opponent was a "Farmer," and Fors's opponent wasn't listed in the wanted list. He wore an expensive suit and didn't seem like a manager hiding two cultists.
Hobert searched the opponent's body but found no identification or similar items.
Not knowing the opponent's identity made him uneasy, so Hobert asked Xio and Fors to disguise the other two bodies, preparing to perform a spirit channeling on this stranger.

chapters.title: Chapter 156 - 156: Unexpected Gains (Bonus 8)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
The previous battle hadn't drained much of Hobert's strength, so he could calmly use the "Spirit Necklace."
The room immediately grew cold, and Hobert's eyes turned completely black. He saw the dissipating spirituality of the stranger, and the surroundings rapidly disappeared, transforming into a vast gray fog.
Hobert grasped the other person's spirituality and began silently chanting in his heart: "Your name and identity."
"Your name and identity."
"..."
After chanting seven times, the gray fog revealed the scene Hobert wanted—a hand holding a document. The deceased man's name was Wayne, and he was an employee of the Feynapotter Embassy.
"You cannot carry this document with you; it will remain with me until your return to the country." A voice said, "You will disguise yourself as a merchant and cooperate with the ambassador's actions."
The scene faded, and the gray fog returned.
Hobert was stunned. Why would a Feynapotter spy be here?
He then asked, "What was your purpose for coming here tonight?"
"What was your purpose for coming here tonight?"
"..."
The gray fog revealed another scene—inside an office, a middle-aged man with Feynapotter's signature mustache and thinning hair angrily said, "The matter with Count Vincent is already frustrating enough, and now those two idiots are causing trouble at this time!
"Have them smuggled out from the dock tomorrow and send them to the Southern Continent. Never let them return."
The scene disappeared, once again turning into the gray fog.
Count Vincent? Could the theft at Count Vincent's estate be related to the Feynapotter Embassy?
As for those two cultists, Hobert had some guesses. To confirm his suspicions, he asked, "Who was the middle-aged man who appeared just now?"
"Who was the middle-aged man who appeared just now?"
"..."
The gray fog changed again, showing a lavish hall. The middle-aged man with the mustache appeared much younger than in the previous scene. A man in his thirties pointed at the middle-aged man and introduced him to Wayne: "This is Mr. Tim, the ambassador to the Loen Kingdom."
The scene turned back into the gray fog.
Hobert noticed that the man's spirituality had thinned due to the mediumship, which put his mind at ease.
Exiting the mediumship, Xio and Fors had already packed up the body. One of the ladies had spent much time in the East Borough and was used to seeing dead bodies on the street, while the other had once been a surgeon, so neither was afraid of corpses.
Hobert nodded to them. He and Xio carried the body while Fors led the way.
Though Xio was short, she was quite strong, effortlessly carrying a body and walking swiftly.
The gunshots from earlier had alerted the security personnel, but they didn't dare approach right away. It wasn't until the security captain arrived with a double-barreled shotgun that they came to investigate.
By then, the only thing they found was a corpse with a shattered head, as Hobert and the others were already scaling the wall.
It wasn't until they got into the carriage that Xio and Fors's faces started to relax into smiles.
Xio smiled and said, "This mission went smoother than expected."
Fors let out a breath, "Ever since meeting Hobert, I've been dragged into all kinds of fights."
She smiled, "But I quite like it. We earn bounties and take down cultists!"
It was only then that they noticed Hobert's serious expression.
Fors sensed something was wrong. "Did you discover something unusual during the mediumship?"
Hobert leaned forward and whispered to Xio and Fors, "That stranger was a staff member at the Feynapotter Embassy, or more accurately, a spy."
Xio and Fors didn't immediately react, which was understandable. Who would associate cultists with an embassy?
After a few seconds, Fors reacted, "You mean... that the cult is backed by the Feynapotter Kingdom?"
Hobert nodded, "That's highly possible."
A beat later, Xio caught on. "I've always heard that embassy staff from foreign countries often engage in espionage and sabotage.
"I never really believed it, but it turns out it's true!
"Feynapotter Embassy staff secretly organizing a cult in Loen to disrupt our peace!"
There was a moment of silence in the carriage before Fors broke it. "What do we do now? Should we go hide in the countryside for a while?"
While disrupting Feynapotter's conspiracy and taking down cultists was satisfying, they were ultimately just a Sequence 8 and two Sequence 9s. If the Feynapotter ambassador wanted to retaliate, he could easily have them killed without anyone knowing.
"No, act like we know nothing." Hobert replied, "This mission has military backing, which is our protection. The Feynapotter ambassador won't make a move on us lightly.
"After all, relations between Loen and Feynapotter have never been good. The ambassador and his staff in Backlund are under tighter scrutiny than those from other countries.
"We might be watched for a while, but as long as we treat this mission as a simple cultist elimination, the ambassador won't make any trouble over a dead spy."
Fors nodded, "If the ambassador retaliates, it only proves his connection to the spy."
"Exactly," Hobert said, "So for now, I'll keep working at the law firm, one of you keeps thinking up... new book ideas in your armchair, and the other keeps working as a bounty hunter."
Fors looked at Hobert, "Were you about to say I've been slacking in my armchair?"
"No," Hobert chuckled, "I know you're hard at work thinking of new stories."
Xio turned to the window, stifling her laughter.
After settling on their plan, they followed through, taking the two bodies to Xio and Fors's previous rental apartment.
As for the information about Count Vincent revealed during the mediumship, Hobert didn't plan to share it with Xio and Fors.
Hobert had a theory—the recent theft at Count Vincent's estate was likely orchestrated by the Feynapotter ambassador.
The reason was simple: it was a test for Count Vincent. Aside from sending a few petty thieves to rob Vincent's residence, Ambassador Tim probably had other ways of testing him, though Hobert wasn't sure what they were.
As for why Count Vincent was being tested, Hobert could understand. It was clear Vincent was serving the king, likely helping George III construct one of his tombs.
The Feynapotter royal family, being Arbiters themselves, had probably sensed something unusual in George III's recent actions.
Hobert thought to himself, 'They might be the ones who least want to see George III become the Black Emperor.'

chapters.title: Chapter 157 - 157: Splitting the Money (Bonus 9)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
By the time they arrived at Xio and Fors' rented apartment, the Beyonder characteristics of the two cultists had already precipitated.
The Beyonder characteristic of the "Farmer" was a clump of thick green liquid, resembling a glob of seaweed-filled water.
The Beyonder characteristic of the "Prisoner" appeared as a grayish stone mixed with some crystals, capable of reflecting light under illumination.
Hobert carefully placed the Beyonder characteristics into prepared wooden boxes, and the three of them took turns resting.
At dawn the next day, the carriage Xio had hired appeared at the door once again.
This time, Hobert noticed that the coachman was a scruffy old man with a thin, disheveled beard and hair.
The three of them rode the carriage, bringing the corpses to the mercenary club's entrance. Hobert went inside alone and headed to the third-floor information wall room to find the attendant, asking them to notify the issuer of the cultist bounty.
While waiting in the reception hall on the first floor, Hobert had two cups of black tea and waited for over half an hour before a few people dressed in black formal attire sat across from him under the attendant's guidance.
After a brief exchange of pleasantries, their superior finally said, "We need to verify that you've caught the right people."
"They put up a fierce resistance when we tried to capture them, and they attempted to flee, so..." Hobert smiled, "The bodies are in the carriage outside."
The superior nodded, not particularly concerned.
Hobert led them outside, allowing Xio and Fors to step out of the carriage first, while two men in black formal suits got inside to examine the bodies.
Queen's Avenue was mostly empty, with only a few passing carriages. Neither the nobles inside the carriages nor their drivers paid any attention to the three carriages parked on the wide street.
The black-suited superior started chatting with Hobert as they stood by the carriage. "So, it was you who broke into the Lobyto Textile Factory and killed someone last night?"
Both Xio and Fors tensed up. They hadn't expected last night's operation to be discovered so quickly.
"You could say that," Hobert replied with a smile, careful not to reveal anything incriminating.
"A merchant from the Feynapotter Kingdom also died at the scene," the superior said nonchalantly as he lit a cigarette.
"He was with the cultists at the time," Hobert explained. "But since he wasn't on the bounty list, we treated him as just another cultist."
At this moment, the inspectors finished their examination and nodded to the superior as they removed their gloves.
"Good job!" the superior said with a smile. "I never liked him anyway."
Taking a drag on his cigarette, he asked, "After keeping the bodies for a while, did anything unusual happen?"
Hobert smiled, "You're asking about the Beyonder characteristics."
The superior nodded. "Since you know, I won't need to explain. Believe me, both of those characteristics will be hard to sell. Let me buy them from you."
"I've sold cultist Beyonder characteristics once before at a mercenary club gathering," Hobert said, subtly indicating that he could attend such gatherings and that he knew the prices of Beyonder characteristics. "Name your price."
"How about 280 pounds for each?"
"Too cheap. 'Prisoner' should be 300, and 'Farmer' 350."
The superior was momentarily stunned, clearly surprised by Hobert's accurate knowledge of the prices. "Your asking price is a bit high..."
After some friendly negotiation, they settled on 290 for the "Prisoner" and 330 for the "Farmer."
Once the price was agreed upon, Hobert took the wooden box from Fors, climbed into the superior's carriage, and completed the transaction.
After counting the money and ensuring everything was in order, Hobert handed over the Beyonder characteristics and the corpses. With a simple nod of acknowledgment, both parties parted ways.
In the carriage, Xio and Fors watched as Hobert pulled out a stack of gold pounds. The sight of the large sum made both women's breathing grow slightly heavier.
They weren't strangers to large sums of money, but it was rare for them to see over a thousand pounds in one go.
Xio chuckled, "This is definitely the most profitable job I've ever taken!"
The earnings from this job were equivalent to what she usually made in a year.
Hobert smiled and said, "Now comes the most exciting part: splitting the profits."
He continued, "The bounty for the two cultists is 200 each, making a total of 400. The two Beyonder characteristics sold for 620, so our total income is 1,020 pounds.
"I introduced the job to Xio, so taking a 5% broker fee isn't unreasonable, right?"
"Not at all," Xio quickly replied. "That's a very fair fee."
For high-paying jobs like this, it was common for broker fees to reach 8% or even 10%.
Hobert took out 51 pounds for himself, and they began dividing the remaining 969. Xio took half, amounting to 484 pounds and 10 soli, while Hobert and Fors each took a quarter, earning 242 pounds and 5 soli apiece.
With that, the task was successfully concluded, and the carriage headed towards Blanca Street.
Fors asked Hobert, "Earlier, you mentioned having a lead on the main ingredient for 'Trickmaster'..."
Hobert smiled and replied, "I've already acquired it. If you're planning to advance soon, you'll only need to buy the supplementary materials."
Fors smiled back, "Great."
The earnings from this task, combined with her savings, were enough to pay for the main ingredient of "Trickmaster."
Hobert added, "Given the potential consequences of last night's operation, I suggest we stay together for a while, at least until the Feynapotter embassy's surveillance ends or we're sure they aren't monitoring us."
Fors nodded in agreement. "That's a good idea. We can take turns keeping watch at night to prevent any ambushes."
Xio also agreed, so their planned move was postponed by a few days.
Back at 192 Blanca Street, since they hadn't rested well the previous night, Hobert and Fors went to sleep first, while Xio stayed in the living room reading a magazine and keeping an eye out for any potential surveillance.
Around noon, Hobert woke up after a couple of hours of sleep, feeling refreshed. When he went downstairs, he found Xio preparing lunch.
"Sorry, Hobert, I only know how to make pasta," Xio said as she served Hobert a plate.
The popular pasta in Loen was similar to what Hobert remembered as Italian pasta. The noodles were boiled, then mixed with salt and olive oil, mushrooms were added, and the dish was topped with either meat sauce or tomato sauce.
Hobert smiled. "When you're hungry, a big plate of pasta is perfect... though, I can't eat that much."
Xio, a bit embarrassed, said, "That's the portion I set aside for myself."
Hobert finally understood why Xio was so strong: she could eat!
After filling their stomachs, Hobert glanced at the clock, noticing it was already around one in the afternoon. "Fors hasn't woken up yet."
"Let her sleep a little longer," Xio said while cleaning up the dishes. "You should head to work. Once Fors wakes up, I'll take a nap."
Hobert didn't argue, helped wipe the table, then grabbed his briefcase and left for the law firm.
When he arrived at the office, Hobert received an official notice, and its contents surprised him: "The court date has been moved up!"

chapters.title: Chapter 158 - 158: Demonstration (Bonus 10)
chapters.content:
Generally speaking, cases in formal courts are sometimes postponed, but rarely are they moved up! Bob's case was originally scheduled for next Thursday, but now it has been moved to this Friday, which is the day after tomorrow.
Originally, Hobert wanted to find a few witnesses, but now he has no time at all!
Something's not right!
Hobert immediately realized that something was very wrong.
Just then, the receptionist from the law firm entered the office: "Lawyer Hobert, someone is looking for you."
"Oh." Hobert came to his senses, put away the official letter, pondering how to respond, and went to the reception room.
In the reception room, there was a well-dressed butler who smiled and said, "Mr. Hobert, my master Mr. Arnold invites you to a dinner tonight. Here's the invitation."
Hobert looked at the butler and suddenly understood. He smiled and said, "Alright, I'll definitely go."
The butler nodded slightly, politely bid farewell to Hobert.
Hobert tossed the invitation on the desk, glanced at the official letter again, and realized this was a demonstration!
He sat in his chair, crossed his arms, and began to ponder how to deal with it.
Ten minutes later, he suddenly jumped up from his chair, threw on his coat, grabbed his briefcase and cane, and quickly left the law firm.
As soon as he left, Hobert noticed two tailing men following him almost openly.
This was also part of the demonstration.
Hobert shook his head with a smile. If this had been in ancient times, when these people threatened his family and his life, he might have compromised.
But now he wasn't compromising at all. If they pushed him too far, he might just storm Arnold's house and hang him from a lamppost.
But it wasn't time to flip the table yet. Back at the rental house, Fors was dining, and Xio was yawning, preparing to nap again after a little more preparation.
Fors saw Hobert: "Is it only a few points? You're off work already?"
"I have urgent matters!" Hobert said, "Xio, I'll take up your rest time to give you an urgent commission."
He handed her a neatly arranged note: "Remember Arnold, the employer of my client Bob?"
Xio put down her magazine: "I remember."
Hobert said, "The names on the note are former employees of Arnold's factory. Go find them as quickly as possible. It's okay if you don't find them all; four or five will do."
"Then ask them to testify in court on Friday. You can give them some money, but when you give them money, make it clear that it's compensation for their lost wages, not for testifying."
As he spoke, he took out 30 pounds in cash: "This is the commission for this task."
Xio took 20: "This will do." She said, putting on her hat and leaving immediately.
Hobert then turned to Fors, who was eating slowly: "I have a commission for you too. Go to Viscount Glaint's mansion and inform him and Miss Audrey that I will hold an emergency meeting of the 'Justice League' tomorrow morning."
He took out a 2 pound note from his wallet as he spoke.
Fors, however, only took out one pound: "It's just delivering a message, one pound is enough."
She began to speed up her meal.
Hobert said hello and left immediately, with the two tailing men arrogantly smoking at his doorstep.
Hobert walked forward as if nothing had happened. As he passed them, Hobert suddenly approached them, lifted his foot, and stomped hard!
Crunch~
The sound of the arch bone breaking.
The stomped man yelled in pain, hopping around holding his foot.
The other tailing man hadn't figured out what was going on yet, and Hobert lifted his foot again and stomped hard!
So there were two people on the street hopping around holding their feet.
Hobert smiled and shook his head, "Sorry for stepping on your feet. Please watch where you're walking in the future, or I might accidentally step on your heads."
After saying that, Hobert called a cab and left, leaving behind two crying men holding their feet.
Passers-by on the street were puzzled. It was just a footstep, why were they in so much pain?
Hobert took a cab to Obsidian Bar, gave the bartender a tip, and asked him to bring Daly Simone over.
Several minutes later, a black-haired woman in her thirties followed the bartender back: "Let me introduce myself, Loretta, your new contact."
She had a decent appearance and dressed somewhat masculine, giving her a unique sense of androgynous beauty.
Hobert was stunned, "Where's Miss Daly?"
She didn't quit her job because she couldn't save Dunn, did she?
Loretta whispered, "She joined the Red Gloves and just left today. I'll be your contact from now on."
Hobert nodded slowly, "I understand. Hello, Ms. Loretta, I'm Hobert. I believe I don't need to introduce myself too thoroughly, right?"
"No need." Loretta smiled, "You're a special case in the entire Nighthawks team of the Loen Kingdom."
She asked, "It's not payday yet. What's the matter?"
Hobert smiled bitterly. Who told you I was so eager to get paid?
He asked back, "Do you know about Bob's case?"
"I've heard of it."
"Recently, the defendant Arnold is using some despicable means to try to win the lawsuit," Hobert said, "I want you guys to protect Mr. Bob closely in the next day or two. If he dies, this lawsuit won't go on."
Loretta said, "The church also attaches great importance to this case. I believe the captain will send someone to protect Mr. Bob after receiving your message."
Hobert picked up his cane, ready to get up, "Then I'll leave it to you."
Then he suddenly remembered, "By the way, when I met Qilangos before, please ask Captain Thomas to help me pick up my cane that I left at the scene.
"I forgot to ask when I went to the security company last time. Is the cane with you?"
Loretta was stunned, "There was no cane at the scene."
"It's a black sandalwood stick."
"There's no black sandalwood stick." Loretta said, "I was at the scene at the time, and the captain mentioned this, and didn't find the cane you mentioned."
Hobert had a bad feeling, "Someone picked it up!"
At the time, the home was in a terrible mess, and the people who looked around were probably only going to scream and run away at a glance, with only a small probability of taking them away.
The greater likelihood is that someone has taken away the cane for a clear purpose.
This was the second "Wood of Order" that couldn't be completely recovered. If it weren't for its high level and sufficient anti-divination properties, Hobert would have considered joining the Nighthawks team completely now.
Loretta asked, "Is that cane special?"
"Nothing." Hobert smiled, "I just suddenly remembered this."
