Hobert looked at Jessica, who was slightly nervous but overall dignified and composed, and his thoughts wandered: she should be a "Lawyer", otherwise Rafter wouldn't have used a "Barbarian's" potion formula as her reward.
But he wondered if her friend with the warhammer was also a Beyonder of the "Lawyer" pathway?
While thinking, he politely greeted Jessica.
Jessica warmly said to Hobert: "Hello, Lawyer Hobert, I've attended your defense as an observer, it was wonderful, and I hope to learn from you in the future."
Hobert smiled slightly: "Mutual learning."
Jessica obviously wanted to chat with Hobert a bit more, but it wasn't appropriate to say too much in front of everyone, so she had to go and greet other colleagues with some regret.
A few minutes later, Jessica went to other offices to meet other colleagues.
Hobert's colleagues were all male, and they immediately began discussing the new beautiful colleague.
Judging solely on appearance, Jessica was definitely a beauty, and she was dressed smartly, with a ponytail, giving off a very energetic feeling.
Just as everyone was talking enthusiastically, a colleague suddenly said: "What's the use of us talking about the new colleague here? She clearly has a good impression of the great lawyer Hobert."
For a moment, everyone lost the interest to continue talking.
Hobert, who was reading a letter, heard the sourness in that sentence, but he didn't respond, not even raising his head.
No matter what industry, as long as you do well, there will always be people who are jealous.
Hobert focused his attention on the letter in front of him, which was from Captain Ikanser, first conveying Bob's gratitude for receiving the compensation, and then briefly mentioning their arrangements for Bob: sending him to Constant and changing his identity and household registration.
The industrial city of Constant also has a large working-class population, and there are many clergy members of the Church of Steam and Machinery there, who will constantly monitor Bob's condition.
At the end of the letter, Captain Ikanser talked about the "Roselle Memorial Exhibition" which would open this Wednesday, that is, tomorrow, and enclosed 15 VIP exclusive tickets with the letter.
Hobert scratched his head, he had been too busy recently and had forgotten about it. Now that it was about to open, the matter of the "Black Emperor" card had to be put on the agenda. As a Beyonder of the "Black Emperor" pathway, he definitely had to obtain this blasphemy card.
Hobert put the tickets and letters in the drawer, and took out letter paper, preparing to write a reply to Ikanser.
But just after writing a few words, Barton appeared at the door: "Hobert, come here for a moment."
Hobert capped his round-bellied fountain pen and followed.
Arriving at Barton's office, a middle-aged man was also sitting in the reception area: the great lawyer Aslan.
Since coming to the law firm, Hobert had only seen this great lawyer with short brown hair and glasses twice.
He specialized in commercial dispute cases and had some fame throughout the country, so he usually traveled all over the country.
The simultaneous appearance of two great lawyers must mean there was a major issue to discuss.
After a brief exchange of greetings, Barton began to talk about the "Work Injury Compensation Case" that ended last week, and the impact of this case. Aslan occasionally echoed, expressing his affirmation of Hobert's achievements.
Then Barton mentioned that the firm intended to establish a lawyer team for Hobert, specializing in handling such work injury compensation cases.
Barton said very frankly: "There are two reasons for this plan. The first is that the defense you made had a huge impact. The letters on your desk are enough to illustrate this point. I think our firm will receive many similar cases in the future.
"The second is that in this lawsuit, you offended the gentlemen of Backlund. Besides this type of case, it may be difficult to receive other cases."
As for the treatment offered by the two great lawyers, it was very generous. Hobert would become the third partner of the firm, and he could receive 50% of the remuneration for the cases he handled, and receive 10% of the dividends at the end of the year.
Because Hobert was not yet a recognized great lawyer, and had joined the firm relatively late, he could only receive 10% of the dividends for now.
Hobert certainly understood that this was actually a choice and compromise made by Barton and Lancaster.
Their choice was not to abandon Hobert, but in order not to affect the firm's other business, they made a certain separation of Hobert's business, which was a compromise to reality.
With such good treatment, Hobert certainly wouldn't refuse. His current workload was not enough for him to establish his own law firm, and the key was that his "Lawyer" potion had already been digested, and he didn't want to go through such troublesome operations again.
Barton finally said: "I will arrange three independent offices for you, and you can also transfer three colleagues to help you."
After thanking him, Hobert immediately mentioned Rasga and Dico, two colleagues who were relatively familiar and had enough goodwill towards him.
But Hobert hesitated about the third candidate. He spent less time in the office and was not very familiar with his colleagues.
Suddenly, Jessica's name appeared in Hobert's mind. She was a "Lawyer" and might be helpful for future business, and could barely be considered "well-known".
After confirming the colleagues to be transferred, Lancaster got up to leave. After sending away this great lawyer, Barton took Hobert to see the offices. The three offices were two small and one large, with the large office opposite the small offices.
The people from the logistics department were already cleaning, and Hobert asked them to add some filing cabinets and other office supplies.
Then he talked to the three colleagues. When talking to Rasga and Dico, he didn't avoid the others.
Several other colleagues in the office looked at the colleague who had spoken sourly just now. That colleague seemed not to hear, and was still sitting there reading the materials, but he hadn't turned a page for several minutes, seemingly revealing that he was pretending to be calm.
Whether it was Rasga, Dico, or Jessica, they were all willing to join Hobert's team. For them, this was an opportunity. Generally, entering a professional team would have more opportunities to appear in court, and the types of cases handled would be similar, unlike now where they had to take on any type of case.
That morning, the four of them moved to the new office location.
The new office was on the first floor and close to the side door, making it easy to enter and exit.
Hobert divided the three offices: one was for his own use, one was for the assistant to use and also as a reference room, and the large office was used by the remaining two colleagues and also as a conference room.
After dividing the offices, Hobert asked: "Who is willing to be my assistant? In addition to handling cases, the assistant's job also includes organizing materials, receiving and sending letters, etc. Of course, the weekly salary will also be 1 to 2 pounds higher."
"Me!" Jessica's reaction speed was extremely fast, and she took the initiative to persuade the other two colleagues: "In addition to organizing materials, the assistant is also responsible for receiving visitors. Women are more suitable for this job."
Rasga and Dico both thought it made sense, so Jessica became Hobert's assistant.

chapters.title: Chapter 186 - 186 Payday (Bonus 13)
chapters.content:

After lunch, Hobert held a meeting with his three subordinates.
The team's current tasks are primarily to sort through the incoming mail. Jessica is mainly responsible for reading and replying to letters from newspapers and magazines, and for creating an interview schedule, inviting reporters to come in for interviews soon.
Rasga and Dico are to sort through consultation and commission letters. Rasga and Dico can reply to consultation letters at their discretion, but commission letters must be approved by Hobert before a reply is sent to accept the commission.
At the end of the meeting, Hobert announced that he would treat everyone to dinner that evening to celebrate the team's formation.
After arranging the work, Hobert returned to his office and wrote a reply to Ikanser. While writing, Hobert suddenly remembered Ulysses's instructions, so he wrote a letter to Elizabeth as well.
In the letter, Hobert shared some 'tough love,' telling Elizabeth that death happens every day and that she should not only dwell on sadness and awe of life but also look forward.
After finishing, Hobert gave both letters to Jessica and instructed her to mail them that afternoon.
Then, Hobert put on his trench coat, picked up his cane, and went to 'visit clients'.
He first walked back to his rented apartment and left notes for Xio and Fors, telling them that he wouldn't be home for dinner.
Only then did Hobert take a hired carriage to the 'Obsidian Bar' in the North Borough.
He arrived more than ten minutes early, but Loretta was already sitting at the bar, having ordered a beer but not taken a sip.
"You're here so early?" Hobert placed his cane and also ordered a beer.
"I just happened to be free today, so I came early." Loretta took out an envelope: "This is your salary for last week. We pay salaries every Saturday afternoon. You can either pick it up directly at Blackthorn Security Company, or we can mail it to you, but you'll need to submit a written request for that."
Hobert naturally chose to have it mailed. He immediately took out paper and pen, wrote a request, and asked Loretta to submit it for him.
The format and wording of the official document were fairly standard. Loretta glanced at it and put the request away.
Hobert asked, "Is there something else you wanted to see me about today?"
This was the first time a member of the Nighthawks team had proactively contacted Hobert.
"It's just to give you your salary, and you're already two days late in receiving it."
"Just to give me my salary?"
"Just to give you your salary."
Hobert recalled his previous encounters with Loretta. This woman seemed obsessed with paying salaries. Had the Nighthawks team been known to delay salaries?
That couldn't be, right? If an official Beyonder organization had a financial crisis, it wouldn't be far from disbanding.
"Okay, that's definitely a big deal." Hobert casually agreed and then asked, "I previously reported a 'Secret Supplicant' named Cate. How far has your investigation progressed?"
He added, "Ms. Daly promised to inform me of the investigation results at the time."
"We've already found the Hyman you mentioned." Loretta looked around to make sure there were no customers nearby before saying, "He seems to be in contact with two other Aurora Order members. We plan to launch the operation this week or next week."
"Oh, right, the captain said that you might have to participate in the operation as well. Prepare yourself these next two days. Well, that's one of the reasons I contacted you today!"
That's the more important reason for the meeting, isn't it! Hobert couldn't help but complain in his heart: Did the Nighthawks really owe you salary?
Hobert took a deep breath to calm himself and nodded, "I will never be soft on these lunatics. You can write to me or directly notify me when the operation time is set."
"No problem."
On the way back to the law firm, Hobert realized that Loretta might be wearing some kind of mystical item that made her so focused on 'salary'.
The more Hobert thought about it, the more he felt it was the case. Otherwise, wouldn't the Nighthawks team be afraid of Loretta's debt collection? How could they dare to have a member who was so focused on salary?
Back at the firm, as Hobert was hanging up his trench coat, Jessica came to Hobert's office: "Lawyer Hobert, I've read all the letters from newspapers and magazines and drafted an interview schedule."
"Take a look and if it's okay, I'll write back according to this schedule."
That's fast!
Hobert took the schedule and glanced at it: "No problem."
Jessica said a little embarrassed: "Lawyer Hobert, um, do you, do you have any extra tickets?"
Hobert was stunned for a moment before realizing that Jessica was talking about tickets to the "Roselle Memorial Exhibition."
Jessica continued stuttering: "Um, I have a friend who admires Roselle very much, but, but we don't have a way to get VIP tickets for a close-up visit, so..."
During the meeting in the afternoon, Jessica saw Hobert take away a stack of VIP tickets while sorting the letters. At that time, because there were two other colleagues present, she was embarrassed to ask.
She hesitated for a long time this afternoon, always feeling that it was not good to make such a request on the first day of work, but thinking of her friend's happy smile, she decided to ask for a ticket for her friend.
"Yes." Hobert generously gave out two tickets: "These tickets are the Church of Steam and Machinery's gratitude to me."
Jessica thanked him repeatedly, her face filled with joy.
Back at her desk, Hobert handled official business for more than an hour, and then it was time to get off work.
Hobert's team had dinner together at a nearby restaurant. This dinner brought everyone closer together.
However, Hobert had just received his salary in the afternoon and spent 3 pounds and 3 soli, half a week's salary was gone. Now Hobert suddenly understood why Loretta valued salary so much, and valued payday so much.
If you spend a week's salary in two days, then the remaining 5 days, payday would be like looking forward to the stars and the moon!
...
Wednesday, the opening day of the "Roselle Memorial Exhibition." Hobert is now the head of the department, and he doesn't need to ask for leave or go to the firm to go out and "visit clients."
Arriving at the exhibition hall, the queue was already packed with people. Hobert really didn't expect that Roselle had been dead for more than a hundred years, but he still had such a great appeal.
But then he thought that entertainment was scarce in this era, so such a memorial exhibition was very popular among all classes.
Because Hobert had VIP tickets, he could avoid queuing and enter directly from the side door, and he could visit the things Roselle had used up close.
As soon as he entered the door, Hobert saw a member of the "Machinery Hivemind" who had once protected him. He knew that the other party must be very busy today, so he just smiled and nodded to the other party without going up to talk.
Entering the exhibition hall, as a person from the Modern Era, Hobert was not very interested in these things, he only praised Roselle's golden toilet as really luxurious, and wondered if you could really poop on such a toilet?
Hobert tried to make his speed look normal as he came to the study area. He had just glanced at the tall bookshelves in the study when he saw Jessica and the silver-haired woman in front of the bookshelves.
At the same time, Jessica also saw Hobert, she quickly waved her hand and said: "Lawyer Hobert, I'm not skipping work, I took a leave of absence."
Hobert smiled: "I'm not skipping work either."
Jessica was stunned for a moment, as if she understood something.

chapters.title: Chapter 187 - 187: How to Steal the Card of Blasphemy (Bonus 14)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
"Hello, Lawyer Hobert," the silver-haired woman said generously with a smile. "I've attended your defense for Mr. Bob; it was wonderful."
Hobert smiled. "I didn't realize I was so famous now."
Jessica then realized she hadn't introduced them and proceeded to do so.
The silver-haired woman was called Carrie. She had short hair, wore knightly attire, was tall, had tanned skin, and looked very healthy. From a distance, she looked more like a young man.
Carrie thanked Hobert for the complimentary tickets. Hobert exchanged pleasantries while recalling that Carrie's weapon was a warhammer, a rarely used weapon requiring astonishing strength and reflexes.
Carrie's broad frame did prove she had sufficient strength.
After a few pleasantries, they each went to explore.
Hobert began to earnestly search for the "Black Emperor" card. Just then, he heard Carrie whisper to Jessica, "I originally thought your boss giving you such precious tickets meant he had feelings for you, but now it seems I was overthinking it. There's no trace of impure thoughts in his eyes."
Hobert was stunned. 'Are you two intentionally talking loud enough for me to hear? Or do I look like I'm deaf?'
Jessica said, "Keep it down, Carrie."
Carrie flipped through a high-quality replica book provided by the exhibition and casually said, "It doesn't matter if he hears. I'm complimenting him."
"So, you're relieved now?"
"No, Jessica, for a woman, this is where you've failed."
It seemed they were good friends like Xio and Fors, so they spoke so casually.
Hobert smiled and shook his head, then went to observe the bookmarks in the exhibition area from another angle.
Although the VIP ticket allowed close observation of the exhibits, there was still some distance.
Even so, Hobert's spirituality quickly discovered the "Black Emperor" card. He couldn't explain why he had such a judgment, but he knew that bookmark was the "Black Emperor" card!
Hobert pondered for a moment, then began to observe the structure of the exhibition hall, leaving after ten o'clock.
Back at the firm, Rasga and Dico had already read all the commission letters and consultation letters. There were ten commission letters in total, which Hobert briefly glanced at and found all within his team's scope of work.
So, Hobert picked the case that seemed the most difficult to handle, and distributed the other nine relatively simple cases to others on the team. Hobert also assigned the consultation letters that needed replies, then he took the work he needed to handle himself back to his office.
Although he appeared to be reading the letters, he was actually thinking about how to steal the "Black Emperor" card.
He had been thinking about this issue on the way back and already had some ideas.
Hobert's first idea was to hypnotize a staff member and have the hypnotized person swap out the "Black Emperor" card, or complete a sacrifice in the exhibition hall.
But considering this exhibition had the background of the Church of Steam and Machinery, operations like "hypnosis" would easily be exposed, and it would be easy to trace back to him.
The second method was to ask Fors to help him steal it. She had the ability to "open doors" and was now a "Trickmaster" who could easily divert people's attention. During the exhibition, she could use the "Trickmaster's" methods to steal it and then pass it out through the opened door.
Even if the anti-theft "building block" sealed artifact detected Fors's door opening", it would be fine because the Blasphemy Card would be passed out quickly, and Fors only needed to immediately leave the place where she "opened the door."
But this plan could only be carried out during the day, when there were many people and it was easy to be noticed. If discovered, it would easily attract the attention of the Machinery Hivemind team.
Hobert took a deep breath, recalling how Klein stole the "Black Emperor" card, which was by summoning himself, entering the exhibition hall in spirit form.
This method was impossible to replicate. The "Sefirah Castle" was above the spirit world, making it relatively easy to borrow the power of the spirit world, while the "Nation of Disorder" did not necessarily have such abilities.
After thinking about it, Hobert decided to try it anyway. He locked the office door. Such a summoning didn't necessarily require an altar, but to increase the probability of success, Hobert set up a simple altar on his desk and solemnly chanted in Hermes, "I, in my name, summon the Creator in the Shadow of Order..."
After reciting the summoning incantation, he immediately entered the "Nation of Disorder" and saw a majestic bronze giant door appear at the entrance of the palace he had built. At this time, the two bronze giant doors were slightly ajar, and he could roughly hear his summons to himself.
Spreading his spirituality into it, a huge suction force sucked Hobert's entire spirit body in.
Hobert saw himself standing motionless in front of the altar with a dazed look.
He was now in spirit form and could easily pass through all obstacles unless a Beyonder activated "Spirit Vision", otherwise no one could see him.
Hobert began to try to penetrate the walls, to a greater distance. He saw Rasga and Dico discussing how to reply to letters.
Penetrating the walls again, Hobert came to the street, but soon, he encountered an invisible barrier and could no longer move forward.
As he had envisioned, the "Sefirah Castle" was above the spirit world and had the help of the spirit world, so Klein's spirit body could move long distances through the spirit world, while the "Nation of Disorder" did not have such a deep connection with the spirit world and could only support Hobert in this form to move about twenty meters away from his body.
Ending his summoning to himself, Hobert left the "Nation of Disorder" and returned to the real world, cleaning up the altar.
Sitting back in his chair, Hobert sighed. He couldn't use the method Klein used.
Then he suddenly thought of Medici's Evil Spirit. He could ask other spirits for help, but he would rather not have the "Black Emperor" card than ask Medici for help. First, Medici was currently unable to leave his territory, and second, it would only complicate matters further.
So, who to ask for help?
Spirit world creatures? For example, find a messenger of Klein's level. He believed that even if "Miss Messenger" carried her head and directly killed her way into the exhibition hall to take the Blasphemy Card, Ikanser would not dare to object.
But such "spirit world creatures" were hard to come by. Hobert decided to think about whether there were other ways first.
Teleportation Statue!
Hobert suddenly thought of the abilities of this sealed artifact. It was very suitable to use the "teleportation" ability to get the "Black Emperor" card, and even a switch should be no problem.
But the problem was, once the ability of the "Teleportation Statue" was used, it should be immediately detected, and they would definitely conduct an investigation. How to avoid the investigation?
Also, the Nighthawks had a record that the "Teleportation Statue" was in his hands. Once the "Machinery Hivemind" saw through his methods, it would be easy to expose himself.
Hobert leaned back in his chair. If he had Amon's methods, stealing something would be like a game.
He rubbed his temples, about to work first to change his mind, and talk about stealing the card later. Suddenly, Hobert thought of a way: Rafter should be used here!

Hobert's thoughts immediately cleared up. From the moment he took control of the "Nation of Disorder," the star representing Rafter had appeared in the pool in front of the "Iron Throne." Before that, Hobert didn't think this down-and-out baronet was of any use.
Only today did he realize that this guy was meant for this!
With this pawn, things would be easy. Hobert immediately had a feasible plan. He deduced it several times in his mind and didn't find any obvious loopholes.
After making up his mind, Hobert immediately got up, picked up his cane, and returned to 192 Blanca Street. This matter had to be completed as soon as possible, otherwise, in a few days, he might encounter "Huang Beibei" visiting the "Dear Daddy Memorial Exhibition," which would make the situation very complicated.
Just as Xio and Fors were out, Hobert returned to his room, locked the door, drew the curtains, and entered the "Nation of Disorder," also bringing the "Psychological Spoon" and "Spirit Necklace" into the "Nation of Disorder" by offering himself as a sacrifice.
On the star representing Rafter, there was still a thin red line wrapped around it.
Hobert's spirituality extended to the star. He saw Rafter fighting at the gambling table, and the ghost wrapped around him was also watching the game, obviously enjoying the pleasure of gambling.
After carefully observing for a while, Hobert confirmed that the power of the spirit on Rafter was still very weak, at most a clone of Medici's evil spirit.
So he waved his hand and held the "Spirit Necklace" in his hand. In his vision, Medici's ghost immediately became much more solid.
After preparing, Hobert immediately took action. Through Rafter's star, he descended his power and pulled Medici's evil spirit from Rafter's body. Immediately afterward, the surging "Power of Distortion" descended, wrapping the evil spirit. Hobert clenched his fist, and the power of distortion tightened, distorting the order in a very small area into an environment extremely unsuitable for ghosts to survive.
Poof~
Medici's ghost clone shattered, as if it had never possessed Rafter.
Hobert had deduced this operation countless times in his mind, so when he actually operated, the speed was so fast that Medici didn't even react.
In the underground ruins of Backlund, Medici was stunned: "What just happened?"
Sauron in the evil spirit said: "It's the power of distortion. I've only seen such pure power of distortion on one person, the Black Emperor is back!"
Einhorn said: "Were we really watched by the Black Emperor some time ago? Why would He target us?"
"Our plan may have been discovered by the Black Emperor," Medici said.
Einhorn sneered: "I said before, the people we possess look so stupid, this plan will definitely not succeed."
Sauron also said: "Medici, your choice has exposed us to extreme danger."
"Argue, argue," Medici said, "It's best if we're still arguing when the Black Emperor finds us."
"At worst, we'll submit to the new Black Emperor again," Sauron said, "Anyway, it's not the first time we've submitted."
Einhorn said coldly: "Does the Black Emperor need the submission of an evil spirit? What use are we? To guard His treasure, to be as loyal as Fulgrim's Hound? The thought of such a job is disgusting."
"… …"
This argument was far from over.
… …
At the gambling table, Rafter felt that his spirituality seemed to suddenly become very active, and his spirit suddenly improved a lot.
He didn't know what was wrong a few days ago. He always felt very tired, and no amount of rest helped.
The sudden change in spirit and spirituality made Rafter realize that he might be encountering something.
He looked left and right, and then opened his spiritual vision, but he couldn't see anything.
At this time, Hobert in the "Nation of Disorder" was preparing to carry out the second round of operations. He could use the stars in the pool to descend his power, but he couldn't directly capture anything with the stars.
This showed Rafter's usefulness.
After Hobert cleanly resolved Medici's possession, he began to descend the power of the "Psychological Spoon" on Rafter.
In the noisy casino, Hobert quietly hypnotized him using Rafter's star: "You suddenly don't want to gamble anymore, you suddenly really want to see the 'Roselle Memorial Exhibition'."
Rafter immediately pushed away the cards in front of him, frowned and said irritably: "No more playing, no more playing, how can playing this thing be as interesting as going to see the Roselle Memorial Exhibition?"
The casino was quiet for a while, and then everyone burst into laughter.
A gambler said: "Sir, remember to bring us souvenirs!"
Another gambler shouted: "It seems that Sir's luck is not very good today, he's so angry that he's preparing to go to the memorial exhibition."
Normally, when faced with the gamblers' sarcasm, Rafter would definitely put on the airs of a baronet and teach them a lesson.
Today, Rafter left in a hurry, just waving his hand, unwilling to entangle with the gamblers.
It wasn't until Raft got into the carriage that Hobert began to use the ability of "Psychological Cue": "When you see the 'Manuscript' left by Roselle, immediately summon a mysterious existence.
"The incantation is: I, in my name, summon the Creator in the Shadow of Order…"
Finally, Hobert instructed: "When you finish reciting this incantation, you will immediately forget the content of this revered name."
… …
On the first day of the Roselle Memorial Exhibition, this day was not a day off, but the number of people visiting the exhibition still exceeded the expectations of the Church of Steam and Machinery. At nine o'clock, there was a long queue at the ticket office, and at around ten o'clock, there was also a long queue at the entrance.
At around one o'clock in the afternoon, the trend of congestion had not been alleviated.
This made Ikanser, who was in charge of security work, have to sigh at the appeal of Roselle, this legendary figure.
At the most crowded time, Ikanser saw Archbishop Horamick getting out of the carriage with two friends, obviously also here to visit the memorial exhibition.
Horamick is not only the Archbishop of the Church of Steam and Machinery in Backlund, but also a well-known scientist and honorary professor of the Physics Department of Backlund University.
They all had VIP tickets and entered directly from the side door.
Ikanser quickly stepped forward: "Your Excellency Archbishop!"
Horamick nodded. He looked at each guide, each followed by a large group of people: "Do a good job in security, don't let stampedes occur, and also pay attention to the distance between visitors and exhibits."
"Yes, we have done relevant rehearsals. This way, please." Ikanser personally gave them the explanation.
When they came to the "Roselle's Notes" exhibition cabinet, Ikanser introduced: "As we all know, what is used above is the mysterious symbols created by Roselle, and these symbols have not been deciphered by people so far.
"Many historians and archaeologists believe that these notes should record the unknown secrets of Emperor Roselle."
Two friends of Archbishop Horamick were examining those notes when suddenly a visitor interjected: "Could this be the curse left by Roselle? After all, he had so many regrets when he died."
Ikanser looked back and saw that the person who interjected was a middle-aged man with graying temples and puffy eye bags, but judging from his clothes, he should be a figure in the upper class.
"Are you also full of curiosity about these notes?" Ikanser asked.
"No," the middle-aged man said, "I'm very interested in Roselle's study. There are so many people!"
The middle-aged man without a VIP ticket shouted: "Make way, make way, make way for Sir Rafter Pound!"
Hobert, who had been paying attention to Rafter, smiled in his heart when he saw this scene: Sir Rafter has come to compete to be a pawn.

When Hobert saw Ikanser, he was a little nervous, fearing that the other party would notice his gaze.

Hobert couldn't help but wonder, could he be so unlucky as to run into the Archbishop of the Church of Steam and Machinery?
Fortunately, the old man only seemed to notice something and glanced at Rafter a few more times.
This was the reason Hobert used "psychological cue" instead of "hypnosis." Although "hypnosis" was more effective, people who had been "hypnotized" would always reveal some abnormalities in their words and actions.
Using "psychological cue" was much better, and it was difficult for security personnel to detect.

Ikanser smiled and continued to explain to the Archbishop and his two friends.
Horamick, the old man, also shook his head slightly and stopped paying attention to Rafter.
Hobert breathed a sigh of relief and followed Rafter into the study area.
The study area was some distance away from the notebook area. Hobert re-rehearsed the plan and felt that even with Ikanser and the old man present, he was still confident in obtaining the "Black Emperor" card.
So the plan continued.
Hobert knew very well that once such a plan was implemented, it had to continue unless it completely failed.
If he started over, other problems might arise.
… …
Because Jessica and Carrie had VIP tickets, no one would drive them away.
So Carrie simply skipped lunch and took notes furiously while flipping through the high-quality replica of the "Manuscript" provided by the exhibition hall.
Jessica also helped her friend organize her notes, and inadvertently, she saw Rafter.
Jessica quickly tugged at Carrie and pointed at Rafter.
Carrie said coldly, "If he dares to pester me here, I'll kick him out."
The two of them stared at Rafter coldly, but strangely, Rafter clearly saw them, but immediately looked away.
Jessica also noticed this: "He seems to be looking for something."
When Carrie saw Rafter's gaze stop on the original "Manuscript," she said with disdain: "This kind of scum, what does he know about creativity?"
But then, the two ladies seemed to notice something was wrong with Rafter. He lowered his head as if he was praying, but soon, a surging power descended, tearing open a space above Rafter's head. Then, two majestic bronze doors appeared in the ladies' vision.
Immediately afterwards, a terrifying force swept up the original "Manuscript."
The crowd suddenly became chaotic. Although ordinary people could not see the two bronze giant doors, they could feel the powerful pressure emanating from the giant doors. Their less sensitive spirituality also made their spirits terrified and panicked, and they ran around holding their heads.
The peaceful exhibition scene just now was suddenly filled with screams and cries.
Carrie's eyes narrowed: "Some hidden existence is trying to steal Roselle's 'Manuscript'!"
"This can't even be called stealing anymore," Jessica smiled helplessly. This was simply robbery!
… …
Horamick, who was in another exhibition hall, seemed to realize something and immediately went to the study area.
However, there were too many people, and they were running around in panic, so Horamick couldn't get in at all.
Horamick stretched out the index finger of his right hand, opened the fingertip, revealing the sharp thorns inside.
Pointing upwards, the sharp thorns in his fingertip shot out with thin steel cables, nailing them to the roof.
Horamick clenched his fist, and using the pull of the rope, he rose into the air and flew over the heads of the crowd.
Entering the study area, Horamick first saw the majestic bronze giant door, and then he saw a black, blurry figure, like a spirit, steadily catching the swept-up "Manuscript."
Horamick opened his left palm, revealing a small-caliber muzzle in the palm of his hand, but there were too many people around, and so many exhibits, which made Horamick hesitate slightly.
It was this hesitation that gave the black shadow time to bow slightly to Horamick, and then, disappear!
At the same time, the bronze giant door also disappeared instantly, and the oppressive terrifying power disappeared without a trace.
Horamick's pupils changed from black to blue, but he still couldn't find the black shadow. His pupils turned red again, but he still didn't see the black shadow.
Horamick landed on the ground, scrutinizing his surroundings, hoping to find some clues.
In the end, his gaze fell on Rafter, who was full of confusion and was also running around with the crowd, holding his head.
Rafter's confused and bewildered expression was the most eye-catching, because everyone else's expressions were panic and fear.
Horamick ordered the security personnel to arrest Rafter: "What did you just do?"
"I don't know!" Rafter said with a bewildered expression: "Wasn't I at the casino? Why am I here?"
Horamick tightly grabbed Rafter's wrist and stared at Rafter motionlessly, as if to see through his soul.
Rafter immediately showed a very painful expression.
Three seconds later, Horamick threw away Rafter's hand: "He has been 'hypnotized'!"
… …
How Rafter escaped was completely beyond Hobert's consideration.
Because of the existence of the "Nation of Disorder," divination would also be blocked. No one knew what connection the hidden existence that took the "Manuscript" in full view at the Roselle Memorial Exhibition had with Hobert.
Hobert on the "Iron Throne" opened the "Manuscript" and searched for the bookmarks inside.
This one is so ugly, what is this lump supposed to be? Why are the graffiti on these bookmarks so ugly?
Only two of them are drawn decently, one of which is the "Black Emperor" card, which depicts Roselle sitting on the throne.
Even in the "Nation of Disorder," he couldn't feel the specialness of the "Black Emperor" card, but Hobert's spirituality could faintly feel that this bookmark seemed a little special.
"Bernadette!" Hobert chanted the incantation in Hermes, and the bookmark in his hand suddenly sank, emitting a clear brilliance.
On the card, the image of Emperor Roselle became more three-dimensional and more realistic. He sat on an ancient stone throne, wearing a black crown inlaid with various gems, wearing black armor, covered with a black cloak, holding a scepter, and looking forward with cold eyes.
The original flat card became like a notebook with thickness, and star-like fonts condensed in the upper left corner of the card:
"Sequence 0: Black Emperor"
Finally got it. Hobert smiled and immediately looked at the blasphemy card, skipping the parts from Sequence 9 to Sequence 6, and looking directly at the sequences above that.
"Sequence 5: Mentor of Disorder
Order and chaos are opposites, but they also encompass each other. There is a code of chaos in order; when people are tired of chaos, order will inevitably appear.
The Beyonder of this sequence can plunge the order of a certain area into chaos. He will become very majestic, making people unconsciously submit to him. They already have their own understanding of order, distortion, and chaos. Usually, they will teach several students to spread their understanding of order and distortion, and to verify their ideas.
Potion Formula:
Main Materials: Complete crystal of the Crown Tree, heart of the Phantom Chameleon.
Auxiliary Materials: 10 ml of Crown Tree sap, one black giant golden monster flower, 10 grams of Dragon-patterned Tree bark, 80 ml of white wine stored for more than three years.
Ritual: There must be a territory belonging to oneself, and the potion must be taken in the heartfelt support and recognition of the people in the territory."

Seeing the content on the Blasphemy Card, Hobert was a little surprised, never expecting it to describe the various sequences.
The first part of the description was a guide on how to act, while the second part described the sequence's main abilities and people's impressions of the Beyonder.
What a bargain!
Absolutely worth it!
For Hobert, it was just abandoning a "small account," but he obtained his complete sequence potion formula and so much valuable information.
He hurriedly looked at the following content:
"Sequence 4: Earl of the Fallen
Main Materials: The complete essence of a Black Mist Lord Tree, the complete brain of a Six-Legged Imp.
Supplementary Materials: 20 ml of Black Mist Lord Tree sap, 12 grams of Six-Legged Imp bone marrow, 15 grams of powdered Atle Flower, 70 ml of white wine aged for more than ten years.
Ritual: Orchestrate a conspiracy about power. The strength of the conspiracy's victims must be at the same level as or higher than that of the conspirator. Obtain all the victim's authority and wealth in this conspiracy, and consume the potion amidst the victim's despair and pain, and the support of the people belonging to the victim."
Hobert was stunned. Why was there no description for Sequence 4?
He looked further, and there was no description for Sequence 3, Frenzied Mage, either. It seemed that the sequence descriptions only went up to Sequence 5.
Then Hobert looked again at the advancement rituals for Sequence 5 and Sequence 4. Sequence 6 was "Baron of Corruption ," which meant "corrupting" the people in his territory, but he still had to make them sincerely support him during the advancement?
No, no, Hobert suddenly thought that "corruption" generally doesn't affect the people. Usually, "corruption" affects colleagues or superiors.
Hobert had an idea of how to play the role of a baron: corrupt superiors, treat the people well? Uh, sometimes giving them preferential treatment doesn't necessarily mean they will support you.
Hobert thought: The core of the acting is there, now all that's missing is the title and territory of a baron. Heh, it's not like I can just go to some baron's territory and "start working" anytime.
As for the Sequence 4 advancement ritual, Hobert seemed to remember that the ancient name of Sequence 5, "Mentor of Disorder," was something like viscount.
Does that mean that a viscount has to seize the territory and authority of another viscount to complete the ritual? Uh, this is really a "rebellion pathway." Hobert wondered if he should find some time to seriously recall the contents of Selected Works of Mao Zedong?
After pondering for a while, Hobert realized that instead of considering these rituals, he should rather think about how to become a baron.
Then Hobert looked at the description of Sequence 7: "Order cannot be shaken, but it can be biased in your favor by bribing the agents of order, allowing loopholes to appear in order and rules. Order is not meant to be obeyed; its existence only tells people: When your strength is not strong enough, you must learn to obey the arrangements of the strong.
This sequence's Beyonders might not be bad people, but they will always exhibit characteristics such as flattery and fawning. Anything they give may be a bribe. A true briber has understood the true meaning of 'loopholes.'"
"The true meaning of 'loopholes'!"
Hobert keenly grasped the key words. Because he needed to understand "the true meaning of 'loopholes,'" the ability to "find loopholes" that he possessed since Sequence 9 didn't become correspondingly stronger?
He immediately realized that this was something to pay attention to in future "acting."
As for the expressions of flattery and fawning, Hobert estimated that it should be an "occupational disease" when playing the role of "briber," but Hobert himself could avoid such expressions because he had found a shortcut to acting: bribing gods!
As for the core of acting described by the Blasphemy Card, it can be summarized as finding ways to make order and rules beneficial to oneself, which is similar to Hobert's previous ideas.
After understanding the relevant information that he needed to focus on now, Hobert re-gripped the Blasphemy Card. Its high level and its connection to the same pathway as the "Nation of Disorder" allowed Hobert to operate the power of the "Nation of Disorder" with ease.
The "Nation of Disorder" space that he could control didn't change much, but the operation of its space became more diverse.
For example, the mountain below the "Iron Throne." Now, if Hobert wanted to, he could change the terrain of the mountain at any time and turn it into a plain. This was an operation that was impossible before.
Of course, the greater role of the "Black Emperor" card was to greatly increase the power that Hobert could descend, especially his control over these powers was greatly strengthened.
Before, Hobert only had an empty shell in the "Nation of Disorder," but now he really had some of the strength of an "Evil God." The role of the "Black Emperor" card in the "Nation of Disorder" was definitely greater than in the "Sefirah Castle"!
If Hobert, holding the "Black Emperor" card at this time, encountered a spawn of an Evil God, he wouldn't need the help of that "black eye" at all. Hobert's own power would be completely capable of crushing that little brat.
In addition, the Blasphemy Card had greatly changed Hobert's level. In the eyes of the outside world, the person sitting on the "Iron Throne" at this time was no different from the "Black Emperor" himself.
At this time, going to swindle... cough, cough, going to scare enemies, the probability of success was higher. Even the spawn of an Evil God wouldn't dare to look directly at him now.
Reluctantly putting down the "Black Emperor" card, Hobert considered what impact his actions today would have.
First of all, he was holding the "Spirit Necklace" at that time, and his spirit body was very powerful, so he simply snatched the entire Manuscript. Even now, Ikanser and the others probably don't know his true purpose. In other words, they are unlikely to realize the existence of the "Blasphemy Card" now or for a long time to come.
The impact on the Steam and Machinery Church can be ignored. The biggest impact is still on Klein.
Klein will use the "Black Emperor" card in the future to save Little Sun, and play the role of "Hero Bandit Black Emperor" to digest the "Magician" potion, saving the girls locked in the basement.
Currently, Hobert has no plans to play the role of "Hero Bandit Black Emperor," and there is no way to save Little Sun. This may bring no small variables to the future. It is very likely that the one with the monocle may take advantage of the "Fool" being weak and "climb" into the "Sefirah Castle" along the connection between Little Sun and the "Sefirah Castle."
Whether it's losing the "Forsaken Land" proxy or the "Sefirah Castle" changing hands, these are results that Hobert is unwilling to accept.
But it's impossible to give the "Black Emperor" card to Klein. If it were any other card, it would be fine, but the "Black Emperor" card and the "Justiciar" card cannot.
Then how can he make the development of the situation meet his expectations?
As thoughts churned, Hobert decided to think about this problem later. Today, he should rejoice for obtaining the Blasphemy Card. Problems that he can't think of a solution for today can be left to tomorrow. If he can't think of a solution tomorrow, there are more tomorrows.
...
Outside the Roselle Memorial Exhibition, Jessica and Carrie waited for the reopening.
The venue was already crowded with people, some of whom had escaped from the exhibition hall during the previous chaos, or were asked to leave. Most people didn't know what had happened and were preparing to enter the exhibition hall to visit, and some were there to watch the excitement.
Amidst the noise, Carrie whispered to Jessica, "Does your family have any connection with any secret existence?"
Jessica shook her head: "Maybe, but I don't know."
Rafter's actions just now were evidence of Carrie's guess, but Jessica, as the illegitimate daughter of the family, had never heard her father mention this.
Just as everyone was speculating about what was going on with the chaos in the exhibition hall just now, someone suddenly shouted: "Make way for the King, pay tribute to the King!"
Everyone looked incredulously at the outer edge of the crowd, and sure enough, they saw a luxurious carriage with the royal crest stopping: it really was the King!

Inside the Roselle Memorial Exhibition hall, security personnel had completed an emergency evacuation.
In the study exhibit area, Rafter sat slumped on the ground, as if he had lost his soul, his eyes staring blankly ahead.
Horamick frowned and said, "The other party is very cautious and left no information behind."
He had just used relatively brute force methods to invade Rafter's spirit, but found no clues.
Because of this intrusion, Rafter's astral and spirit bodies suffered varying degrees of damage. For the next three to four days, he would appear dull, like a walking corpse, and it might take one or two weeks to fully recover.
Ikanser had no choice but to take out an ancient silver mirror with strange patterns from the special pouch at his waist. The mirror had "eyes" decorated with black gemstones on both sides.
Ikanser lightly brushed the mirror surface three times: "Honorable Arrodes, my question is, who instructed Raft to disrupt the order of the venue and steal Roselle's Manuscript?"
The surrounding light became deep, like paint seeping from an oil painting.
An extremely blurred picture appeared on the mirror. Ikanser looked at it carefully for a long time before determining that it was a towering bronze gate.
Such a bronze gate had appeared just now in the study exhibit area.
The picture disappeared, and blood-red words appeared on the mirror: "According to the principle of reciprocity, it's my turn to ask a question. If you lie or can't answer, you will accept the task and punishment I arrange."
Two or three seconds later, these sentences disappeared, and new words formed a question: "Do you like to solve problems with violence?"
Ikanser breathed a sigh of relief: "I don't like it."
The blood-red words disappeared, and Ikanser did not receive any punishment.
Immediately, Ikanser asked Horamick, "Your Excellency, does the bronze gate have any special significance?"
"It represents some abilities of the Death domain," Horamick said with his hands behind his back. "It also represents some sacrificial gates of the gods. As far as I know, the sacrificial gates of the Sailor pathway, the True Creator, and others are all bronze-colored."
Ikanser looked at the silver mirror in his hand: "This is the first time the Arrodes Mirror has given such a vague answer."
"This shows that the person who stole the 'Manuscript' has a very high Sequence," Horamick said. "Change your question and try to find a breakthrough from Rafter."
"Yes." Ikanser smiled helplessly and picked up the Arrodes Mirror again: "Honorable Arrodes, when did Rafter decide to visit the Roselle Memorial Exhibition?"
The mirror rippled like water, revealing a picture: Rafter was scattering sweat on the gambling table. Suddenly, his movements became a little stiff, and he began to look around. After a while, Rafter's expression changed obviously, and he stood up and said, "I'm not playing anymore. How can playing this be as interesting as going to see the Roselle Memorial Exhibition?"
(The Arrodes Mirror used text to indicate what Rafter said.)
The picture in the silver mirror ended, and everyone could see that Rafter's decision-making appearance was very wrong.
Blood-red words appeared on the mirror again: "It's my turn to ask a question. Have you ever wanted to hang up and ravage a colleague around you?"
Ikanser' face turned livid: "No."
A silver-white lightning bolt appeared out of thin air and struck Ikanser on the top of his head.
Zzzzz...
Ikanser' hair stood on end, and a little black smoke came out of his body. If he hadn't held onto the wall in advance, he would have fallen to the ground.
The other team members thought of the previous question. Since the captain doesn't like to solve problems with violence, why would he hang up and ravage someone? Or is the "ravage" here not referring to beating?
Although everyone wanted to pretend they didn't see anything, they moved away from Ikanser as if they had a telepathic connection, still betraying their inner thoughts.
Ikanser took a few seconds to recover, and then spit out a puff of black smoke: "Your Excellency, Arrodes doesn't even know who influenced Rafter."
As for the tricky questions in the mirror just now, and the consequences of answering the questions, Ikanser was already used to it.
Horamick still had his hands behind his back: "Find that casino as soon as possible and see if you can find any clues."
This demigod couldn't help frowning. He rarely encountered such an event with no clues. Not only did the Arrodes Mirror not provide clues, but he also didn't find any clues with his own abilities.
The similar cases he had encountered before were all related to true gods. Could it be...
Impossible! Horamick immediately denied his idea. The power of the black shadow in the study exhibit area was very weak, and it had nothing to do with gods, but those two bronze gates...
Just as he was thinking about this, a security guard ran over quickly: "Your Excellency, the King's carriage has arrived. Viscount Stratford wants to see you."
Horamick was stunned. Why is the King here? Is he also here to see the exhibition? Even if he wants to show that he is close to the people, there is no need to show it like this.
Before Horamick could say anything, Stratford entered with a loud laugh: "Archbishop Horamick! I am relieved to have you here. You will definitely be able to find the culprit who caused the chaos."
Viscount Stratford was the captain of the Royal Guards. He walked closer and gave a noble salute, and then said: "The King asked me to ask, who caused the chaos? Do you need help?"
Horamick smiled and said, "We are investigating."
Then he seemed to think of something: "Is the King coming to visit the Roselle Memorial Exhibition?"
"Of course not!" Viscount Stratford said: "No leader is more enlightened than King George, and Roselle is no exception."
"Yes, yes." Horamick said casually: "Then, why did the King suddenly appear here today?"
"The King suddenly recalled that he had passed by here a long time ago, and today he suddenly wanted to pass by this street to take a look."
Horamick smiled and said, "I see."
After sending away Viscount Stratford, Horamick immediately said to Ikanser: "The chaos just now was probably caused by a high-Sequence Beyonder from the Loen or Feynapotter royal family!"
He paused and then said: "The possibility of the Feynapotter royal family is higher. After all, George III was the one who was attracted here."
Ikanser immediately understood the basis for Horamick's judgment: the Law of Beyonder Characteristic Convergence!
Since the King, who was born into the "Arbiter" family, was attracted here, it must be that other High-Sequence members of that pathway are committing the crime.
The other members of the team did not understand why His Excellency the Archbishop made such a firm judgment because they did not have the relevant knowledge.
Ikanser glanced at Rafter: "What should we do with him?"
"He is just a pawn," Horamick said: "Send someone to monitor him for two weeks. If no abnormalities are found, withdraw the surveillance personnel."
As he spoke, he was already considering how to investigate the Feynapotter royal family, after all, this was the only clue to the robbery.
Hehe, let's complain about this Archbishop: this result is worse than "no result".

He also began processing the second batch of letters he had received, working with astonishing efficiency.
When it was time to leave work, Hobert stretched luxuriously, picked up his cane and briefcase, and went home.
Back in his rented apartment, Hobert only found Fors.
Upon asking, he learned that Xio had received a contact signal from the Masked Man and had gone to the agreed meeting place.
Hobert nodded, trying hard to recall. Why did he remember Xio wouldn't receive the Masked Man's commission until much later?
...
The heavy fog in Backlund blocked the sun in the sky early, and the not-so-wide street immediately became dim.
Xio arrived only a dozen seconds earlier than the agreed time. The Masked Man had not yet arrived, and she crossed her arms, vigilantly observing her surroundings.
A little over a minute later, the Masked Man appeared.
Xio said, "You're late!"
"No, I arrived earlier than you," the Masked Man said. "You seem to be a 'Sheriff' now."
Xio understood what he meant. The reason he arrived early was to use the opportunity to observe her.
"Yes," Xio admitted frankly.
"I'm curious, what is your relationship with General Christian's eldest son?"
"Does this question have anything to do with the task you're going to give me?"
"No, it doesn't," the Masked Man said gently. "You may not know, but three months ago, General Christian's eldest son was very ordinary. He seems to have been very active in the last three months, as if he suddenly became a different person."
Xio asked again, "Does this have anything to do with the task you're going to give me?"
"Still no," the Masked Man said. "Alright, let me tell you about the task I'm giving you today: track Rafter Pound, here is his information."
Xio took the Masked Man's information but did not immediately look at it. "How long do I have to track him? What is the level of danger?"
"Track him for two weeks initially, the reward is 20 pounds!" the Masked Man said. "There may be no danger, but the level of danger could also be very high."
"However, you are only responsible for tracking. If you discover any danger, you can immediately end the mission and contact me using the emergency contact method."
Xio nodded: "Okay, I accept this task."
The Masked Man took out 10 pounds in cash: "This is the deposit. When you report the tracking results in two weeks, I will give you the other 10 pounds. If any abnormalities are discovered during the mission, the mission ends, and the reward will still be paid. Oh, right, the tracking results should preferably be in the form of a written report."
...
Hobert sat on the sofa, reading the "Backlund Evening News" he had just bought. On the second page, he found the report about the chaos at the Roselle memorial exhibition this afternoon:
"...Regarding the chaos that occurred at the Roselle the Great memorial exhibition, staff claimed that it was a farce caused by a baronet because he could not buy a VIP ticket. It is reported that the exhibition area was not greatly affected, and order was quickly restored, and the exhibition reopened.
"Some viewers claimed that they saw an old man flying over their heads, and others seemed to see the outlines of two large doors in the air. As expected, Roselle was full of mystery, and his memorial exhibition was also full of mystery..."
Because it had just happened, the report on the incident was very short.
Hobert couldn't help but smile. It seemed that the Church of Steam and Machinery planned to deal with the matter lightly and did not even plan to publicly announce the theft of the "Creative Manuscript".
Holding up the newspaper, Hobert considered that, in order to show his frankness and what he had said to Ikanser before, that he was very interested in Roselle the Great, Hobert planned to visit the exhibition in the next few days.
Fors had already prepared dinner, but Xio had not yet returned, so she could only read magazines and wait.
It wasn't until around 7:30 that Xio came back with a file bag: "Thank goodness, there's such a delicious dinner waiting for me. My stomach is almost empty."
She put down the file bag and helped Fors serve the food while saying, "You don't have to wait for me."
Hobert put down the newspaper: "If we wait until eight o'clock and you still haven't returned, we'll eat first."
All three were hungry and quickly finished their dinner, then sat around the table, chatting and drinking tea.
Xio talked about the task she had just received. She would be monitoring a baronet named Rafter for the next period of time and might rarely come back for dinner.
Through Xio's description, Hobert learned that Rafter had been released.
The consequences were better than Hobert had imagined. He had originally thought that Rafter would not be able to withstand the "interrogation" and would go crazy.
He believed that the Church of Steam and Machinery would also send people to monitor Rafter. For Hobert, this baronet no longer had any value. For safety's sake, he didn't plan to observe him through the stars in the future.
The next morning, Jessica went to work as usual. Hobert held a small meeting to remind them of the precautions for the cases they had on hand.
After the meeting, Hobert had just returned to his office when Jessica knocked on the door and came in: "Lawyer Hobert, thank you again for the VIP tickets you gave us. My friend has prepared a gift for you."
As she spoke, she opened a small box, inside was a keychain with a golden badge, on which was drawn the symbol representing the "Eternal Blazing Sun": "This is a small thing my friend made herself, it's not much."
Hobert did not refuse: "Thank your friend for me."
Taking the keychain in his hand, he immediately felt the warmth of the badge.
Hobert immediately judged that a small amount of extraordinary materials from the Sun pathway had been added during the making of this keychain, giving the keychain some Beyonder characteristics of that pathway.
Although it does not have active abilities, some undead creatures will stay far away after sensing the existence of the keychain.
This was made by himself...
Hobert thought of the lady he met at the "Eye of Wisdom" gathering who was looking for the "Barbarian" potion and had contact with a wild craftsman. Could that be the combination of Jessica and Carrie?
Hobert did not expose them. He chatted with Jessica for a while. During the chat, Hobert learned from Jessica that George III had also arrived at the scene yesterday!
Hobert immediately realized that George III was attracted by himself or rather the "Nation of Disorder". It was because George III learned of this incident that he ordered people to start monitoring Rafter again.
It is estimated that the Masked Man is just one of the forces monitoring Rafter.
Thinking of this, Hobert mourned for Rafter for three seconds, no, one second. He had finally tricked the monitors by pretending to be crazy, but he didn't expect to be monitored again.
However, this monitoring should not last long, because the process of Rafter being used as a pawn is too obvious.
Then Hobert thought that in the future, the use of the power of the "Nation of Disorder" in Backlund should be restrained. Although George III's process of becoming a god was a bit hasty, and his state must be very bad, he remembered that he seemed to have used a loophole to jump directly from Sequence 5 to Sequence 1.
But with Adam's blessing, George III's current state should be very delicate, possibly more easily attracted by the power of the "Nation of Disorder" than the "King of Angels."
After talking for a while, Jessica said goodbye.
Looking at the keychain in his hand, Hobert didn't think much about it and put it in his briefcase. Although these two female Beyonders had shown enough friendliness, they were not very familiar with each other.
After a fulfilling day of work, Hobert left the office with his briefcase. He was wondering what to eat for dinner when he saw a carriage with the "Dark Sacred Emblem" blocked at the door.
Lorreta opened the door and smiled: "Time to work!"

chapters.title: Chapter 193 - 193: Joining the Nighthawks' Operation (Bonus 20)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
In the carriage, Hobert, rubbing his stomach, asked, "Is food provided?"
"Our salary doesn't include a meal allowance," Loretta said. "We can buy two simple meals at the restaurant ahead to make do."
"Alright," Hobert said. "I need to go back and grab a few things for final preparations."
"No problem."
Back at the rented house, Xio and Fors hadn't returned yet. Hobert left them a note, then went back to his bedroom and, in his own way, brought the 'Teleportation Statue,' 'Spirit Necklace,' and 'Psychological Spoon' into the real world.
Then, he checked his 'Order Wood' and 'Uncontrollable Stone,' especially the 'Uncontrollable Stone,' which should be particularly effective against the Aurora Order.
After putting on the 'Spirit Necklace,' Hobert immediately felt like he had a small heater in his pocket—Jessica's keychain!
Hobert held the keychain in his hand, feeling it was warmer than usual. It seemed he couldn't carry it with the 'Spirit Necklace' at the same time.
Putting the keychain in the drawer, Hobert did a final check of his belongings before heading to the operation site with Loretta in the carriage.
Only then did Loretta say, "After tracking Hyman, we found a total of six Aurora Order members, including Hillman, who you mentioned before."
Hobert was stunned. The Nighthawks had done a lot of work recently...
Wait, this isn't quite normal. Hobert felt like the results were too good. "Are those people really Aurora Order members?"
"I know what you're questioning," Loretta smiled. "The Aurora Order has existed for so long; their members aren't fools, of course."
"But according to our observations, Hyman is deliberately letting us discover these Aurora Order members."
Hobert immediately understood, "He wants to escape the Aurora Order's control?"
He remembered that Lanevus had done something similar.
"That's right, that's what we think too," Loretta said. "If we continue to monitor, we might find more Aurora Order members, but based on our judgment, continuing to monitor could alert them, so we decided to take action and capture all six Aurora Order members now."
Hobert nodded. This was the wisest choice. If the Aurora Order noticed the Nighthawks' surveillance, they might not even be able to catch six people.
Loretta added, "Our team has three people: you, me, and Borgia. Borgia has already arrived at the scene and has been monitoring the target.
"The target is a Sequence 7 'Shadow Ascetic.' You have experience fighting that sequence, so I don't need to explain their abilities.
"It's precisely because you have experience fighting that sequence that our team will be led by you, with me and Borgia assisting you. The captain's requirement is not to harm innocent people and to subdue the opponent, dead or alive."
She smiled, "I believe the three of us Sequence 8s should be able to handle the opponent relatively easily."
"You're wrong," Hobert said. "It's one Sequence 7 and two Sequence 8s."
"Oh, then you should quickly write an application so you can get at least 6 pounds more salary next week," Loretta said with emotion. "12 pounds a week, that's a relatively high income even among the middle class."
Hobert smiled helplessly, "Your focus is really... hard to describe."
While speaking, the carriage stopped in front of a restaurant. Hobert and Loretta went to buy a simple meal, and Loretta didn't forget to bring one for Borgia.
Then, the carriage headed to Gaspin Street 107 in the Southern Bridge District, the location of the capture operation.
The carriage stopped just after entering Gaspin Street. Hobert and Loretta got out of the car and walked for a few minutes to the surveillance point.
The surveillance point was a utility room opposite 107. As soon as he entered, Hobert smelled the dampness.
The three of them kept an eye on the opposite side while eating their simple meals. 107 was an apartment building with three floors and only one door. The target lived on the second floor. Although they couldn't directly see the target from here, they could observe them whether they went out through the door or the window.
It was currently the end of the workday, and many residents were dragging their tired bodies home after finishing a day's work.
Hobert and the others had to carefully examine everyone who came out of the apartment to prevent the target from escaping in disguise.
Borgia, upon hearing that Hobert was now Sequence 7, finally gave a more normal reaction: "Our team's combat power is excessive. We can go support other teams after completing the capture mission."
From Borgia, Hobert learned more detailed plans. The Backlund Nighthawks team had almost come out in full force for this capture operation, divided into six teams to simultaneously capture the targets at midnight.
There were a total of six targets, including one Sequence 6, Hillman, who Hobert had mentioned before, led by Thomas himself. One Sequence 7, which was the target of Hobert's team.
There were also two Sequence 8s, including Hyman. Two Sequence 9s, including Kate, who Hobert had discovered.
At first, Thomas wanted to find an opportunity for these six Aurora Order members to gather together, or for two or three of them to gather together.
But these cultists already had a set of methods to counter official Beyonders. They didn't gather at all, only communicated through single lines, and the meetings were very short, so there was no opportunity to capture them all at once.
So, they could only split into teams and capture them together.
After finishing their meals, Hobert and his team first confirmed their plan of action.
Thomas was very confident in this team. He didn't give Loretta and Borgia any instructions regarding the capture plan, so the two of them looked at Hobert.
"Since I'm the main force in this operation, please follow my command for now," Hobert said without hesitation:
"The plan doesn't need to be too complicated. You two lie in ambush on the street, and I'll attack from the direction of the door. If my attack goes smoothly, I'll drive him out, and you immediately open fire, trying to turn him into a sieve.
"If my attack doesn't go smoothly, you rush in from the windows and attack from both sides."
Hobert had used this trick when he participated in Xio's operation to capture cultists, and the effect was very good.
Borgia agreed: "The simpler the plan, the greater the chance of success."
Loretta also nodded, expressing her agreement with Hobert's plan, so they took turns monitoring, preparing to act.
Around seven or eight o'clock in the evening, the smell of food from the surrounding residents' homes permeated the entire street. Around nine o'clock, the gas lamps were gradually extinguished. By ten o'clock, there was almost no one on the street.
Hobert and the others made their final preparations, and around eleven fifty in the evening, Hobert took the lead.
He pried open the anti-theft window on the stairwell window, climbed to the second floor, holding the 'Teleportation Statue' in one hand and a gun in the other, and kicked the door open.
Hobert sighed. After Sequence 7, his strength had increased a lot.
"Hee hee hee hee hee~"
A sinister laughter came from the dark room, as if some ghostly figures were flashing.

chapters.title: Chapter 194 - 194 Hobert's Current Strength (Bonus 21)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
[Thanks to Jonathan Guedes, bonus chap release]
Hobert didn't immediately open fire upon seeing the figure because, according to the information from the "Teleportation Statue," there was only one person in the room, and these figures were just illusions.
However, the atmosphere in the room felt like the domain of the Grim Reaper, and Hobert felt a sudden sense of dread in his spirituality.
Nevertheless, Hobert stepped into the room, immediately feeling as if eyes were staring at him from all directions, making it difficult even for the "Teleportation Statue" to distinguish the real enemy.
The feeling of being surrounded by evil spirits was unbearable, and Hobert guessed that this ghost domain must be a special ability the opponent gained during the "Listener" stage.
Beyonders of that sequence often obtained many bizarre abilities from the information they gleaned while 'listening,' which were further enhanced in the "Shadow Ascetic" sequence, becoming unpredictable and formidable.
Hobert holstered his gun, took another step forward, and pulled out several "Uncontrolled Stones" from his pocket.
A series of sinister voices echoed, "Arrogant fool, do you really think you can defeat me?"
In the darkness, the figures in the room reached out to grab Hobert, and his spirituality warned him that being caught by them would cause some damage to his astral body.
Moreover, the room was filled with a chilling atmosphere of terror; although Hobert didn't find the scene particularly frightening, his spirituality was constantly trembling.
However, thanks to the "Spirit Necklace," the fear was still within an acceptable range.
Just as the shadows were about to grab Hobert, he finally made his move, throwing three "Uncontrolled Stones" in quick succession toward the direction of the voice, achieving "saturation bombardment," while chanting the incantation:
"Distort!"
"Distort!"
"Distort!"
In the room, the high-ranking power of "Distortion" erupted, and order seemed to suddenly collapse, as if everything around was shrouded in this force, becoming exceptionally fragile.
The movements of the surrounding shadows froze, like puppets with severed strings, only able to maintain their final poses.
While throwing the three "Uncontrolled Stones," Hobert also completed the process of "bribery," and then continued with his "combo move":
"Weaken!"
A large portion of the surrounding shadows immediately vanished, and the room was no longer pitch black; a few rays of light filtered in, indicating that the opponent's power had been significantly weakened.
This was the main reason why Hobert dared to be so reckless in this operation: his strength was there!
He was now Sequence 7, and he possessed many mystical items, some of which were particularly effective against Beyonders of the "Secret Supplicant" pathway, so Hobert directly chose to confront the enemy head-on.
Having been a Beyonder for so long, Hobert had roughly realized that the entire "Black Emperor" pathway, on the whole, was about challenging order and challenging rules.
Such sequences often required a spirit of daring to face enemies head-on, which was the biggest difference from the "Seer" pathway.
Hobert even considered whether Klein became "Klein the Coward" because he chose the "Seer" pathway?
Was he Klein because he was a Seer, or was he a Seer because he was Klein?
After all, each pathway had its own characteristics; the charlatan-like aura of Sequence 9 "Seer" was sometimes very annoying, and since they didn't have much self-defense ability, they could only "follow their heart's" choice.
And one of the characteristics of Sequence 9 "Lawyer" was that they liked to argue with others; because this sequence didn't have very strong abilities, they often had to endure.
By the time they reached "Barbarian," they couldn't endure anymore; at this stage, they had both the habit of arguing with others, and if they pushed the other party too far and they wanted to fight, the "Barbarian" could continue to "physically persuade" them.
Because of the difference in abilities, the Beyonder's temperament would often change accordingly; anyway, Hobert felt refreshed every time he acted recklessly, and even his spirituality would become more lively.
Of course, he would be reckless when he should be, but if the opponent was a Sequence 6, Hobert wouldn't have any psychological burden to use dirty tricks.
For example, using the "Teleportation Stone Statue" to move a "Uncontrollable Stone" under the enemy's feet to seize the initiative.
And when encountering enemies of higher sequences, he should still run when he needed to.
Recklessness didn't mean stupidity.
These thoughts were just some of Hobert's previous reflections, flashing through his mind. Returning to the scene of the capture operation, although this was originally the "Shadow Ascetic's" home turf, Hobert gained an absolute advantage as soon as he made a move.
"Got you!" Hobert laughed.
The "Teleportation Statue" finally found the "Shadow Ascetic" who was struggling to resist losing control! Now the opponent was moving slowly and was very weak, like a lamb waiting to be slaughtered.
With a "teleportation," the "Shadow Ascetic" appeared in front of Hobert.
Hobert smiled as he grabbed his gun, "Who's the fool?"
With that, he fired at the "Shadow Ascetic."
At the moment of firing, the "Shadow Ascetic" used his ability with a face full of pain, making himself ethereal to avoid Hobert's bullet.
The "Shadow Ascetic's" left shoulder suddenly swelled up, as if a new head was about to grow, because he had used his Beyonder power again, bringing him closer to losing control.
Hobert calmly fired another shot, and all the shadows in the room gathered around, and these ghostly powers helped the "Hermit" block the shot.
The "fear" atmosphere emitted by the ghost domain immediately dissipated, and the "Shadow Ascetic's" eerie abilities had been completely defeated by Hobert.
Taking advantage of the shadows blocking a shot for him, the "Shadow Ascetic" quickly jumped out of the window.
But just as he ran to the window, he was moved back by Hobert using the "Teleportation Statue."
The "Shadow Ascetic" was stunned. Didn't he just get to the front of the window? Could it be that he had signs of losing control and was hallucinating?
Hobert didn't hold back.
Bang~
He fired a third shot. The "Shadow Ascetic" didn't dare to use his Beyonder abilities anymore. He desperately dodged, taking the shot on his shoulder, and then jumped out of the window.
Whoosh~
The window was smashed by the "Shadow Ascetic," but the "Shadow Ascetic" returned to Hobert's face.
He opened his mouth wide: That's not right, wasn't I jumping out of the window? How did I jump in front of him?
If it were normal times, the "Shadow Ascetic" could have guessed that this should be the ability of an enemy's sealed item, but now his mind was full of maddening whispers, and the reason left to him was full of unreality.
Bang~
Another shot, this shot hit the "Shadow Ascetic's" head solidly.
The "Shadow Ascetic" almost instinctively etherealized his head. Although he dodged the bullet, his loss of control became more severe.
Seeing that the time was right, Hobert poured his spirituality into the "Psychological Spoon": "Madness!"
The "Shadow Ascetic" lost his last shred of reason. Just as he was about to completely lose control, Hobert fired the remaining two shots, blowing through his head.
Seeing that the opponent's loss of control was still continuing, Hobert simply put away his gun and used the "Teleportation Statue" to move the "Shadow Ascetic" to the street.
Bang bang bang bang~
Lorreta and Borgia, who were ambushing outside, fired continuously, emptying all their bullets.
The "Shadow Ascetic" fell to the ground, the signs of losing control stopped, leaving only instinctive twitches.
Lorreta blew on the muzzle of her gun: "I can collect my salary with a clear conscience after firing all the bullets."
