On the carriage back, Hobert remained tense, only truly relaxing after leaving the embassy carriage and returning to his office, where he finally let out a long breath.
Hobert calmed down, and after some deliberation and conjecture, the logic of the matter gradually became clear to him: it must have been that the "Dawn Paladin," during negotiations with Carrie, had Tim send people, or the "Judgement Group," to follow Jessica.
However, they didn't track her to the negotiation site in the suburbs, possibly because nighttime surveillance in the suburbs is easily detected, or for other reasons. They didn't know the exact movements of Hobert and his group, nor could they confirm if they were the killers...
No, no, Hobert realized that if that were the case, they would "rather believe it than not," and should have already launched retaliatory actions.
Hobert thought that at the time, he was wearing a signet ring made of "Order Crystal," making it impossible to find the culprit through extraordinary means.
The information they had should be minimal; Tim had no way to confirm the murderer.
Perhaps the only clue they had was that Hobert was also involved, likely determined later through investigation and information obtained from the "Judgement Group."
Following this clue, they could certainly find out that Hobert and Jessica left together in a carriage on Tuesday night last week.
Although the disappearance of the four members made Hobert and the other two the prime suspects, an 'Artisan' unskilled in combat, a Sequence 7, and a Sequence 9 could not possibly have silently eliminated Bolton and the others.
Based on some of Tim's questions, it was clear that they didn't believe Hobert and his group were the killers.
Therefore, Hobert and the other two would instead be used as bait to lure out the "big fish" behind them.
After today's "interrogation," Hobert believed Tim would continue to observe and only take new action after finding new clues.
Hobert decided to find an opportunity to put on his mask and use the "Travel" ability to counterattack, creating an alibi for himself and completely clearing his suspicion.
Thinking of this, Hobert frowned. If that were the case, Jessica and Carrie might be in some danger now.
Carrie had moved, so she might not be easily found by the "Judgement Group," but Jessica had been working normally during this period, making it easy for them to find her.
He was about to call Jessica in to give her a few words of warning, but before his hand could touch the bell cord, he suddenly thought: "Tim wouldn't harm Jessica and Carrie. If Tim arrested Jessica or Carrie, it would almost be like 'showing his hand'.
"If Military Intelligence Section 9 learned that the Feynapotter ambassador had suddenly captured a wild Beyonder, they would definitely investigate, and this investigation would easily lead to the 'Judgement Group'.
"The Loen royal family certainly wouldn't care about the life or death of a 'low-sequence' wild Beyonder, but they would definitely use this to extort a large sum from the Feynapotter Kingdom!
"If Tim has any brains, he wouldn't do this, but it's still necessary to prevent Jessica and Carrie from being found by the 'Judgement Group'."
Thinking of this, Hobert still pulled the bell cord.
This type of bell design was very popular in Backlund's office buildings or homes. The supervisor's side had a rope; pulling it would ring the bell on the assistant or secretary's side.
The assistant would then know the supervisor needed them and would immediately go to the supervisor's office.
The home version of the bell had the rope in the owner's room and the bell in the servant's room.
Because electricity hadn't been widely adopted yet, electric bells hadn't appeared.
A dozen seconds later, Jessica appeared at the door.
Hobert raised his chin and pointed to the opposite side of the desk: "Sit."
Jessica understood Hobert's meaning, closed the door, and sat opposite Hobert.
"Be wary of the 'Judgement Group's' retaliation in the near future. If necessary, take a leave of absence for a while. I will communicate with Barton the barrister, and you can return to work normally in two or three months."
Jessica was taken aback: "Did you receive any news?"
"Sort of," Hobert said. "That 'Dawn Paladin' is, after all, a backbone member of the 'Judgement Group,' and they will definitely investigate.
"And we had agreed to negotiate with the 'Judgement Group' at the time, and then something happened to the 'Judgement Group' members. You and Carrie are, of course, the prime suspects."
At the time of the negotiation, Hobert never thought those four Beyonders had such deep backgrounds, let alone that an ambassador would help investigate.
Hearing Hobert's explanation, Jessica visibly relaxed: "Even if they find our current residence, they would never dare to act. And with you at the law firm, I am safe. There's no need to worry."
This time, it was Hobert's turn to be surprised: "So confident?"
Jessica smiled and nodded.
Hobert smiled: "Alright. Oh, right, I prepared a few Beyonder materials for Carrie. I'll bring them back to her next week... no, I have something to do tomorrow. I'll bring them back on Saturday."
"You can hand them to Carrie yourself," Jessica said with a smile. "We trust you completely and aren't afraid of you knowing our current hiding place."
"Alright, I want to see where you're hiding that makes you so confident."
After Jessica left, Hobert spent the entire afternoon working.
Actually, he didn't have much to do. Most of the time, he was handling documents, helping his subordinate lawyers review their defense plans, and so on.
After work, Hobert took a rental carriage back to his home in the Empress Borough. As the carriage drove down the street, Hobert saw a performer putting on a "puppet show" on the side of the road.
The entertainment options of this era are scarce for a modern person like Hobert, but for the people of this era, they are already quite rich.
More refined options include dramas, operas, dances, symphonies, etc. More common options include circus performances and the "music box," also called the "magic sound box," which can often be seen on Backlund streets.
The "magic sound box" generally has the appearance of a cart with a box or some animal-like shape on it. There is a handle outside the shape. As long as the handle is wound, it can start playing music.
In fact, there is a music cylinder inside the shape. For citizens who rarely hear music, this is a good entertainment option.
This is actually a means of attracting customers. Small vendors will play music to attract many children and then sell small toys or small tools and cosmetics used by the children's mothers.
Another common option is the "puppet show." For Hobert, who has watched cartoons, puppet shows are actually nothing to see.
First of all, the balding uncle who messes up the speech while imitating the princess is very distracting, and secondly, the movements of the puppets are actually very stiff. Many times, they are actually dragged back and forth on the small stage by ropes.
However, it still attracts a lot of viewers, most of whom are children, and some citizens who have finished a day's work.
The puppet show actor's income mainly comes from the audience's tips.
The children will use their meager pennies to ask the puppet show actor to continue performing.
Today, Hobert, sitting in the carriage, glanced at the puppet show on the side of the street, and a thought suddenly occurred to him: I wonder if that balding puppet show actor is a "Marionettist"?
Along this line of thought, Hobert suddenly thought of an application of the "Nation of Disorder." He planned to go to the "Nation of Disorder" to try it out at night.
Back at home, the dining table was much quieter. At the dining table, Hobert told Christian that he planned to follow a mercenary team to explore an ancient tomb tomorrow.
"Be careful. More than the ancient tomb, you should be careful of your teammates and prevent being double-crossed by those who have been eyeing you for a long time." Christian seemed to think of something: "Don't feel burdened. Just live your normal life. There's no need to worry that your actions will conflict with me here."
Hobert nodded: "I know."
After dinner, Christian called Hobert to the study.
Arriving at the study, Hobert realized that the three mystical items had been completed: a dinner knife, a small wine glass, and a soup spoon.
The soup spoon was larger and deeper than the "Psychological Spoon," making it easy to distinguish the two.
Needless to say, this must be the master Artisan that the original owner's birth mother found to make the mystical items. Hobert didn't understand how that craftsman got involved with tableware.
The appearance of these mystical items was too distracting. He was supposed to be looking for someone to fight, but he went with a dinner knife and a dinner fork.
People who didn't know would think he was going to a restaurant to eat and went to the wrong place.
After thanking Christian, Hobert took the three mystical items and returned to his room to study them.

chapters.title: Chapter 289 - 289 Three Mystical Items Arrived
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
In addition to giving Hobert the magical items, Christian also gave him a list.
It detailed the abilities and negative effects of the three magical items. As an "Artisan", he could clearly understand the capabilities and drawbacks of the magical items he created.
First was the dinner knife, with the abilities: Travel, Blink, and Record.
Hobert was very pleased to see these abilities. Although each had its limitations, all three classic abilities of the "Apprentice" pathway had been preserved.
The limitations of the three abilities were:
"Travel" could only be used once per minute.
"Blink" was limited to five consecutive blinks, followed by a half-minute cooldown.
"Record" had no time limit, but could only record one demigod-level ability at 40% of its original power; two Sequence 5 abilities at 60% of their original power; or six Sequence 6 or lower abilities at 80% of their original power.
Compared to a true "Traveler", there were indeed many restrictions, but Hobert wasn't a "Traveler". These abilities were enough to keep him alive, just as "Hanged Man" Alger had described: enemies would find it difficult to kill him easily, and a metropolis like Backlund wouldn't be able to trap him.
Next were the negative effects: the holder would become very afraid of cats. Removing the knife would eliminate this effect.
Indeed, it was a classic trick. A fear of cats was unlikely to be exploited by enemies unless by sheer coincidence.
Hobert couldn't help but try it out. He poured his spirituality into the dinner knife, and everything around him became unreal. He re-entered the spirit world, where there was no up, down, left, or right.
In just a few seconds, he appeared in his rented room on Blanca Street, holding the dinner fork.
Looking at the dark rental room, Hobert couldn't help but smile: if Fors saw him like this, she would definitely think he had woken up from hunger.
After waiting a minute in the living room of the rental, Hobert used the "Travel" ability again and returned to his bedroom in Empress Borough.
A carriage ride that took more than an hour now only took four or five seconds. Hobert thought to himself that he would never be late again.
He continued to look at the list. Next was the small wine glass, only about two fingers thick, a metal goblet.
Its abilities were: Spirit Channeling, Corpse Manipulation, the ability to sign contracts with two Underworld creatures, and Underworld Gate.
There was also a "passive skill": Spirit Vision. As long as he wore it, he would be in a state of Spirit Vision without consuming his spirituality.
"Spirit Vision", "Spirit Channeling", and "Corpse Manipulation" were, of course, characteristic skills of the "Death" pathway.
The last two abilities were completely unexpected bonuses. Although Hobert himself couldn't create an environment similar to the Underworld and couldn't become a vessel for undead or spirit creatures, he could sign contracts with two Underworld creatures, which was equivalent to having two more assistants.
When needed, he could summon them from the Underworld with a simple incantation.
The list provided a more detailed explanation of this ability: the spirit creatures summoned using this ability were relatively high-level, and they needed to be respected to prevent them from attacking. Once a contract was signed, they wouldn't attack the holder, but they had to share the spoils of war with them, or they would tear up the contract and attack the holder.
When Hobert saw the "share the spoils" clause, he decided not to summon them easily.
"Underworld Gate" opened the gate to the Underworld. If only a crack was opened, the creatures of the Underworld would only stare at the enemy, filling their hearts with fear.
If the gate was fully opened, the creatures of the Underworld would rush to pull the enemy in, and if the enemy didn't have a proper response, they would eventually be dragged into the Underworld.
The limitation of this ability was: it had to be used with an interval of more than 24 hours, otherwise the ability couldn't be used.
As for the negative effect of the small wine glass: a chill throughout the body, no matter how thick the clothes were, or even sitting by a fire.
Hobert held the small wine glass and felt it. For him, the degree of cold was not a big problem. For ordinary people, a chill throughout the body could easily lead to a cold, but for a physically strong Beyonder, it was just cold and unlikely to cause illness.
Then Hobert sighed: with this small wine glass, the "Spirit Necklace" could be retired.
Finally, he looked at the soup spoon, which only had two abilities: Iron Skin and Rot.
"Iron Skin" was exactly the ability Hobert wanted. It was more like a passive skill, which he would have as long as he held the magical item.
"Rot" was like a "gift" ability, allowing creatures to rot quickly, withering plants, and creating a small patch of rotten mud on the ground.
It didn't seem to be of much use, only useful in specific places and specific situations.
So Hobert felt that this skill was like a freebie: useless, but reluctant to throw away.
But as long as he had the ability of "Iron Skin", it would meet Hobert's requirements.
As for the negative effect, it was greater than the sum of the previous two magical items: he would become fond of killing and bloodthirsty, and would involuntarily become cruel.
This made Hobert sigh that even the best "Artisan" was somewhat overwhelmed by the Beyonder characteristics of the "Prisoner" pathway, and it was difficult to control the negative effects of the magical items.
And these negative effects generally affected the holder's temperament.
Hobert considered using the negative effect of the "Fighting Ring" to neutralize the negative effect of the "Soup Spoon", and at the same time, he could use the "Baron of Corruption" level of "Distortion" to constantly distort the cruel and bloodthirsty thoughts.
Hobert held the soup spoon and felt it. After such neutralization and distortion, he really didn't feel much bloodlust and cruelty.
Next was the naming phase. He still named them according to their attributes. Hobert named the dinner knife "Traveler's Knife", Hobert named the small wine glass "Spirit Wine Glass", and the soup spoon was of course "Iron Soup Spoon".
When naming the soup spoon, Hobert was slightly stunned. "Iron Soup Spoon" didn't seem to express its extraordinary attributes, and "Rotten Soup Spoon" didn't sound good either.
Finally, Hobert decided: just call it "Zombie Soup Spoon"!
After equipping these three magical items, Hobert's strength reached a new level, and he became more confident in tomorrow's exploration.
Then he considered how to carry these things in combat. Hobert had encountered this problem in previous battles.
The Tang Dao would need to occupy one hand. Did he have to take it out of his pocket when he needed to use something?
Taking out all spoons, forks, and the like would be too disrespectful to the opponent. After all, he was here to fight. Why did he have to eat a meal while fighting?
The key was that it was easy to take the wrong one and it took time.
After thinking for a long time, Hobert went to the first floor and asked the maid to sew a few cloth buttons on his shirt, insert the magical items into the cloth buttons, and then carry them close to his body. When he needed to use something, he could inject spirituality into the item.
Then Hobert took down all his shirts and asked the maid to sew cloth buttons on these clothes tomorrow.
The only impact was that no matter how hot it was in the future, he couldn't just wear a shirt out, otherwise others could easily judge from the shape on the shirt that Hobert was carrying knives, forks, spoons, and the like on his chest, and he even carried a small wine glass.
Others had medals hanging on their chests, but he hung cutlery, as if he was afraid that others wouldn't know that he was a foodie.

chapters.title: Chapter 290 - 290 Puppet of Order
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Hobert returned to his bedroom, it was already past 9 PM.
He didn't feel tired, so he entered the "Nation of Disorder" to conduct the experiment he had thought of when he returned in the afternoon.
Sitting on the "Iron Throne", he first glanced at the pool of water to make sure no one was praying to him, assuming Rafter hadn't arrived in Conant yet, or if he had, he hadn't had time to go to the cemetery.
Hobert beckoned towards the stone platform, holding the skull of the Gold Horned Evil Creature in his hand.
Its skull was nothing special, just like the skull of an ordinary animal, but the two golden horns were very unique, with very bright colors, a bit like the colored gold Hobert had seen in the Common Era.
Hobert manipulated the skull, making it fly to the opposite side of the pool, then he mobilized the surging power of "Order", "Disorder", and "Distortion" and piled them onto the skull.
When these forces touched the golden horns, the three forces suddenly began to shape themselves.
After a moment's thought, Hobert let these forces pile up on their own, after all, this was in the "Nation of Disorder", and he could extract the three forces at any time.
A few seconds later, a giant beast emitting a black, illusory light appeared in front of Hobert.
It wore a black, gorgeous robe, had black, illusory hair, and its facial features were all black, but very clear, and the two golden horns began to emit a golden light.
Overall, in addition to the indescribable magical feeling, it actually had a sense of holiness and divinity.
Hobert felt it, and as he expected, he could use the connection between the "Nation of Disorder" and the monster to give the monster in front of him simple commands, such as attacking a target or protecting a target.
After all, the monster was entirely composed of the power of the "Nation of Disorder", but the two golden horns gave this monster very basic intelligence. Hobert was actually using the golden horns to control the power of the "Nation of Disorder".
This monster could also exist in the real world, and without a granting ritual, Hobert could directly project it into the real world based on the stars in the pool.
Hobert clearly understood the abilities of this monster through spiritual perception, but the magnitude of its power was not clear.
It would be best to find it an opponent to see what level of monster it was.
After thinking for a while, Hobert thought of the vague figure sealed in the pool at the foot of the mountain, so he beckoned, and the vague figure appeared in front of the monster.
Hobert ordered the monster to attack the vague figure. The golden horns on the monster's head shone brightly, and Hobert's constructed hall was immediately filled with a crazy atmosphere.
This was a mental attack. For ordinary Beyonders, as long as they saw the shining golden horns, their spiritual bodies would be injured.
All the power of filth in spirituality and all the power of madness in the spirit would become boiling, and they could completely lose their minds at any time.
This was a "group attack" skill, and its level was not low.
The vague figure hadn't even reacted before it was hit by such a fierce impact, which made it look much fainter.
Then the monster launched a second attack. It opened its mouth and let out a voice that seemed to be the most filthy sound in the world, causing the figure to instantly become corrupted. If he were a normal Beyonder, he would already be an irrational, ugly monster.
Hobert discovered that the "Nation of Disorder" seemed to be constantly providing power to the vague figure, so that he had not collapsed and had been recovering.
This made Hobert sigh: Is there a better target in the world?
Then the monster used the powers of "Order", "Disorder", and "Distortion" on the figure one after another.
This made the vague figure miserable. At first, he wanted to sit on the "Iron Throne" under Hobert's butt as usual, but later he seemed to have given up this idea and only wanted to escape the monster's attack range.
Hobert nodded, satisfied with the effect of this experiment.
He resealed the vague figure, who was already somewhat doubting his existence, back into the pool at the foot of the mountain, and Hobert drained the monster's power, and it returned to its original state of having no signs of life.
Through the experiment just now, Hobert roughly understood that the golden horns had two abilities: mental attack and filthy speech.
The levels of these two abilities were probably between Sequence 4 and Sequence 3. Hobert estimated that the Gold Horned Evil Creature should be a Sequence 3 level monster, because the process of its descent was not completed at the time, so the two golden horns could only provide Sequence 4 to Sequence 3 level.
Now that Hobert thought about it, he was still a little scared. Fortunately, he and the members of the Nighthawks team in Tingen City stopped the descent process, otherwise the consequences would have been unimaginable.
In addition, the power of the "Nation of Disorder" also allowed the monster to use the three abilities of "Order", "Disorder", and "Distortion". Due to the limitations of the monster's level, the power of these three abilities was also between Sequence 4 and Sequence 3.
Also, because this was the power of the "Nation of Disorder", and the source of the power had a very high level, even if the power did not reach Sequence 3, enemies of Sequence 3 or even Sequence 2 could be affected by these three abilities.
This monster could exist in the real world for about 5 minutes. After 5 minutes, it would collapse because the power given to it by the "Nation of Disorder" was diluted by the real world.
The power in the golden horns was not inexhaustible either. Hobert estimated that it could still be used about 10 times.
The success of this experiment greatly enriched Hobert's methods, and this could become Hobert's helper in the real world.
Hobert could completely come to the "Nation of Disorder", let this monster descend into the real world, and then use a sealing wax made of "Order Crystal" as a medium to guide the monster to its target.
Before this, Hobert could either only be in the "Nation of Disorder" or only in the real world, but now he had a channel to connect the power of the two.
This was like opening a brand new channel for Hobert. Hobert took out the eye he got from Old Neil's ritual and the umbilical cord of the evil god's offspring he got from the Blackthorn Security Company in Tingen City from the stone box and experimented with them one after another.
These two items also had the same effect as the golden horns. They could automatically shape themselves with the power of the "Nation of Disorder", and the level of the monsters formed after the shaping was quite high, actually around Sequence 2.
Unfortunately, they had the "Will of God" in them, and Hobert couldn't control them at all. The monsters they formed were constantly attacking indiscriminately.
This made Hobert sigh: Such good things can only be used in specific situations.
For the sake of easy distinction, Hobert named these three monsters separately. The monster formed by the golden horns was called "Bull Demon King", the monster formed by the black eye was called "Hundred-Eyed Demon Lord", and the monster formed by the umbilical cord of the evil god's offspring was called "Holy Infant King".
Hobert put these three special magical items back into the box one after another, satisfied with the names he gave them.
Then he tried to wrap the "Black Emperor" card with the power of the "Nation of Disorder". Although he got a majestic Black Emperor image, it was as motionless as a statue, lacking sufficient spirituality.
Wrapping a Beyonder characteristic with the power of the "Nation of Disorder" also yielded similar results. The resulting image had no autonomy at all, like a real puppet.
It seemed that not all magical items could be used.
Finally, Hobert suddenly thought, what would happen if the power of the "Nation of Disorder" was injected into the corpse of the Ancient Sun God?

chapters.title: Chapter 291 - 291: Digging Graves in the Mountains
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
The morning mist in Backlund was at its thickest, making the entire winter in Backlund feel gloomy and damp.
Thursday morning, Hobert rode in a rented carriage towards Order Square, his mood far from cheerful as he watched the people hurrying for a living in the mist, or the vagrants who looked like walking corpses.
This morning, after getting into the rented carriage, he remembered that he already had the ability to "Travel", so why bother with a carriage?
But he was already in the carriage, and considering how crowded Order Square was, using the Travel ability might be too conspicuous, so he had to take the carriage after all.
Recalling the astonishing idea from last night, Hobert was still a little afraid. What if injecting the power of the "Nation of Disorder" into the corpse of the Ancient Sun God revived the Ancient Sun God?
Perhaps this was the resurrection opportunity that the "Undying Bird" Gregrace was desperately waiting for?
Today, Hobert reconsidered this issue and felt that yesterday's idea was completely unnecessary. First of all, what he injected was the power of "Order", not the power of "Undying", which was "incompatible" with Gregrace's pathway.
Secondly, the power of Order did not have the ability to resurrect the dead, as depicted in a web novel Hobert had read.
At best, these powers could only recharge a lifeless object, allowing them to regain brief spirituality and vitality, but this was not life, only a loophole in death that would not produce intelligence.
It would not revive a certain Ancient God. On the contrary, the power of Order would also block some of the channels for that Ancient God to revive.
After all, it was normal for the "Black Emperor" to be resurrected through the loopholes in death found by the shadows of Order, but resurrections of other significance would not conform to the relevant order.
Hobert sighed, "Order is always so two-faced."
Lost in thought, he arrived at Order Square, where Austin and his six team members had already arrived.
In addition to Hobert, the new member, there was also a woman in her thirties named Lena joining the team. It was said that this lady, whose face looked as pale as a dead person, had rich experience in exploring ancient tombs, or rather, tomb raiding.
Hobert guessed that she should be a Beyonder of the "Death" pathway, but he couldn't tell her specific Sequence yet.
Once everyone was present, under Austin's command, they boarded two different carriages, and the group of nine officially set off.
There were many small Beyonder teams like this in Backlund. They were mainly divided into two categories: one was the mercenary team form, living a life of fighting and killing, or like Austin's team, searching for treasures of the Beyonder world.
The other was an organization of teachers and students, with a relatively loose organizational structure, more like a mutual aid society.
Hobert rode in the same carriage with Austin and Lena. Austin said, "Although this is the first day you two have joined our team, you are either retired officers or have inextricable connections with the military. I believe you know the importance of team discipline."
Hobert thought to himself, "Sure enough, he wants to establish the captain's authority first."
Lena nodded slowly beside him.
Austin continued, "I hope that in this operation, you can execute my orders without compromise. Many times, this may save our lives."
Hobert smiled, "That's no problem, but I also hope you can understand that respect is mutual."
The implication was: don't plan to use me as cannon fodder.
Austin frowned, but thought of Hobert's strength: "It's good that there's no problem." He didn't seem to hear Hobert's last words.
Next, Austin began to talk about some details of this operation.
According to the clues, they found the ancient tomb in the mountains northwest of Backlund, the specific location was almost in East Chester County.
Because there was no steam train directly to there, it was more convenient to travel by carriage, but it would take about 6 hours.
Hobert looked at his pocket watch. They set off around eight in the morning and would not reach their destination until two in the afternoon.
Then he sighed in his heart, in order not to expose his specific strength, he could only take the carriage with them.
It was nothing when he didn't have the "Travel" ability before, but now that he had the "Travel" ability, he couldn't use it, which made Hobert a little speechless.
After the carriage had been traveling for more than three hours, they began to enter the mountainous area, and the surrounding population gradually became sparse.
Around twelve o'clock, they stopped by the roadside for more than ten minutes and ate some dry food or simple meals.
The road gradually became desolate. At first, there was only withered grass on both sides of the road, and later the road surface also began to have grass. Because it was already winter, most of these grasses had withered, and a small part still stubbornly retained a touch of green.
According to Austin, this was the road of the forest farm. After winter, it was the time for the workers to cut wood. The cut wood would be transported out of the mountains in the spring of next year.
So the mountains were lively at this time, but there were few pedestrians and vehicles on the road.
Until they could no longer see any people, they needed to walk the remaining road. The two coachmen would camp here and guard the carriages.
Everyone carried some necessary equipment and food on their backs. There was almost no pause as they continued on their way. They were all Beyonders, and each person didn't feel burdened by a large package of equipment.
Soon, the group came to a hill. The view was good here, and they could clearly see a small basin in front of the hill.
This kind of terrain was very common in this hilly area. The surrounding peaks surrounded a basin that could be seen to the end at a glance. A small river flowed through the basin, but it was a seasonal river. Now the river was very small, and you could see a few small lakes or large puddles left by the river water on the riverbed.
Austin, who was walking at the front, said, "We can be sure that the ancient tomb is in this basin, but we have searched here carefully for more than a week and have not found any trace of the ancient tomb."
Hobert asked Lena, "If we communicate with the surrounding spirits, can we find clues to the ancient tomb?"
"The probability of getting clues is very low." Lena replied in a cold tone: "Most spirits don't care about these things. If it's a vengeful spirit in the ancient tomb, it probably won't need us to find him, he will come to us."
Hobert nodded and said to Austin, "I'll lead the way ahead."
As he spoke, he opened a black box and took out a bracelet with characteristics of the Southern Continent.
This was the Sealed Artifact that easily allowed the holder to encounter ancient tombs. If he didn't actively use it, it had two negative effects: it was easy to be hated by undead creatures; the wearer would increasingly like to tell ghost stories, and the plots in the ghost stories were easily encountered by the holder.
Hobert didn't care much about being hated by undead creatures, but he still wanted to avoid the point that the plots of ghost stories were easily encountered by the holder, so he would only wear it when it was most needed.
So Hobert led the team in front, and a team member reminded him: "The road you chose is very difficult to walk."
"That means we are on the right path!" Hobert said as he walked forward, hitting the obstructive withered grass with his cane.

chapters.title: Chapter 292 - 292 Extraordinary Mechanism in the Tomb Passage
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Actually, Hobert didn't know where to go either. He was just letting his spirituality guide him, leading the way randomly, sometimes circling around, sometimes retreating.
If it weren't for the fact that everyone else knew Hobert had an artifact that easily attracted ancient tombs, they probably would have kicked him out of the team long ago.
After stopping and starting, Hobert finally stopped in front of a small lake on a riverbed.
There was a small open space nearby where Austin and the others had camped before. It was now around four in the afternoon, so Austin left a few people here to build a camp, while he personally followed behind Hobert.
Hobert walked around the small lake several times. He looked at the lake. The water was clear, and he could see the bottom at a glance. He didn't see any structures like entrances inside.
Hobert handed the bracelet to Austin: "Take this and walk around. Don't have any specific purpose, just walk around randomly."
Austin was slightly stunned. He didn't expect Hobert to be so generous in handing over this sealed artifact to him.
For Beyonder mercenaries, sealed artifacts are rare and good things. Even if they encounter them, they are generally reluctant to buy them, after all, buying potion formulas and main materials can cost them all their savings.
What Austin didn't know was that Hobert had as many as seven mystical items on him, and also a level 2 sealed artifact. Even Hobert's cane, the stone chip in his pocket, and the sealing wax stamp on his waist were all disposable mystical items.
For Hobert, the ability of this bracelet was very tasteless, and he didn't even bother to name it.
Austin left the camp that was under construction with the bracelet, but he came back after a while. Austin was also slightly stunned, left again, and came back after a while.
Hobert smiled and said, "Alright, alright, the entrance to the ancient tomb should be under this small lake."
Everyone gathered in front of the lake, but no matter how they looked at it, it didn't look like there was an entrance to an ancient tomb.
A team member guessed: "Could it be that the tomb door is blocked by stones and mud?"
If that were the case, it would be troublesome. They would have to drain the water first, then move the stones away, and transport the mud before they could enter the ancient tomb.
Then everyone looked at each other, wondering who would dive down to explore first?
It was already winter, and the lake water was icy cold. Even Beyonders wouldn't like this feeling, and for a while, no one was willing to go down.
Lena suddenly said, "I'll find a spirit to go down and explore."
Everyone then realized the role of the new teammate.
Lena took a deep breath, the whites of her eyes turned completely black, and she stood there motionless.
Hobert guessed that this should be a Sequence 7 "Spirit Medium".
Then he roughly understood the strength of this team. Austin was a "Judge", his deputy captain was a "Briber", and the other members were all Sequence 8 and Sequence 9.
After a full seven or eight minutes, the whites of Lena's eyes returned to normal: "The tomb door is indeed below, and it's in a half-open state. The entrance is completely buried by stones and mud."
Austin asked the question that everyone was more concerned about: "It's in a half-open state?"
"Yes, someone went in a long time ago." Lena said, "But they seemed to have encountered an unknown danger and died in the tomb passage. The Beyonder characteristics have been covered with dust."
Everyone was stunned at first, then excited. Since the other party didn't succeed, not only were the treasures in the tomb chamber not taken away, but their Beyonder characteristics would also be the gains of this exploration.
Austin asked, "Who will go down to explore the entrance?"
Several team members were enthusiastic and willing to go down and explore.
Lena pointed to the highlands not far away and said, "The underwater path is difficult to walk, why not dig open the tomb passage directly from there, we might as well enter the tomb passage."
She walked to the highlands and pointed in the opposite direction of the camp: "It's probably in this position. The tomb passage is quite wide, even if we dig a little off, it doesn't matter."
Everyone quickly went to get tools, while marveling in their hearts that the two new teammates were really helpful. The ancient tomb that they had been looking for for so long was quickly found directly to the tomb passage with the cooperation of the two new teammates.
It wasn't yet the frozen soil season, and the soil here was very soft, but some intricate tree roots were more difficult to dig, but this was not difficult for the Beyonders.
At dusk, everyone had dug through the tomb passage. They threw a torch in, and they could see the dead bodies and Beyonder characteristics that Lena was talking about not far away.
Everyone discussed it and decided to have a preliminary exploration after dinner.
At dinner, because there was already a bonfire, they could eat something hot, at least drink a cup of hot tea.
During the meal, Austin made personnel assignments. The team's deputy captain, Roy, and two team members were on the ground to respond. Austin, Hobert, Lena, and three other team members went down together.
After eating and drinking, everyone sorted out their equipment and lit the horse lanterns and torches to prepare to enter the tomb passage.
Before the action, Hobert asked Deputy Captain Roy: "Do you have any candles?"
Roy was slightly stunned: "Candles are not as convenient as torches."
Hobert said: "My hometown has a custom that when entering the tomb chamber to open the coffin, you must light a candle in the northeast corner."
Roy didn't continue to ask and found a candle for Hobert.
At about seven o'clock in the evening, a team member jumped into the tomb passage first, followed closely by Austin and Lena, then the other two team members, and Hobert brought up the rear.
The tomb passage was only a little over a meter wide and two meters high. Walking in it felt a little oppressive.
The tomb passage in front was only five or six meters long. In the approximate middle position, there was a skeleton, which looked a bit old, and even the bones had turned gray.
On the skeleton, there was a gem-like Beyonder characteristic, which was very dazzling in the light.
Austin, who was walking in the front, put it in a wooden box: "I'll put it here first, and it will be distributed uniformly after we go out."
He was saying this to Lena and Hobert. From now until the end of the division of spoils, it is a high incidence period of infighting.
Then Austin checked the skeleton: "It looks like it was killed by a sharp weapon."
The skeleton's death time was too long, and it was impossible to see much useful information.
Ahead was a corner, and at the corner there was another corpse, and the Beyonder characteristics were already covered with dust.
The density of corpses was a bit too frequent.
Austin said, "From now on, cheer up!"
The team member walking in the front took out his revolver, took a deep breath, and led the way in front.
But as soon as he passed the corner, the people behind immediately noticed that this team member became wrong. He looked at the front with fascination: "What a beautiful scenery!"
While talking, he picked up the revolver and shot himself in the temple.
All this happened too fast, Austin didn't even have time to stop it, this team member was already dead.

chapters.title: Chapter 293 - 293 The World in the Painting
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Now, Austin, who was at the front of the team, looked grave. He asked those behind him, "What did you see just now? Or did you notice any clues?"
Hobert, who was at the rear, had been carrying the 'Spirit Wine Glass,' so he was constantly in a state of spiritual vision. He saw that the spiritual essence of the team member at the front was turning black, as if he had been attacked by a curse.
However, Leina, who was behind Austin, said, "My spiritual vision didn't detect anything unusual."
Hobert was taken aback by this statement. Could he have been mistaken?
He examined the dead team member again, confirming that his judgment was correct.
So, Hobert re-examined Lena, but subtly and without making it obvious, as if nothing had happened.
Austin pondered for a moment, "I'll close my eyes and try going into the corridor ahead. If there's any danger, warn me immediately!"
This was a good idea, but it reminded Hobert of some unpleasant experiences. However, he was certain that there were no high-level monsters or sealed items from the 'Death' pathway ahead; otherwise, everyone in the tomb passage would already be corpses.
Austin took a deep breath, closed his eyes, and stood at the corner. The two team members behind Lina quickly stepped forward, ready to pull back their captain if he tried to harm himself.
Everyone held their breath for one second, two seconds, three seconds.
Austin suddenly said, "I feel very curious, constantly wanting to open my eyes and look ahead, but I can resist the urge to open them by using Beyonder powers."
He returned, leaning on the wall, and breathed a long sigh of relief before saying, "Let's blindfold ourselves. As long as we don't look ahead, we can feel our way forward through the tomb passage and avoid this mechanism."
Lena immediately agreed, "Good idea."
But Hobert, at the back, said, "I don't think so. After we close our eyes, there will definitely be other mechanisms waiting for us. Perhaps the tomb owner's intention is for us to close our eyes, and then, without our sight, we'll step on other, more despairing traps."
Lena frowned, "I've explored many ancient tombs, and generally, there aren't very complex mystical mechanisms. Blindfolding ourselves should solve the problem."
Hobert smiled and shook his head, "I can't speak for ancient tombs of other pathways, but if you deal with an ancient tomb of the 'Seer' pathway according to common sense, you'll definitely fall into the tomb owner's trap."
He pointed to the ground, "See that skeleton? The previous group of explorers also had someone die in this place, but why didn't any of the other explorers make it out alive? And on the tomb passage just now, an explorer who was seriously injured also died."
When Hobert said this, everyone realized that the other members of the previous exploration team must have died in the tomb passages ahead, with only one person escaping with serious injuries, but they didn't make it out either.
The muscles on Austin's chubby face twitched slightly, "What should we do then?"
"I'll go to the front," Hobert said, "I'll lead the way."
Austin was slightly taken aback, but still reminded him, "It's very dangerous."
"Of course, I know," Hobert suddenly smiled. He had already made an assessment that the rank of the curse was not too high.
Having reached the front, Hobert held the pocket watch key made of 'Order Crystal' at his waist in one hand, and grasped his cane in the other. He stepped out of the corner of the tomb passage and looked ahead.
The tomb passage ahead wasn't long either, about three or four meters. The light from the carbide lamp revealed an oil painting hanging on the tomb passage at the corner.
Under the blue sky and white clouds, a lush green tree swayed in the wind, and as far as the eye could see, there was a verdant meadow. The clouds were low, like fluffy cotton candy that could fall from the sky at any moment.
At the end of the meadow, there seemed to be a figure, but it was very, very far away, and its appearance couldn't be seen clearly, not even whether it was male or female.
"What a beautiful scene," Hobert couldn't help but exclaim.
The people behind him were all shocked. Austin was even preparing to close his eyes and rush over to rescue Hobert.
At that moment, Hobert saw the branches in the painting actually swaying, and the meadow was rippled by a gust of wind. Hobert even felt the cool summer breeze in the gloomy and damp tomb passage.
The meadow seemed to suddenly 'leap' out of the oil painting, and the tomb passage was filled with sunlight. Hobert felt as if he was in a sea of green grass and wildflowers.
The pocket watch key in Hobert's hand prevented him from feeling any infatuation.
Just then, the figure at the end of the meadow began to move.
The figure moved quickly, approaching like a flash, and soon came into view.
It only had the shape of a person, more than two meters tall, but it was emaciated, without a head or neck. Its eyes were on its chest, with no other facial features.
This shape was somewhat similar to Hobert's impression of Xing Tian, but without Xing Tian's mighty and valiant, fearless feeling. Instead, because it was emaciated and its hands had sharp claws, it had an indescribable sense of eeriness.
After Hobert saw those evil eyes, he immediately poured his spirituality into the pocket watch key, forming a 'Wall of Order' in front of him.
Clang~
A small spark flashed on the wall of spirituality, blocking the monster's curse.
Austin and the others behind saw the black crystal-like 'Wall of Order.' They felt a strong sense of oppression and stepped back one after another.
Especially Austin, who had a new understanding of Hobert's strength. For him, this was already the second magical item on Hobert's body.
The monster that came out of the painting showed angry eyes and stretched out its claws to stab Hobert.
Hobert drew his Tang blade and rushed forward.
Clang~
The sound of metal collision was made. The monster was very strong, but apart from curses and claws, it didn't seem to have any other means of attack.
"Madness!" Hobert used the ability of the 'Psychological Spoon'.
The monster immediately fell into a state of 'Madness'. Hobert stepped forward, blocked the monster's claw with his arm, and stabbed out one of its eyes in the chest with a knife.
Hobert, strengthened by the 'Zombie Spoon', had arms as hard as steel. This claw only tore his clothes.
The severe pain quickly woke the monster from its state of 'Madness'. Its other eye was full of fear.
Hobert raised his knife and slashed from the monster's left shoulder to its right waist. The monster, cut in two, fell to the ground and struggled a few times before becoming still.
Putting away his knife, Hobert glanced at the painting, which was still a beautiful landscape painting, and the scene inside still seemed to be able to descend into reality at any time.
Hobert said to the people behind him, "Come over, this mechanism has been destroyed by me."
Austin cautiously asked, "Is it okay to open our eyes?"
Hobert said, "I'm opening my eyes right now."
Everyone then turned around the corner and saw the appearance of the monster, and they all breathed a sigh of relief. When they looked at the painting again, it was indeed a beautiful landscape painting.
One of the team members said, "Hey, at the end of the meadow, there seems to be a figure."

chapters.title: Chapter 294 - 294 The Tomb Master's Curse
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Wiping his Tang sword, Hobert also went over to take a look. Sure enough, the figure in the depths of the grass was still there, but he didn't come out of the painting again.
Hobert took the painting down, facing the picture towards the wall: "The effect of this sealed item is still there. I need to go back and study it carefully to understand its ability."
Now this painting will not bring danger to everyone for the time being.
So everyone's eyes turned to the next section of the tomb passage.
The next section of the tomb passage became much wider, and the length was only about five or six meters. At the end of the tomb passage were two tomb doors.
In the middle of the tomb passage, there were two stone statues. The stone statues looked like ancient knights, wearing armor and holding severely rusted weapons.
In front of the stone statues lay three skeletons. They seemed to have been cut in half directly, or split into two pieces. They looked very messy. It was only through the number of Beyonder characteristics that it was known that they were three skeletons.
Hobert held the Tang sword to clear the way. When he was about half a meter away from the stone statue, the eyes of the stone statue suddenly turned scarlet. They waved two rusty weapons and slashed at Hobert.
Hobert raised his sword to block one of the rusty weapons. He stepped forward and kicked one of the stone statues down.
Austin in the back also pulled out a sword made of refined iron and blocked the attack of the other stone statue.
After Hobert kicked down the stone statue, he continued to move forward, stomping on the head of the stone statue. The two red eyeballs rolled out a long way, and the stone statue completely lost its life.
He then swung his sword and chopped off the head of the other stone statue, and that stone statue also remained motionless.
Hobert's clean and neat offensive made the two team members behind him cast admiring glances.
Then their attention focused on the three skeletons. As long as they entered a certain range, the stone statues would attack the people in the tomb passage. It was conceivable that if they had come in blindfolded, they would definitely be easily killed by the stone statues.
Austin put away his sword, took out the wooden box again, and collected the Beyonder characteristics on the ground and two pairs of red eyes.
So far, they have harvested five Beyonder characteristics, one sealed item, and two pairs of mystical materials. It can be said that this exploration has made a lot of money.
The group walked past the stone statues and came to the tomb door.
Hobert asked Austin: "What are you going to do next?"
"Of course, push open or pull open the tomb door." The strength shown by Hobert made Austin's tone a lot more polite.
He had already decided that in addition to Hobert's choice, he would also give Hobert a trophy, after all, Hobert played a huge role in the exploration process.
"If that's the case, you can't push or pull." Hobert raised the Tang sword and pierced it into the tomb door.
The tomb door was made of bluestone, but under Hobert's sharp Tang sword, it was like tofu, no, there is no tofu in the North and South continents, it was as fragile as fresh cheese.
Hobert relied on his brute force to cut an irregular hole in the tomb door that could accommodate one person.
With a gentle push forward, the cut stone slab was pushed inside. Austin raised the torch and looked in. Inside was a spacious tomb chamber, with a stone coffin on the inner side of the tomb chamber, and a row of burial objects on each side.
In addition, there was also a rusty armor hanging on the wall, and a piece of animal skin that could not be seen what kind of animal it was.
Was the tomb owner a military general during his lifetime? The armor was a personal item, and the animal skin was the fur of his favorite prey?
After waiting for a while, it seemed that there was no danger inside. Austin was the first to enter, holding his sword in both hands, vigilantly looking at the tomb chamber.
After a few seconds, he asked Lena: "Are there any wraiths?"
Lena said: "No."
Only then did everyone enter the main tomb chamber one by one. Hobert took out candles from his pocket and asked, "Where is the southeast corner?"
Several people looked at each other, obviously losing their sense of direction in the winding tomb passage just now.
Hobert was helpless, so he randomly found a corner that was not in the way and lit the candle, which was a little psychological comfort to himself.
Austin and his two subordinates first looked back at the tomb door. There was a bolt on the lower part inside the tomb door, which looked like there was a mechanism.
Then Austin asked a subordinate to guard the door, and he took another subordinate to check the burial objects.
Hobert was not in a hurry to step forward, but intentionally or unintentionally stared at Lena.
The harvest in the tomb chamber was not small, there were some gold and silver utensils and gems, and a necklace. Everyone's spirituality could feel that this necklace was a magical item, but its specific ability was not clear.
The boxes containing the items were also antiques, which could be sold for a good price.
Then, everyone turned their attention to the stone coffin.
There was also a wooden box on the stone coffin, which was not locked. Austin opened it and saw a yellowed parchment paper in the wooden box, with the following written in Hermes language: Open my stone coffin, disturb my sleep, you will be cursed, take the other burial objects and leave, this is the final warning.
Several people looked at each other. In this Beyonder world, curses are real. It's just that they didn't know if the curse would have expired after thousands of years?
In the end, Austin said: "We're already here, how can we not see what's in the stone coffin?"
So everyone moved the burial objects that had been obtained to the side, and Austin and two subordinates took crowbars to open the coffin.
After a lot of effort, the coffin was finally pried open.
Hobert also came over to help, and everyone successfully pushed the stone coffin.
The things like the imagined gale blowing through, and the vicious curse echoing in the tomb chamber did not happen.
Thump~
The coffin lid fell to the ground, revealing the scene inside.
To everyone's surprise, there was only a corpse and a thick, dusty book in the coffin.
The tomb owner's Beyonder characteristics were not here. He must have died of natural causes and was not buried with him at all.
Austin muttered: "Bad luck!"
At the risk of being cursed by the tomb owner, there was nothing of value inside.
At this time, Hobert suddenly noticed that when cleaning up the burial objects just now, it was Austin and a mercenary subordinate, but when opening the coffin, it became Austin and two mercenary subordinates?
Looking at the direction of the tomb door again, the mercenary guarding the door was still there!
A mercenary was created out of thin air!
However, the light in the tomb chamber was dim, and it was not clear what the mercenary guarding the door looked like.
Hobert clenched his cane, ready to leave the tomb chamber at any time.
At this time, Austin also found that there were two subordinates around him. He took the dusty book out of the stone coffin and said: "Pete, I asked you to guard the door, so just guard the door obediently, go back!"
The young man called Pete seemed not to have heard Austin's words, and showed a strange smile.
At the same time, in the direction of the tomb door, the mercenary guarding the door asked: "Boss, did you call me just now?"
Everyone's movements stopped, and the temperature in the tomb chamber reached freezing point in an instant.

chapters.title: Chapter 295 - 295: It's really an inside job!
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Pete, who was next to Austin, suddenly lost his thickness and became like a paper man. He opened his arms and rushed towards Austin, as if to give Austin a bear hug.
Austin was too close to "Pete", and there was no time to draw his sword or dodge, not even enough time to drop the cumbersome books in his hand.
Just at this critical moment, a black blade shadow drew a beautiful arc on "Pete". Because the blade was drawn too fast, the sound of the blade could be heard throughout the tomb.
"Pete" was split in two, turning into two pieces of leather that looked like human skin and animal skin.
The one who drew the knife just now was of course Hobert.
He was originally ready to rush out of the tomb and leave this place, but he soon discovered that the animal skin hanging on the wall was gone. He immediately understood what was going on and drew his knife to save Austin.
"Human Skin Shadow." Hobert explained while putting away his knife, "Its characteristic is that it is the main material of Sequence 6 level."
At the same time, he sighed in his heart that Klein's pathway is really the spokesperson of "Mysticism". Just a Beyonder creature with a certain amount of wisdom can create such a bizarre event.
Austin had a feeling of surviving a disaster: "Storm above, thank you for letting me recruit Hobert into the team."
Hobert had saved him twice.
Boom~
Austin was about to thank Hobert when he heard a muffled gunshot from the direction of the entrance.
Everyone's attention was drawn to the direction of the tomb door. Austin dropped the book in his hand: "Quick! Return to the ground!"
He judged that this should be a warning from his teammates to the underground.
Pete, the real Pete, who was guarding the door, rushed out first, followed by Austin and another mercenary. Lena and Hobert walked at the back.
When passing the first corner, Hobert took the painting with him to see if it could be used later.
When they arrived at the entrance of the tomb passage and the ground, Austin and others stopped. They did not rush out, but chose to wait and see.
But there was no sound outside, which made Austin and the others worried about their companions outside.
Just as everyone was looking at the entrance, Lena had a dagger in her hand at some point, and stabbed it towards Austin's lower back.
Hobert noticed this and was about to kick Lena's wrist away, but Austin reacted one step faster and grabbed Lena's wrist: "Psychic Piercing!"
Lena tried to dodge in pain, but was firmly grabbed by Austin. She gritted her teeth and summoned a undead, throwing it towards Austin.
"Exile!" Austin exiled the undead, but still firmly grabbed Lena's wrist.
Hobert, who was about to take action just now, took a step back and sighed in his heart that the mercenaries in his team are generally veterans. Although Austin looks very simple and honest, it is estimated that he had long suspected that Lena had a problem and had been quietly paying attention to her every move.
And Austin made the wisest choice, to capture Lena alive when the situation outside was still unknown.
Lena endured the huge mental pressure, and the whites of her eyes turned black.
"Whip of Pain!" While being careful of the new undead offensive, Austin intensified his mental offensive against Lena, trying to make Lena's spirit collapse and faint as soon as possible.
Just when Lena was about to be unable to hold on, a giant sword composed of light suddenly pierced down from the tomb passage above Austin's head, so he had to let go of Lena and quickly dodge.
Lena's desire to survive stimulated all her potential. She jumped up suddenly, grabbed the top of the tomb passage at the entrance, and jumped out.
Boom~
Pete fired a shot and hit Lena in the back. Lena's body obviously paused, but she still jumped out of the tomb passage.
Hobert had already taken out the "Teleportation Statue". He immediately sensed that there were several Beyonders guarding the entrance, and according to his "feel", the one who stabbed the "Dawn Sword" just now should be a Sequence 5 "Guardian".
There are at least two Sequence 6s among the other people.
Although Hobert had the opportunity to move Lena back, he did not do so.
He still needed Lena to convey some wrong information and make the enemy unprepared for "Blink".
Then Hobert thought that Austin and the others had obviously been targeted long ago, and an internal agent had taken the opportunity to sneak in when they were recruiting people. After they entered the tomb passage, he did not know what method she used to notify her accomplices who were waiting not far away.
Since Lena, who had spiritual vision, did not remind that the dead mercenary team member committed suicide because of a curse, Hobert began to pay attention to her and guessed her purpose, so Hobert, who was mentally prepared, was not worried about the current situation.
"Let's rest for a while." Hobert said to Austin and others who were preparing to jump out of the entrance: "There are many enemies outside. It is best for us to go out after they relax a little."
Austin and the other three were slightly stunned, but still followed Hobert to the depths of the tomb.
Hobert put the painting against the wall and actually leaned against the wall and sat down on the tomb passage to rest: "We have consumed a lot of physical strength and energy just now, and it is difficult to maintain the best state if we rush out like this."
"That makes sense." Austin also sat down with Hobert.
Hobert added: "I have a magical item that can roughly determine that there are a total of seven or eight enemies outside, one of whom is Sequence 5."
Austin looked surprised, and then a little desperate. After wandering in the Beyonder world for so long, he of course knew the gap between Sequence 6 and Sequence 5.
Theoretically speaking, a Sequence 5 can deal with the four people in the tomb passage, and the three team members outside should have met with misfortune.
Of course, Hobert could use "Travel" to leave, but he wanted to try his new equipment through battle, so he decided to stay and fight, and it would not be too late to run if he really could not beat them.
"There are two options now." Hobert smiled: "My magical item can also send you to the ground, so I suggest that we divide the spoils that are easier to carry here, and after reaching the ground, escape in different directions.
"The second option is that I send you to the enemy's side to launch a surprise attack and try to complete a wave of counter-kills."
Austin pondered for a while before saying: "Let's divide these magical items and Beyonder characteristics. Those gold and silver utensils and jewelry are not easy to carry, so we don't need them."
In his concept, even two Sequence 6s would find it difficult to kill a Sequence 5, let alone the fact that the other party has other helpers.
Austin added: "According to the previous agreement, you choose first."
"This painting and that necklace belong to me." Hobert said.
"Okay." Austin almost ignored Hobert's request to choose two spoils, after all, this painting was also difficult for him to take away.
Austin took out the necklace and handed it to Hobert: "There are four of us in total, we will go in four directions later..."
Hobert smiled and said: "Don't get me wrong, after you escape, I will swagger out of the entrance and then start hunting!"
"You're crazy!" Austin looked surprised: "Lena will definitely tell the enemies outside all our situation. Even if we go up first, we can lure away some of the enemies, they will leave one or two masters to guard the entrance."
Hobert kept smiling on his face: "I just want to have a hearty fight!"
Austin opened his mouth wide, not knowing if Hobert was crazy? Or was he crazy?

chapters.title: Chapter 296 - 296: Sudden Attack
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Inside the tomb passage, Pete and another mercenary grew increasingly anxious, but Austin remained relatively calm, sitting across from Hobert and focusing on recovering his strength.
Watching Hobert play with the necklace, Austin still found it hard to believe that a Sequence 6 was going to challenge a Sequence 5.
After resting for about half an hour, Hobert suddenly stood up and asked, "Ready?"
Austin nodded, rising nimbly and dusting himself off, his agility belying his size.
Hobert held up the "Teleportation Statue" for one last reminder: "Appearing suddenly from outside the entrance will catch the enemy off guard, but you can't afford to be caught off guard. Once you're up there, immediately identify your escape route and don't run towards the enemy."
Austin asked, "What's the probability of victory for your counterattack?"
Hobert pondered for a moment: "I'm reasonably confident that I can defeat them, and there might even be some gains, like the already heavily injured Lena."
Austin seemed to make up his mind: "I want to join your plan."
Pete and the other subordinate were both surprised. In their minds, Austin was a cautious leader, so why would he make such a risky choice today?
Hobert was also a little surprised: "I have a way to escape in a critical moment. If there's danger, I'll leave the battlefield immediately."
That would leave Austin alone, and the result was predictable.
But the hesitation had vanished from Austin's eyes: "I have to try to avenge Roy and the others, otherwise, even if I escape the pursuers, the guilt will haunt me for the rest of my life."
Besides, he had just thought about it, and the probability of escape was very small. It was better to fight to the death and gamble that Hobert really had the ability to fight a Sequence 5.
Pete and the other mercenary were also fired up by Austin's words: "Captain, we'll join the action too!"
Austin patted them on the shoulders: "Good for you! But if you have a chance, you should still try to escape."
"You're still young."
For a moment, the atmosphere in the tomb passage became both tragic and fervent.
"Alright, with all of you joining, the odds of defeating them are even greater," Hobert said with a slight smile. "Let me explain the battle plan I just came up with."
...
As winter descended, the wilderness at night had become somewhat cold.
The campfire at Austin's mercenary team's original camp was still burning, but no one was warming themselves by the fire.
This was a simple trap. People in the dark would unconsciously be drawn to the light and instinctively move closer to it, especially when feeling insecure.
The leader of this operation, the "Guardian," leaned against a tree, a smile on his face as he stared at the entrance to the tomb passage.
Although he wasn't a "Hunter," he knew how to hunt.
In the "Guardian's" view, they now had an absolute advantage. The four prey below only had this one exit, and they just needed to wait patiently for the prey to lose their nerve and jump out. Forcing an attack on the tomb passage would not take advantage of their numerical superiority.
Most importantly, the "Guardian" knew the situation of the four enemies in the tomb passage. The captain, Austin, should be a "Judge."
There was also a new teammate named Hobert, suspected to be a "Hypnotist," because he had used the "Madness" skill and had discovered Lena's problem early on, all of which were characteristics of a "Spectator" pathway Beyonder.
In addition, he had a magical item that could create a black barrier, and a bracelet that easily discovered ancient tombs.
These two enemies were not difficult to deal with because they were not good at close combat.
The "Guardian" believed that the prey would definitely fight to the death tonight. If it was tomorrow, without water and food, they would lose their best condition.
Just then, the "Guardian's" spirituality suddenly felt disturbed, which made him slightly stunned: Could it be that the "Briber" who had escaped earlier had brought reinforcements? He hadn't heard of this mercenary team having any background.
He looked at a companion, a Sequence 6 "Conspirer."
A figure suddenly emerged behind the "Conspirer," holding a black saber and gripping the scabbard in his other hand.
According to Lena's description, this person should be the new member, Hobert. At the same time, the ability "Blink" appeared in the "Guardian's" mind.
Could the opponent be a "Traveler"?
The person who suddenly appeared was, of course, Hobert. He had given the "Teleportation Statue" to Austin and had Austin "teleport" him next to a Sequence 6.
The main reason for giving the "Teleportation Statue" to Austin was that Hobert really didn't have a hand to hold it, and he didn't want to use a precious "Blink" opportunity at the beginning.
The key was that he wasn't afraid that Austin would run away with the "Teleportation Statue," after all, it had the aura of the "Nation of Disorder," making it easy to find.
Hobert's sudden appearance caught his opponents off guard. In the first couple of seconds of the battle, the "Guardian" and the others found it difficult to react effectively.
He used the fastest and most direct attack method, thrusting the Tang saber forward, stabbing towards the "Conspirer."
The "Conspirer retreated as hard as he could, while immediately causing layers of flames to appear on his body surface, but he was still half a beat too slow, and the flames on his body surface did not stop Hobert's Tang saber.
Pfft!
Hobert stabbed the "Conspirer" in the chest. At that moment, the surrounding area of dozens of meters was enveloped in the light of dawn, and time seemed to suddenly jump from night to morning.
The Sequence 5 "Light of Dawn" was much stronger than the Sequence 6.
The "Guardian," holding the "Sword of Dawn" and wearing the "Armor of Dawn," charged towards Hobert.
The injured "Conspirer," although filled with fear, thought that the sudden appearance of the enemy had startled him and didn't take it to heart.
Logically speaking, such an injury was not too serious for a "Conspirer." He simply held the Tang saber, preparing to trap Hobert or force Hobert to abandon his weapon.
Hobert didn't panic as the "Guardian" had imagined after failing to strike. Instead, he suddenly thrust the scabbard into the ground: "Order!"
In an instant, a tree more than ten meters tall, with a crown spanning tens of meters, appeared in front of the "Guardian."
The "Guardian" was slightly stunned, holding up the "Sword of Dawn" to chop down the tree.
Dong~
A sound of heavy objects colliding was heard. The "Guardian" was surprised to find that the "Sword of Dawn," which was as sharp as mud and could break through Beyonder abilities, had not caused the tree the slightest damage!
Taking advantage of this gap, Hobert pulled back the Tang saber, and the sharp blade cut off three or four fingers from the "Conspirer."
In his hand that was originally holding the scabbard, there was now a piece of stone: "Disorder!"
The stone was thrown towards the "Guardian" and others who had come to support, and their Beyonder characteristics were all affected to varying degrees.
"Weaken!"
The "Guardian," whose "Sword of Dawn" was visibly dimmer, wondered: Which pathway Beyonder is this kid from?

chapters.title: Chapter 297 - 297 Battle Sequence 5
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
When Hobert used "Weaken", his raid was already successful.
The "Guardian" was obviously weakened, and the "Disorder Stone" also made him pause obviously, once again blocking his attack on Hobert.
Another Sequence 7 who came to support was affected by the "Disorder Stone" and "Weaken", standing there, trying to recover.
And a Sequence 8 who came to support the "Guardian" lost control on the spot, his flesh and blood swelled up like a blown balloon.
When he was underground, Hobert used the "Teleportation Statue" to find out the enemy's details. The enemy had a total of one Sequence 5, two Sequence 6s, two Sequence 7s and three Sequence 8s.
As Hobert expected, although his raid caught the enemy off guard, their combat literacy was not bad. They did not swarm all over to support. Only the "Guardian" brought a Sequence 7 and a Sequence 8 to support.
The other enemies are still waiting near the entrance.
This provided conditions for Hobert to cut the battlefield. After Hobert took back the knife, he quickly abandoned the "Conspirer", "Blink" to the Sequence 7, and raised his hand with a knife.
Only surprise was left in the eyes of the Sequence 7, and he couldn't react at all.
Just when the Sequence 7 was waiting to die, a barrier emitting the light of dawn appeared in front of him, blocking the fatal blow for him.
At the same time, Hobert felt a whistling sound behind him, and the fireball of the "Conspirer" had reached behind him.
So Hobert used Blink for the second time, dodged the fireball, and then used it again to come to the Sequence 8 guarding the entrance, and killed the Sequence 8 with a single knife.
It wasn't that the "Guardian" failed to use "Dawn Barrier" to block Hobert's attack in time, but according to Hobert's estimation, he used Blink three times and moved a total of nearly 20 meters. Adding the distance between him and the "Guardian" before, this has exceeded the distance where "Dawn Barrier" can be used!
At the beginning of the battle, a Sequence 8 had already died and a Sequence 8 had lost control.
The "Guardian" reminded loudly: "Be careful! He is a 'Traveler'!"
This is a huge discrepancy with the information provided by Lena!
Although Hobert also used some Beyonder abilities of the "Black Emperor" pathway, abilities like "Blink" are rarely encountered in Beyonder battles, and such magical items are even rarer. Compared with magical items, it is more likely that this is an Beyonder of this pathway, so the "Guardian" judged that this is a "Traveler".
As for the Beyonder abilities of other pathways, in the eyes of the "Guardian", they should come from the "Recording" ability of the "Traveler".
The "Guardian" and the "Conspirer" are both very fast. During the time Hobert killed someone, they had already outflanked Hobert from the left and right.
The "Conspirer" bent over and pressed on the ground. Two fire dragons set off from his hands and quickly surrounded Hobert along the ground.
Hobert was about to dodge when the "Guardian" holding the "Sword of Dawn" had already blocked Hobert's retreat.
Although the power of the "Guardian" has been greatly weakened, Hobert will still not fight him in terms of strength.
With another Blink, Hobert escaped the siege of the "Guardian" and the "Conspirer".
But as soon as he reappeared, the fireball of the "Conspirer" roared and smashed over, and the "Guardian" strode forward again holding the "Sword of Dawn", and once again blocked Hobert's retreat to dodge.
So Hobert used "Blink" for the fifth time, but as soon as he appeared, he was still within the attack range of the "Conspirer" and the "Guardian".
The "Conspirer", who had been moving, had an scarlet whip made of orange-red flames in his hand. There were barbs on the whip, and it lashed towards Hobert.
The "Guardian" appeared in another direction of Hobert, and went to block Hobert again.
The two people, one long-range and one close-range, cooperated very skillfully, especially the "Guardian". He was wearing the "Dawn Armor", which made him look a circle fatter than others. He looked like a tank rushing around the battlefield, but his speed was very agile, even as fast as the whip that the "Conspirer" lashed out.
Their "positioning" is also very advanced. Hobert, who can only move seven or eight meters with each Blink, will be within their attack range no matter how he Blinks.
The five "Blink" opportunities have been used up, and Hobert has been completely suppressed by two enemies: "Distortion!"
Hobert's "Blink" also pays attention to tactics. Although the last two Blinks looked embarrassing, they led the "Guardian" and the "Conspirer" back under the "Order Tree".
With the blessing of the "Order Tree", Hobert's "Distortion" hits every time, and without any discount.
The "Scarlet Flame Whip" that the "Conspirer" lashed out suddenly turned to the "Guardian".
Hobert took advantage of this gap to avoid the two people's attack.
The "Guardian" didn't pay attention to the "Scarlet Flame Whip" at all. The scarlet whip hit his "Dawn Armor" and drew obvious cracks, but in the "Dawn Light", the armor quickly recovered.
This is still the case when the "Guardian" is weakened, the "Dawn Armor" will have cracks, if it is in full bloom, it will only ripple slightly.
While the "Guardian" was still two or three meters away from him, Hobert already had a pocket watch in his hand. He grabbed in the direction of the "Guardian", and the surroundings suddenly dimmed, and the light of dawn disappeared.
This time Hobert stole the "Dawn Light" of the "Guardian", which is equivalent to depriving the state that is beneficial to the "Guardian".
But Hobert will not use "Dawn Light" in battle, because that is equivalent to creating a favorable environment for the enemy.
"Madness!" Just as the "Sword of Dawn" of the "Guardian" was about to fall, Hobert used a new ability.
The sanity in the "Guardian's" eyes quickly disappeared, perfectly missing the close target.
Although the "Madness" used by Hobert seems risky, it is actually not very risky, because the "Guardian" is still in a weakened state. The key is that the "Dawn Light" can block most of the Beyonder abilities for him, but now the "Dawn Light" is gone, so Hobert succeeded with one blow.
If the "Guardian" was in the "Dawn Light", "Madness" would not have much effect at all.
The "Conspirer", who had also rushed to Hobert's vicinity, moved the long whip in his hand to cover the "Guardian".
"Distortion!"
Hobert distorted the target of the long whip again, and said in a deep voice: "Gate to the Underworld!"
In the illusion, a bronze door with mysterious patterns appeared, and indescribable eyes looked out from the door, causing the fear in the "Conspirer's" heart to flood like a tide.
The battle situation has twists and turns, and now it is beneficial to Hobert again.
