chapters.title: Chapter 298 - 298 Laying the foundation for victory (Bonus 1)
chapters.content:
[Thanks to VisionaryCipher for becoming a member, +5 bonus]
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
From the moment the "Tree of Order" appeared, Hobert had been building an order that could enhance the power of the Underworld.
Not far away, the corpses of the mercenaries in the camp began to twitch again, and several times they were about to sit up again.
While the "Guardian" was in a frenzied state, Hobert immediately used the "ultimate move" of the "Spirit Wine Glass": Gate to the Underworld.
The "Conspirer" was already wounded by the Tang blade, and he had been suppressing the fear in his heart and the discomfort of his spirit body.
But at the moment when the "Gate to the Underworld" appeared, at the moment when countless indescribable eyes appeared, the fear in the "Conspirer's" heart and the injury from the Tang blade suddenly erupted at this moment, his whole body was like rusting, cold and stiff.
Immediately afterwards, pale arms stretched out from the Gate to the Underworld, pulling at the "Conspirer", and at the same time, screams that humans could hardly make directly hit the "Conspirer's" soul, causing him to tremble involuntarily.
The "Conspirer" wanted to conjure flames to burn those pale arms, but because his hands were shaking so badly, the flames flowed out of his palms like water.
Hobert took a step forward, ready to deliver the final blow, but the "Guardian" had recovered some sanity from his frenzied state, and he almost reflexively used the "Sword of Dawn" to block the blow for the "Conspirer".
So Hobert turned his blade, and with a single strike, he pierced the "Guardian's" armor.
He realized that the material rank of the Tang blade was very high, and it was estimated that even the demigod-level "Armor of Dawn" could be pierced with a single strike, but the "Light of Dawn" of the "Guardian" was not the same, it would take at least three strikes to break it.
The "Guardian" was taken aback, in his memory, the "armor" on his body had not suffered such a large area of damage for a long time.
The "Gate to the Underworld" rapidly amplified the "Guardian's" fear, and the "Guardian" involuntarily took a step back.
At this time, his reason had basically recovered, and while re-condensing the "Armor of Dawn", he was surprised why a "Gate to the Underworld" appeared in front of him?
Over there, one arm of the "Conspirer" had been pulled into the bronze gate, and a scarlet flame finally formed in his palm, but under the influence of the "Gate to the Underworld", the scarlet flame quickly changed color, turning into a ghastly green.
Not only did it have no effect on the pale arms, but it was also burning the "Conspirer's" spirit body.
Hobert was preparing to deliver the final blow again, he felt his spirituality rapidly draining away, the "Gate to the Underworld" was very useful, but the consumption of spirituality was also very large.
The "Guardian" once again used the "Light of Dawn" to block this blow for the "Conspirer", and at the same time used the "Light of Dawn" to jam the "Conspirer" at the door, and began a spiritual tug-of-war with Hobert.
Hobert's spirituality was definitely not as good as a Sequence 5, and coupled with the fact that the Sequence 7 state that was affected by the "Disorder Stone" had recovered a lot, he was pulling out his sword to help.
After a little consideration, Hobert gave up summoning the "Gate to the Underworld", the pale arms, the indescribable eyes, and the heart-wrenching howls quickly faded, became illusory, and soon disappeared.
The "Conspirer" was pale, covered in cold sweat, and collapsed on the ground.
If it was just the "Gate to the Underworld", it wouldn't have caused such a serious effect, but the "Gate to the Underworld" caused the Tang blade's injury to completely erupt, and the "Conspirer" had lost his combat effectiveness.
If he doesn't treat the injury to his spirit body as soon as possible, he may not see the sun tomorrow.
At this time, the "Guardian's" weakened state had been alleviated, his "Sword of Dawn" gradually became more solid, and he slashed heavily at Hobert.
The Sequence 7 over there saw that the "Guardian's" offensive had become sharp again, and took out a revolver and fired three shots at Hobert's back.
A new pincer attack formed.
Unfortunately, this pincer attack was not as sharp as before, Hobert simply ignored the bullets flying towards him: "Distortion!"
The "Guardian's" heavy slash deviated from the target again, and the bullets hit Hobert's back, but only made him stagger.
Sequence 7 "Weapon Master" was slightly stunned, he really didn't expect Hobert to be so "versatile", he could even withstand bullets!
Taking advantage of this gap, Hobert shouted towards the entrance of the tomb passage: "Now!"
The battle situation was much better than Hobert had expected, originally his plan was that while he was being besieged by Sequence 5, Austin and the other three would open a second battlefield as the second echelon.
At that time, Hobert would use Blink, and Austin would use the "Teleportation Statue", and strive to severely damage a Sequence 6 with the cooperation of the two.
But the current situation is that one Sequence 6 has lost combat effectiveness, and two Sequence 8s are dead and one is out of control, which greatly reduces the number gap between the two sides.
Not far from Hobert's battlefield, Pete appeared suddenly holding an oil painting.
Although it was in the dark night, the two enemies in front of Pete still saw the beautiful grass, trees, and the figure at the end of the grass under the summer sun.
The two people exclaimed at the same time: "What a wonderful landscape."
So the sinister-looking monster without a neck and head appeared and cursed the two people who exclaimed.
The two almost simultaneously took out knives and guns, ready to commit suicide.
Fortunately, they still had a companion who was not affected, a Sequence 6 "Spirit Guide", he waved his hand, and two undead appeared next to the companions who were about to commit suicide, grabbing their hands holding knives and guns.
Bang bang bang~
Pete, who was good at marksmanship, fired three shots in a row and still killed the Sequence 8 not far from him.
Seeing that his curse was not very effective, the monster raised its claws and grabbed at the Sequence 7 under the curse.
The "Spirit Guide" was about to come over to help dispel the curse, but a big fat man jumped out of the tomb passage entrance: "Death!"
Austin, who had been itching with hatred for a long time, used his most powerful attack ability as soon as he came up!
The "Spirit Guide" did not dare to neglect, and summoned an undead to block this unavoidable blow for himself.
Over there, Pete put down the oil painting and fired continuously to assist the monster, but unfortunately the monster's curse was not very strong, and the Sequence 7 had already escaped from the cursed state, and then he rolled around in embarrassment, dodging bullets and the monster's claws.
At this time, Pete's companion appeared, two mercenaries and a monster, joined forces to attack the Sequence 7.
The battle on the "Spirit Guide's" side was not optimistic either, Austin held the "Teleportation Statue", using a "Whip" on the left and a "Psychic Pierce" on the right, taking full advantage.
At this moment, a voice suddenly came from the forest: "Weaken!"
The "Spirit Guide's" power was immediately weakened, and Roy, with blood on his body, appeared pale on the edge of the battlefield.
The "Guardian" saw everything on that battlefield, he never expected that the battle situation would suddenly take a turn for the worse.

chapters.title: Chapter 299 - 299: Sequence 6 Defeats Sequence 5 (Bonus 2)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
The "Guardian" looked at Hobert in front of him again, who was still unscathed. What was most annoying was that he had never seen such a useful "Distortion" before, which was successful every time. The "Sword of Dawn" in his hand seemed to never be able to touch Hobert.
Not only that, Hobert had been using "Distortion" to influence Sequence 8, which had turned into a monster. The monster had been dealing with the "Weapon Master", making the two of them fight separately.
After a little consideration, the "Guardian" shouted, "Withdraw!"
As he said this, he stabbed out with his sword, taking the opportunity to distance himself from Hobert. Then, he strode over, picked up the "Conspirer", and was about to leave.
How could Hobert let him succeed? "Madness!"
The "Guardian" grabbed the "Conspirer" and held him in front as a shield. "Madness" hit "Conspirer".
The "Weapon Master" on the side also fired a shot, causing the monster to retreat. He took the opportunity to disengage from the battle and ran away, ignoring the others.
On the battlefield over there, a barrier emitting the light of dawn appeared in front of the "Spirit Guide" and Sequence 7, helping them escape the battle as well.
Hobert chased after them, flashing in front of the "Guardian", wanting to kill the "Conspirer", who was being used as a shield, with one strike. However, just as the knife was about to fall, a layer of "Dawn Barrier" appeared in front of the "Conspirer" again.
Hobert was a little helpless. This was the Guardian's "Dawn Barrier". Even a demigod-level frontal attack would find it difficult to break through this barrier.
Under the cover of the "Guardian", the "Spirit Guide" even conveniently picked up the Beyonder characteristic of the Sequence 8 that Hobert had killed at the beginning.
Each time the "Teleportation Statue" in Austin's hand "teleported", it would be blocked by the "Dawn Barrier", making it impossible to keep the enemy.
So, the group could only watch as the "Guardian" covered his teammates and left.
The "Guardian"'s choice was correct. Ever since the eight of them were artificially divided into two battlefields by Hobert, the battle on Hobert's side had a great advantage for them. After all, Hobert was suppressed by the "Guardian" and had almost no power to fight back.
However, the other battlefield was disadvantageous for the "Guardian" and the others. It was already a two-on-four situation, and they had no advantage in terms of numbers or sequence.
They still had the opportunity to retreat calmly. If they waited a little longer, the "Spirit Guide" and Sequence 7 on the other side would not be able to hold on and would be killed one after another. Then, it would be their group besieging a Sequence 5 and a Sequence 7.
The key was that the "Guardian" was not confident in quickly killing Hobert, otherwise the battlefield battle could continue for a while.
Originally, Hobert wanted to use the reusable "Blink" to kill one of the opponent's Sequence 7s, but after thinking about it, he gave up.
The "Guardian" and his teammates had almost left the range of the "Order Tree", and The Guardian's Light of Dawn was about to recover. Hobert thought it would be a little risky to chase after them alone.
In the blink of an eye, only a monster from the oil painting and the out-of-control Sequence 8 monster were left on the battlefield.
Hobert raised his knife and killed the out-of-control monster first, then walked towards the monster with sharp claws, knife in hand.
It seemed to have the memory of the previous monster, remembering being killed by Hobert not long ago. Seeing Hobert, the monster, who had been baring its fangs and claws, turned around and prepared to drill back into the oil painting.
Hobert sprinted forward and killed the opponent with another strike.
Austin and the others didn't know if they were experiencing a rebirth or if they couldn't believe the current result. They all stood there staring blankly at the weeds that had been ignited by the "Conspirer".
It wasn't until Hobert gave Roy a healing spell that everyone came back to their senses.
Roy noticed that his wound was healing rapidly. After thanking Hobert, he said, "Virgil is still in the grassland over there, but, but he may not make it."
"Take me over to see," Hobert said, "As long as he's not dead, there's a chance to save him."
Austin also reacted: "Everyone follow, we can't separate before returning to Backlund."
If that "Guardian" and the others wanted to turn back and ambush them, they would definitely attack the straggling companions.
While going to save people, Roy talked about what happened on the ground.
Earlier, when Hobert killed the Human-Skin Shadow in the tomb, the camp was attacked by the "Spirit Guide" who had just escaped. Roy first gave a warning to the companions in the tomb, preparing to defend the camp and wait to join Austin and the others.
However, the enemy's attack was too fierce, and Roy and Virgil, who were injured, managed to escape.
They ran for a distance and found that the enemy did not chase after them at all, as if they had no intention of pursuing them.
They had been here for more than a week before, and Roy was familiar with the surrounding terrain. He rested for a while in a hidden grass beach.
Later, Roy saw the "Light of Dawn" emitted from the camp. He carefully sneaked back and happened to meet Austin jumping out of the cave, so he immediately joined the battle.
Returning to the grass beach, Virgil was already dead, and his Beyonder characteristics had already been extracted.
Everyone was silent in front of the corpse for more than half a minute, as if mourning, and as if lamenting the fate of mercenaries.
Finally, Austin put away Virgil's Beyonder characteristics, and the other team members carried Virgil's body back to the camp.
Hobert said to Roy and the others: "To prevent accidents, Austin and I will stay in the camp, you guys hurry up and transport the things in the tomb."
Because of Hobert's performance in the battle just now, they were very convinced of Hobert's words and immediately jumped down to move things.
Hobert found a dark gray stone emitting a strong stench around the out-of-control Sequence 8.
This was the monster's Beyonder characteristic. To be precise, this should be a sealed artifact, because the Sequence 8 had lost control. Although it still had the appearance of an Beyonder characteristic, it could no longer be used as a normal Beyonder characteristic.
Austin took the Beyonder characteristic of the Sequence 8 killed by Pete and handed it to Hobert: "This is your trophy. Even now, I still feel like the experience just now was a dream.
"Storm above, we actually drove away a Sequence 5 and his subordinates!"
Hobert was not polite and put away the Beyonder characteristic: "If it was a head-on confrontation, we would definitely have no chance. The "Teleportation Statue"'s surprise attack gave us a huge advantage.
"It was also in the surprise attack that we laid the groundwork for the enemy's Sequence 6 to lose combat power."
If the enemy had always maintained a lineup of one Sequence 5 and two Sequence 6s, then this battle would have been difficult to win.
Austin smiled: "Anyway, this is enough for me to brag about for the rest of my life."
As he said this, he put the bodies of the two subordinates together, then went to the tent to get a shovel, preparing to dig a hole on the spot to bury the bodies of his companions.
When he opened the tent, he found: "Oh, it's Lena, Lena's body!"

chapters.title: Chapter 300 - 300 Candles in the Tomb (Bonus 3)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Hobert also went over to take a look and confirmed that it was Lena's corpse. She was leaning against her backpack, her eyes wide open, her face as pale as wax.
Soon, Austin determined the cause of Lena's death: "Wrist slitting suicide."
Lena's wrist was a bloody mess. The dagger used to cut her own wrist was on her body, and there was a pool of blood under her body, as if all the blood in her body had flowed out.
Her other hand, stained with her own blood, wrote a phrase on the tent.
Because it was written very sloppily, Hobert took a long time to recognize it. What Lena wrote was: Curse in the dream.
Hobert and Austin exchanged glances, neither of them understanding what this meant.
If just talking about curses, Hobert would first think of the tomb owner's curse, but what does that have to do with dreams? Could it be that the tomb owner's curse is in the dream? Or is this some kind of hint Lena gave to her teammates?
Since Lena committed suicide, was it because of the monster in the oil painting again?
In any case, Lena's suicide made Hobert remain vigilant. The tomb owner's curse may not be entirely a scare tactic.
Austin lifted Lena's body, found the iron shovel and shovel, and left the tent.
Hobert carefully examined Lena's body, and then injected spirituality into the "Spirit Wine Glass" to try to communicate with the spirit.
However, Lena had obviously been dead for more than an hour, her spirituality was already very weak, and there was no way to communicate with the spirit.
Hobert got up and quickly walked towards the Sequence 8 who had just been killed by Pete.
Now it has been more than 15 minutes since the death of this Sequence 8, but it is still possible to communicate with the spirit.
The whites of Hobert's eyes disappeared, and he grabbed the other party's spirituality. He came to the world full of gray fog again during the spirit communication.
In front of him was the blurry figure of the Sequence 8. Hobert asked: "Lena's death."
"Lena's death."
"..."
After chanting seven times silently, a picture appeared in the gray fog. Lena jumped out of the tomb passage in a disheveled manner, and she was carried into the tent by her companions.
Although she was injured, it was difficult for a gun to kill a Sequence 7. Lena leaned against her backpack and reported the situation in the tomb passage to the "Guardian" with a natural expression.
The picture changed, and when the tent was opened again, Lena's eyes were wide open and she had committed suicide.
The spirit communication picture disappeared, and Hobert's vision was blocked by gray fog again.
He recalled the picture he had just seen, which meant that Lena's companions didn't know when and why she committed suicide?
The other party's spirituality was already very weak, and Hobert quickly asked the second question: "What organization are you from?"
"What organization are you from?"
"..."
Judging from the skillful cooperation between the eight of them, they must be from a Beyonder organization, not temporary partners.
After chanting seven times silently, a new picture appeared in front of Hobert, but this time the picture was very blurry, and only a blurry figure could be barely seen.
Hobert couldn't see the other person's appearance clearly, but only heard the other person say: "Welcome to join the 'Intersea Mutual Aid Society'. Our purpose is to help each other between wild Beyonders.
"Of course, we are not a charity organization, and we will also plunder the resources and property of other organizations, and even rob the property of the Loen government if conditions permit.
"That's right, it's a disaster to hand over taxes to those fat-headed politicians to manage. Instead of letting them secretly put it into their own pockets, it's better to buy mystical materials and potion formulas from us."
The picture shattered, the spirituality of Sequence 8 completely dissipated, and Hobert automatically withdrew from spirit channeling.
Intersea Mutual Aid Society! Hobert shook his head, wondering if he was really the "Nemesis of Evil"? How could digging a grave provoke another terrifying organization in Loen?
Hobert also recalled that the eight Beyonders just now were basically from the "Warrior" and "Hunter" pathways, which completely conformed to their Feysac Empire background.
As for the "Spirit Guide", Hobert remembered that among the "Judgement Group" members he killed, there was also a "Spirit Medium". Perhaps they all obtained the magic potion formula from the Church of the God of Combat.
After all, the "Death" pathway and the "Twilight Giant" pathway are also adjacent pathways.
Austin, who was digging a pit, asked: "Did you get any clues?"
Of course, he could see that Hobert was communicating with spirits just now. Even if Hobert said that he could build a train, Austin wouldn't be surprised.
Hobert didn't hide anything: "They are from the Intersea Mutual Aid Society."
The iron shovel in Austin's hand almost fell. Obviously, he knew the "Intersea Mutual Aid Society" and also knew that he had gotten into big trouble.
But after a few seconds, he returned to normal: "I didn't hear clearly just now, and I don't care where they came from. In the future, I will honestly stay in Backlund.
"No, I will stay in Backlund for the rest of my life."
If he didn't have bad habits such as gambling, and didn't plan to advance, the gains from this grave excavation would be enough for him to spend the rest of his life.
If it was an acquaintance, such as Xio or Fors, who made a similar reaction to Austin, Hobert would definitely tell her again that the people they had just driven away were from the "Intersea Mutual Aid Society".
If the other party pretended to be deaf, he would write it down and show it to them.
It has to be said that Austin's choice was right. The main forces of the "Intersea Mutual Aid Society" are in Intersea County and Ahova County. As long as they stay in Backlund, they would not dare to retaliate blatantly.
Austin continued to dig the pit: "I'm more curious. I've been paying attention to Lena's every move. How did she contact her companions?"
"Spirits." Regarding this point, Hobert understood after learning that there was an "Spirit Guide" among Lena's companions:
"The two sides must have been communicating through the spirits. For example, when Lena used 'Spirit Communication' to drive spirits to explore the tomb door and tomb passage under the pool, she also drove a spirit to pass this message to the 'Spirit Mentor' not far away, thus completing the communication.
"This can also explain why the first echelon of the enemy's surprise attack on the camp was composed of Beyonders led by the 'Spirit Guide'.
"For example, when Lena was caught by you, she also used a spirit to inform the 'Spirit Guide' on the ground of her situation, and the 'Guardian' provided precise support under the guidance of the 'Spirit Guide'."
Austin nodded and connected these details together.
…
At this time, in the tomb chamber, Roy and two mercenary members had packed up all the gains. When they were about to leave the tomb chamber, Roy glanced at the candle that Hobert had lit in the corner of the tomb chamber, and only a small section remained.
Roy ignored the small section of candle and was the last to leave the tomb chamber.
The tomb chamber returned to silence and dimness, with only the candle in the corner burning flickeringly, giving the tomb chamber a little bit of light.
Suddenly, the candlelight "whooshed" and became higher, and the color also changed to a creepy green!

chapters.title: Chapter 301 - 301 Clues to the Frenzied Mage (Bonus 4)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Roy and the others returned to the ground, where they buried their three companions. They took only some food, water, and their grave robbing spoils. All their equipment was discarded, and they began their return journey that very night.
After walking for more than an hour, they reached the location where they had left their carriage.
The two coachmen had also been killed by the enemy, but fortunately, the enemy had not killed the horses or driven the carriage away.
So, one of the mercenary team members drove the carriage, and the group continued on their way back.
While two carriages had been needed to come, only one was sufficient for the return journey.
Only after the carriage left the mountainous area did Austin return the "Teleportation Statue" to Hobert. Once they reached the plains, villages lined both sides of the road, making it unlikely that the enemy would launch another surprise attack there.
Then, Austin laid out their spoils in the carriage and said to Hobert, "Thanks to you, we were able to bring all these things back. Choose a few more trophies for yourself."
Hobert nodded and selected a pair of red eyeballs obtained from the stone statue, the Wraith of Human Skin's characteristics, and a book from the tomb owner's sarcophagus.
Hobert suspected that the eyeballs were likely the core crystals of the Six-Winged Gargoyle, making the first two materials suitable for trading with "The World" at the Tarot Club.
As for the book, since the tomb owner had taken it into the coffin, it likely contained important content or research results. Generally, Beyonders of the "Seer" pathway were half-scholars, making this a valuable piece of Beyonder data.
As for the five Beyonder characteristics, Hobert glanced at them and saw that they were basically Sequence 9 and Sequence 8, possibly not even as valuable as the Six-Winged Gargoyle's core crystals combined.
After Hobert made his selections, Austin proceeded with the distribution. He divided the spoils into seven portions, with three of them to be converted into pounds and given to the deceased's relatives.
Austin then asked, "Mr. Hobert, if we need your help in the future, where can we find you?"
Hobert gave the address of the law firm.
Once everyone relaxed, they began to feel tired. Austin arranged the order for sentry duty and driving, then closed his eyes to rest. Soon, the sound of snoring filled the carriage.
Hobert did not sleep. He observed Austin and Pete, the three people who had entered the tomb and opened the tomb owner's sarcophagus with him. Asleep, they showed no suicidal tendencies or signs of being harmed in their dreams.
This made Hobert wonder, could the tomb owner's curse have ended with Lena?
If so, Lena was truly unlucky.
Hobert gazed out the carriage window, gradually hearing the crowing of roosters, seeing smoke rising from farmhouses, and watching as the sky slowly brightened, with farmers beginning their work in the fields.
The horses had been pulling the carriage day and night and were very tired, so the group had not been able to return to Backlund overnight.
As the outside of the carriage began to brighten, Hobert noticed that the scenery outside was somewhat familiar.
At this moment, Austin knocked on the carriage and asked, "Is this the road back to Backlund?"
Pete, who was driving, replied, "Boss, I took the wrong road, but I saw the road signs just now. This road also leads back to Backlund."
Hobert saw an abandoned villa by the roadside: "I'll get off here."
Austin was taken aback and knocked on the carriage again, telling Pete to stop.
Hobert, carrying the oil painting covered in black cloth and his personal belongings, got out of the carriage.
In a corner by the roadside, he injected his spirituality into the newly acquired necklace.
This necklace possessed some of the abilities of a "Faceless": it could transform into another person's appearance, use "Paper Substitute Doll," perform divination, and create simple illusions.
Hobert was not yet clear about the specific negative effects, but based on his spiritual perception, they were not too serious.
Using the necklace's ability, he transformed into Pete's appearance and went to the abandoned villa he had just seen.
This was the Henry family's villa. It was a case Hobert had taken on when he was Sequence 9. In this case, he had obtained the "Teleportation Statue" and established a cooperative relationship with the Nighthawks team.
Now, this ownerless villa had become somewhat dilapidated. The police tape was still there, but the door frame of the villa was still empty, and the house was full of desolation.
It was estimated that this villa would remain abandoned, as it was unlikely that anyone would buy it after people had died there.
At this moment, Hobert's spirituality sensed that someone had come out of the villa behind him.
He remembered that the owner of that villa was Mr. Polly.
Sure enough, Mr. Polly's voice sounded from behind: "Young man, are you also here to find the owner of this villa?"
Hobert was taken aback, "Also"?
He turned around and smiled slightly: "Hello, sir. Yes, I am a distant relative of their family. I haven't been in contact for a long time, and I happened to be passing by, so I came to take a look. Have they moved away?"
Polly sighed: "They're all dead."
Then, Mr. Polly began to recount the process of discovering the Henry family's bodies. Perhaps because he had signed a confidentiality agreement, Mr. Polly only spoke about the general process and omitted some details that sounded like ghost stories.
Seeing that the time was right, Hobert asked, "Has anyone else come looking for them?"
"Yes, someone came to look for the Henry family some time ago and asked me about their situation."
Hobert immediately thought: Could it be someone from the Solomon family?
He asked, "What did he look like? How old was he? I might know him."
"He looked quite old, with graying hair and beard, as if he had been traveling outside for a long time, but he looked very healthy, walking as fast as the wind."
Hobert pondered for a moment, then took out the paper and pen he carried with him: "Does he look like this?"
He began to draw the "Frenzied Mage" who had taken a "Order Wood" in Tingen City.
In this era when photography technology was not yet widespread, fine arts was a compulsory course in universities and liberal arts colleges. Almost everyone who had attended school for a few years could draw a few strokes.
Hobert was no exception. Without the help of rituals, the portrait he drew had no artistic sense or the realism of a photograph, but it still captured the vicissitudes and weary look of the "Frenzied Mage"
Before he could finish drawing, Polly said, "Yes, yes, yes, that's the old man. You really know him."
Hobert smiled: "Yes, I know him. Did he say anything else when he left?"
Polly took out his pipe, packed tobacco into it, and thought for a moment: "He said some strange things, something about a family and how it was, and that he felt some disharmony, and that the source of the disharmony came from Backlund."
Hobert nodded: "Thank you for providing the information."
He planned to stay at home and in the office for the next few days, avoiding going out and running around carelessly, lest some "Frenzied Mage" find the "source of disharmony."

chapters.title: Chapter 302 - 302: Adventure in the Dream World (Bonus 5)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for 150+ chapters advance
Hobert found a deserted corner and used "Travel" to return directly to his bedroom in Empress Borough.
Back in his familiar surroundings, Hobert finally breathed a sigh of relief.
It was still early morning, and the kitchen was already bustling, but Christian hadn't gotten up yet.
Hobert first placed the oil painting next to the desk, then changed his clothes and took a shower, preparing for a good nap.
As soon as he lay down, he couldn't help but review yesterday's battle, and he was quite satisfied with his performance.
However, the coordination of Beyonder abilities needs to be improved. Three magical items were used for the first time in actual combat yesterday, and he wasn't very proficient with them. If he had some experience, he might have been able to kill a Sequence 6 yesterday.
For example, the power of the "Underworld Gate" exceeded Hobert's imagination. Combined with the Tang Blade, it was simply a match made in heaven.
But the speed at which the "Underworld Gate" consumed spirituality far exceeded Hobert's expectations.
Also, the ability of the "Spirit Wine Glass" to summon two undead assistants should also be put on the agenda as soon as possible. If he could summon two powerful assistants, yesterday's battle wouldn't have been so passive.
In addition, there's the accumulation of "Traveler's Knife" and "Record". If he "records" the abilities of a few more Sequence 5s and Sequence 6s, it could also have unexpected effects.
Thinking about it, Hobert, already somewhat tired, felt himself gradually falling asleep.
Just as he was about to fall asleep, he suddenly felt a swelling in his lower abdomen, as if he needed to urinate urgently.
Hobert turned over, but the urge to urinate didn't subside. He got up irritably, and was about to go to the restroom when he suddenly noticed that the oil painting was standing upright at the foot of the bed.
Hobert was shocked. He clearly remembered putting the oil painting next to the desk!
Then he calmed down and went to the restroom first, but didn't urinate much.
Hobert understood that the feeling of urgency just now was a warning from his spirituality. It was conceivable that if he really fell asleep and entered the dream world, some unpredictable things would definitely happen.
After a moment's thought, he knocked on Christian's door.
When in doubt, find a backer; when in trouble, find a backer.
Christian had just finished dressing. Seeing that it was Hobert, he smiled and said, "I thought I wouldn't hear your adventure story until tonight."
Hobert smiled wryly, "I may have brought back a trouble."
Christian was stunned and let Hobert into the living room.
Hobert described his experiences of discovering the oil painting and the monster inside.
Christian asked Dophis to go to Hobert's room and bring the oil painting over.
He put his hand into the black cloth and touched the oil painting for a while: "This oil painting seems to be connected to a dream, most likely the dream of a 'High Sequence'."
Withdrawing his hand, Christian thought for a moment before saying to Hobert, "Go change into clothes suitable for battle. We have to go into the oil painting and take a look."
Hobert nodded, got up and changed out of his pajamas, put on a shirt and windbreaker, and took all his magical items and sealed items.
When he returned to the living room, Christian was also ready. He was carrying a briefcase in one hand, as if preparing to go to work: "I have a sealed artifact from a 'Spirit Warlock'."
He briefly explained and added: "Grab my arm."
Hobert took a few steps forward and grabbed Christian's arm as instructed.
Christian's other hand reached into the black cloth again and touched the oil painting, and layers of invisible ripples rippled through the surrounding air.
A second or two later, the world in front of Hobert suddenly seemed to be splashed with the colors of an oil painting, becoming extremely unreal.
Then the oil paint seemed to be smeared by something, becoming colorful. When these colors formed a new scene, Hobert found himself in a green meadow.
Not far away was a large tree full of green leaves, and the green leaves rustled in the wind.
This warm summer breeze blew on Hobert, making him feel infinitely comfortable and peaceful.
The knee-high green grass seemed to be blown into waves, which almost made Hobert exclaim again: "What a wonderful scenery!"
"This is the dream world, don't pay too much attention to the details," Christian reminded. "Here, your abilities and the abilities of your magical items are still effective.
"For example, you can use 'Travel' to take us to the hall over there."
Hobert followed Christian's finger and saw a pure black hall at the end of the grass.
In the painting, that was the location of the monster's figure, but after entering the painting, the monster turned into a hall. That should be the root of the problem.
Hobert grabbed Christian's shoulder, and the scene in front of him suddenly became unreal, but he didn't feel like he was entering the spirit world. There was just a flash in front of him, and the two of them appeared in front of the black hall.
The Gothic hall looked tall, magnificent, and oppressive.
There was no hall door in front of them. From the outside, the hall looked like a cathedral, but looking inside from the hall door, it seemed that they couldn't see the end of the hall.
They could see that the floor of the hall was covered with tulips and azaleas of various colors. Although there was no wind, these flowers swayed back and forth, looking like a sea of flowers.
In the distance, in the sea of flowers, there seemed to be many wooden statues standing. The wooden statues were also covered with flowers, giving them a strange beauty.
The top of the hall and the walls were covered with realistic murals.
Hobert saw that the content of the paintings was the monster with eyes on its chest, hunting and killing. Their prey included animals and humans.
Christian stood at the door for more than ten seconds: "There is no great danger."
As he spoke, he took the lead and entered the hall.
The monsters in the murals on the wall seemed to come alive suddenly, and together cursed Christian and Hobert.
Christian clenched his fist, forming a layer of pure white "bubbles" around him and Hobert, blocking the curses of the dozen or so monsters.
The monsters rushed out of the sea of flowers with their sharp claws. Just as Hobert was about to draw his knife, Christian used the "Spirit Warlock's" sealed artifact again, creating ripples of sleep.
The monsters suddenly stopped, and like pieces of paper, were blown back into the murals by an invisible wind.
Christian explained: "They are not real monsters. They should be the dream owner's 'impression' of these monsters."
The two of them continued forward through the sea of flowers and came to the wooden statues. Hobert quickly discovered that one of the statues looked exactly like him.
There were also wooden statues of Austin, Pete, and enemies such as the "Guardian".
Not far away on the ground, there were two seriously broken statues piled together. Hobert recognized from their faces that they seemed to belong to Lina and the mercenaries who died in the tomb passage.
The surrounding vines had begun to cover the two broken statues, and they would soon be covered by the sea of flowers.
This suddenly reminded Hobert of Lena's reminder: the curse in the dream.

chapters.title: Chapter 303 - 303 Beyonder Master Christian
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Hobert recalled the hint Lena had written on the tent before she passed away. Seeing the scene before him, Hobert suddenly understood that Lena might have been a little delirious at the time and had used the wrong grammar.
The hint should have been: The curse is in the dream.
Moreover, this "curse" is actually the curse of the oil painting. Anyone who has seen or approached the oil painting will have their own wooden sculpture in this hall.
In other words, regardless of whether the tomb owner's sarcophagus is opened or not, one will be "cursed" by the oil painting and silently killed in the dream world, or attacked by monsters again when weak.
Lena was a Beyonder of the "Death" pathway, and her spirituality was more acute than that of Beyonders of other pathways, so she probably understood the meaning of the curse before she died.
Of course, her hint before death was not for Hobert and the others, but for her companions, because as long as they saw or touched the oil painting, they would definitely suffer the same curse as her.
But how to solve this problem?
Hobert realized at this moment that he didn't have much Beyonder knowledge about dreams, and the problem he was facing was a mixture of dreams and curses, which made Hobert unable to find a good solution for a while.
If not, he could only try to move the wooden statue from the hall to the real world.
Christian, who was beside him, was also pondering with his chin pinched. After a while, he suddenly said, "Maybe that item might be useful."
He opened his briefcase and actually stretched his entire arm in to rummage.
This made Hobert couldn't help but sigh, he didn't expect that the briefcase that Christian carried to and from work every day was also a magical item.
After some rummaging, he finally found what he was looking for: a classical blower.
This was a blower that looked like it was used by a blacksmith in the Middle Ages, with two handles and pleats in the middle like an accordion. Holding the two handles and squeezing them towards the middle would blow out a gust of strong wind.
Christian threw the briefcase to Hobert. He took the blower and blew it towards Hobert's wooden statue. What blew out was a pure white smoke, and Hobert's wooden statue also seemed to turn into gas, tumbling and disappearing with the blown-out smoke.
"It really works." Christian explained: "The oil painting 'collected' some of the spirituality from you, so it can find you anytime, anywhere.
"The essence of this wooden statue is actually a wisp of your spirituality, and the blower in my hand can blow away the spiritual bodies of ordinary people. Blowing it with it will make this wisp of your spirituality disappear."
Spirituality can be recovered, so it didn't cause any substantial damage to Hobert.
Christian was about to open his briefcase to put away the blower, but Hobert quickly said, "Father, those four wooden statues are teammates who survived yesterday's exploration. Let me blow away their wooden statues too."
Christian took the briefcase and handed the blower to Hobert.
Hobert picked up the blower and blew it four times in a row, and the wooden statues of Auston and others disappeared as well.
As for the wooden statues of the "Guardian" and the others, Hobert certainly wouldn't care about them. Let them seek their own blessings.
Hobert helped Christian put away the blower and realized that Christian was looking at the murals in front.
The murals in front were completely different from the murals at the entrance. They depicted giant spiders with human faces and compound eyes.
They were weaving webs, and under the webs were people and beasts with expressions of intoxication.
"Dream Spirit Spiders." Christian explained: "Their compound eyes are one of the main materials of the 'Soul Assurer' potion.
"Your guess is right. The oil painting will use the power of the 'Dream Spirit Spiders' to sneak into your dreams and kill you in your dreams."
Hobert looked at these spiders and thought of a certain unfortunate Dragon King in "Childhood Classics."
In the Beyonder world, killing someone in a dream doesn't seem too difficult.
Christian took off a gray button from his clothes: "This is the sealed artifact from the 'Spirit Warlock' that I mentioned earlier. I can use it to do some disguise."
Christian injected spirituality into the button, and ripples rippled again with the button as the center, but this time the ripples were visible, after all, this is the world of dreams.
Under the effect of the button, Christian and Hobert were like spiritual bodies that were overflowing spirituality, gradually fading away. Hobert could even see the tulips behind Christian through his body.
Christian raised his hand and looked at his arm, very satisfied with his operation. Then he tried to enter the area in front, and sure enough, it didn't cause any changes in the murals.
Following Christian's actions, Hobert realized that some of his previous ideas were really superficial.
Christian's performance was more like a Beyonder of the "Black Emperor" pathway, able to quickly find and exploit loopholes in the rules. Solving the problem of the wooden statues was like this, and avoiding the harassment of the "Dream Spirit Spiders" was also like this.
At the same time, Hobert realized: Knowing is not enough just to see it, you must also have your own understanding!
Currently, Hobert's state, in terms of force alone, is definitely more capable than others at his level, but in a mysterious Beyonder world, being able to fight is just the most basic requirement.
The more he came into contact with the mysterious parts of this world, the more he realized his lack of knowledge.
Unfortunately, this kind of deficiency is difficult to make up for. He can only follow behind people like Christian and Azik who have knowledge, watch more, learn more, and think more.
"Have you noticed that the prey in the murals includes people, Beyonder creatures, and beasts." Christian's words interrupted Hobert's reflection: "It's like, it's like in the eyes of the owner of this dream, there is no difference between humans, Beyonder creatures, and beasts."
He suddenly stopped: "This seems to be a philosophical question, what is the difference between humans, Beyonder creatures, and beasts?"
"Virtue." Hobert blurted out almost.
"A strange pronunciation, what does it mean?"
Hobert suddenly realized that words like "morality" and "social rules" in Loenese couldn't explain what "virtue" is.
This is one of the cornerstones of Eastern culture in his heart. Duke Zhou used this to distinguish between humans and beasts, but Western culture has never had a similar philosophical concept.
In today's North and South continents, there is no similar philosophical concept, so many people think that the idea that slaves are two-legged livestock doesn't seem to be a problem at all.
After thinking for a long time, Hobert said: "It can be understood as the opposite of moral decay and lack of conscience!"
"Virtue" is not easy to explain, but "lack of virtue" is very easy to understand.
Christian thought for a while, then smiled and said, "A very good idea. The things taught in philosophy classes at universities are quite good!"
Hobert smiled guiltily. Neither the university he attended when he first arrived in this world nor the university in the AD era taught this.
The former is because there is no such philosophical concept, and the latter is because there is no need to teach it, it is engraved in the bones.

chapters.title: Chapter 304 - 304 The Throne in the Sea of Flowers
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Hobert also noticed the problem Christian mentioned, and the clothing of the humans in the mural was completely different from what they wear now. He wondered if this was a dream of an "ancient person"?
Perhaps he was born in the "Dark Epoch," which is the Second Epoch. At that time, humans were not the masters of the world, and were still enslaved and ruled by some powerful creatures.
So in the dream owner's concept, the status of humans is similar to that of Beyonder creatures and beasts.
The two continued to walk for a long time, and finally saw the end of the hall. At the same time, at the end of the hall, in the boundless sea of flowers, they saw a black stone throne.
The murals in front changed again, turning into a barren wilderness. Demons with curved goat horns were gnawing on the prey in their hands, with blood flowing down the corners of their mouths, looking particularly hideous.
Some demons were watching their prey fight and kill with great interest, and they were enjoying it.
Christian touched the ring on her ring finger: "These demons are likely to detect our disguise. Even if these demons are just the dream owner's 'impressions' or projections, if they come out of the murals, it will be difficult to deal with so many of them."
Hobert pondered for a moment: "I'll use the 'Psychological Spoon' to keep 'hypnotizing' them. I wonder if it will work?"
Christian shook her head: "The level of the 'Psychological Spoon' is a bit low, not very stable."
Hobert said again: "It would be great if there was a mystical item from the 'Sun' pathway, which would just restrain the demons."
Christian nodded in satisfaction: "I happen to have a sealed artifact from the 'Sun' pathway."
Hobert then understood that Christian was testing him to see if he had improved in this adventure.
Christian took out a gold coin from his pocket. He stroked it with her hand, and the coin immediately emitted a dazzling light.
The demons in the mural moved, all covering their eyes with their hands, or simply hiding behind rocks and trees.
Christian held up the sun-like gold coin, as if illuminating the entire hall.
The two continued forward and came to the throne.
The black stone throne has a strange beauty in the midst of the bright flowers.
It stood there quietly, as if waiting for its owner to return.
After looking at it for a while, Christian suddenly said: "This oil painting seems to be a mark, or a sign left by the owner of the dream to himself, leaving his beautiful memories in this dream."
Hobert asked: "What will happen if the owner of the dream returns to this throne?"
Christian shook her head: "I don't know."
He said: "The owner of the dream is of a higher level than I expected. I hope our exploration has not disturbed Him and has not given Him any signs of awakening.
"Let's leave quickly before the owner of the dream discovers us.
"If there is a passage here connected to the dream owner, then His unintentionally projected will may contaminate us."
Hobert nodded and used "Travel" to leave the hall and return to the place where they first appeared.
Christian ended the dream, and the two left the oil painting and returned to Christian's living room.
He carefully put the "Spirit Warlock" sealed artifact and the button and gold coin corresponding to the "Sun" pathway sealed artifact into his briefcase, and then looked at the oil painting covered with a black cloth and said: "This is a very good sealed artifact, but use it well and don't be harmed by its power.
"Maybe you can find the Church of the Evernight Goddess or the 'Ferryman' you know, and ask them to help you seal it again."
The "Ferryman" in Christian's mouth refers to Mr. Azik.
"Okay." Hobert already had an idea.
Then, under the care of Christian and Dophis, Hobert returned to his room, relaxed his spirituality, and soon fell asleep, without encountering any curses or attacks from the dream.
Christian didn't go to work until after ten o'clock, and Hobert slept directly until after one o'clock in the afternoon.
After getting up and having some lunch, Hobert carried the oil painting on his back and used "Travel" to come to the rental house on Blanca Street.
Hobert saw the bedroom on Blanca Street and sighed that it was really convenient to have "Travel", otherwise he would have to take a carriage for more than an hour to get here.
He drew the curtains, lit a candle on the desk, and sacrificed the oil painting and the newly obtained necklace to the "Nation of Disorder".
Sitting on the "Iron Throne," Hobert first held the necklace in his hand. Using the level of the "Nation of Disorder," he immediately knew the necklace's abilities and negative effects.
Hobert had already sensed the abilities before: "Can transform into another person; Sequence 6 level divination; Paper doll substitute (can only be used once in ten minutes); Create illusions."
The negative effects are: "Long-term wearing will unconsciously cause some habitual movements, spoken language habits, etc. of others, and then the personality will become more and more like others, gradually losing oneself and losing oneself; Will involuntarily revere fate, believing that everything is a fate-arranged ending, thus becoming drifting with the tide, without any positive emotions."
Hobert suspected that the Beyonder who provided the Beyonder characteristics for this mystical item did not know the "Acting Method" at all, or he completely messed up the direction of his acting.
"Too much reverence for fate" obviously does not truly understand the meaning of "Seer", and "losing oneself" obviously has not found the core elements of playing "Faceless".
Overall, the negative effects of this necklace are not too serious, because "long-term wearing" generally refers to wearing it for years and months, and the negative effects may not appear after a year or two.
Even if wearing it in moderation, such as wearing it for two hours and resting for two hours, these negative effects cannot be avoided.
From the first time you wear it, it is counted into the "long-term wearing" process. Wearing it in moderation can only prolong the time for the negative effects to appear.
Wearing it for one or two hours and resting for one or two months may effectively avoid the negative effects, but in that case, what is the use of this necklace?
So Hobert summoned a surge of "Order Power" to wrap the necklace. After his re-sealing, although the negative effects did not change much, wearing it for 12 hours and resting for 3 hours could effectively avoid the negative effects.
Hobert named the necklace the "Faceless Necklace" and officially included it in his "Mystical Item Army".
Then, he took the oil painting again. Using the level of the "Nation of Disorder," he also understood the oil painting's abilities and negative effects.
The ability is: "As long as you see the monster in the painting, you don't need to see it clearly, as long as your eyes have contact with it, it will immediately jump out of the painting, curse the person who sees it, and try every means, or take advantage of the other party's weakness or sleep, to kill the other party. Within three meters of it, you will be marked by it and invaded by it in your dreams, and suffer misfortune."

chapters.title: Chapter 305 - 305 The Humble Baron
chapters.content:

The negative effect of the oil painting is: "The holder will irreversibly fall into a world of dreams. They will become increasingly drowsy, always dreaming about the content of the oil painting, until all the dreams are connected, and the holder will become a part of the oil painting."
Hobert withdrew his spirituality. Whether it's the ability or the negative effect, it's easy to accidentally injure innocent people. It really needs to be re-sealed.
He then mobilized the surging "Power of Order" to wrap the oil painting, so that as long as one doesn't enter the main hall in the oil painting, the owner of the dream won't be disturbed.
Wrapped in the "Power of Order", the grass in the oil painting swayed back and forth like the waves of the sea. Eventually, the grass seemed to give in and became still again.
The re-sealing effect of the "Power of Order" is very good. The abilities of the oil painting are still those abilities, but Hobert, as the holder, can "turn it on" or "turn it off."
In the "off" state, it is an ordinary oil painting. Both turning it on and off require the power of the "Nation of Disorder". These operations can be completed with things made from "Order Crystals".
The negative effects are not so serious, merely for Hobert, the holder of the oil painting. Only when within a three-meter radius of the oil painting for more than 10 hours will one be affected by the negative effects. As long as the time spent near the oil painting does not exceed 10 hours each time, the negative effects can be effectively avoided.
Because he has the aura of the "Nation of Disorder" on him, he has such "treatment."
At the same time, Hobert can also designate three people who will not be marked by the oil painting, which greatly avoids the probability of the oil painting accidentally hurting people.
Hobert was very satisfied with these two seals today. He glanced at the oil painting again and then placed it on the stone platform over there.
He might be leaving Backlund recently, and it would be quite inconvenient to carry it with him, so he might as well just put it in the "Nation of Disorder".
Back in the real world, Hobert put on the "Faceless Necklace" and went out of the rented house to go to work at the law firm.
As soon as he entered the firm, Hobert saw Austin and others in the reception hall.
They were all a little anxious, constantly looking towards the door. The moment they saw Hobert, Austin immediately "bounced" up from his chair: "Mr. Hobert, we've finally waited for you."
Seeing that their mental state was not very good, Hobert roughly understood what was going on: "Did you have dreams related to that oil painting?"
The anxiety on Austin's face instantly vanished: "Yes, yes, luckily Roy hadn't fallen asleep at the time and woke us up with cold water, otherwise we might have really died in the dream. Those spiders were really too difficult to deal with."
"It's okay now, go back and sleep peacefully." Hobert smiled and explained a few words simply: "The reason why such a thing happened is because that oil painting absorbed a trace of our spirituality."
He looked around to make sure no one was there before whispering: "I asked a master to enter the oil painting with me and dissipate our traces of spirituality, so the oil painting can no longer locate us."
Austin enthusiastically grasped Hobert's hand: "This is not the first time I've said this. Storms be praised, we were lucky to have met you, otherwise we really wouldn't know what to do.
"In any case, we owe you a favor. Mr. Hobert, if you need anything, you can feel free to ask us. I gave you the address before, and you will definitely be able to find me at that address."
Hobert smiled and said, "It should be said that we are all quite lucky."
Fortunately, Christian is still at home to back him up, just as the saying goes: Having an elder in the family is like having a treasure.
Hobert smiled knowingly: If Christian heard this, he would be unhappy again.
After seeing Austin off, Hobert went to his office. He first wrote a letter to Loretta, asking her to meet at the firm tomorrow.
After finding a rented carriage and sending the letter out, Hobert was just about to deal with official business when Jessica came to report: "Lawyer Hobert, a Mr. Sherlock is visiting."
Hobert was stunned. Klein has arrived: "Please let him in."
Klein, whose beard had grown to four or five centimeters long, pushed his glasses and entered Hobert's office: "Lawyer Hobert, hello, long time no see."
"Long time no see."
The two shook hands in a pretentious manner, and Hobert closed the door: "How have you been recently?"
"I've been fine."
"That Sunday, I saw someone who looked very similar to you at the Roselle Memorial Exhibition."
"You must have seen wrong."
After a few simple pleasantries, Klein lowered his voice and said, "I'm here to ask if you have any channels to get mystical items of the 'Sun' pathway?"
"I do know a friend who has a sealed artifact of the 'Sun' pathway, but he probably wouldn't be willing to sell it."
What Hobert was referring to was the coin that Christian used in the morning. Theoretically, Christian doesn't lack money and doesn't need to sell his collection.
Then he realized that Klein was preparing to help "Miss Bodyguard" fight?
Klein asked again: "I want to buy a mystical item for use in actual combat. Do you have any corresponding trading needs?"
"I don't plan to sell, but I do have mystical items and sealed artifacts that I can rent to you."
Klein was stunned: "Aren't you afraid that I will take those mystical items and leave Backlund?"
"Of course not afraid." Hobert smiled and said, "You have prayed to that one for help. If I want to find your whereabouts, I just need to pray to that one."
Klein thought: It seems I've been marked!
He had been mentally prepared for this for a long time, so he wasn't surprised.
Klein asked: "What mystical items can I rent?"
Hobert pondered for a moment and explained the abilities and negative effects of the "Teleportation Statue" and the "Dream Stealing Pocket Watch". One is a sealed artifact and the other is a mystical item, both reaching the level of a Grade 2 sealed artifact.
Moreover, he had used these two items in front of Klein before, and it wouldn't reveal too much information about himself.
Klein said: "I'll think about it."
He still wanted to find a mystical item of the "Sun" pathway, because that would just happen to counter the enemy.
After seeing Klein off, Hobert finally had time to deal with the backlog of official business.
After work, he didn't return to Empress Borough, but had dinner at a restaurant and returned to the rented house on Blanca Street. Today, he was going to summon two assistants from the underworld and sign contracts with them.
In future battles, they would definitely become his help.
Back in his bedroom, Hobert lit the candles again, carefully recalled the incantation for summoning unknown creatures, and then re-drew the curtains and built the wall of spirituality.
He cleared his throat and gripped the "Spirit Wine Glass": "I!
"In my name, I summon:
"Spirits wandering in the underworld, friendly spirits that can be driven, undead with rich combat experience."
Whoosh~
The candlelight suddenly became taller and thicker, turning dark green, and the surroundings suddenly became gloomy.
Two hands stretched out from the candlelight, as if tearing apart the thick and tall candlelight. In an instant, a person wearing a neat knight's uniform appeared in front of Hobert.
If it weren't for the fact that one of his eyeballs seemed to have been flattened by a blunt object and the other eyeball was hanging outside his eye socket, looking only at his clothes, one would think that this was a noble knight.
The other party asked in a gloomy tone: "Humble 'Baron', is it you who summoned me?"
"This, this knight, I'm over here."
This is a blind man!

chapters.title: Chapter 306 - 306: Hobert's Messenger
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
"Of course I know!" The knight, whose eyesight wasn't too good, seemed to be putting on a brave face: "What do you need me for?"
Hobert said: "I originally planned to summon an assistant for the battlefield, but you seem to be…"
Seemingly prone to hurting his own people.
"Hmph!" The knight snorted, suddenly charging forward. Hobert quickly dodged, but this fell right into the knight's trap. He suddenly lowered his body, trying to sweep Hobert's legs.
Hobert quickly jumped up, dodging somewhat awkwardly.
The knight, however, was now holding a gleaming white sword, its tip right in front of Hobert's eyes.
The knight sneered: "You're dead."
Hobert, ever adaptable, said: "Sorry, I shouldn't have questioned your professionalism. Let's sign a contract then."
The knight withdrew his sword: "Alright."
Hobert had already prepared the contract, with clauses including not harming the contractor, obeying the contractor's tactical commands, and so on.
The knight naturally demanded to share the spoils of war with Hobert, so Hobert added this clause, but followed it with: if no spoils are gained in battle, the contractor will not provide any compensation for this summoning.
Because the undead was summoned using the 'Spirit Wine Glass' as a medium, the final part of the contract was the honorific name of the underworld itself:
"The home of all death, the hell hidden deep within the spirit world, the witness of the decay of all living things, one that solely belongs to the kingdom of Death."
The underworld would be the 'witness' to this contract, providing it with notarization.
Finally, there was the signature. Hobert signed his name: Hobert Jeffrey.
The knight's long sword disappeared, and he signed his name: Hunter Van Jacob.
The contract emitted a ghastly green light, indicating that the agreement had officially taken effect.
Hobert said: "The simpler the summoning incantation, the better. How about using 'Knight' as the incantation?"
Actually, he wanted to use "Blind Man" more, but he didn't seem to be able to beat the other party, so he'd better not say it randomly.
"Alright." After saying that, Hunter disappeared, as if fading into the air.
The reason Hobert signed the agreement with him so readily was that although the other party's eyes seemed "not too good", he noticed that Hobert was a "Baron of Corruption" as soon as he appeared, so his level shouldn't be too low.
Hunter seemed to be good at close combat. For the second undead, he should summon one skilled in sneak attacks or possessing strange powers.
Hobert also thought: It would be best if it could fly, to control the airspace.
So he gripped the "Spirit Wine Glass" and began his second summoning: "I,
"In my name, I summon:
"A spirit wandering in the underworld, a friendly spirit that can be driven, an undead that can fly and has strange abilities."
Whoosh~
The candles turned ghastly green again, the flames tall and thick. A skeletal pegasus appeared in front of Hobert.
Its skeleton looked very strong and emitted a ghastly white light, clearly not an ordinary product.
Looking at the length of the wing bones on its back, the wingspan should be four or five meters wide when opened, but because it was in the room, the wings were folded.
In its skull, a ball of light flickered, indicating that it had intelligence.
Hobert asked: "You can fly, right?"
The skeleton nodded.
"What strange abilities do you have?"
Hobert looked at the skeleton, and the skeleton's dark eye sockets stared back at Hobert. The room fell into a long silence.
After a long while, Hobert asked: "You can understand my words, but you can only shake your head and nod, right?"
The skeleton nodded.
Hobert felt the urge to cover his face: What have I summoned? A blind man, a mute!
He asked again: "Can I ride on your back and have you fly me in the sky?"
The skeleton nodded.
That was still good. Even if it didn't have too strong Beyonder abilities, just being able to fly himself was pretty good.
So Hobert signed a contract with it as well. The contract was similar to the previous one, but Hobert added a clause: if the contractor needs it, he can ride on the horse's back and take the contractor to fly in the sky.
He still used the honored name of the underworld as a witness, and then signed his name. The pegasus signed its name with a pen in its mouth.
To Hobert's surprise, the pegasus even had a name: Maximilian.
After the pegasus returned to the underworld, Hobert was about to clean up the altar when he suddenly thought that he was already Sequence 6 and could try summoning a messenger.
If he left Backlund, having a messenger would be very convenient. Even if there was no law firm as a base, he could communicate directly with Xio and others using the messenger.
Hobert carefully recalled Klein's summoning of the messenger, and only needed to modify the incantation slightly:
"I,
"In my name, I summon:
"A spirit wandering in the void, a friendly creature that can be driven, a unique existence willing to become my messenger."
Whoosh~
The candle became even taller and thicker than the previous two times. A big guy came out of the candlelight, looking like a wooden box, but it seemed very long.
After it fully appeared, Hobert discovered that it was actually an ancient black coffin. His eyes narrowed. When Mr. Azik took him through the spirit world before, coffins had appeared "on the roadside"!
But immediately afterward, Hobert breathed a sigh of relief. After all, what he summoned was a "friendly creature that could be driven".
The coffin's wood looked very thick and sturdy, and the style was simple and elegant. Judging from its appearance alone, it looked like something that ancient nobles could afford.
He just didn't know if the coffin had "become a spirit"? Or if the person inside the coffin had become a creature that could freely soar in the spirit world?
After the coffin came out of the candlelight horizontally, it stood upright, and a muffled voice came from inside: "Are you summoning me?"
It sounded like a female voice.
Hobert nodded: "Yes, are you willing to sign a contract and become my messenger? Uh…"
"Sorry, I don't mean to offend you, I'm just curious. If I need you to deliver a letter, where should I put the letter?"
After all, coffins don't have hands.
Who knew that the other party would answer: "You can stuff it in through the cracks in the coffin."
"I…" Hobert was immediately a little speechless, feeling like he was doing something disrespectful to the dead.
The other party added: "I can become your messenger, on the condition that the reward for each letter delivered is three donuts."
What a strange reward.
Hobert said: "That's fine, but I'm still curious, how do I give you the donuts?"
Squeak~
A crack opened on the side of the coffin, and a fair and slender hand reached out, with a bracelet on its wrist. It looked like a good thing: "You can give it directly to me."
"Then let's sign a contract."
Hobert took out paper and pen from the drawer and quickly wrote a few clauses, roughly that she must not harm the contractor, must not peek at the letters, must not discard the letters, must deliver the letters as quickly as possible, and so on.
Later, Hobert also added the reward requested by the messenger. As for the honored name that needed to be notarized, Hobert originally planned to use the honored name of the spirit world, but he suddenly realized that he didn't know the honored name of the spirit world.
In the future, he could ask 'The Fool' to be the witness, but it's not possible now. 'The Fool' has very little control over the spirit world.
So he changed it to the honored name of "Red Light" Aiur Moria: "The Inextinguishable Light of the Spirit World,
The Embodiment of infinite knowledge,
The Red who wields authority and will"
When signing the name, the hand in the coffin reached out again and wrote: Beverly Heather Tudor.
Hobert was stunned: Did he summon Christian's old aunt?

chapters.title: Chapter 307 - 307: One Killing Every Ten Steps
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Hobert didn't acknowledge any prior relationship with him. After the contract took effect, he asked, "Have we met in the spirit world before? Or rather, were you waiting for me there?"
"Indeed," Beverly said. "I can sense a unique aura on you. You seem to be hiding a great secret."
So that was it. Hobert had thought he was attracting creatures because of Mr. Azik, but it turned out they were drawn to the aura within him.
Hobert simply smiled and didn't pursue the topic. He suddenly thought of another "use" for the messenger: "If I need help in a fight, can I ask for your assistance?"
He wondered how skilled the Tudor family's young lady was in combat.
"Yes," Beverly replied. "The reward is donuts, or a piece of wood from your cane."
How much did she love donuts!
Hobert roughly understood that Beverly could sense the aura of the "Nation of Disorder" on him and could also perceive the magical items produced by the "Nation of Disorder."
After the coffin returned to the spirit world, Hobert blew out the candles, tidied up his desk, and sat on the edge of the bed to rest for a moment. Just as he was about to go home, he suddenly heard a prayer from the "Nation of Disorder."
Hobert immediately entered the "Nation of Disorder" and saw the star representing Rafter flickering in the pool, spreading its spirituality. He saw Rafter in a cemetery.
The grave had been dug open, and the coffin had been pried open. By the light of a bright lantern, Rafter held a wooden box containing the mutated fire rose spider and prayed to the "Creator": "...Mysterious and great being, I have come to Conant as you instructed and dug out the Beyonder materials hidden in the coffin.
"What should I do next? Also, I feel that my every move is being watched. How can I get rid of them?"
Hobert used "True Sight" to look around and indeed saw two people watching from the depths of the cemetery.
To Hobert's surprise, there was no ambush, only two people keeping watch.
But then he thought about it, and it made sense. After all, this was just a wild Beyonder organization, quite different from official organizations. They had limited manpower and couldn't deploy heavy forces here around the clock.
...
Desi County, on the outskirts of Conant, in Bostan Cemetery.
Next to a dug-open grave, Rafter had a lantern beside him, its light illuminating his devout gaze, but the area below his eyes was covered with a strip of cloth.
After the prayer, Rafter waited for a response from that great being. As for the people watching him, he didn't take them to heart. He knew very well that those two would wait patiently to see if he had any accomplices.
Or perhaps some of them had already gone to report and were gathering more companions to come over. In any case, they wouldn't act for the time being.
This made Rafter even more fearless. Now he could be sure that the "Creator's" mission must have a deeper meaning.
He could feel that the material in his hand was of a high level, but such a powerful and mysterious being couldn't be attracted by just this one material.
This should involve a struggle between Beyonder organizations, perhaps even a battle at the level of gods.
In that case, that mysterious being must have already arranged a way for him to escape, since this Beyonder material was still in his hands.
Although Rafter couldn't see the whole picture, he was excited to be involved in such a struggle, even if he was being used as a pawn. The Pound family hadn't played even the slightest role in the Beyonder world for many years.
While Rafter was lost in thought, a figure suddenly appeared on the tombstone next to him.
This person wore a windbreaker, carried a cane, and wore a black crystal mask with occult patterns on his face.
Rafter's heart trembled. This person's eyes were cold, as if he wanted to kill!
Fortunately, he wasn't here to kill Rafter. The figure disappeared again, and then Rafter heard screams from the woods.
Rafter looked in the direction of the sound. By the light of the crimson moon, he only saw corpses falling to the ground.
A figure darted out of the woods, holding a short sword, his face full of horror, desperately trying to escape.
But the masked man appeared in front of the man with the short sword like a ghost. The knife in his hand, which gleamed coldly even in the dark night, thrust forward, piercing the enemy's chest and exiting from his back.
Rafter was shocked because the enemy's short sword also pierced the masked man's chest at the same time.
The masked man pulled out his knife, and the enemy fell to the ground. Strangely, the enemy's short sword also fell to the ground. Although he had stabbed the masked man, he hadn't pierced the masked man's flesh.
Rafter stood there blankly, not knowing what to do for a moment.
The battle just now was clean and efficient, even far exceeding Rafter's understanding of Beyonder combat.
But what surprised Rafter was still to come. The corpse that had fallen in the woods suddenly got up and jumped out of the woods, then lay down next to the corpse of the enemy holding the short sword.
The masked man stared at the two corpses for a few seconds. Soon, a magical light appeared on both corpses. The masked man seemed to pick up two items from the corpses, and then the two corpses rolled over and hugged each other.
The masked man took out a glass bottle from his pocket, opened the rubber cap, and poured the liquid inside onto the corpses.
A sizzling sound was incessant.
At this time, the masked man came over and threw a black object to Rafter.
Rafter caught it somewhat awkwardly. By the light of the lantern, he saw that it was a round plate made of black crystal, with mysterious symbols engraved on it.
"Carry this with you, and the enemy won't be able to divine your whereabouts," the masked man said coldly. "Return it to me after you return to Backlund."
"Thank you, thank you," Rafter first thanked him, then asked, "How can I find you?"
The masked man asked coldly, "Don't you report your whereabouts to the 'Creator'?"
Rafter suddenly understood, and then he was a little worried because he hadn't reported his process of coming to Conant to that mysterious... to the "Creator". He wondered if the "Creator" would blame him?
"Thank you for the reminder, thank you for the reminder," Rafter quickly thanked again. He felt that he had returned to his teenage years, understanding nothing and knowing nothing.
The masked man stretched out his hand, and Rafter immediately reacted, handing the wooden box containing the mutated fire rose spider to the masked man.
The stern masked man bowed slightly politely, and then disappeared into the night.
Rafter stared blankly at the place where the masked man disappeared. It was the hooting of owls in the cemetery that brought him back to his senses. When he looked at the two corpses not far away again, there was nothing left. If it weren't for the short sword that fell on the ground, Rafter would have wondered if a battle had taken place in the cemetery just now?
Everything just now made Rafter sigh: "This is what an Beyonder should be like, mysterious, powerful, and stern. When can I be as powerful as him? Wearing a mask and calmly killing two Beyonders in the blink of an eye."
If Hobert were to describe a similar mood, it must be "A great man should be like this."
At this time, the figure sitting among the sharp swords suddenly appeared in Rafter's mind: "Very good, from now on you can call me 'Creator'."
That great figure disappeared, and Rafter was a little excited. His efforts had been recognized by the "Creator"!
But he quickly calmed down, checked that he hadn't left any traces, and quickly left the cemetery.
