chapters.title: Chapter 363 - 363 The Bloody History of the Elves
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Hobert explained, "The fourth dimension is definitely not length, width, and height, but an additional dimension on top of length, width, and height. In that dimension, we are like paper figures in three dimensions.
However, thinking about how we could travel through closed spaces in the spirit world, the fourth dimension must be able to easily jump out of the other three dimensions.
It's like drawing a circle on paper. If there were two-dimensional creatures, the circle would be an insurmountable barrier for the creatures within.
But if we have the third dimension, we can simply walk and step out of a circle on the ground."
Alger exclaimed, "This is a very logical new discovery! It, its theory seems to be very mature."
Hobert smiled and shook his head: "In short, we have to walk around this kind of two-dimensional space. You saw just now that once you enter it, you lose your thickness when you come out, and we become paper figures."
This reminded him of a very classic science fiction novel he saw in the AD era.
Alger nodded, but then he had a new question: "When we return from the spirit world to the real world, why don't we feel the damage caused by the dimensions?"
Hobert smiled and said, "That's because we are returning from a higher dimension to a lower dimension. A higher dimension can contain a lower dimension, just like there are planes in the real world. So when we enter a higher dimension, we as lower dimensions will not be harmed by the dimensions.
"But when a higher-dimensional creature enters a lower dimension, such as the two of us entering the two-dimensional space in front of us, then we will lose our thickness. I don't know if there is a way to recover it. Anyway, I haven't thought of a way to recover it."
The two of them talked about this issue while detouring around the two-dimensional space in front of them.
Alger was a little strange: "Then where did these two-dimensional spaces come from? Theoretically speaking, the spirit world is a high-dimensional space, but I have never heard of any place that corresponds to a two-dimensional space."
Hobert was also a little puzzled: "It doesn't seem to be a product of the fusion and distortion of the real world and the spirit world."
He didn't understand where it came from specifically.
These two-dimensional spaces are not difficult to bypass, and they show no signs of expansion, like fruit particles in jelly, with a clear distinction from the surrounding space, but irrelevant.
The two of them had to detour while trying to stay away from the mist as much as possible. Although the mist looked harmless, who knows what the scene inside the mist is like.
Today, we can explore the area outside the mist first, and it will not be too late to explore inside the mist when we have time in the future.
They walked until noon and arrived at the mountain in the center of the island. At the foot of the mountain, they found a freshwater stream and some long-abandoned elven ruins.
At the same time, they saw a building like a palace. This building has a typical elven style and looks relatively well-preserved.
The two of them were prepared and brought some food and water. At this time, they each ate a simple lunch and rested for a while before starting to explore the palace.
After entering the main hall, Hobert discovered that this should be a temple. In the middle is an altar and a statue covered with dust, and the surrounding walls are murals.
However, the statue is very strange. It is a multi-angled, multi-faceted, and multi-edged crystal-like structure. Each of its sides is engraved with some mystifying symbols, as if each side represents a different meaning.
Hobert was stunned for a long time before asking Alger, "Have you seen this kind of statue? Is this a statue?"
Could this be the abstract image of the "Elf King"?
Alger shook his head: "I have never seen such a belief."
Then Hobert was attracted by the murals on the wall. The order of the murals is from left to right, one after another.
The first picture is a battle scene. The main character in the mural is an elven king with pointed ears and blue hair. He is stepping on the waves, surrounded by storms, and holding a lightning spear.
Hobert believed that this should be the image of the Elf King. He is leading the elves to fight against the dragons. This depicts a war in the Second Epoch.
It seems that the elves living on this island have a long history. The second picture is still the Elf King, fighting against a great figure exuding sunlight.
Alger guessed: "That is, is that the Eternal Blazing Sun? No, is it the Ancient Sun God?"
Hobert nodded and went to see the next mural. As a result, this mural depicts a scene of hell on earth. A group of people holding crosses and emitting light from their other hands are hunting elves.
Some elves were beheaded, some elven women were being insulted, and some elves' heads were cut off and hung on spears, like a declaration or deterrence.
This is definitely the dark history of the Ancient Sun God, but Hobert felt that this should be the truth of history. When the spiritual leader and power leader of a race fall at the same time, most elves should be slaughtered or enslaved.
After all, although the Ancient Sun God is much more rational than the ancient gods, He must still have a distorted and crazy side. His divinity is greater than his humanity, and He will not stop His believers from carrying out such massacres.
Only a part of the elves, under the protection of the saint, escaped to some islands to survive.
Hobert didn't think this was so cruel, because before that, humans were the ones who were enslaved and slaughtered.
The next mural shows the elves performing some curses, and on the other side, the sun fell to the ground.
Hobert pondered for a while before he understood. The elves on this island believed that their curse caused the Ancient Sun God to fall. They may also know that such an idea is a bit far-fetched, but it is more refreshing for them to draw it like this.
A stone door separated the murals. Hobert passed through the stone door and continued to look down. On the new murals, an elven leader is leading the elves to fight against a group of people wearing Storm Church costumes.
Alger's heart tightened when he saw this mural. Although the costumes of the Storm Church on the mural are clearly different from the current ones, he certainly knew that this represented the people of the Storm Church.
He didn't expect that there was such a history.
Hobert believed that this battle should have taken place in the Fourth Epoch. It is said that there were still many elves on the sea at that time, but by the Fifth Epoch, elves and giants had basically disappeared.
Of course, they would not disappear for no reason. That was "A History of Human Rise". Whether on land or at sea, humans became the undisputed protagonists, and the remaining elves could only escape to small islands like this at the edge of the world to live.
Continuing to look down, the history of this group of elves did not end there. Suddenly, one day, the sea suddenly became violent. The elf saint holding a scepter and wearing a golden ring blocked the violence of the sea around the island, forming a spectacle like an iron barrel.
Immediately afterwards, the saint holding the scepter seemed to hear a voice from the void.

chapters.title: Chapter 364 - 364 Infiltration from Higher Dimensions
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
This mural is somewhat abstract. The saint on the previous mural, who drove away the violent weather, is listening intently towards a dark place.
This should be something that already happened in the Fifth Epoch. The violent weather on the sea before should represent the scene when the Berserk Sea formed.
No one knows what that saint heard, but the Elven race changed their faith from then on and erected new idols.
The last mural depicts a bloody sacrificial scene. A tall Elf lies on the altar, his face full of pain, while the priest is cutting open his chest and heart.
Hobert said, "The Elven race living here probably died out in this kind of bloody sacrifice, and their leader seems to have been corrupted."
Alger nodded, feeling as if he had just witnessed a heavy and bloody history.
Then, the two of them looked at the stone door behind the temple. There was a crack in the stone door, and a cold wind blew out from inside.
The two of them pushed open the stone door together, revealing a cave connected to the mountain, like a long and dark corridor.
Hobert injected his spirituality into the warm ring and then wiped his staff with his hand.
The staff immediately emitted a dazzling light, illuminating the path ahead and covering Hobert and Alger in a layer of sacred light.
After passing through the corridor, they arrived at a spacious cave. Both of them were surprised after seeing the scene in front of them clearly.
In this cave, there were actually two formations, with many Elf mummies standing neatly.
They must have turned into mummies immediately after death, or died as mummies, otherwise, the remains could not have been preserved so well.
In front of the small altar in the middle of the cave, there was also a kneeling mummy, who was probably an Elf priest.
Hobert and Alger carefully came to the altar, and their eyes narrowed. The symbol drawn in the center of the altar was actually the symbol representing the "Lord of Storms".
Hobert looked at the surrounding mummies again. There were men and women, old and young, some with Beyonder characteristics, but most did not have any.
If they only saw these mummies, the two of them might have thought it was a bloody sacrificial scene, but with the symbol on the altar, everything became strange.
Why would the last remaining power of the Elven race in the North and South Continent paint the symbol of the "Lord of Storms", whom they regarded as a deadly enemy, on the altar?
Inside this cave, there was another cave. Since they had already come here, of course, they had to continue exploring.
The two of them moved forward again, passing through a not-very-long cave. Some mystical symbols were drawn on the stone walls of the cave. Hobert, who was quite knowledgeable, roughly understood that they seemed to be common symbols representing seals.
After passing through the cave, they arrived at another spacious cave, which contained many corpses lying in disorder. Only skeletons remained of the corpses inside, and each skeleton had an Beyonder characteristic.
Alger could even feel that some of those Beyonder characteristics were Sequence 6 or even Sequence 5.
There were also many seemingly brand-new ornaments on the skeletons, which must be magical items.
They've struck it rich this time!
However, neither of them immediately bent down to pick up the Beyonder characteristics in front of them but carefully observed the surroundings. Hobert's staff emitted a more dazzling light to illuminate the entire cave.
They had the same idea: to find out the cause of death of these Elves first.
The light from the staff allowed them to see a headless corpse sitting cross-legged at the deepest part of the cave.
Hobert noticed that the corpse was holding a staff in its hand and wearing a golden ring on its finger.
Around the headless corpse, a head, a heart, lungs, a liver, and kidneys were floating and slowly moving. The corpse also had several circles of intestines wrapped around its waist.
No one knows how long the corpse has been there, but there were no signs of decay, and the approximate structure of those internal organs could still be seen clearly.
The corpse's torso was cut open, and those internal organs should have come from inside the corpse.
However, the head floating around the corpse was obviously cut open, not only the head but also other internal organs such as the heart had traces of being cut open, and even the intestines seemed to have been cut open if one looked closely.
Hobert and Alger looked at each other and recalled the bloody sacrificial scene in the mural.
"Who are you?" Just as the somewhat shriveled head floated to the front of the corpse, a solemn and old voice suddenly echoed in the cave.
The voice spoke in Elvish, but Hobert and Alger, who often came into contact with mysticism, could understand it.
Hobert replied in broken Elvish, "My companion is a descendant of the Elven race. He has received a great guidance to come here and inherit the power of his ancestors."
Alger was stunned. He didn't expect that "Emperor" could make up such a lie so easily.
But he could also understand that he didn't know whether the headless corpse in front of him was an evil spirit or something else? But the other party should have intelligence.
Hobert's words elevated the purpose of their actions from digging graves to inheriting the power of their ancestors.
Moreover, Alger's blue hair indicated that he did have Elven blood, so "Emperor's" words were not entirely lies.
"That's really great!" The voice said, "I've been waiting for helpers for too long!"
Hobert was stunned: "What helpers?"
"Helpers to kill me!"
The cave became silent.
After a full ten seconds, Hobert asked, "Are you serious? Do you still need to be killed again?"
Your head has been cut off, and your heart has been cut open, okay!
"Maybe my words are beyond your comprehension, but I'm really not dead yet." The voice sighed, "We were cursed, a curse from the Astral World!
"You should have seen it when you came in. The last Elven group in this sea area was destroyed!"
Hobert was not interested in that curse, because it might indicate great danger: "Killing you will end that curse?"
"No, killing me will completely prevent the descent of that power from the Astral World." The voice explained, "Suddenly one day, something unknown happened in this sea area, and the spirit world was distorted and merged with the real world.
"In the distorted spirit world, we heard a voice, a voice that claimed it could help us kill Leodero and regain our former glory.
"So we changed our faith and erected new idols.
"But that was the beginning of the disaster. We should not have listened to his bewitchment and prayed to Him for power.
"When He descended on me, I felt his malice.
"In order to prevent his continued descent, I could only make sure that my body had no enclosed places, so I cut off my head, cut open my skull to expose my brain, so I dug out my heart and cut open the atria and ventricles, so..."
"Okay, okay." Hobert said, "No need to say it in such detail, we all understand."
"It's good that you understand, hurry up, come and kill me! Many people in the cave wanted to kill me back then, but they all failed. But after so many years of struggle, I have taken the initiative of this body, and it is easy to kill me."
Hobert thought for a while: "Sorry, but I refuse!"

chapters.title: Chapter 365 - 365: The Evil God’s Plot
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
"Emperor"'s refusal was so blunt that Alger was somewhat surprised. Although he had no intention of becoming a so-called "helper," he also didn't plan to refuse.
Instead, he intended to respond in a way that neither agreed nor refused.
However, considering his strength, Alger always positioned himself as a guide, a second-in-command, during this expedition.
Therefore, although he didn't agree with "Emperor"'s approach, he didn't voice any objections.
The old and solemn voice didn't seem to expect that Hobert would refuse so thoroughly.
After a long while, he asked, "Child, don't you know how much disaster the arrival of an evil god will bring to this world?"
"It is because I know that I refuse," Hobert said, "I noticed just now, the scepter and ring in your hand, which reminded me of the murals I saw in the temple before.
"I also noticed that on these skeletons in front of us, there are also two rings of the same style as the one on your hand. If my spirituality is not a problem, judging from the Beyonder characteristics around them, the two elves wearing the rings were both Sequence 5 before their death.
"In terms of strength, I think this kind of ring should be similar to the symbol of leadership among the elves.
"And the scepter in your hand represents the power symbol of the highest leader."
The old voice said, "You guessed right, this ring has a symbolic meaning you can hardly imagine.
"But what does this have to do with refusing my request?"
"It has a lot to do with it!" Hobert said, squatting down and saying to Alger, "For example, this Beyonder characteristic of the elves. You are a Beyonder of the 'Sailor' pathway. Feel it, is this an Beyonder characteristic of Sequence 5?"
Alger was slightly stunned, but immediately showed the shrewdness of an old hand. He took the Beyonder characteristic handed over by Hobert, held it in his hand, and pretended to feel it, saying, "Yes, it is an Beyonder characteristic of Sequence 5."
After speaking, he smoothly put the Beyonder characteristic into his pocket, the whole movement was exceptionally smooth.
Hobert, who was squatting on the ground, continued, "Look, how exquisite this ring is, how beautiful this pendant is, all of which are showing his distinctiveness in identity."
While saying this, he smoothly put the ring and pendant into his pocket, the movements were equally smooth.
"Most importantly, before he died, his face was facing the outside of the cave." Hobert seemed to be trying to divert the attention of the old voice, and immediately pointed out the key point:
"This shows that he didn't die in the process of preparing to kill you, but rather died while trying to escape outside the cave.
"Associating it with the last mural in the temple, what you said about not allowing your body to have any closed places should be about creating a container for the arrival of the evil god in the astral world, that is not a sacrifice.
"And after countless experiments on the elves on this island, all of which ended in failure, you, the leader of the elves, a saint, tried to become a container for the evil god.
"Perhaps because of your demigod physique, the experiment of creating a container for the evil god was finally successful!
"But at the same time as the success, the evil power descended, causing all the leaders of the elves in this cave to lose control and die!"
"Child, has your thinking always been so abnormal?" The voice seemed to be amused, "If the evil god has already arrived, it will trigger a catastrophe in the North and South continents! The key is that you, who are so close to me, would have died long ago!"
Hobert said seriously, "That's because the priests and the elves outside the cave realized that they had made a big mistake.
"So they and the priests sacrificed their lives to their mortal enemy, the 'Lord of Storms,' allowing the 'Lord of Storms' to immediately descend and seal you in this cave, in this body.
"Although I belong to a different race from them, I think they are very respectable people!
"If I'm not mistaken, as long as this body is destroyed, you will descend again, right? Lord Evil God!"
In fact, the reason why Hobert initially suspected that there was something wrong with this corpse was the corpse itself.
In the cave outside, it was full of mummified corpses. If there was a skeleton among them, Hobert would definitely suspect that there was something wrong with the skeleton.
Similarly, the cave inside was full of skeletons, and there was only one corpse without any signs of decay, then it must have a big problem!
Hobert therefore became suspicious, and then launched some series of deductions and associations.
The cave fell into silence, and Hobert slowly raised his hand and placed it on Alger's shoulder.
In fact, the reason why he said so much just now, first was to naturally pick up certain spoils, and second was to disrupt the other party's attention.
When Hobert realized that there was something wrong with the corpse in front of him, he knew that this matter could not be resolved peacefully today. Whether he refused or agreed, the other party could not easily let them go.
Evil gods would not be satisfied with some ambiguous answers.
Rather than answering according to the other party's intentions, it would be better to simply "overturn the table"!
Of course, Hobert would take such a risk, which was inseparable from his "travel" ability.
The corpse suddenly raised its withered arm holding the scepter, "The elves have a saying: Too smart people tend to die early."
Hobert felt that the entire cave seemed to be filled with electricity, and he quickly used "Travel" to escape.
But the space in front of him and Alger had just become illusory, and immediately returned to normal.
The solemn voice said, "No one can escape from here!"
Lightning and thunder suddenly flashed in the wide cave, and lightning bolts fell from the top of the cave.
Hobert and Alger quickly separated to avoid them. Alger's balance ability allowed him to make acrobatic-like movements to avoid the dense lightning.
"Distort!"
Hobert could only use "Distort" to dodge repeatedly. If he really couldn't dodge, he had to use "Paper Figure Substitute."
Even so, he was still struck by lightning, his hair and sweat standing on end, and his whole body was pitch black.
Even if Hobert had the blessing of the "Zombie Spoon" and the strong physique of the "Baron of Corruption," he was still paralyzed by the electricity and his movements were stiff.
And Alger's "Sapphire Scepter" showed a huge effect at this time. Even if he couldn't avoid it, he could use the "Scepter" to slightly deflect the lightning.
Fortunately, both of them were old hands. In the process of avoiding the lightning, they had already approached the exit.
Hobert, who had been struck by lightning, scrambled and stumbled, and fled into the cave in a mess.
Alger was not much better. Even if he was not struck by lightning, the hair on his body stood up, and there were many charred marks on his clothes.
Hobert looked back and saw that the corpse had appeared behind them.
The heart, liver, spleen, lungs, and kidneys floating around the headless corpse were all in full view, and even a strange fishy smell could be smelled.
It's just that this corpse could not leave the cave inside. Seeing the two of them escape, its somewhat withered head showed an angry expression, and its brain was moving around in its skull in anger.
Hobert and Alger didn't dare to stay and hurried out.
But after walking a few steps, a hurricane blew in front of them.
Whoosh~
The hurricane was terrifying, and the two of them quickly fell against the wall to reduce the area of contact with the wind.
Hobert's two hands were like steel claws, clasping the cracks in the stone, so as not to be blown back by the wind.
Alger did not have such great strength, nor did his body have such great strength. He was blown back again and again, and was about to be caught by the headless corpse.
Hobert quickly stretched out a leg for Alger to grab.
But the wind was getting stronger and stronger, and it was not a solution to continue like this. The two of them would be blown back into the cave sooner or later.
Hobert's mind raced, and he suddenly thought of the "Cursed Jade" he had taken out of the "Nation of Disorder" a few days ago.

chapters.title: Chapter 366 - 366 A Polite Young Man
chapters.content:

The second time Elliott bribed the "Creator", the main offering was a sealed artifact that looked like a sleeve.
Because the negative effects of the sealed artifact could not be sealed again, Hobert simply crushed it.
While obtaining the Beyonder characteristics of a "Zombie", he also received a blessing from the "Mother Tree of Desire".
With Hobert's current abilities, he couldn't completely eliminate the remaining power of the "Mother Tree of Desire", so he transferred this power to a stone from the "Nation of Disorder".
This formed a manipulable, high-level "blessing": it could make the target spontaneously believe in the "Mother Tree of Desire" from the bottom of their hearts.
Hobert originally intended to use this curse against the people of the "Theosophy Order".
The people of the "Theosophy Order" are still relatively rational and willing to cooperate with Hobert, so the "Cursed Jade Stone" has not been used.
Hobert, unable to move in the gale, realized that now was the time for the "Cursed Jade Stone" to come in handy.
He shouted to the back: "In my left pants pocket, there is a piece of jade!"
"Take it out and throw it to the back!"
Hobert didn't know if this jade stone would work, but it was the highest-level thing he had on him now, and it wouldn't be a burden to throw it.
Hobert didn't dare to throw the "Disorder Stone and the "Order Crystal" randomly.
Alger struggled to reach out, tore open Hobert's left pants pocket, and a piece of jade twisted with red and green fell out, quickly falling to the back under the blowing of the hurricane.
The hurricane suddenly stopped.
Only a muffled voice was heard saying: "Mother Tree of Desire!"
Hobert and Alger took the opportunity to run out quickly.
When leaving the cave, Hobert saw that the headless corpse was holding the jade stone tightly in one hand, and fresh blood was flowing from the head, heart, and other parts suspended around the body.
The old and solemn voice from before said: "Stay here, stay here with me, and never think about going out."
The muffled voice said: "I didn't expect this jade stone to awaken your will again. Hehe, this is not my main body, what's the use of you keeping me?"
The old voice: "This is a punishment for me, and also a punishment for you."
The last scene Hobert saw when leaving the cave was that the headless corpse, with blood flowing from its torso, sat down again, and the expression on its head became peaceful, no longer angry.
Hobert guessed that the "Cursed Jade Stone" might have awakened the unwillingness and remorse of this headless corpse, as well as the guilt of bringing the disaster of extinction, and the desire not to let the evil god succeed. The consciousness of the Elf Saint awakened, suppressed the will of the evil god again, and no longer sought to break the seal.
Fortunately, the cave between the two caves was not long, and the two quickly came to the outside cave.
After such a strong wind just now, there was no change here.
Whether it was an illusion or not, Hobert and Alger both seemed to feel the gaze of the mummified corpses.
Hobert, who was in front, stopped, wanting to take off his hat, but found that it had already been blown away by the wind.
He tidied up his clothes, bowed solemnly to the high priest in front of the altar, and then bowed deeply to the mummified corpses on both sides.
Hobert said unhurriedly: "Please accept the respect of a human being, thank you for your contribution, thank you for your selflessness, you are respectable people."
Alger was stunned and followed suit.
After speaking and bowing, Alger felt that the eerie gaze he had felt just now had disappeared.
Hobert bypassed the altar before continuing to flee for his life, as if the one who bowed just now and the one who was running for his life were two different people.
Alger hurried to keep up, feeling that he had learned a lot from this exploration, such as being polite to the corpses in the ruins.
Finally, they arrived at the outer temple, and the two immediately realized that something was wrong, because it seemed to be night outside.
The exploration of the temple and the cave just now took them only two hours in total. The two also took out their pocket watches to check and confirmed that it was after two o'clock in the afternoon.
Hobert once again used the power of the ring to make the cane shine brightly.
Bypassing the polygonal statue, the two saw a thick fog outside the temple: the misty area they had seen before now covered the Elven ruins at the foot of the mountain!
Hobert tried again, but still couldn't use the ability of "Travel".
He took out the potion he had bought from Viscount Glaint earlier with a blank expression, opened the potion to restore spirituality and restore power, drank half of it, and handed the other half to Alger.
They had consumed a lot of spirituality and strength when they were escaping just now. Although the recovery effect of the potion was very slow, it was better than nothing.
This time, Hobert walked in front and entered the mist: "I should have thought of it when I saw the two-dimensional space. There may be a problem with the space here.
"And that evil god seems to have authority over space, so it's impossible to use 'Travel' in front of him."
Hobert smiled and said: "We are lucky, or we should thank the Elves for their dedication and thank the 'Lord of Storms' for the seal, which sealed the evil god in that corpse.
"So the evil god can only use the abilities of that Elf Saint. Even if the evil god showed a little bit of his own power, we would have lost control and died."
Alger didn't say a word. At this time, he was glad that this exploration was in cooperation with the "Emperor". If he was alone, he would not have been able to escape from the hurricane just now.
Moreover, he realized that with his knowledge, many problems would be unclear because he did not realize those clues, which would eventually put him in danger.
The two walked one after the other for a while, and both found that something was wrong around them. They did not see the Elven ruins, nor did they see the forest and the two-dimensional space in the mist.
The land under their feet was very desolate, as if it had not seen the sun for a long time.
Alger took out his compass, and the pointer turned around like it was drunk, but it didn't point north.
Hobert looked at the compass and said: "We have entered the area where the spirit world and the real world merge. For us and the compass, the north is now suddenly left and right, constantly changing direction."
Alger asked with his eyes, what should we do now?
Hobert pondered for a moment: "Keep moving forward. Whether we completely enter the spirit world or return to the real world, we will be safer than we are now."
He said: "If it doesn't work, we can still pray to Mr. Fool."
I just don't know to what extent the "Dominator of the Spirit World" now dominates the spirit world? Can he help us out of trouble?
Dong dong dong~
Just then, a knocking sound came from the mist.
Hobert and Alger immediately became alert. Not only did Hobert not make the light of the cane brighter, but he also made the light weaker.
In the mist with extremely low visibility, they listened carefully.
Dong dong dong~
The sound suddenly appeared behind them again, and it sounded closer.

chapters.title: Chapter 367 - 367: Ghost in the Mist
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
In the dense fog, where one couldn't see their own fingers, a "thump, thump, thump" sound suddenly echoed, as if it were sometimes in front and sometimes behind.
Alger said, "I think I also hear the sound of waves."
Hobert pondered for a moment, "This place already possesses some characteristics of the spirit world. We can't use the concepts of distance and position from the real world to determine our location. Perhaps we think we're standing still, but our position is constantly changing."
He paused and added, "Let's head towards the sea. At least that's a point of reference."
However, the closer they got to the sea, the louder the "thump, thump, thump" sound became.
The two stopped again. Although neither of their spiritual senses issued a warning, based on their experience, strange sounds in this kind of fog often foreshadowed bizarre powers or terrifying things.
So, the two tried to walk in the opposite direction of the sound, but as soon as they started walking, the sound was still behind them. After a few steps, the "thump, thump, thump" sound reappeared in front of them.
They tried several times, and it was always like this. Instead, they were getting closer and closer to the source of the sound.
"It seems like it's targeting us," Hobert said, checking his magical items. "Or we're in a state of mutual attraction."
"Since we can't escape, let's go. We'll see what's making the sound."
Alger had a similar idea and followed closely.
Soon, a huge dark shadow appeared in the fog ahead.
Hobert seemed very generous when he spoke earlier, but when he saw the huge dark shadow, his steps became exceptionally cautious.
Thump, thump, thump~
The sound rang out again, not far ahead.
Alger suddenly said, "It looks like a stranded ship."
He was an old pirate who had spent his life at sea, and things on the sea were his area of expertise.
After Alger said that, Hobert realized that the behemoth in front of him did indeed have the shape of a ship's bow.
Thump, thump, thump~
The sound seemed to knock on their hearts, making their chests feel heavy.
Why was such a sound coming from the ship?
Taking two more steps forward, they saw a figure under the ship, swinging a hammer and striking the hull.
The figure holding the hammer stopped his movements and asked in a hoarse voice, "Who's there?"
Hobert retorted, "Who are you?"
"Of course, I'm a sailor from the 'Arianne'! The storm just now ran us aground. We're waiting for the tide to rise. Before the tide rises, the captain told me to repair the leaks in the bottom of the ship."
Hobert and Alger's gazes pierced through the fog and saw the sailor. He had a pair of pitch-black eyes, the eyeballs were completely black, with no whites.
The sailor's hair was disheveled, making it impossible to see his exact appearance. He wore a relatively neat sailor's uniform, holding a hammer in one hand and several planks of wood under the other arm.
Except for his eyes, the other person's appearance seemed completely normal, but the place where he appeared was not normal.
The two experienced old foxes, although very vigilant in their hearts, didn't show it on their faces.
Hobert even looked at the bottom of the ship in a convincing manner: "You've worked hard. It looks like this ship suffered considerable damage in the storm."
In fact, the ship was already broken into two pieces, but not completely broken. All the masts were broken off, and there were four or five large holes visible in the hull. Fortunately, it was on the shore. It was estimated that it would sink immediately upon entering the sea.
Hobert looked at the iron hammer in the "sailor's" hand and the planks of wood in the other hand. Even if he had a shipyard, he would have a hard time repairing the ship.
"Yes," the sailor said. "The storm just now was really big! The captain said that even the underworld was blown open! Hehehe. But even so, we didn't lose sight of our target."
Hobert smiled insincerely, "Your captain is quite humorous."
He asked, "What is your target?"
"Of course, it's the 'Trunsoest Empire's Number One'!" The sailor pointed his finger forward. "Look, it's right there, it hasn't gone far yet!"
Following the sailor's finger, the fog in front of Hobert and Alger suddenly parted, and they saw clear skies again, and cumulonimbus clouds stretching from the coast to the sky.
Crack~
On the cumulonimbus cloud, a huge lightning bolt flashed past, illuminating a huge ship shadow in the cumulonimbus cloud!
Hobert felt goosebumps all over his body. The ship was estimated to be at least a dozen stories high. The huge sails were like they were full of wind, pushing the giant ship forward rapidly!
Hobert said in surprise, "That's the legacy of the Trunsoest Empire."
Alger said, "The legend of the Trunsoest Empire's treasure is true!"
"Hahahaha!" The sailor laughed loudly. "These despicable Trunsoest people built this big ship, preparing to set a trap for the emperor of the great undead empire.
"But the wise Underworld Emperor discerned all of this. He grabbed the small island where this big ship was built, which was originally close to the Northern Continent, and moved it to a location close to the Southern Continent, and then issued a curse from the Undead Kingdom to them.
"But these Trunsoest people really didn't tarnish their reputation. They actually drove the ship away, so we were ordered to chase after them and sink them!"
The fog reappeared, obscuring the sky and cumulonimbus clouds again.
Hobert quickly calmed down from his shock. He remembered that in the room where Lester stored the corpse of the ancient death god, there was a note left by Duke Southville, which recorded this matter.
At that time, Mr. Azik said that the Underworld Emperor had not yet stepped into the trap when the Night Emperor fell.
It was probably because of the Night Emperor's fall that the Underworld Emperor noticed the trap and destroyed it.
In any case, this was an "old case" from more than a thousand years ago!
Hobert didn't continue to think about it, but smiled and said, "I wish you success soon. We won't disturb your work."
The sailor stared with his completely black eyeballs: "You haven't told me yet, who are you? Why are you here?"
Hobert and Alger both felt that this dilapidated ship in front of them… or rather, some kind of power on the ship was awakening, and a surge of terror permeated the surrounding fog.
Hobert was too familiar with this kind of fear. Before, in the ruins of the Trunsoest nobles, his mind had suffered enough from the ravages of this fear.
But at this time, he had to remain calm, so Hobert took a deep breath and said, "We are messengers who transport the dead in the nearby sea area. We encountered you in this special fog."
As he spoke, Hobert poured his spirituality into the "Spirit Wine Glass," allowing his body to exude the aura of the undead.
The sailor asked again, "Are you here to guide me to the great Undead Kingdom?"
"No," Hobert said. "Your captain wasn't joking. The storm just now really blew open a hole in the underworld, so you can see us."

chapters.title: Chapter 368 - 368 Attitude is Everything
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Hobert genuinely believed that the captain wasn't joking. The massive storm they had encountered was likely a storm generated by the Berserk Sea.
And there might be a Saint on board who sensed the changes in the underworld and the spirit world, which was why he said that.
Of course, the sailor didn't know that he was already a spirit world creature, but did their captain have such a concept?
Hobert's lie, told without batting an eye, worked, and the surging sense of fear didn't continue to spread.
The sailor also smiled and said, "We are all serving the great Underworld Emperor!"
"Yes, after all, He is 'the final resting place of all living beings'!" Hobert affirmed again, "It's just that our positions are different."
The sailor had no further doubts, "I hope we can chat more when we meet again in the future. Goodbye, you two."
Hobert smiled and said, "Goodbye."
He and Alger could still feel the sailor's gaze, so they had to remain calm and leave step by step.
It wasn't until the mist obscured their vision, until the "dong, dong, dong" sound rang out again, that the two quickened their pace and finally started running.
After running for more than ten minutes, the two saw a two-dimensional space ahead. After cautiously bypassing it, they finally heard the familiar bird calls from the forest.
After running a few more steps, they finally saw the high cumulonimbus clouds, the azure sky, and the dense forest.
The two were surprised to find that they were now in the elven ruins.
They quickly left along the way they came, and after more than an hour, they finally returned to the beach where they had landed.
Looking at the island again, it still had high mountains and forests, a two-dimensional space that looked like a huge mirror from a distance, and the mist on the side of the mountain, which seemed to remain constant.
Hobert and Alger exchanged glances, both feeling a sense of surviving a disaster.
Hobert smiled and said, "This is what adventure is all about. During the adventure and right after it ends, you always feel like you'll never take such a risk again in your life, but in a couple of days, you start to miss the adventure, and in another couple of days, you can't wait to go on a new adventure."
Alger nodded, "That's the standard adventurer's mindset."
The two laughed heartily. Everything terrifying and life-threatening they had encountered today became a part of their memories.
Although it was only a little after three in the afternoon, the sky on the island, like the bottom of a well, was already somewhat like dusk. Hobert reached out and put his hand on Alger's shoulder, and the space in front of them became illusory. They finally successfully entered the spirit world, which had obvious distortions.
A few minutes later, they appeared in the forest of Oravi Island.
The two took out the spoils of this exploration and placed them on a stone in front of them.
There was a pendant-like mystical item, an Beyonder characteristic of Sequence 5, a ring with a special pattern, three Beyonder materials, and corresponding blood, juices, and fruits.
Of course, there were also the main materials formed after the deaths of the Blue Shadow Falcon and the Dragon Eye Sea Eagle, but according to the previous agreement, these two main materials belonged to Alger, and he would give up one chance to choose spoils.
So Hobert used his first chance to choose spoils to select the mystical item.
In the second round of choosing spoils, Hobert had the priority, and he took the Beyonder characteristic of Sequence 5.
Alger chose the main material of Sequence 7 level and the corresponding blood.
In the third round of choosing spoils, Hobert took the ring, and Alger took a main material of Sequence 8 level and the corresponding fruit.
When it came to the last spoil, Alger was about to say that he would sell the materials in the next two days and split the proceeds, but Hobert spoke first, "Let's sacrifice it to Mr. Fool."
Alger was stunned and didn't quite understand what Hobert meant.
Hobert explained, "We chatted with the evil god in the cave for so long, we may have been secretly contaminated, so we should ask Mr. Fool to examine us. For this, we should of course offer sacrifices."
In fact, it was mainly to remove the contamination from "Hanged Man" Alger. Hobert had the "Nation of Disorder", so he wasn't afraid of this kind of contamination.
Alger felt like he had learned another trick, "But this sacrifice is too..."
Too shabby! Would Mr. Fool accept it?
Hobert smiled and said, "This mainly depends on our sincerity. Otherwise, we don't have anything that Mr. Fool would be interested in. If we really made Mr. Fool interested, we might have to sacrifice another card."
Hobert deliberately emphasized "a card", and Alger immediately understood that "Emperor" was talking about the "Blasphemy Card", that is, a complete pathway.
Alger nodded. Acting with Hobert today, he had felt more than once that he really lacked high-level knowledge, such as the high-dimensional and low-dimensional things Hobert had said before, which still gave him a headache when he thought about them.
Seeing that Alger agreed, Hobert quickly set up the altar and recited the honored name of "The Fool" in Hermes, "...Respected Mr. Fool, we encountered a sealed evil god during this exploration.
"I suspect that our spiritual bodies may have been contaminated by the evil god unknowingly, so we ask for your help and ask you to check our spiritual bodies.
"For this, we are willing to offer an Beyonder material obtained in this exploration, as well as the corresponding spiritual juices.
"We know that you may not be interested in these sacrifices at all, but this represents our attitude of dedication and respect to you."
Hobert certainly knew that "Mr. Fool" would be very interested in this. The Beyonder ingredient could be sold for 300 pounds without any problem, and those spiritual juices were also worth 30 pounds or more.
These sacrificial words were more for Alger's ears than for "Mr. Fool's" ears.
Alger also realized today that the sacrificial words were not fixed and that you could also flatter the gods.
Then he thought: No wonder Mr. Fool could tolerate "Emperor" blaspheming the gods at the Tarot Gathering. First, this was tacitly approved by Mr. Fool, and second, it might be related to the fact that "Emperor" knew better how to deal with the gods.
He also recalled "Emperor's" lie in the mist just now. He had been prepared to fight hard at that time, but he didn't expect "Emperor" to simply portray him and himself as people from the "Ghost Ship".
This made Alger have to sigh that sometimes the more you know, the easier it is to avoid some battles.
As Hobert said, a dozen seconds later, the sacrificial gate of "The Fool" appeared and accepted their sacrifices.
Immediately afterwards, Hobert and Alger were pulled into the hall above the gray fog together. Just as they came back to their senses, a polygonal transparent crystal with magical colors fell out of their bodies.
Alger's eyes narrowed. The shape of this crystal was similar to the idol enshrined in the temple of the elves!

chapters.title: Chapter 369 - 369: Mr. Fool's Exorcism Function (Bonus 1)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
[Thanks to GaapSpecter for joining the Church of MissRaven, +1 bonus]
Alger saw the crystal falling out of his body, looking like a polygonal object, but within the polygonal object seemed to contain some illusory stars.
He could see clearly all the structures inside the crystal, as if it were completely open, displaying all its structures to people.
This reminded Alger of the scene when he first saw the Spirit World, as if countless detailed pieces of information appeared before his eyes, and he felt that his eyes simply couldn't handle it all.
Later, he would automatically ignore some information, and he no longer had such troubles.
At this moment, Alger suddenly understood what "Emperor" meant by the fourth dimension.
The two crystals, as if alive, bounced around on the bronze table, emitting desperate roars: "Mysteries!"
Boundless gray fog began to flow onto the bronze table, tightly wrapping the two crystals, crushing them, and disappearing into the void.
Alger noticed that throughout this entire process, the mighty and powerful Mr. Fool didn't even lift a hand; everything was resolved so effortlessly.
Little did he know that this gray fog, in resisting external intrusions, was like the "Bell of Order" in the "Nation of Disorder," completely "automated."
Hobert quickly stood up and bowed to the Fool: "Praise the Fool!"
Alger also quickly stood up: "Praise the Fool."
"The Fool" Klein asked, "What is his current state?"
Alger was slightly stunned before realizing that "The Fool" was asking about that evil god: Mr. Fool knows who we encountered; Mr. Fool refers to the evil god as 'he,' so he probably knows that evil god!
He thought to himself: Yes, Mr. Fool certainly knows what existence we encountered. The desperate roar of the crystal was 'Mysteries!' That should be another image of Mr. Fool, or rather, Mr. Fool's image in ancient times, when he was in good condition! Since the crystal recognized Mr. Fool, Mr. Fool certainly knows which evil god we encountered.
Alger sighed, feeling that he had actually shown his face in front of two gods today.
Of course, Hobert knew that this was Klein's way of asking indirectly, but he still said in a respectful tone: "His avatar seems to be sealed by the 'Lord of Storms' in a cave.
"We are too low-level to know the specifics, nor are we very clear about which evil god it is, but from my observation, that avatar is not in good condition and cannot infiltrate any power into the real world."
Mr. Fool nodded slightly: "Go back."
Hobert and Alger's vision was covered by gray fog, and in the blink of an eye, they returned to the forest.
Hobert neatly cleaned up the altar, and then smiled at Alger: "Now let's talk about the ownership of that island.
"Although you provided the location information, I provided the means to get to that island. I think that island should be our joint discovery, and all the property on it belongs to us jointly."
Alger said somewhat helplessly, "You are right."
"If I need extraordinary materials from the island, I will inform you in advance and go to the island to find the materials I need," Hobert continued. "As for the cave and the mist, there is also a huge wealth, but before we become demigods, no one can enter the cave again.
"Until we find a way to seal the evil god, we will pretend that the Beyonder characteristics in the cave and the 'Ghost Ship' in the mist do not exist."
"For safety reasons, your idea is correct." This was also the helpless part for Alger. "Emperor" has the ability to "Travel," but he does not.
So, although the extraordinary creatures on the island nominally belong to both of them, Alger must have the "Emperor's" help to go to that island again.
And the "Emperor" can hunt the Beyonder creatures on the island as he pleases, only needing to inform Alger after the hunt.
But Alger also thought that his Sequence 6 main materials were complete, and the "Emperor" had a copy of the Sequence 5 Beyonder characteristics, so he wouldn't have to worry about potions for a long time in the future.
So, for him, it would only be a loss of some property, and this result was acceptable.
Hobert extended his hand: "Happy cooperation!"
Alger shook his hand: "Happy cooperation."
Hobert took two steps back, and the space behind him became illusory. The illusory space quickly swallowed Hobert.
Alger stood in the forest for a long time, feeling that today's adventure was the most thrilling and wonderful one so far.
...
Hobert still returned to the cemetery in Conant City first. He took off his mask and realized that he was very disheveled at this time.
His hat was blown away, his clothes were covered in scratches, especially his pants, which had a large tear ripped open by Alger!
Hobert had no choice but to change his appearance first, and after waiting for a minute, he used "Travel" to go to Feynapotter City, bought a new set of clothes, and found a public bathhouse, spending 5 copper Lire to get a private room to take a bath.
Generally, taking a bath in a public bathhouse only costs 1 to 2 copper Lire. It's not that Hobert wanted to flaunt his aristocratic status by getting a private room; nobles usually have their own luxurious bathrooms, and even beautiful maids to wash them.
It was because Hobert had too many magical items on him, each of which was worth several thousand gold Lire. If someone stole one, he would have to spend energy to find it.
Nowadays, public bathhouses can be seen everywhere in the countries of the Northern Continent, but before Roselle the Great became the consul, bathing was still a very unfamiliar thing for many nobles and ordinary people.
Many nobles never bathed in their lives, and ordinary people just took a shower in the rain.
Why did perfume become popular among the nobles? It was to cover up the smell!
In this regard, Hobert still had to thank Roselle.
Coming out of the bathhouse, Hobert finally regained some of the appearance of a Feynapotter nobleman, but his hair was still standing on end and couldn't be combed down no matter what.
Finally, Hobert used the ability of the "Faceless Necklace" to restore his hair to its original appearance.
Using "Travel" again to return to his fief, Hobert had just entered the door when Seel came out to greet him: "Lord, that, that lady said she wants to live in the lord's mansion."
Hobert glanced at Helen standing on the other side of the courtyard, and Helen responded with a flirtatious wink.
Hobert smiled slightly and called Philip over: "Arrange a room for this Miss Helen. She will enjoy the same diet and living environment as me.
"But without my permission, no one is to disturb this beautiful lady, and no one is to obey this lady's orders."
After speaking, he smiled at Helen again, but this time Helen was not in the mood to wink at Hobert anymore.
Hobert returned to his room, and after confirming that there was no one in the courtyard, he "opened" the oil painting again.
Then, using the method of sacrificing himself to himself, he sacrificed the pendant, Beyonder characteristics, and ring to the "Nation of Disorder" to disinfect them.

chapters.title: Chapter 370 - 370 High Dimension Overseer (Bonus 2)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
[Congratulations to Alrazi az for advancing to Sequence 9: Reader, +5 bonus]
As Hobert expected, these mystical items and Beyonder characteristics had once "witnessed" the descent of that evil god and were indeed affected to some extent.
The "pendant" and "ring" were fine after "listening" to the chimes of the "Bell of Order".
If it weren't for the "Bell of Order" disinfecting them, Hobert would often carry the pendant with him, and he would definitely be contaminated after a long time.
The former owner of the Beyonder characteristic died from losing control, so it was severely contaminated and could not be taken directly.
So Hobert simply crushed it with the "Power of Disorder", and the contamination in the Beyonder characteristic easily dissipated.
Hobert planned to divide this Beyonder characteristic into five parts. Alger, the "Hanged Man", was a potential customer for the "Ocean Songster". The other Sequence 9 to Sequence 6 opportunities would be dealt with through other channels.
Then Hobert took the pendant in his hand again, and using the authority of the "Nation of Disorder", he quickly understood the pendant's ability:
"It can use the ability of 'Lightning Strike' to create a lightning attack with a paralyzing effect on the opponent, which is very effective against undead opponents; it can fly in low altitude for three minutes; it can dive underwater and move freely for 1 hour; it can create sharp wind blades to attack enemies; it can control a small area of water."
Hobert could guess most of the negative effects: "Wearing the pendant makes you prone to irritability, and even when there is no advantage, you will use all your potential out of anger to fight the enemy to the death. After wearing it continuously for one hour, the wearer's actions tend to become reckless, and they will attack as soon as they sense hostility!"
Hobert summoned the "Power of Order" to seal it again as usual, otherwise who could stand becoming an "irritable old man" after wearing the pendant?
Even if he could exert all his potential, he would still die if he encountered a demigod opponent now.
After being resealed, the negative effects have been greatly improved: "The wearer is prone to irritability and recklessness when using this pendant, and will try every means to defeat the enemy until there is no other way."
Although it is still easy to become irritable and reckless, at least it won't fight the enemy to the death, and it will only be affected when using the pendant. The negative effects have been greatly improved.
Originally, Hobert planned to leave it in the "Nation of Disorder" temporarily, but after recalling the pendant's abilities, Hobert, sitting on the "Iron Throne", sighed: "The 'Tyrant' pathway has many attack skills, including three elements: lightning, wind, and water, and most of the skills are biased towards being strong and fierce."
With this pendant, Hobert felt that his strength could reach a new level, and it would be a pity to leave it on the stone platform to gather dust.
After thinking for a while, Hobert had a proper way to use it: "Whenever I encounter an enemy that is difficult to defeat, I will run away quickly and not use the pendant.
"If I encounter an enemy that I am confident I can deal with, I won't be afraid of fighting him to the end."
Thinking of this, Hobert decided to name the pendant the "Ocean Pendant" and take it out to use.
At this time, Hobert remembered that he had not named the ring given by Philip I, so Hobert named it the "Light Ring" according to his naming habits.
After dealing with the mystical items, Hobert's eyes turned to the last trophy, the golden ring.
Taking the ring in his hand, Hobert found that the ring was not made of pure gold, but rather a colored gold material, and the colors were very bright under the light.
On one side of the ring, Hobert found a simple pattern, depicting a tortoise carrying a snake on its back.
Although the brushwork was simple, it was very vivid.
Hobert thought for a while, but couldn't recall any place in the North and South Continent where this pattern was popular. Instead, he thought of the image he had seen in the Common Era: Xuan Ming.
He was the sea god, wind god, and plague god of the "Eastern World", or rather the "Western Continent". When he appeared in the image of a tortoise and a snake, he represented the image of the sea god, also known as Xuanwu.
When he appeared in the image of a human face and a bird body, he represented the power of the plague god.
So it is understandable that the elves, who have modified the "Western Continent" culture, would carve the pattern of Xuan Ming on the ring.
Hobert threw the ring on the stone platform over there. He felt that although this ring had no extraordinary effect, it should have a significant effect in a certain occasion or a certain place.
After dealing with the three trophies, Hobert began to review today's adventure.
In fact, when entering the "Sefirah Castle", Hobert, who had recovered the memories related to the Outer Gods, had already realized that what he encountered today was not an evil god, but most likely the "High-Dimensional Overseer".
Among the Outer Gods in Hobert's memory, it seems that only the "High-Dimensional Overseer" can form a close logical chain with the clues found on the island.
Hobert did not know the specific abilities of the "High-Dimensional Overseer", but since the title contains the word "high-dimensional", it should represent that He has relevant authority in terms of space.
Moreover, slightly different from the "Door" pathway, He seems to be able to manipulate low-dimensional space.
The spatial magic of the "Door" pathway, explained by the "scientific concept" in Hobert's mind, is to open up a three-dimensional space in the fourth dimension, and use the fourth dimension to accurately find the entrance to the opened three-dimensional space no matter where you are.
No matter how closed a three-dimensional space is, from the perspective of the fourth dimension, there are countless ways to bypass obstacles.
Just like what seems to be an insurmountable obstacle for two-dimensional creatures is just a circle on paper for three-dimensional creatures.
For the three-dimensional world, or for the real world, because the fourth dimension is not restricted by the real world, spatial magic can open the three-dimensional space established in the fourth dimension at any time.
The above is the authority of the "Door" pathway in terms of space, and the "High-Dimensional Overseer" also has the authority to manipulate low dimensions. The two-dimensional spaces on the island are the evidence.
So in addition to the spatial authority of the "Door" pathway, He seems to also have the authority to distort the real world into two-dimensional space.
That's right, Hobert believes that this should be an extreme "distortion", or a corresponding "spatial grafting" has been done.
In addition, the "High-Dimensional Overseer" can obviously find loopholes in low-dimensional space from high-dimensional space.
Space, grafting, loopholes, this makes Hobert guess that the "High-Dimensional Overseer" possesses certain authorities close to the "Lord of Mysteries".
Of course, this is just Hobert's guess. After all, the authorities of the Outer Gods and the Outer Deities in the Cosmos are quite distorted, and it may be an unknown authority.
But in any case, it is beyond doubt that the "High-Dimensional Overseer" has the corresponding authority of space. He should have used the spirit world to corrupt the elves' saint.

chapters.title: Chapter 371 - 371: Missing a Baroness (Bonus 3)
chapters.content:
join p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Hobert recalled the murals he had seen in the temple. It was after the formation of the Berserk Sea that the elven sages heard the voice from the darkness.
What Hobert was also concerned about was that the murals did not depict the misty area, or rather, the place where reality and the spirit world intersected.
Connecting these doubts with the "High-Dimensional Overseer," a relatively rigorous chain of logic formed in Hobert's mind:
After the formation of the Berserk Sea, although the elven sages blocked the stormy weather outside the island, they could not prevent the collision between the spirit world and the space on the island.
The "High-Dimensional Overseer" used the spirit world to bypass Earth's protection in the astral plane and project a weak force onto this special area, polluting the sage and the remaining elven population in this sea area.
As a result, they changed their faith and tried to bring the "High-Dimensional Overseer" into the world.
The process of the "High-Dimensional Overseer"'s descent caused violent chaos in the space on the island, which is why so many two-dimensional space fragments appeared, and why one-third of the island was shrouded in mist, becoming a place where reality and the spirit world merged.
Hobert had described what happened next in the cave. Because the elves were already sacrificing their lives to the "Lord of Storms" when the mist appeared, there were no descriptions or clues about the mist in the elven ruins.
This was the most logical guess Hobert made based on the available clues, and he believed it should be close to the truth.
Then Hobert thought of the "Trunsoest Empire," which looked even bigger than an aircraft carrier, and was located in a corner of the Berserk Sea.
Like the legends, it was as big as a city, but he didn't know if the passengers they expected were members of the Trunsoest family or the Underworld Emperor Salinger?
Since this was a trap, he wondered what its specific abilities were?
Thinking of this, Hobert shook his head. He had too little information to make a logical guess.
However, thanks to the ghost ship he encountered in the mist, Hobert had some guesses about the location of the "Trunsoest Empire": it should have been blown by the storm to the place where the spirit world and the real world merged.
It was hard to say exactly where, but it was certainly within the unexplored area of the Berserk Sea.
After figuring out these questions, Hobert took a deep breath and brought the "Ocean Pendant" into the real world through bestowal.
At this time, it was already dark. Hobert temporarily "closed" the oil painting, rested for half an hour, and came to the front yard for dinner.
To his surprise, Helen also appeared at the dinner table. When she learned that today's dinner was only stewed mutton and Feynapotter noodles, she said, "Your Lordship, you are also a nobleman, how can you eat these things?"
Hobert used chopsticks. Yes, he had the carpenter who repaired the mansion specially make him a few pairs of chopsticks, which were just a little longer and thicker than he had expected.
Fortunately, Hobert's strength had also improved a lot, so he could use them fairly smoothly.
After eating a mouthful of noodles with chopsticks, Hobert sighed, this was the correct way to eat noodles. Using a knife and fork to eat noodles was too boring.
After chewing the food in his mouth, Hobert said, "Tell the chef in advance what you want to eat. As long as the request is not too excessive, let him try his best to satisfy you."
It was just a little food, Hobert certainly wouldn't be stingy.
"I want to eat you." Helen stuck out her tongue and licked her tempting lips lightly.
Hobert was a little helpless: "Using 'Charm' at the dinner table is very unappetizing."
Helen smiled and put away "Charm": "At least it proves that you are a normal man."
As she spoke, she happily ate her dinner, and the plate of mutton in front of her seemed even more delicious than before.
After dinner, Hobert returned to his bedroom again, and then used "Travel" to come to Christian's mansion. The paper, pens, ink, stationery, etc. that he had asked Dophis to purchase had been neatly piled up in the room.
When Hobert went to thank Dophis, he learned that Christian had not gone out to attend the banquet today, so he and Dophis went to Christian's living room to meet.
During the chat, Hobert roughly talked about the situation of his territory.
Christian said: "If you really can't deal with those hidden organizations, I can take action to deter them. It's not good to have a witch staying in the mansion."
Then he changed the subject: "Maybe there is another way."
Christian smiled and said, "Now I am also a favorite in front of the king. Although I have offended some dignitaries because of the reform, there are also many people who want to use my power to obtain more political resources."
"So they used the simplest and most effective trick: marriage!
"But your mother and Donna and Tyron are coming to Feynapotter City in a few days. They seem to have just remembered at this time that Earl Christian has a wife."
Hobert asked: "Are mother and the others okay?"
"They left Backlund so early that they were not affected." Christian explained, and continued: "And Donna and Tyron have never been famous, so they have set their sights on you.
"In the past two days, more than a dozen nobles and arms dealers have hoped to send their daughters and dowries to your territory.
"I can arrange a marriage for you. The woman's family's power can help you develop the territory, and you can also use your wife or her family's power to contain the representatives sent by the 'Theosophy Order', but don't expect to get love in this marriage."
This made Hobert slightly stunned. He remembered the last time he was so popular was in high school.
At that time, he was tall and handsome and could play basketball.
Hobert smiled wryly: "Can I refuse?"
He had so many secrets on him that he really didn't dare to find a confidante he didn't trust at all.
"Yes." Christian smiled and said, "But unless you are like me and have a wife on the way, it is difficult to refuse the enthusiasm of the nobles."
He paused and said: "Especially when you have made some achievements in your territory, maybe earls and dukes will ask the king to intervene in your marriage. At that time, you won't be able to refuse even if you want to."
Hobert thought for a while: "Give me a few days to think about it."
Christian nodded: "Of course."
Back in his territory, Hobert thought for a long time, wondering if he should accept Christian's arrangement?
So he changed his mind: "Do I need a wife now?
"No, what I need is a shield, a trustworthy and close partner, but I don't need a wife.
"Then the problem is simple, I can hire a wife!"
Hobert seemed to have found a solution and fell asleep in constant fantasy.
Early the next morning, Hobert looked at the Lord's Mansion under renovation and asked Philip, "The mansion is about to be repaired, and I have regained control of the territory. Do you think there is anything else I lack as a baron?"
"Your Lordship, you are still missing a baroness."

chapters.title: Chapter 372 - 372 A New Round of Tarot Club (Bonus 4)
chapters.content:

Hobert nodded slightly upon hearing Philip's reply.
Perhaps with a Baroness, he could better play the role of 'Baron'.
Then he needed to 'find' a Baroness as soon as possible.
However, there was a more pressing matter today. Hobert called over the three teachers and the fifteen literate individuals: "Have you mastered those forms?"
After receiving affirmative responses, Hobert instructed them to move the paper, pens, and stationery from his courtyard to the front yard: "Alright, now, using the previous forms as a guide, transcribe at least three thousand new forms! The deadline is within two days."
During his inspection of the territory, Hobert estimated that there were just over two thousand people under his rule.
Everyone was stunned, which meant they had to produce 100 forms per person per day.
The female teacher said, "Your Grace, this is an impossible task."
They had tried it these past two days and could only produce one form in about 15 minutes, four forms in an hour. It would take 25 hours to complete this workload, but there are only 24 hours in a day.
Hobert took the paper and pen and smiled: "I know this task is challenging, but as long as you pay attention to the methods, it is not too difficult to complete.
"You have a total of 18 people, who can be divided into two groups. Then, break down this form into nine equally sized parts, with each person only responsible for the same part. This will greatly improve efficiency.
"I suggest dividing it into these nine parts. Give it a try."
They divided into groups and tried it according to Hobert's instructions, completing a form in nearly two minutes.
But instead of being discouraged, they were very happy. Of course, they knew that after drawing dozens of them, they would become very proficient in their respective processes, and then a group could probably produce a form in one minute.
Hobert smiled again: "If you complete the task, you will receive double pay for these days."
The enthusiasm of the dozen or so people was completely mobilized.
Hobert glanced at the motivated group and returned to his room alone to drink tea.
After lunch, Hobert came to check again and found that more than four hundred forms had been produced. If they worked overtime in the evening, producing 1500 forms today should not be a problem.
In the afternoon, Hobert took a nap and woke up around three o'clock, attending the Tarot Gathering on time.
When the members reappeared in the giant-like hall, sitting at the long copper table that seemed to have a long history, this week's Tarot Gathering officially began.
"Good afternoon, Mr. Fool." The Tarot Gathering entered the first segment: "Miss Justice's" greetings.
While "Justice" Audrey greeted everyone individually, Hobert was thinking about the candidate for Baroness.
Today, he already had some ideas: he could ask a female member of the Tarot Gathering to become his wife.
Although they were all in Backlund, Hobert's 'Travel' ability perfectly solved this problem.
They could be in Backlund in the morning without affecting their role as Baroness in Jeffery Town in the afternoon.
The current candidates were three: "Justice" Audrey, "Magician" Fors, and Xio, who had not yet joined.
Just as Audrey was greeting him, Hobert had already quietly eliminated her. The reason was simple: she had no freedom at all, and he believed she had no interest in being a Baroness.
Although it was only a cooperative relationship, Hobert felt that the probability of Audrey agreeing was very small.
Unless he personally went to propose to Earl Hall and won Audrey's heart.
Hobert knew that, at this stage, this was impossible. First, because he was only a Baron, and a Baron whose fief was in a remote area. Such a proposal would only be ridiculed.
Secondly, he was now a traitor, and Earl Hall would certainly not take this risk.
So Hobert turned his attention to Fors. Miss 'Magician' was very suitable!
First of all, she was already independent and had enough freedom, and she didn't have a proper job... cough, her working hours were flexible.
As long as he offered a price that made being a Baroness more profitable than writing books, and then explained the concept of cooperation to her, so that she wouldn't feel any psychological pressure, the probability of success should be high.
Moreover, Fors' image was also very good. Although she had not received noble training, her detached and lazy temperament was more attractive than that of a noble.
Hobert also remembered that Fors' figure was quite impressive. She might not have Helen's charm when using 'Bewitchment', but with his support, suppressing the other party was not a problem.
If it were Xio, it would be difficult to say. Helen would only think that Hobert was a pervert who liked 'a student who is still in grammar school'.
This would not only be difficult to suppress Helen, but would also make her more excited, and perhaps even try to sneak into Hobert's room.
Audrey, who had finished greeting, felt that Hobert's eyes were a little strange today, and his body language seemed to be planning something.
However, her attention was quickly drawn to "Sun" Derrick. "Sun" was obviously a little anxious.
Fors also felt that "Emperor" seemed to be staring at her chest for a moment, but another thing prevented her from thinking about this issue in detail.
Just last week, another case occurred where Tarot cards were left at the scene. This time, the cards left at the scene were 'Death' and 'Judgment'.
"Hanged Man" Alger was in a very good mood. He had become a Sequence 6, so this old fox did not even notice "Emperor's" strangeness.
Next was the time for everyone to contribute their diaries. Alger contributed three pages of his diary and communicated with Mr. Fool separately, not knowing what information he had exchanged.
However, Alger looked unusually excited after the separate communication, as if he had exchanged for some information that he thought was important.
After "Fool" Klein finished reading the diary, Alger turned his head and asked "Sun": "What did you learn from the former captain of that exploration team?"
Derrick honestly replied: "He is dead."
"Dead?" The other members were a little surprised, but "Emperor's" surprise was obviously half a beat slower.
Derrick briefly described what had happened a week ago. When he heard that the captain had suddenly lost control, Alger asked: "So, which elder saved you?"
Derrick's mouth opened little by little, his face full of surprise.
Alger spread his hands: "According to your description, the high-level members of your City of Silver are consciously letting people contact that guy to see if they can extract useful information from him. Then they will definitely carefully observe the changes at the bottom of the round tower.
"This is obvious. As long as you have enough knowledge, you can easily see it."
Audrey said somewhat depressedly in her heart: I didn't think of that.
Fors stroked her hair with a sense of shame: I didn't see it.
