Using his "Spirit Wine Glass," Hobert accelerated the extraction of Beyonder characteristics from the three enemies. To his surprise, the one he had just killed with a single punch was actually a "Reaper"!
He hadn't expected that after his Sequence 5 trap was discovered, he would be so easily defeated!
Then Hobert realized that it wasn't that the opponent was weak, but that the qualitative change of a demigod had created a large gap between him and Sequence 5.
This reminded him of when he encountered the "Demoness of Despair" in Backlund. Wasn't he also completely outmatched then! Fortunately, he had a Grade 1 Sealed Artifact at the time, or he would have been easily killed.
Hobert also recalled when he killed his first Sequence 5. He was very excited then, but from today on, killing a Sequence 5 was going to be a very easy thing.
After collecting the three Beyonder characteristics, Hobert continued to chase. With a "Distortion," he was already seven or eight meters away, and with another "Distortion," he was another seven or eight meters.
Unless the other party was sitting on a rocket, how could they possibly outrun Hobert?
After chasing for more than ten seconds, Hobert found that he had chased back to the pier again. It turned out that the other party had run a circle and returned to his ship!
At this time, the "Vice Admiral Dusk's" flagship, the Dawn Light, was operating at full power. It unexpectedly turned its head sharply against all reason, and after capsizing another pirate ship, quickly left the port.
Until this moment, the sails on the flagship showed no signs of being unfurled. The whole process was as if an invisible giant hand was pushing the giant ship away from the port.
Hobert flew low to catch up, and as he got closer to the giant ship, he was hit by a "Storm of Light."
"Disorder!" The attacks, like fragments of light spots, suddenly fell into directional chaos in the area ahead. The attacks that were originally aimed at Hobert scattered.
Some of these light fragments hit the sea, some hit the land not far away, and some bounced back and hit the giant ship itself.
Each fragment of light exploded with about the same power as a cannonball. For a time, the sound of explosions in the surrounding sea was constant, and the water mist that was set off submerged Hobert.
"Distortion!" Hobert, in the water mist, "Distorted" the giant ship's direction of advance, turning the departure to sea into entering the port. So the giant ship once again turned its bow 180 degrees against all reason and rushed towards Hobert.
The water mist dissipated, and Hobert, standing on the water, "Distorted" the buoyancy of the sea under his feet, and punched the giant ship fiercely: "Magnify!"
The giant ship, several tens of meters long, shook violently on the sea, as if it had collided with another ship, and almost lost its forward momentum.
Hobert was pushed back a distance by the giant ship. He did not expect that his full blow would only create a fist-sized hole in the giant ship!
This giant ship seemed to have some of the "Barrier" ability of a Sequence 5. Even a full blow from a demigod had limited destructive power.
Hobert adjusted his posture: "Magnify!"
He "Magnified" the low-flying ability of the "Ocean Pendant," and like a swift flying bird, leaped up onto the deck.
"Vice Admiral Dusk" Bulatov, wearing "Dawn Armor" and holding a "Dawn Greatsword," had been waiting on the ship for a long time.
After Hobert boarded the ship, the greatsword in Bulatov's hand shattered, and he once again used the "Storm of Light" against Hobert!
Of course, Bulatov could feel the gap between himself and the enemy, but what he had to do now was to delay as much time as possible. He had already informed the Feysac Empire's military of his situation through prayer.
In a few minutes, his own demigods would arrive to support him. He just needed to find a way to hold on for a while longer.
"Connection!" Hobert strengthened the Connection between the fragments of light flying towards him and the "Dawn Light" emanating from the ship.
To Bulatov's surprise, his "Storm of Light" all hit the ship's hull. Most of the sailors on the deck were killed or injured, including the flagship's boatswain.
Hobert drew his knife and rushed towards Bulatov: "Magnify!"
"Vice Admiral Dusk" quickly re-condensed the "Dawn Greatsword," but it was too late. He was cut through the "Dawn Armor" by Hobert and was knocked away by his great force, crashing heavily onto the ship's hull.
At this time, a corpse beside Hobert suddenly attacked him, the rapier in his hand pointing directly at Hobert's vital point.
However, Hobert was prepared. He had noticed when the "Storm of Light" exploded that this person had not been directly hit by the fragments of light, but he had fallen to the ground.
So when the other party suddenly attacked, Hobert didn't panic: "Exploit!"
He made the other party's "Cull" end prematurely, so when the other party's rapier stabbed over, Hobert easily deflected it with his black knife, and then kicked the other party in the chest: "Magnify!"
This "Reaper" didn't even have time to let the flames all over his body emerge and assume a defensive posture before being kicked away, knocking down the giant ship's main mast.
Hobert abandoned the other party and "Distorted" the distance between himself and the "Vice Admiral Dusk": "Corrosion!"
On the entire deck, the people who were preparing to jump into the water to escape suddenly thought of the wealth they had hidden on the ship, or suddenly thought of the captain's wealth, and rushed into the cabins one after another.
The "Vice Admiral Dusk" was also affected by "Corrosion." His heart became very dark, and the dawn light on the entire ship suddenly went out.
He knew that it would be difficult for him to wait for the support of his own demigods. Since he couldn't live, no one else should think about living, so he removed all the defensive power of the ship.
Hobert stepped on Bulatov's chest and was about to kill him with a knife.
Thump~
With a muffled sound, the ship shook violently, and Hobert took a few steps back to maintain his balance.
It turned out that after the ship lost control, it slammed into the pier.
Amid the exclamations of the people on the shore, the giant ship finally stopped, but because the defensive power of the giant ship disappeared, a large hole was knocked out of the bow, and seawater was rapidly pouring into the cabins.
The violent vibration awakened Bulatov from the state of "Corrosion." The "Dawn Armor" on his body became solid again, and there was a solid "Barrier" on the outside.
With these two layers of protection, he could at least withstand three blows from the demigod in front of him!
Moreover, with these two layers of protection, his resistance to Beyonder abilities greatly increased!
But he underestimated the ability of a demigod too much. "Tamper!" Hobert "Tampered" the intensity of the surrounding light, fundamentally weakening Bulatov's ability.
This was an "Tampering" of the basic laws of nature, not aimed at Bulatov, so Bulatov's basic resistance did not play any role.
Then Hobert stabbed out with a knife: "Magnify!"
Bulatov's two layers of protection were pierced like fragile bubbles, and Hobert's knife directly pierced into his head.
With an unbelievable expression, the dawn light on Bulatov's body gradually weakened.
The "Reaper" who had been kicked away by Hobert earlier had already run to the edge of the deck, just as he was about to jump into the water to escape.
Hobert reached out to him: "Arrogance!"
So the "Reaper" arrogantly thought that he had a chance to defeat this demigod. After he threw a "Blazing White Spear" at Hobert, he used "Weakness Investigation" to look for the other party's weaknesses.
Hobert kicked a weapon on the deck towards the "Reaper" to test the ability of "Bestowal."
The "Reaper" immediately showed a very impatient performance. Before he could find the enemy's weakness, he rushed towards the other party.
Hobert concluded: First "Bestow," then use abilities such as "Charm." That was a technique to deal with demigod targets. When facing opponents below the demigod level, "Bestowal" itself has the ability to make the target impatient and irrational.
Hobert kicked the "Reaper's" leg and broke it, and then punched the other party unconscious.
At this moment, Archibald climbed onto the ship with two puppets: "You guys ran too fast. I finally caught up with you!"
Only then did Hobert notice that Bulatov's body was gone: "This 'Reaper' is yours!"
This "Reaper," as well as the "Dawn Paladin" just now, were the rewards he had promised Archibald when he hunted the six-legged imp before.
He came to the place where Bulatov had died just now. There was still a small pool of blood on the ground, proving that Hobert had indeed killed the other party just now.
Hobert began to look for "Connection," but he found that this blood had a lot of Connection with the entire ship!
Archibald saw Hobert's confusion and divined: "This ship will not sink, and the captain will not die!"
Hobert was stunned, marveling that the "Pirate Admiral's" ship was simply a Grade 1 Sealed Artifact.
The reason why it wasn't Grade 0 was because Hobert realized that the so-called "The ship will not sink, and the captain will not die" must have certain limitations. Otherwise, this ship would not appear on the sea, but would appear in the Feysac Empire's palace for their emperor to use.
Archibald divined again: "The captain is in the captain's room."
Hobert nodded and immediately entered the captain's room. Sure enough, he saw the more than two-meter-tall Bulatov sitting on a golden chair and smiling: "Unless you can sink the ship within two minutes, your raid will fail, because my reinforcements will be able to arrive by then."
The wound on his forehead had healed, and he looked as if he had never been injured.
Although there was a large hole in the bow, it would not sink for a while, and it might only run aground in the port, making it even more difficult for the giant ship to sink completely.
Hobert ignored the other party's words, but carefully observed the golden chair. He noticed that there was a knife mark on the back of the chair, which looked very much like it was caused by his black knife.
So, Hobert charged forward fiercely. Bulatov quickly dodged, but Hobert "distorted" the distance between them, quickly catching up and kicking "Vice Admiral Dusk" to the ground.
This time, Hobert twisted "Vice Admiral Dusk's" neck.
Crack~
A table next to the golden chair shattered. The "Vice Admiral Dusk," who should have been dead without a doubt, broke free from Hobert and once again sat on the golden chair.
Hobert finally understood what was happening. He smiled and said, "It's not that you've been resurrected, it's just that this ship is taking the fatal attacks for you."
"Also, possibly influenced by your 'Hunter' pathway colleagues, you really like setting traps!"
"You deliberately sat on this chair just to make me think this chair is the key."
"The shattered table just now has proven that whatever on this ship or in the captain's cabin is taking the fatal blow for you. The golden chair is just like the table, nothing special!"
"This is clearly a trap you came up with on the spur of the moment! Just to stall for a little more time."
Bulatov was slightly stunned, not expecting the other party to find the pattern of his "resurrection" so quickly, and even expose his trap.
"Don't underestimate a 'Lawyer's' ability to summarize patterns and their logical abilities!" Hobert smiled. "I've already figured out how to kill you!"
Saying this, Hobert charged over again. Bulatov ran a few steps before being caught by Hobert once more.
However, this time Bulatov didn't give up resisting. Instead, he had a dagger in his hand, and fiercely stabbed at Hobert, hitting Hobert's chest!
"Distort!"
Almost at the same time, Hobert distorted the concept between himself and Bulatov. A hole immediately appeared in Bulatov's chest, and blood flowed freely.
Hobert had long discovered that this "Pirate Admiral" wasn't quite right, because even a Sequence 5 couldn't be caught so easily.
Therefore, Hobert judged that the reason the other party had been easily caught twice in a row was that he was brewing some kind of attack that could harm a demigod, so he had been on guard.
It's just that the other party's attack should be something like a "fatal attack" that couldn't be dodged.
Hobert snatched the dagger and "distorted" his injury, turning a serious injury into a minor one. The wound quickly stopped bleeding.
Then, he "magnified" Bulatov's injury, turning a serious injury into a fatal one. Bulatov once again looked like he was on his last breath.
This time, however, Hobert wasn't in a hurry to kill the "Vice Admiral Dusk." Instead, he grabbed him and left the captain's cabin, walking step by step towards the edge of the deck.
At this time, Archibald, who had successfully turned the "Reaper" into a marionette, was commanding the marionettes to attack the enemy sailors.
He glanced at Hobert and immediately understood that this "Vice Admiral Dusk" was about to be completely killed.
Bulatov seemed to realize something and began to struggle violently, but Hobert's hand was like an iron hoop, gripping his neck. No matter how he struggled, he couldn't break free.
Hobert jumped from the tall ship to the shore, and while leaving the giant ship, he said, "That's right, only on the ship can that ship take the fatal damage for you."
"If you leave the ship, the connection between you will be broken! It will no longer be able to take the damage for you!"
Hobert smiled and said, "That's why you went through such a big detour and returned to the ship. Logically speaking, your best choice would have been to jump into the sea, or continue to play cat and mouse with me in the dense forest."
Bulatov shouted, "I can take you to our base! There, I and my pirate crew have ten years of savings, with a total value of over 300,000 pounds!"
Because Hobert spoke in Loenese, his unit of measurement for property was pounds!
Hobert smiled, "That's the part that the Feysac Empire got, right! I don't believe a pirate has so much savings!"
He felt that the distance was about right, threw Bulatov on the ground, and stepped on him.
Bulatov was shocked, not expecting the other party to know his secrets. He quickly said again, "I know the location of the Spring of Immortality! I can take you there."
Hobert remained unmoved, "Last Monday afternoon, I just learned that the so-called 'Spring of Immortality' is actually a trap set by the 'King of Immortality,' Agalito."
Bulatov was completely desperate, not expecting the other party to even know this!
Hobert raised his knife and chopped off the other party's head with one strike!
This time, Bulatov's headless body twitched a few times and quickly died completely.
Hobert smiled, as if speaking to the corpse in front of him, and as if speaking to himself, "Never underestimate a lawyer's ability to summarize patterns and find loopholes."
At this moment, Hobert suddenly paused and looked towards the distant sea.
A fireball was flying towards them rapidly.
The enemy's demigod had arrived ahead of schedule!
Hobert once again "magnified" the "Glide" ability, quickly flew to the ship, and stood in front of Archibald.
Although Hobert had just been promoted, if the two cooperated well, it wouldn't be difficult to leave the other party behind as well.
Hobert released the seals on "1-101" and "1-107," preparing to face the enemy. However, the fireball drew a beautiful arc on the surface of the sea and flew away again.
Hobert was slightly stunned, but immediately understood. The other party should be a demigod of the "Hunter" pathway. He must have sensed the danger, so when he realized that "Vice Admiral Dusk" was probably beyond saving and didn't have the confidence to defeat the opponent, he flew away.
However, the enemy's first wave of support had already arrived, and the second wave of support might not be far away, so Hobert and Archibald no longer expanded their gains and began to clean up the battlefield.
While accelerating the extraction of Beyonder characteristics, Hobert also found a pirate who was injured and unable to escape, knocked him unconscious, and was going to use him for an experiment later.
Then, Hobert jumped to the shore, picked up Bulatov's Beyonder characteristic, and wrapped the other party's head in a cloak to take it away.
After initially cleaning up the battlefield, Hobert divided into two waves, first taking Archibald and his marionettes to a nearby island. Hobert went back twice, once to take away the captured pirate, and once to take away the "Vice Admiral Dusk's" boatswain and the head of the "Reaper" who was killed by Hobert in the forest.
After taking all the spoils to the nameless island, Hobert resealed the sealed items on his body before sending Archibald and the spoils back to Jeffery Territory in trips.
… …
The port where "Vice Admiral Dusk's" fleet was docked. About three minutes after Hobert and Archibald left, the fireball from before flew back.
The fireball landed on the shore, forming a burning humanoid figure. The flames dissipated, revealing a man with a stern face.
At the same time, a touch of twilight radiance came from the horizon, quickly streaking across the sky like a shooting star, and finally exploded on the giant ship. A large man over two meters tall, wearing battle-suitable bishop's robes, walked out from inside.
This wasn't his own ability, but he was "launched" from afar, with the target being this ship.
The two demigods looked at each other and respectively grabbed a sailor to ask about the situation just now.
Because Hobert's surprise attack was on Bulatov's flagship, the other pirate ships, except for one that was destroyed by the collision, all managed to escape.
Finally, the two demigods met in front of the giant ship. The one who came in the form of a fireball was "Iron-Blooded Knight" Grisha, and the one who came using the twilight radiance was "Demon Hunter" Orezka.
Orezka guessed, "A demigod from the Loen military?"
The Loen military and the Feynapotter military each have several demigods of the "Lawyer" pathway.
Grisha shook his head, "Doesn't seem like it."
If it were a demigod from the Loen military, he wouldn't be wearing a mask.
Moreover, the demigods of each country are numbered and watched by each other. If a Loen military demigod ran to the sea to kill people, Grisha would definitely get the news.
Grisha frowned and said, "Could it be a newly promoted demigod from the Loen military?"
He had such a guess because the three enemies (including Archibald's marionettes), although wearing Feynapotter-style clothes, spoke Loen.
And since it was a "group crime," there was likely an organization behind them.
The first thing the two demigods thought of regarding an organization hostile to the Feysac Empire was the Loen military.
But a new problem arose. Orezka asked, "How did they find Bulatov?"
One of the "Pirate Admiral's" greatest advantages was: it's difficult to find them on the vast sea!
Their flagships all have anti-divination designs. Even a demigod-level divination, without corresponding related items, simply cannot divine their location.
So, theoretically speaking, the demigods of various forces can relatively easily kill the "Pirate Admiral" in direct combat, but such things rarely happen.
In addition to the balance between the forces, another reason is that it is difficult for the demigods of other forces to find the "Pirate Admiral."
And it doesn't make much sense. Everyone knows that this is the Black Gloves. The death of one "Pirate Admiral" will be immediately replaced by another Sequence 5 pirate.
Since the murderer had a way to find Bulatov, it meant that the other party had rich channels. So, the two demigods once again thought of the Loen military.
Because today was the day Bulatov secretly met with the Feysac Empire's intelligence personnel, they guessed that the Loen military personnel might have intercepted this information and found Bulatov.
… …
Feynapotter Kingdom, Jeffery Territory.
Hobert sent Archibald back to the military camp again. From today onwards, Archibald had two more adjutants.
For Archibald, this wasn't just a simple increase in strength; it was also a form of recognition from the "Creator," bringing him closer to completely resolving the seal on his body.
During this time, Archibald continued to pray to the "Creator" every three days, asking the "Creator" to remove the corruption on his body. However, after that first time, Archibald had never seen the image of the "Creator" again.
It guessed that the subsequent removal of corruption was likely due to a "divine automatic response" mechanism, as the "Creator" couldn't possibly always pay attention to such trivial matters.
What it didn't know was that the great "Creator" hadn't found a suitable worker yet, so he had to handle everything himself, big or small.
The reason Hobert so frequently eliminated the corruption for Archibald was to establish the image of the "Creator" in Archibald's mind.
Since he was preparing to tame... ahem, preparing to subdue this extraordinary creature, he had to patiently establish his position in the other's mind.
Hobert remembered that this trick worked best when training dogs.

chapters.title: Chapter 527 - 527: Hobert in Audrey's Eyes
chapters.content:
join the Church of MissRaven and become a Sequence 9: Reader p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Returning to the study, Hobert took the "Psychological Spoon" from the "Nation of Disorder", and brought the still-unconscious pirate to a small, nameless island at sea.
First, he woke the pirate with seawater, and then used the "Psychological Spoon" to hypnotize him.
After Hobert left the deserted island, the pirate began to set up an altar and perform a ritual of bestowal to the "Creator".
Hobert did not return to the Jeffrey Territory. Instead, he randomly found a wilderness in the Northern Continent. After confirming that there was no danger nearby, he entered the "Nation of Disorder".
Sitting on the "Iron Throne", Hobert saw a strange star flickering in the pool. He extended his spirituality and, sure enough, it was that pirate.
So Hobert dragged out the phantom of Trunsoest from the distant pool. The other party seemed to know what Hobert was going to do and smiled contemptuously at Hobert.
Hobert snorted coldly and threw the other party into the somewhat shaky "Gates of the Divine Kingdom".
However, the other party only went as far as the "Gates of the Divine Kingdom" and refused to go out, as if stuck there.
Hobert mobilized the power of the "Nation of Disorder" to push the other party out with force. It looked like he was flattening the other party, but it was still useless, and they remained stuck there.
After trying for a long time, Hobert had no choice but to give up and send the somewhat deformed phantom of Trunsoest back to the pool to seal it up.
This method won't work! I have to think of another way, but for the time being, Hobert had no ideas.
After checking again to ensure that the seal was secure, he decided to maintain the status quo and wait until he had a good idea.
Returning to the real world, he first killed the pirate on the nameless island and erased the traces of the altar's existence.
Only then did Hobert contact "The Hanged Man" Alger through Mr. Fool, and met Alger in the forest of Simm Island in the southern Berserk Sea with the two corpses.
Alger knew that "The Emperor" was coming to him again, most likely to deal with the pirate bounty. He was surprised only after seeing the faces of the corpses clearly: "The first mate and boatswain of 'Vice Admiral Dusk'?"
The scene of helping to deal with the important members of "Admiral of Blood" was still vivid in his mind, and now "The Emperor" was targeting "Vice Admiral Dusk" again?
Hobert, wearing a mask, smiled and said, "That's right, they just died not long ago. You'd better deal with the corpses quickly, and don't show yourself, otherwise it will easily cause you some trouble."
Alger nodded repeatedly: "I know."
Of course, he wouldn't show himself. These were people from "Vice Admiral Dusk". It would be troublesome to be targeted by this "Pirate Admiral".
Hobert was about to leave using "Travel" when he suddenly thought: "By the way, what are their bounties?"
"The first mate, 'Radical' Olivier, has a bounty as high as 8200, and the boatswain, 'Water Cannon' Monco, has a bounty of 4500 pounds," Alger knew this very well.
Hobert nodded: "A small profit."
Hearing this, Alger thought: It's more than just a small profit. The bounty alone is more than 10,000 pounds, not to mention the Beyonder characteristics in their bodies.
He looked at his watch and saw that there was still time. He would hand over the two corpses to the Governor's Office today!
By the time "Vice Admiral Dusk's" people came to investigate, the bounty would be in hand.
… …
Hobert used "Travel" to return to his study, took a sip of tea to rest, and began to review today's battle.
First of all, Hobert had to say that it was so satisfying to use a demigod to abuse Sequence 5!
The gap between the two sides was even greater than that between Sequence 5 and Sequence 6. Hobert even felt that it was roughly equivalent to the gap between Sequence 5 and Sequence 7.
Secondly, Hobert was impressed by the cunning of the "Hunter" pathway. One careless move could fall into the other party's trap, so he had to be careful when encountering Beyonder from this pathway in the future.
Otherwise, even if a Sequence 5's trap wouldn't kill a demigod, being tricked would be quite embarrassing.
Finally, Hobert realized a skill that he had previously ignored but was very useful in actual combat: Connection!
Its usefulness lies in its unexpectedness, such as when he established an Connection between Bulatov's "Storm of Light" and the light emitted by the giant ship. Not only was Bulatov stunned at the time, but the effect was also unexpected to Hobert!
Drinking tea, Hobert followed this line of thought and thought about how to play the "Earl of the Fallen".
One thing that Hobert is now very clear about is that the "Black Emperor" pathway is very closely related to "Rulership".
Previously, Hobert had always had a misunderstanding, thinking that the "Justiciar" pathway should focus on rulership.
However, when leading the people back to the lord's mansion, Hobert suddenly realized that, apart from the Sanguine, only the "Black Emperor" pathway's potions had titles such as Baron, Earl, Duke, and Emperor.
Of course, the earliest potion names may not have had descriptions like Baron and Earl, but no matter what, the later addition of such descriptions could very well explain the problem.
As for the Sanguine's peerage titles, they were only used to distinguish levels and were not the names of potions.
Others only had "Death Consul", "Pale Emperor", or "Knowledge Emperor", etc. The entire pathway only had one or two such potion names.
Just from this point of view, it seemed to be reminding the Beyonder of this pathway that after becoming a "Baron", they should pay attention to the rulership of the territory!
As for how to rule, Hobert believed after experiencing the digestion of the "Mentor of Disorder" potion that the Beyonder of this pathway should establish a ruling system that was different from the norm, preferably a system that was contrary to common sense.
This was not difficult for Hobert, and he also had to thank Roselle. It was Roselle who established the colonial system, and the essence of this system was plunder and slaughter.
In today's world, this system has been accepted by everyone in the Northern Continent. Then, the system that Hobert established, which was detailed to the village, people-oriented, and focused on making his own cake bigger instead of always thinking about robbing other people's cakes, was contrary to common sense in this era.
As for how to play the "Earl of the Fallen", Hobert felt that the focus should still be on the "Fallen" aspect.
The essence of the potion was ultimately a kind of distortion and madness, and it was perfectly normal to have a fallen side.
However, Hobert drew a bottom line for himself: he could not fall, nor could he let the people around him fall.
Thinking that the entertainment center in Jeffrey City was about to be completed, Hobert felt that he could let the nobles and wealthy people of the Feynapotter Kingdom fall, let the nobles and wealthy people of Backlund fall, and by the way, earn their money.
Thinking about it, it was already evening. Hobert glanced at Bulatov's head wrapped in a cloak. He decided to rest for a while this afternoon and send it to the Church of the Goddess tomorrow.
So Hobert sacrificed today's spoils to the "Nation of Disorder". Sitting on the "Iron Throne", Hobert checked today's spoils.
Today, he seized two mystical items, one from the "Hunter" pathway and one from the "Sun" pathway.
The mystical item from the Hunter pathway was the dagger in Bulatov's hand. It could be transformed into a flame spear and could launch a "fatal attack" that could cause considerable damage even to demigods.
However, it required "charging up", and it had to withstand two attacks from a demigod before it could use a "fatal attack" that could injure a demigod.
It seemed quite uneconomical, after all, each of the demigod's two attacks could potentially kill a Sequence 5, while the Sequence 5 could only injure the demigod.
For enemies below the demigod level, there was no such requirement, and "fatal attacks" could be launched continuously, even breaking through the "Dawn Barrier" of the "Guardian".
The other spoils were Beyonder characteristics. At the Sequence 5 level, there was one "Guardian" and one "Harvester" Beyonder characteristic.
At the Sequence 6 level, there was one "Wind Blessed" Beyonder characteristic.
At the Sequence 7 level, there was 1 "Weapon Master" and 1 "Seafarer" Beyonder characteristic.
Although Hobert had nearly advanced to a demigod, he still picked up the enemy's "low sequence" Beyonder characteristics.
At the Sequence 8 level, there were 3 "Folk of Rage" and 2 "Provoker" Beyonder characteristics.
At the Sequence 9 level, there were 2 "Warrior" and 1 "Bard" Beyonder characteristic.
Except for the two Sequence 5 Beyonder characteristics, which Hobert obtained through battle, the others were basically sailors who died or were seriously injured under Bulatov's "Storm of Light".
After disassembling what should be disassembled and putting what should be put into storage, Hobert glanced at the currently large number of "Hunter" pathway Beyonder characteristics.
Hobert planned to use the Beyonder characteristics of the "Hunter", "Warrior", and "Sailor" pathways to train the Beyonders of his military.
Of course, if he encountered a good buyer, he could also sell some of them.
Leaving the "Nation of Disorder", Hobert had a pleasant dinner with Fors and Donna. Then, the Earl and his wife sat in the rocking chairs in the yard, chatting leisurely while watching the stars.
Now that the weather was gradually warming up, sitting in the yard at night would not feel too cold.
… …
Sunday morning, Backlund North Borough, Evernight Church Back Street.
Hobert got out of the car with a wooden box in his hand, looking at the Blackthorn Security Company sign in front of him, feeling a bit like he was revisiting an old place.
He knocked on the door of the security company and said to the receptionist: "I'm looking for Captain Thomas and Lorotta."
After drinking a few sips of black tea in the reception area, Hobert saw Lorotta, who was wearing gender-neutral clothing and had black hair. He joked: "Your face looks so bad, did you get your salary deducted?"
"Not really," Lorotta said. "It's not payday yet, but my money is already spent."
Hobert smiled: "This is the problem for most people in Backlund!"
"Ah, Earl Hobert!" Captain Thomas said with a smile, walking down the stairs. "Are you coming back to report for duty? But I wouldn't dare command an Earl as a team member."
Hobert smiled and said, "I suddenly remembered that the Nighthawks haven't paid me my salary for more than half a year. I'm here to see if I can get it reissued."
Before Thomas could say anything, Loretta immediately said, "That's absolutely necessary!"
Then Thomas said, "I think the Red Gloves should be responsible for paying your salary from now on."
As Hobert's captain, he already knew that Hobert was an outside member of the Red Gloves.
Hobert didn't continue the topic, and pushed the wooden box on the coffee table towards the two of them, "This is a gift for you."
Loretta seemed to sense something. With a solemn expression, she opened the wooden box. First, she was surprised, then incredulous. Finally, with tears in her eyes, she took off the ring on her hand and said, "Did you see that? This is that bastard Bulatov's head! He's dead! After more than ten years, he has finally received his due punishment."
It was obvious that this lady's emotions were somewhat out of control.
Thomas called over a female team member and comforted Loretta with a few words.
After all, she had been a Nighthawk for so many years, and Loretta's emotions quickly stabilized. Hobert noticed that she seemed much more relaxed.
Loretta said, "Captain, let me go claim Bulatov's bounty."
Thomas nodded, "No problem."
After Loretta left, Thomas said, "I just bought a can of coffee. Want to come to my office and try some?"
"Sure."
While grinding and brewing the coffee, Thomas briefly recounted the story of Loretta and the ring on her hand.
When she first joined the professional Nighthawk team, Steve, a sunny and handsome team member, was responsible for teaching her mystical knowledge and the official Beyonder precautions.
The story was cliché. The two quickly fell in love. During a mission after their engagement, Steve, whose strength was only Sequence 8, encountered Bulatov, who was already a 'Mid-Sequence' Beyonder at the time.
The result was predictable. Steve was killed.
However, Steve's Beyonder characteristics gathered on their engagement ring, forming a Sealed Artifact with negative effects that weren't too strong.
To take care of Loretta's emotions, the Nighthawk team gave her the ring to use.
Loretta's habit of asking for a raise was actually a negative influence from the Sealed Artifact.
For a while, Loretta worked hard to improve her strength, almost losing control because of it. After realizing that she had no hope of revenge, she began to ask team members who she felt had a chance to take revenge to help her kill the 'Vice Admiral Dusk. In the end, Hobert helped her complete her revenge.
Hobert took a sip of coffee, "Very touching."
Now, more than ten years have passed, and Loretta obviously still can't forget her lover.
Moreover, Loretta had actually adjusted her mentality and didn't let hatred occupy her entire life. Otherwise, she would have lost control long ago due to emotional pressure.
"What I'm about to say might ruin this beautiful story a bit." Captain Thomas said, "We have been closely monitoring Loretta's condition. As of now, we still need to observe her further before we can be completely relieved."
Hobert thought of Old Neil and nodded in understanding.
As the conversation came to an end, Hobert inquired about Leonard's whereabouts from Thomas.
"How could I possibly have the address of a Red Glove member here?" Thomas said with a smile, "According to the rules, I can't inquire about it either, but if I see Leonard, there shouldn't be a problem asking him directly."
After agreeing that he would write to Hobert as soon as he got the address, Hobert got up and said goodbye.
Just as he came out of the security company's door, Hobert noticed Earl Hall's carriage coming from the other side of the street. He guessed that it was Sunday today, and the Hall family must be coming to the St Samuel Cathedral to pray.
Hobert stood on the steps, preparing to greet Earl Hall, but to his surprise, Audrey, who was a sight for sore eyes, opened the car window and said in a crisp and moving voice, "Hobert! Are you here to pray too?"
"I guess so!" Hobert noticed that Earl and Countess Hall were not in the carriage.
Audrey got out of the carriage as she spoke. Today, she was wearing a long dress with lace, exuding purity amidst extravagance.
Hobert asked, "Just you alone?"
"My father and brother had something to do temporarily and left first." Audrey smiled and sized Hobert up, "Hobert, if other nobles saw your attire, they would think you were on the verge of bankruptcy."
Hobert was wearing his favorite Loen-style trench coat today. It was convenient to move around in, and as long as he stood up the collar, he wouldn't need an umbrella in Backlund's recent drizzly weather. It could also block the cold air in winter.
He laughed, "My butler told me the same thing."
"You have a competent butler."
"But I told him I really like trench coats, and he didn't insist anymore."
Audrey smiled, "He must be powerless against such a mischievous Earl like you."
Hobert was slightly stunned. Isn't 'mischievous' used to describe children?
Audrey added, "I think, as a friend, I should take you to pick out a few formal suits. After all, the social season is about to begin in about a week."
The so-called social season refers to April to August. Nobles, whether or not they have businesses in Backlund, will gather in the capital to engage in noble social activities. These four months can be said to be full of endless dances and drinks.
Hobert thought for a moment, he didn't have anything else to do today, "Okay, as a reward, I'll treat you to lunch at noon."
… …
On the Berserk Sea, the 'Future' sailed steadily through the undulating waves.
"Admiral of Stars" Cattleya stood by the window, gazing at the vast ocean that stretched beyond the horizon. From the position of the front deck, Nina's exasperated voice could be heard from time to time. She was angrily scolding Frank Lee for creating a pile of beef-flavored mushrooms that reproduced extremely quickly and loved to eat fish.
Cattleya sighed silently. At this moment, her intuition was suddenly touched. She turned her head to look at the desk, only to see a few yellowed pieces of paper that had appeared there at some point.
"The Emperor's Diary!" Cattleya turned around happily, but when she saw the question raised by the Queen, she was slightly stunned, "This, I can answer this question, um, if the 'Emperor' intelligence is accurate enough."
On one of the pages of the diary was a piece of paper with a line written on it: Why did he go mad in his later years?
… …
Backlund.
In the drizzly weather, Hobert got into Earl Hall's carriage, and his carriage followed behind.
"I'll take you to Laufder Tailor Shop to take a look." Audrey said, "This tailor shop has been around for more than three hundred years and specializes in serving nobles. Their craftsmanship is better than the tailors in many Earl's families."
Hobert realized that Dophis had probably already hired a tailor for himself!
How extravagant, I'm just one person, and I actually need a tailor.
The young and beautiful Audrey across from him continued, "I think you should at least order five formal suits, but because this is your first year participating in the social season, it's best not to be too extravagant and keep it low-key."
Hobert thought to himself: Keeping it low-key is easy, right? Big shorts and a vest are low-key enough, right?
But he said, "You're the expert, I'll listen to you. But, do I really need five formal suits? I have a tailor at home too!"
"He must be too busy in the first year." Audrey said, "Because each suit can only be worn once at formal occasions, and can't be worn on other occasions."
Hobert nodded. He had forgotten about that.
At this time, he didn't think this was very elegant. Instead, he complained in his heart: What an unthrifty group.
But being in it, especially just joining the Backlund noble class, Hobert would only complain. He wouldn't make himself an exception among the nobles when he just joined this circle.
He thought, five suits it is, it's just five suits of clothes.
Laufder Tailor Shop was located in the Empress Borough. It consisted of a huge showroom and production room, and was staffed by a well-dressed, elegant middle-aged man and several servants responsible for reception.
Audrey came to the showroom with ease. There were many samples on display here. These samples were used for trying on. If you felt it was suitable after trying it on, you would place an order.
But it wasn't a complete copy of the sample. When the tailor was taking measurements for the nobles, they would give a suggestion for modification based on the noble's temperament.
So they claimed that every piece of clothing here was unique.
Hobert chose two formal suits that looked good and refused the maid's help to change clothes, coming to the fitting room alone.
The service here was quite attentive, and they wouldn't treat Hobert badly just because he was wearing a 'cheap' trench coat. First, there was Audrey's endorsement, and second, they knew that ordinary people wouldn't dare to enter such a tailor shop.
After changing into one of the suits, Hobert came out of the fitting room.
Audrey felt that Hobert's entire temperament was different. Hobert's appearance was still good, after all, he had the genes of the 'Goddess of Beauty', especially when he smiled, he was very sunny and cheerful.
Today, Audrey realized that Hobert's appearance could handle different styles of clothing. When he wore a trench coat before, he looked like a young and energetic young man who was working hard for his career and made people feel positive and upward.
After putting on the formal suit, Hobert's temperament immediately changed. The originally casual movements became very elegant and confident, his smile was still very cheerful, but it also revealed a sense of nobility.
Hobert spread his arms and looked at himself in the mirror, "How is it?"
Audrey then came back to her senses and said with an elegant smile, "Very good!"
"But I don't really like this color," Hobert said, "And also the silk design in this area."
A well-dressed attendant standing nearby took out a notebook: "What color would you prefer? We can change anything."
Hobert was slightly stunned. Just now, those two complaints of his were purely a habit from when he wasn't very wealthy and was buying clothes. Only by pointing out flaws, and making sure to express his strong dislike, could he haggle for a better price later.

chapters.content:
