chapters.title: Chapter 565 - 564: Joint Action of The Emperor, The World and The Hanged Man (Bonus 2)
chapters.content:
[Thanks to Naufal Sakho' Gusnaya for becoming a free member]
join the Church of MissRaven and become a Sequence 9: Reader p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Audrey could tell from Hobert's expression that the Backlund Morning News was probably making up stories again.
As for the reason, she could guess that it was to use Hobert's "heroic deeds" to cover up the fact that this diplomatic mission had been unsuccessful.
Hobert quickly asked Dophis to bring him a copy of the Backlund Morning News to see what he had supposedly done.
At the same time, he thought to himself: These people are too unprofessional. They didn't even say hello or ask for my opinion when they were making things up. I might have even been able to give them some ideas! I'm a professional at bragging!
"The content is basically true," Hobert said after reading the report about himself, "but those spies were actually Beyonders from enemy countries, and the so-called gunfight was actually a battle between Beyonders."
He smiled at Glaint and said, "Ah, and that part that moved you, it was actually Princess Alice who made the choice, not me."
At the time, Hobert was quite surprised that someone who had almost been assassinated by the royal family and the Demoness Sect could still choose to risk maintaining national interests in that situation.
So Hobert didn't even try to dissuade her, nor did he use his power as a demigod to ignore Alice's choice, but instead chose to help her.
Glaint was slightly stunned when he heard Hobert's words, and finally smiled helplessly.
Then Hobert talked to Glaint about hiring another batch of noble children.
Hobert had already read a batch of briefings sent by Fors last night, including Corwin's report, about Longtail Island and the South Colson area during this period.
In his report, he mentioned that the noble children who had accepted "transformation" could enter the working state more quickly, were very motivated, and could infer other things from one instance. With a little experience, they could flexibly handle the affairs encountered in their work.
Of course, Hobert understood that these people had received a very good education and had a strong ability to accept new things.
Moreover, under the influence of their upbringing, they were better at dealing with people, which was almost inevitable. In the future, there would definitely be many such noble children in Hobert's power structure.
Therefore, Hobert had an important requirement for their selection: to fully accept the core idea of "people-oriented".
In the previous assessment, noble children who refused to accept this idea, no matter how capable they were, were all dismissed by Hobert with a salary of 1 pound a day.
For him, a lack of ability could be cultivated, but if the path was wrong, then "people with different ideals cannot make plans together."
Glaint immediately agreed to help Hobert contact another batch of noble children, and said that this time there would definitely be more people applying.
Because Hobert had given the noble children who had passed the assessment and been assigned positions three days off before he went on a business trip.
Not many people cared about their experiences, everyone was staring at the positions they eventually obtained.
Currently, things looked good. They were either grassroots officials in the territory or management in Backlund, which was a very good way out for many noble children.
If this group of people had a good future, then Hobert wouldn't have to actively recruit them. People who wanted to find a way out for themselves would definitely find a way to recommend themselves.
After a good night's rest, Hobert came to Longtail Island and began to implement the second step of his plan.
Two more weeks passed, and Hobert once again paid the planters the second batch of rubber, to the penny, at 1.5 times the market price as previously agreed.
This immediately aroused the enthusiasm of all the planters. They had already begun to plant the new varieties provided by Bishop Jodi on a small scale.
At this time, most of them were determined to take out all their savings to plant rubber trees!
Although these seedlings and potions were very expensive, it was estimated that they could recover their costs in four or five months.
And even if Earl Hobert no longer had such a large demand for rubber and the purchase price returned to the market price, it would only take two or three months to recover the costs.
For the planters, it was already a very profitable crop for this perennial economic crop to recover its costs so quickly.
The most important thing was that after recovering the costs, they could get more than ten times the income of ordinary rubber trees. For them, this was simply a lucrative investment.
But at the third banquet, Hobert gave everyone another stimulant.
Hobert said very seriously: "The rubber you provide is still too little! For a long time to come, I will need a lot of rubber. If you can't meet my needs, I will have to send people to other islands to purchase it!"
At the same time, he also said: "Before meeting the huge demand for rubber, the price I pay will be 1.5 times the market price!"
As Hobert expected, the planters began to complain, saying that they only had so many rubber trees, that the new rubber tree varieties were too expensive, and so on.
At this time, Bishop Jodi explained that those potions and new varieties used many expensive materials, and that they were giving everyone this price because they had a good cooperation with Earl Hobert. There were no such seedlings in other places, and the Earth Mother Church was hardly making any money.
Because the planters didn't understand the mystical logic behind this, they didn't know how to refute Bishop Jodi's explanation.
Hobert pondered for a while before saying: "I will issue you a loan to plant rubber trees, and you will pay it back after you start producing rubber."
Because the Earl had previously advanced a payment, everyone was not surprised by this proposal.
Moreover, planters with connections had already inquired that the Earl was producing a large number of wires in Backlund, and had purchased almost all of the rubber in Backlund, which had caused a certain premium on rubber in Backlund.
So everyone had discussed before coming to see if they could ask the Earl to advance some money to buy seedlings? Even if they paid some interest.
Unexpectedly, the Earl took the initiative to offer a loan, and didn't even mention the matter of interest.
Hobert continued: "The maximum loan for each person is 3,000 pounds, and this loan can be collected from the Governor's Office tomorrow!"
He said: "I have a requirement, which is that this money must be spent on planting rubber trees. This must be written into the loan contract. Once a breach of contract occurs, I will recover the loan in advance!"
3,000 pounds!
Unexpectedly, the Earl would lend them such a huge sum of money. In addition to being surprised, everyone promised that they would abide by the agreement.
The next day, Hobert disbursed the loans as promised, and more than 70,000 pounds were loaned out that day!
For a time, Longtail Island was filled with enthusiasm for planting rubber trees. In order to grab rubber tree seedlings and land for planting, the planters had clashed more than once.
Under Hobert's previous step-by-step stimulation, not only the loan given by Hobert, but everyone's savings, and the money they could borrow, were used to plant rubber trees!
In addition, some people felt that they could buy a large batch of rubber from other islands with such a large sum of money, and then return to Longtail Island to sell it to the Governor's Office.
Someone had calculated that it would be profitable to buy several thousand pounds.
Hobert temporarily had no intention of interfering in the affairs of Longtail Island, and just allowed the situation to develop.
At this time, he was more concerned about the construction of cement plants and other factories. Relatively simple brick factories, gravel factories, lime factories, etc. had been built and started mass production, and cement plants had also begun to be capped.
Only factories such as smelting plants and steel plants, which required higher craftsmanship, were still being built in full swing.
Hobert was very satisfied with this progress. After the completion of his first step plan, Longtail Island would have the ability to build on a large scale!
Returning to the Governor's Office, Hobert glanced at the rubber plantations that were in full swing, smiled slightly, and returned to Backlund.
...
Before you knew it, the harvest season had arrived.
For the farmers of South Colson, this year's harvest season was especially happy. The dozens of villages around Jeffrey City had long known that all the harvests in their fields belonged to them.
They would look at the golden wheat ears under the scorching sun, then "hehe" smile and continue to bury themselves in harvesting.
The people in the area west of the West Bank that had once been ruled by the Blood Sanctify Sect were told when they were about to harvest that if they did not continue to believe in demons, did not carve statues for them, and did not perform any sacrificial actions, the wheat in the fields would all belong to the owners of the wheat fields.
But if they wanted to continue to believe in demons, they could continue to believe, but all the harvests in the fields would be taken over by the town government.
For several months, the people had not been exposed to anything about demons. Most people's spirits had returned to normal, and even those whose mental bodies still had some problems had calmed down and regained their enthusiasm and hope for life.
So they basically chose to leave the wheat behind and chose a future that looked pretty good.
So the town government on the west bank of Full Moon Lake seized the opportunity to strike while the iron was hot, and the policy of redistributing land was not so difficult to implement.
The East Bank also took advantage of the harvest season to tell everyone that they would not collect any agricultural taxes, but because the city government had a large shortage of food, it would purchase the excess grain from the people at market prices.
Most areas completed the process of land distribution in an atmosphere of joy.
This made Hobert feel that his potion had been digested a lot, which proved that everyone felt the huge changes in this area, and also proved that his rule over the South Colson area was more solid.
In this harvest season, on the west bank of Full Moon Lake, when everyone was resting at noon, an old man found a corpse in the wheat field, but when the old man went to ask the village chief Mike to come, the corpse was gone.
If it weren't for the traces of the corpse pressed out in the wheat field, everyone would have thought that the old man was mistaken.
In the end, people thought that maybe a passerby was tired and lay down in the wheat field to rest, but was awakened by the old man, so the passerby left.
This Mike was directly sent down from the town government. He had undergone many trainings and was a relatively knowledgeable person in the local area.
He found that the place where the wheat was pressed down was under the scorching sun. If someone wanted to rest, they should be in the shade of a tree. Who would rest under the scorching sun?
The key was that Mike also found a clump of fishy and smelly mucus in the wheat field that had been pressed down, which seemed like blood but not blood.
Mike found a leaf, collected the mucus, and then told everyone that someone was tired and lay down in the field.
He also asked everyone to continue to harvest the wheat to avoid rainy weather.
But Mike took the mucus to the town government and handed it over to the security officer of the town government.
To Mike's surprise, one of the security officers told him that it was corpse fluid, and similar things had happened in several surrounding villages, and some people had seen people digging graves at night.
The security officer took Mike to a small office, where three young people, one woman and two men, were sitting wearing uniforms that were similar to the security officer's, but also different.
Two months ago, the Lord's Mansion had unified and standardized the uniforms in the territory, and even Mike had received two sets of uniforms for village-level cadres.
This made Mike feel that he was more energetic than before, but the uniform manual did not have the uniform style worn by the three people sitting opposite him.
The leading man smiled and said: "It can be seen that you are a careful grassroots worker. You have even discovered that our uniform styles are a little different.
"We are a special department in the Lord's Mansion, specializing in solving the strange things you encounter."
Then he introduced himself: "My name is Monet, and I will ask you a few questions now. Did it happen at noon? Were there any other traces found around? Was that corpse a dead person from your village? Are there any other witnesses?"
Mike found these questions a little strange, but he still answered them one by one. After that, Monet thanked Mike and asked him to pay attention to the movements in the village after he went back. If he encountered similar situations again, he must report them in time.
The captain of the security team praised Mike a few words and told him that he would report his initiative to report this matter to the town government and record it in his monthly assessment.
Mike left very happily. On the way back, looking at the scene of harvesting wheat on both sides of the road, a heartfelt sense of pride once again arose from the bottom of his heart.
Turning over the mountain pass ahead was the village where he worked. He saw that some villages had already finished harvesting wheat. He felt that his village should also work harder and strive to finish harvesting tomorrow and start drying the day after tomorrow!
Mother Earth is above! It must be sunny these two days!
Crossing the mountain pass, the expression on Mike's face gradually stiffened. He saw that his village was lifeless, and some people had fallen at home! Some people had fallen in the fields!
Mike seemed to realize something and raised his foot to rush over.
"It's too late!" Monet's voice suddenly appeared behind Mike: "We were already too late when we found something was wrong."
Mike pointed to the people in the wheat field in the distance: "They..."
"Are all dead!"
Mike burst into tears: "Are all dead? Why? The young man Clee at the entrance of the village just got married, and Conra's wife just got pregnant. I also promised old Vit that I would invite him to drink in the town after I got paid..."
"Those demons just left a few months ago! Everything just had new hope!"
As he spoke, Mike slowly squatted down and cried with his head in his hands.
Monet sighed with emotion: "Some things are so hateful, they always give people a blow when there is just hope!"
He took out a bottle of wine: "I heard you like to drink, drink it, it's on me!"
Mike opened the bottle cap and took two gulps.
Raymond persuaded: "Take two more sips."
Mike was slightly stunned, feeling that the wine was not bad, so he took a few more sips.
Raymond crouched down, patting Mike's shoulder and saying, "There's something I have to tell you. Actually, you're already dead!"
Mike's eyes widened, and he finally remembered everything that had happened last night: "A... a cloud of black mist, enveloping the entire village!"
After saying that, Mike fell to the ground, motionless.
Raymond sighed and then said to the female officer, "Quick, go get Sir Dunn. This case is too strange; we can't handle it."
...
Hobert rested for half a day in Backlund and made some preparations. On the night he had agreed upon with 'The World' and 'The Hanged Man,' he put on his mask and used 'Travel' to arrive at the entrance of a cemetery in the suburbs of Bayam. This was their meeting place.
'The Hanged Man' Alger, with his rough blue hair, had already arrived. He smiled and said, "Long time no see!"
Hobert also smiled and said, "Long time no see."
At this moment, the space beside them was torn again, and Gehrman Sparrow, also known as Klein, with a cold expression, arrived last.
Hobert smiled and said, "Look, our great adventurer has arrived!"
"I'm not an adventurer anymore," Klein said, his face unchanging. "Are you all ready?"
Alger was slightly stunned: Didn't you say 'The Emperor' is a demigod? Isn't it impolite to not even smile?
Hobert wasn't angry, but said, "You should smile more, my friend. Is the burden of life about to crush you?
"How about I invite you to Feynapotter for a trip in a few days to relax?"
Klein glanced at Hobert, this time with some warmth in his eyes: "If I have time, I will go."
Alger immediately realized: They knew each other before, and they seemed quite familiar. That's right, they each represent two allied gods and should communicate often.
Then, Hobert and Klein both looked at Alger.
Alger immediately understood: "I know, I'll lead the way."
Klein put his hand on Alger's shoulder, the meaning was obvious, to have Hobert put his hand on his shoulder.
Hobert didn't do so: "The way we look, it's a bit like blind people traveling together."
Alger was stunned, it really did look like that: "Then you can put your hand on my other shoulder."
"That would look like we're escorting a prisoner," Hobert said. "How about this, I'll use 'Travel' to push you into the spirit world."
After discussing the formation, the three of them entered the spirit world together and quickly arrived at the target island.
Walking in front, Alger lit a lantern and explained, "If you come during the day, it's quite lively here. You can even see some bird-like creatures that only exist in myths and legends.
"But at night, the 'power' that dominates here seems to change, and many supernatural creatures hide themselves."
While listening to Alger's explanation, Klein also lit a lantern and asked Hobert, "Didn't you bring a lamp?"
"My night vision is very good," Hobert smiled. "When you become a demigod, you'll understand this feeling."
If it were before, he definitely wouldn't have said the second half of the sentence because it was very annoying.
But when Hobert realized he had to break through the rules he had set for himself, he consciously changed some of his habits.
After hearing Hobert say this, Klein and Alger smiled strangely one after another.
Alger cleared his throat, forcibly skipping the previous topic, he pointed to the front: "We follow this road into the forest, straight ahead, and we will reach the ancient ruins of unknown age.
"Along the way, we hunt supernatural creatures that we encounter and are capable of dealing with. The materials corresponding to those killed alone belong entirely to the killer. Those completed in cooperation are kept by Mr. Emperor, and after leaving here, they are distributed by means of rotation.
"And the order of selection is adjusted according to the specific contributions made."
The members of this team include a demigod and a crazy adventurer.
Alger, who had just been promoted to Sequence 5, was the weakest of them, so he first explained how to distribute the spoils to avoid unnecessary trouble during the trip.
Hobert nodded and said, "No problem."
He patted the leather bag hanging around his waist: "With it, the harvest this time can be handed over to me to the fullest."
Klein nodded indifferently, indicating that he also agreed with this way of distributing the spoils.
So the three of them, holding lanterns, began their exploration.
Klein walked in the front, Alger in the middle, and Hobert at the end.
The reason for this formation was that most of the dangers at night came from behind, so the only demigod in the team was placed at the rear.
After walking for a while, they saw that the trees in front became sparse.
Alger wondered, have we arrived at the ruins so quickly?
After walking a few more steps, they saw hunched or crawling figures.
These figures included humans, baboons, goats, and tigers. They were either holding stones or using their claws and teeth, constantly grinding the accumulated trees and rocks, seemingly building a palace.
Suddenly, these figures seemed to sense something, and at the same time, they stopped their movements. The next second, they turned around in unison and looked at the three outsiders.
Under the light of the lanterns and the moonlight, their faces were pale, their fur was withered, or their bodies were ulcerated. None of them looked alive.
Klein immediately realized that supernatural creatures were driving corpses to build a palace for themselves.
Then his gaze passed over them and saw a dark cave that sloped deep into the ground. The weeds around it were fallen, and several white feathers with pale yellow oil stains were scattered.
Hobert held the head of his staff in one hand and the body of the staff in the other: Did we encounter this guy right away?
Alger, who had also carefully observed for a while, hesitated for two seconds before suggesting, "I haven't seen a similar situation before, and I don't know the level of this Beyonder creature. How about we bypass it..."
Just as he was saying this, the ground suddenly trembled, as if something was turning over below.
Without thinking, Klein and Alger turned their heads and were about to run.
Hobert slowly drew his thin sword: "It seems that there are also Beyonders or Beyonder creatures among those corpses. They are left to you."
This made the two who were about to escape slightly stunned: That's right, we also have a demigod on our side, why are we running!
Then Klein looked at the thin sword in Hobert's hand. The material of the thin sword made him feel very familiar, and it seemed to have some connection with Azik's copper whistle.
Before he could take a closer look, a giant snake that a single person could not hug emerged from the dark cave. It had huge scales that were dark green and black, and exaggerated eyes that burned like flames.
In the gaps between the scales, white feathers covered with single yellow oil stains grew, and there were even a pair of thick wings that could be unfolded on its back.
The giant snake raised its body, watching the three figures who had broken into its territory.
Hobert smiled and greeted, "Quetzalcoatl, please hand over your Beyonder characteristics. I need a demigod butler!"

chapters.title: Chapter 566 - 565 That's a Curly-Haired Baboon
chapters.content:
join the Church of MissRaven and become a Sequence 9: Reader p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Around the feathered serpent, the trees were rapidly withering, the weeds were all withered, and countless corpses crawled out of the soil. Uncountable shadows, of unknown origin, clustered around the feathered serpent.
Klein and Alger immediately judged that this was definitely a demigod-level feathered serpent!
The two of them involuntarily took a step back, because the gathered corpses and shadows alone looked difficult to deal with.
As for the feathered serpent itself, their spirituality warned them not to look at the feathered serpent over there, as looking at it could very likely lead to death.
Hobert walked forward unhurriedly. He could feel his life seemingly draining away, so he immediately used the mark Mr. Azik had given him, and the process of life loss immediately stopped.
If it were other demigod-level Beyonder creatures, Hobert would have to consider whether to hunt them, but for Beyonder creatures of the "Death" pathway, with his rapier in hand and the mark Azik gave him, what was there to consider?
The feathered serpent also seemed to sense Hobert's special nature and did not immediately launch an attack, but instead had those corpses and specters launch probing attacks.
Hobert smiled slightly, very dashingly and handsomely waving the sword in his hand, drawing a beautiful arc in the air, cutting open an "Underworld Gate."
The Zombies and specters realized something. Ignoring the feathered serpent's orders, they turned around and ran!
But it was impossible for them to escape. The "Underworld Gate" produced a huge suction force. This suction force was not the normal wind-like suction, but a suction that seemed to be grabbing all spiritual bodies.
The Zombies fell like dominoes, and the specters suddenly seemed to lose all their power and were sucked into the "Underworld Gate."
Klein and Alger were stunned. Did the "Lawyer" pathway have such abilities?
But they quickly guessed that the rapier in Hobert's hand was very likely a Grade 1 Sealed Artifact!
Klein was a little envious because he currently only had one Grade 1 Sealed Artifact, and it could only be used "above the gray fog."
Alger didn't feel much about it, because Grade 1 Sealed Artifacts were too far away for him.
"Hiss~"
As Hobert got closer and closer to the feathered serpent, the feathered serpent began to emit continuous "hissing" sounds.
A sense of fear filled Hobert's heart, causing his spiritual body to not obey his control.
Klein and Alger, on the edge of the battlefield, felt as if they had fallen into an ice cave. They both turned their heads away, not daring to look at the battlefield over there.
They realized that just watching from a distance was dangerous, so they simply took a few steps back to deal with the corpses that were being manipulated by the feathered serpent to build the palace.
As Hobert said, there were also some dead Beyonders or Beyonder creatures among them.
"Magnify!" Hobert "magnified" the "Words of the Dead" on his rapier to counter the "hissing" sound.
The "hissing" sound was of course defeated, so the feathered serpent suddenly swung its tail and lashed towards Hobert.
Hobert poured his spirituality into "1-109": "Slaughtering!"
This was the ability of the "Iron-Blooded Knight" he had just "shepherded". Hobert's fist seemed to be covered with a layer of orange-red light, and he punched the feathered serpent!
If this ability were used on the rapier, it would temporarily cover the rapier's suppression of Beyonder creatures of the "Death" pathway, so Hobert simply used his own fist to attack!
The feathered serpent also did not expect that its probing attack would attract such a powerful blow.
This was also Hobert consciously changing some of his habits. If it were normal, he would be more cautious than the feathered serpent.
Just as Hobert was about to hit the feathered serpent, a bronze door with intricate mystical symbols suddenly appeared in front of him.
This "Underworld Gate" was hit by Hobert's full blow before it even opened.
The bronze door was visibly skewed and made a "creaking" sound, as if the door hinge had been broken.
"Underworld Gate" is just a general term. The strength of the Beyonder's own ability also determines the strength of the "Underworld Gate" they summon.
Like a demigod-level feathered serpent, the "Underworld Gate" it summons is also at the demigod level, so when hit by the demigod-level "Slaughter", it will be "injured."
Hobert bypassed the "Underworld Gate" and stabbed the feathered serpent with his rapier.
Blocked by the "Underworld Gate", the feathered serpent had already prepared to meet the enemy. It spat a black snake letter at Hobert: "Hiss~"
Hobert immediately felt as if he had been hit by an invisible force. His soul and body seemed to immediately become decayed. This was not a simple feeling, but his skin really immediately ulcerated.
"Bestow!" Hobert immediately "bestowed" these negative states to the feathered serpent. Taking advantage of this opportunity, the feathered serpent struck Hobert with its tail, sending him flying into the gap where the "Underworld Gate" opened.
Streams of pale arms stretched out and immediately grabbed Hobert.
He felt cold all over, unable to move, and his entire life force was draining away.
Just like that, Hobert was dragged into the "Underworld Gate."
Thump~
The door merged and quickly disappeared.
Only then did the feathered serpent have time to look at its rapidly withering scales. This was the injury that Hobert had just given it. The scales seemed to have ulcerated.
But soon, under the feathered serpent's Beyonder power, the scales returned to their original state.
Just as it looked at the other two Beyonders who had broken into its territory, a large opening was suddenly cut into the air, and Hobert drilled out of the Underworld, punching the feathered serpent at close range! Directly sending the huge feathered serpent flying.
Hobert, like a cannonball being fired, punched the feathered serpent in mid-air again, and then kicked the feathered serpent's head hard, shattering one of its eyes and smashing the eye socket.
This was the "Hunter" pathway's "Fatal Blow", each blow heavier than the last. If he could land five consecutive blows, he could even injure an angel.
It's just that the angel wouldn't honestly stand there and be beaten.
Although Hobert only had time to deliver three blows before the feathered serpent flapped its wings to avoid them.
But the feathered serpent only escaped a short distance before it fell to the ground from mid-air due to its severe injuries.
Hobert was about to rush over to continue the pursuit, but the feathered serpent's skin suddenly cracked, spraying out a large amount of black mist.
This mist had the smell of death, and Hobert quickly avoided it!
Then Hobert summoned dozens of fire crows, just about to fly into the black mist to bomb the feathered serpent, when suddenly a smaller feathered serpent suddenly poked its head out of the black mist, almost biting Hobert.
Under the cover of the fire crows, Hobert escaped in a thrilling manner.
This made him a little strange. Could there be two feathered serpents here?
When the black mist dissipated, Hobert saw a thick layer of snake skin on the ground!
Only then did he understand that the feathered serpent had just shed a layer of skin, as if it had shed all the injuries from before along with that layer of skin.
At this time, the feathered serpent was "lightly armed" and looked more agile than before, constantly attacking with bites and whips.
At the same time, a phantom door appeared on its body, releasing three evil spirits one after another to attack Hobert.
Hobert, however, dodged the attacks while opening a "Underworld Gate" again. The three evil spirits imprisoned in the feathered serpent's body were also very powerful, but under the power of the Underworld, they were immediately suppressed, desperately resisting the suction from the Underworld.
It was at this time that Hobert discovered that bloody tears were flowing from the corners of the feathered serpent's eyes.
He suddenly realized that the injury caused by his most ruthless kick had not been completely "shed" by the feathered serpent along with its molted skin.
Hobert seized the opportunity, stretched out his fist, and used the "1-109's" "Flesh Bomb" ability to detonate the blood flowing from the feathered serpent, blasting its eye again, and the feathered serpent was also blasted to the ground, rolling.
At this time, the feathered serpent did not hesitate and immediately turned to its cave.
For it, this battle was too frustrating. The rapier in Hobert's hand made most of its abilities ineffective. It finally managed to capture Hobert to the Underworld, but after all, that was the Underworld, not the Spirit World. Even an angel would have to spend some effort to return from the Underworld.
Of course, Beyonders of the "Death" pathway are an exception.
What the feathered serpent did not expect was that this guy came back as easily as if he had returned to his own backyard.
As for the "Words of the Dead" and "Withering" attacks, these were the feathered serpent's signature skills, but they were of no use at all!
When the feathered serpent saw that the three evil spirits it had used as its last trump card were also completely controlled by the power from the Underworld, it planned to escape.
How could Hobert let it go: "Disorder!"
He rushed forward, and the rapier suddenly lengthened and pierced the feathered serpent's back.
The severe pain awakened the feathered serpent from its brief state of "disorder". It opened its mouth and spat a mouthful of black mist at Hobert, continuing to crawl towards the cave.
This time, Hobert commanded the fire crows to all hit the feathered serpent. The whistling sound of the fire crows flying past was very similar to a string of rockets being fired, and the power was about the same as a rocket.
The violent explosion dispersed the black mist, and Hobert stepped forward again: "Distortion!"
He "distorted" the feathered serpent's idea of "drilling into the cave and escaping through the underground passage" into "there is no way to escape even if you drill into the cave".
So the injured feathered serpent avoided its cave and flew away to escape.
When it realized that its idea was contrary to its original intention, it needed to turn around to get into the cave, but Hobert was already blocking the entrance of the cave at this time, and reached out to the feathered serpent.
The feathered serpent was about to drill into the other holes that had been reserved, but the place where it had been injured before exploded again.
Hobert detonated the flesh and blood in those injured places again, thus launching a secondary attack on the feathered serpent.
"Magnify!" Hobert magnified the feathered serpent's serious injury into a fatal injury.
The feathered serpent immediately became dying. It was about to shed its skin again, but Hobert had already rushed up, and the rapier in his hand instantly turned into a two-handed greatsword, chopping off the feathered serpent's head.
The feathered serpent's entire body suddenly stiffened, and then the huge body began to struggle violently.
According to common sense, it would not die if its head was chopped off, but Hobert's sword was different, cutting its spiritual body in half as well.
So in the process of struggling, the scales on its body turned white for a while, black for a while, and then returned to dark green.
Hobert realized that this feathered serpent was unwilling to die like this and showed signs of losing control!
He quickly jumped onto the feathered serpent, dug his fingers into the feathered serpent's flesh to avoid being thrown off, and placed his other hand on the feathered serpent's scales, injecting spirituality into "1-109."
"Huh?" Originally, Hobert planned to first "shepherd" the feathered serpent's spiritual body, and then release this spiritual body after leaving the island to obtain its Beyonder characteristics.
Who knew that "1-109" was obviously resisting Hobert's spirituality, and seemed unwilling to shepherd this soul?
Hobert could forcibly "shepherd", but he realized that this was not only "1-109's" warning to himself, but also his own spirituality's warning to himself.
So he let go, jumped aside, and quietly waited for the feathered serpent to die in the loss of control, and the Beyonder characteristics were concentrated on a scale, eventually forming a green domino-like thing.
Hobert put away this domino that always caused everything around it to wither, and opened his leather bag to stuff the feathered serpent's body into the leather bag.
This was given to him by Christian before, that leather bag with space magic.
The space inside was as big as a basement, more than enough to stuff a feathered serpent in.
At this time, it was already far away from the original battlefield. When Hobert found Klein and Alger, their battle was over, and they had harvested five Beyonder characteristics.
Hobert said to them: "Solved, let's continue forward."
Klein and Alger both felt a little unbelievable, after all, the battle just now only lasted two or three minutes.
Hobert seemed to see their thoughts, so he smiled and said: "The rapier in my hand has a suppressive effect on Beyonders or Beyonder creatures of the 'Death' pathway."
Klein and Alger's eyes did not change much, because even so, it was too fast! That feathered serpent was a demigod level! A demigod that is difficult to kill!
A few seconds later, Alger cleared his throat and said: "I hope the battle just now didn't wake up any great existence."
The explosion of the fire crows just now was very loud and should be able to travel a long distance.
Hobert nodded: "I should have 'magnified' the explosion just now. If it awakens other guys, it will make our harvest richer."
Alger opened his mouth: That's not what I meant!
Klein said at this time: "We'd better get to that ruin as soon as possible."
Although he did not fight the feathered serpent head-on just now, he still felt a little frightened until now. This is the impact brought by the demigod-level enemy.
This is not a good experience, so don't encounter this level of enemy again!
Alger had a similar idea, pointing to the forest: "Go inside."
The three continued forward. After walking for a few minutes, Alger suddenly stopped: "If we go forward a little further, there will be a psychedelic wind chime tree. I want to try to deal with it myself first."
Hobert didn't think much: "Okay."
He actually prefers to explore with Alger. This guy always knows when to be honest.
In order to maintain his persona, Klein said coldly and politely: "If you can't deal with it, it's best to ask for help actively, otherwise I will assume that you are still persevering."
Alger quietly took a breath, holding the horse lamp and continued to move forward.
As they walked, they heard the faint tinkling of wind chimes, immediately giving them a sense of returning home and relaxing both body and mind.
After walking a few more steps, the three of them saw a strange tree. Its brownish-green trunk had slender cracks, each appearing to house constantly rotating eyes.
Hanging from the outstretched branches were wind chime-like gray objects that swayed on their own, emitting pleasant sounds.
Near the trunk and at the very top branch was a fist-sized, colorless, translucent fruit.
No matter how much Klein and Alger emphasized and repeated in their minds that they were currently under hypnosis, they still wanted to approach this psychedelic wind chime tree, feeling that there was something extremely precious to them there.
Hobert was also affected to some extent, but not much. He sat on a rock, as if preparing to enjoy a performance.
Alger brought the 'Mental Whip,' a mystical item with the negative effect of causing headaches, which would allow him to effectively avoid being hypnotized by the psychedelic wind chime tree.
Then he took out a wooden box containing rats he had prepared in advance.
At this moment, Hobert was already laughing unkindly, but because he was sitting behind, Klein and Alger didn't notice.
Klein was secretly nodding: 'The Hanged Man' wants to use rats as bait to attract the psychedelic wind chime tree's attention, a very thorough preparation!
But Alger seemed to notice something. He picked up the rat and shook it with a strange expression, only to find that the rat was already stiff.
Although he didn't directly fight the feathered serpent in the previous battle, the influence emitted by the feathered serpent was enough to kill ordinary creatures like rats.
The corners of Klein's mouth twitched. He wanted to laugh but didn't dare to, afraid of ruining his persona.
Hobert simply laughed and asked, "Need any help?"
"I have backup plans." Alger cleared his throat and, while walking towards the psychedelic wind chime tree, began to sing loudly: "Surge, surge, surge, the sea, crashing against the gray and cold rocks..."
His singing was rough and bold, but completely off-key, full of irritating, nauseating, and headache-inducing power.
The branches of the psychedelic wind chime tree trembled simultaneously, retracting as if to curl up together. The beautiful chimes that rang out slightly diluted the terrible noise.
Even though Klein had restrained his spirituality, at this moment, the veins on his forehead throbbed, and a sudden urge to kill the singer arose in his heart.
Alger continued to sing as he moved forward: "Surge, surge, surge, the sea, breaking at the foot of the rocks!"
"Disorder!" This 'wonderful' singing was interrupted by Hobert's ability.
Klein and Alger both turned to look at the masked demigod.
Hobert had stood up at some point. Although they couldn't see his expression, Klein could guess that he must be frowning or even gritting his teeth.
"I don't mean anything else!" Hobert said, "That fruit is yours. Whoever dares to snatch it from you, I'll beat them to death! But please don't sing anymore!"
Alger seemed to understand something. He first smiled helplessly, then seized the opportunity to summon invisible wind blades, slashing at the very top of the psychedelic wind chime tree where the fruit was.
The fist-sized fruit fell, and a strong wind swept it into Alger's palm.
The branches of the psychedelic wind chime tree drooped simultaneously, losing their vitality.
Hobert and Klein both breathed a sigh of relief. This hunt was finally over.
Alger was a little embarrassed: "Sorry, my singing was a bit off-key."
At the same time, he couldn't help but consider a very serious question: Even the 'Emperor,' who has advanced to a demigod, can't stand my singing. How am I supposed to act as an 'Ocean Songster'?
Hobert thought: No, your singing wasn't just off-key; every single note was wrong. Calling it off-key is an insult to the composer.
He sighed and said, "Actually, I should congratulate you. After becoming the 'Ocean Songster,' you've gained an ability that can irritate even demigods!"
Klein thought: This ability might be innate, perhaps not related to advancing to 'Ocean Songster.'
Alger smiled wryly. Before he could say anything, Hobert added, "Go and pull out that psychedelic wind chime tree. I remember that the 'eyes' on its bark are auxiliary Ingredients for Sequence 6 of the 'Reader' pathway, and the wind chimes on the branches seem to be higher-level supplementary Ingredients, but I'm not sure where exactly they're used."
Alger was slightly taken aback: "Carrying it with us will be very cumbersome."
Hobert took off his satchel: "It won't be cumbersome. I'll carry it."
Alger seemed to realize that it was an item with spatial magic. So, he stepped forward, shook the psychedelic wind chime tree, broke its roots, and easily pulled it out.
With Klein's help, they worked together to stuff the tree into the small satchel.
Hobert closed the satchel: "Alright, let's continue forward."
The three of them continued forward, walking for over half an hour, and the forest began to thin out again.
"After passing through this sparse area, we'll reach the edge of the ancient ruins," Alger broke the silence. "I've previously discovered traces of demigod-level Beyonder creatures around here."
"But the strange thing is that there are no clues of Beyonder creatures active inside the ancient ruins at all."
Klein muttered in his heart that this was likely because there was something even more terrifying inside the ancient ruins.
However, he wasn't too worried because he had done a corresponding divination 'above the gray fog' beforehand. The revelation he received was: there is danger, there are twists and turns, but the possibility of leaving safely is not small.
The three of them continued forward. After walking only a few dozen meters, Hobert said seemingly casually, "There's a Beyonder creature ahead."
Hobert was about to unleash his demigod's aura, but considering that it would likely scare the creature away, he only gave a warning.
Klein was slightly stunned. His spirituality didn't sense anything related: Is this the difference between a demigod and Sequence 5?
Sure enough, a few seconds later, they saw a pair of ghostly blue eyes.
It was a black baboon squatting on a branch. Its fur had natural curls, and a patch of black crystals grew out of its head. These crystals grew upwards, clustering irregularly into a strange crown.
Hobert thought: True curly-haired baboon!
As soon as they saw the black baboon, Klein and Alger had the urge to lower their heads, as if they dared not look directly at it.
According to the order, it was Klein's turn to act this time. Hobert and Alger both stepped back, watching Klein unleash his attacks. First, he used 'Travel' to approach the target, then used 'Wraith' to control it, and finally, the fatal blow of 'Dirge'.
This Beyonder creature with Sequence 5 power was easily killed.
Hobert nodded slowly: Klein, with the support of his marionette and mystical items, is definitely among the top of Sequence 5.
Then he couldn't help but simulate the tactics of fighting against Klein in his mind: This curly-haired baboon suffered because of its low intelligence. If I were fighting Klein, I would love for these very fast 'Seers' to get close to me. While 'Distorting' his 'Possession' ability, a slap would be enough to make him doubt his life.
In close combat, the 'Marionettist' is no match for the 'Mentor of Disorder.'
Hobert also thought: It's just that Klein probably wouldn't use such tactics when facing me. His most likely tactic would be to use 'Wraith' and his ranged skills to wear me down, and then patiently wait for an opportunity to manipulate the 'Spirit Threads.'
The manipulation of 'Spirit Body Threads' is not like 'Possession,' which can be 'Distorted' this second but not the next.
Faced with such tactics, the only option is to attack proactively, using 'Travel' to get close, and then continuously using 'Arrogance' and 'Disorder.' No matter which ability hits the main body, it can create good conditions for close combat.
Just as Hobert was thinking about this, he suddenly sensed the approach of danger.
He threw the satchel to Klein: "Put the corpse in the satchel, quickly hide inside the ruins!"
Alger was still surprised that Klein had so easily hunted down a Beyonder creature at Sequence 5, and Klein was also waiting for the Beyonder characteristics to separate.
But after hearing the 'Emperor's' warning, they immediately took action, stuffing the curly-haired baboon, whose Beyonder characteristics had not yet separated, into the satchel.
Just as they finished packing, they felt a huge sense of oppression.
This sense of oppression was several times stronger than that of the curly-haired baboon just now. At this time, they not only couldn't lift their heads, but also had a strong urge to kneel.
Hobert stood in front of them, also releasing his own demigod's aura.
Klein and Alger felt as if a huge rock pressing on their chests had suddenly been removed. While still feeling lingering fear, the two quickly ran towards the ruins.
At this time, Klein, who had the danger prediction ability of 'The Fool,' saw in his mind a large, curly-haired baboon running quickly towards them!
In addition to being much larger than the black baboon just now, its black fur seemed to emit a black light, and the crystals on its head were deep black, forming what looked like a solemn crown.
This was definitely a demigod-level curly-haired baboon, and Klein seriously suspected that it might be in a mythical creature state. Fortunately, they ran fast; otherwise, the consequences of witnessing it would have been unimaginable.
Hobert, who had already drawn his thin sword, wondered if he had stirred up a baboon's nest today. How did another baboon come?
Then he began to think about a very serious question: Could the mythical creature state of the 'Lawyer' pathway be a curly-haired baboon?
He shook his head: "Impossible! Absolutely impossible!"
At this time, the demigod-level curly-haired baboon roared at Hobert and was about to charge when Hobert reached out first: "Weaken!"
The curly-haired baboon didn't seem to be affected much, and charged head-on. At the same time, Hobert's surroundings immediately fell into a state of chaos, and he himself felt dazed.
He found that when he wanted to raise his left hand, he raised his right hand instead, and when he wanted to lift his left foot, he turned around in circles.
"Distort!" Hobert 'Distorted' his position with a tree, appearing outside the 'Disordered' area.
Hobert's dazed feeling disappeared, but his body was still a little uncoordinated.
This was the first time he felt that his 'Chaos' could bring so much inconvenience to the enemy.
The curly-haired baboon seemed to anticipate Hobert's movement and slapped him.
"Bestow!" Hobert 'Bestowed' the remaining 'Disordered' state to the curly-haired baboon, and punched the curly-haired baboon head-on in a contest of strength.
As a result, the curly-haired baboon's slap sent Hobert back more than ten meters, and it followed up with another punch.
"Ha!" Hobert shouted as if to cheer himself up, and also punched the curly-haired baboon head-on again in a contest.
Hobert took two steps back, his back hitting a towering tree.
Crack~
The clearly mutated tree on the island was directly broken and flew out vertically.
Crack, crack~
It knocked down two more towering trees before the force of the punch was completely dissipated.
The curly-haired baboon's attacks came like a storm. Although it was in a 'Weakened' state, it didn't look weak at all.
Hobert, who had a further understanding of his own strength and physique, decided to end this battle as soon as possible.
"Charm!" Hobert had planned to use his mental attacks to control the enemy when he used 'Weaken' and 'Grant' in succession.
Because the curly-haired baboon's flaws were too obvious. Like the previous black-haired baboon, they seemed to have put all their talents into 'Strength.'
Even though this guy was in a 'Weakened' state, Hobert was no match for it in terms of strength.
But 'Weaken' not only weakens strength, but also weakens intelligence, spirituality, and other aspects.
The curly-haired baboon's already meager intelligence was weakened again, and under the 'Bestowed' state, 'Charm' and other abilities would be greatly enhanced.
Sure enough, the curly-haired baboon couldn't bring down its raised fist. It suddenly felt that the two-legged beast in front of it looked quite cute.
Hobert certainly wouldn't be polite with it: "Slaughter!"
A punch hit the curly-haired baboon's chest, and the punch went directly into its flesh and bones. He even felt the curly-haired baboon's soft internal organs!
The curly-haired baboon roared angrily, recovered from the 'Charm' state, and then ran away.
"Magnify!" Hobert then magnified the opponent's serious injury into a fatal injury!
At the same time, he thought: 'Slaughter' + 'Magnify' is a perfect match!
The curly-haired baboon staggered, almost falling, but its physique was strong. Even with such a serious chest injury, it could still continue to escape.
Just as it was preparing to 'Bestow' its own injuries to the person behind it, Hobert had already raised his hand first: "Connection!"
The curly-haired baboon looked in the direction of the black baboon that had just been killed by Klein. There was still the other party's brains and blood on the ground.
While the other party was feeling emotional, Hobert's second wave of attacks had already arrived, directly piercing the curly-haired baboon's head with a thin sword, nailing it to a large tree.
The curly-haired baboon struggled desperately, and its surroundings suddenly became chaotic. Whether it was Beyonder abilities or physical attacks, it was difficult to penetrate this chaotic area.
Hobert's sword was still stuck in the opponent's head, but he couldn't grasp the hilt. It was right in front of him, but his outstretched hand kept reaching in other directions.
Hobert had already thought of a way to deal with this situation: "Disorder!"
This method was to "confuse" the opponent's "confusion." Although it wouldn't have a "negative times negative equals positive" effect, Hobert's attacks would have a certain probability of hitting the target.
So Hobert began to use "Fatal Attack." The first strike hit a tree to the side, sending the towering tree flying. The second strike hit a nearby rock, shattering it into pieces.
The third strike hit the woolly baboon, directly breaking its spine. The fourth strike hit it again, shattering the scapula of its left shoulder. The broken bone pierced through the flesh, turning outwards.
The surrounding "disordered" state gradually disappeared, and the woolly baboon's breathing became weaker.
Hobert stepped forward, grasped the hilt, and the rapier instantly transformed into a two-handed greatsword, splitting the woolly baboon's head.
Sheathing his sword, Hobert was about to wait for the woolly baboon's Beyonder characteristics to separate when he suddenly looked up towards the ruins: "So many demigod-level Beyonder creatures?"
...
Klein and Alger quickly headed towards the ruins. As they walked, Klein suddenly felt something. He raised his hand and saw his fingernails gradually losing their luster.
Then his knees stiffened, and his muscles solidified.
Only then did he and Alger's spirituality realize the extreme danger. Klein immediately grabbed Alger's shoulder and entered the richly colored spirit world, preparing to quickly traverse to the ancient ruins.
Suddenly, the colors before Klein's eyes uniformly turned deep black, and presented fine textures, like a head of dark hair!
A chill filled his heart. Klein didn't hesitate to leave the spirit world and return to the real world.
The close contact with the "long hair" had already started to petrify them from their feet, and now they couldn't move their legs.
At this moment, the two saw Hobert dragging the corpse of a three-to-four-meter-long, sturdy woolly baboon, rushing towards them.
His "running" was interesting, as if he was moving forward in fits and starts.
This reminded Klein of some horror movies he had seen before. In the first half of the second, Hobert was still seven or eight meters away, and in the second half of the second, he had appeared in front of them as if he had jumped through space.
Half a second later, he advanced another seven or eight meters.
This "running" speed was very fast. Just as they saw Hobert appear in the sparse forest, he was very close in the blink of an eye. In another blink of an eye, Hobert had already punched out, hitting a lithe body from the air not far from them. Whether it was her or its hair was very long, like a curtain, and once again hid in the air.
Hobert threw the woolly baboon in his other hand into the nearby ruins, and then, with one arm around each of Klein and Alger, quickly entered the ruins using the "distorted" distance method.
As soon as they entered the ruins, the three of them breathed a sigh of relief, and their spiritual warning disappeared.
However, Klein and Alger's petrification had already reached their thighs, and Hobert's fist was also petrified.
Fortunately, the gray-white petrification was gradually fading, and their bodies were rapidly recovering.
Hobert laughed: "This island is a treasure. In such a short period of time, I've already encountered the third demigod-level mythical creature."
"It's a pity that my spirituality has been consumed a lot, and I don't have any miraculous items that can restrain the opponent's abilities, otherwise I could try hunting it."
Klein and Alger were sweating profusely at this time. They had already made up their minds that they must never come to such a dangerous place again before becoming demigods.
At this time, Alger looked at the woolly baboon's corpse that Hobert had thrown in earlier, and he couldn't help but sigh: These two teammates, one at Sequence 5, so easily solved an Beyonder creature of Sequence 5. One at the demigod level, so easily solved an Beyonder creature at the demigod level.
The time they were apart was only a little over half a minute, and "Emperor" had already killed the opponent and chased after them.
Hobert, who recovered first, put the huge woolly baboon into his leather bag in a good mood.
This leather bag with space magic was already full, and it could barely hold the outer buckle.
Hobert sighed in his heart: I really hope Fors can become a demigod soon, so that I will have endless space magic equipment to use.
At this time, Alger, who had also recovered, asked: "What kind of creature attacked us just now?"
If it wasn't for the lithe figure that "Emperor" had punched out of the air, he would have thought that the area was petrifying them.
"That should be an Beyonder creature corresponding to Sequence 3 'Demoness of Unaging'," Hobert said: "I remember that 'Demoness of Unaging' has the ability to petrify."
Then he explained casually: "The Beyonder creatures on these islands are very strange. Many of them have complete Beyonder characteristics of a certain Sequence."
Alger nodded as if he had learned something.
But Klein recalled the "Demoness of Unaging" he encountered on the "Vice Admiral Ailment's" ship.
Then, the three of them looked together at the ruins in front of them. Alger said, "I came here during the day. This looks like a church."
After resting for a while, he led the way into a relatively intact hall: "I explored inward from here last time."
Entering the interior of the building, you could see the outer towers and bell towers from some collapsed places.
Alger continued to explain: "After leaving here last time, I consulted some information. This is the architectural style of the Fourth Epoch."
"Its biggest feature is the upper temple and lower tomb, uniting life and death together, but I cannot be sure of the internal structure of this church, because I didn't explore deeply enough last time."
"Ahead is the mural area, which is the basis for my judgment that there are extremely important things here."
As he spoke, they came to an area with murals on the walls. The first mural contained crosses that emitted layers of light.
In front of the cross was a majestic figure, surrounded by two-winged, four-winged, and six-winged angels.
Hobert simply glanced at it and continued forward, but Klein clearly paused. He had seen similar murals in Amon's mausoleum.
But he quickly found the difference. There was no description of Adam and Amon in it. The majestic divine figure held a simple and unadorned stone slab in both hands.
That stone slab was painted extremely vaguely, but it had a feeling of being ancient and young, sacred and evil.
Klein's pupils dilated slightly, and he immediately realized what it was: "Blasphemy Slate!"
