On the third day of the Feynapotter Kingdom delegation's arrival in the Duchy of Southern Balam, Ambassador Princess Ethel met Grand Duke Hobert in his office with mixed feelings.
Her feelings were complicated because she had witnessed three angels swearing allegiance to the "Creator" the day before. Her original perception of Southern Balam was as an equal, but now she looked up to them.
Hobert still wore a hearty smile, and the initial small talk gave the impression of chatting with an old friend after a long absence.
After chatting for a while, Hobert said, "The Feynapotter Kingdom was the first country to send an ambassador to Southern Balam and establish an embassy."
"During the previous civil war in the Duchy of Southern Balam, you did not participate in the joint forces of Feysac and Intis. This is the quality of an ally. I hope we can maintain a good relationship in the future."
Currently, the Loen Kingdom only has an office in Angers. If they send an ambassador, it would be equivalent to recognizing the independence of the Duchy of Southern Balam.
As for Feysac and Intis, their attitude towards the Duchy of Southern Balam has been wavering. Recently, they have often sent people to show goodwill, but once the war in the Northern Continent ends, they will definitely not adopt their current diplomatic policy.
Ethel smiled and said, "The relationship between our two countries will definitely become closer and closer."
What Hobert didn't know was that Ethel's "bet" on the Duchy of Southern Balam had earned her a lot of political resources and gradually given her a certain advantage in the struggle for the crown.
Like most politicians in Feynapotter, the politicians of Feysac and Intis felt that the Duchy of Southern Balam was just a colonial country and did not pay enough attention to it.
During the previous civil war in Southern Balam, the military and parliament of Feynapotter believed that they should form a joint force with Intis and Feysac, but Ethel strongly opposed the idea and did not participate in the opportunistic looting.
Because she was very clear about Hobert's abilities and knew that the country had the "Creator" as its backing.
Later facts proved that Ethel's persistence was correct, which established her image as having political foresight.
A few months ago, when the Duchy of Southern Balam attacked the Highland Kingdom, all the countries in the Northern Continent except the Loen Kingdom breathed a sigh of relief, thinking that Southern Balam would not be able to get out of the quagmire of the Highland Kingdom within a year or two.
At that time, the Feysac Empire, which had just completed negotiations, felt that it was unnecessary to continue to maintain a good relationship with the Duchy of Southern Balam. The Intis Republic was even planning a new war against the colonies in the Southern Continent.
The Church of the God of Steam and Machinery also completed its alignment at this time, expressing its support for the Intis Republic.
Only Ethel suggested that at this time, they should strengthen their ties with the Duchy of Southern Balam and negotiate the matter of sending an ambassador.
This point was still opposed by many people in the country, but more than two months later, the Duchy of Southern Balam quickly ended the war, once again slapping those opponents in the face.
It can be said that Ethel's political position in the country is basically based on her "political bet" on the Duchy of Southern Balam.
After reaffirming the relationship between the two countries, Ethel said, "We are now encountering a problem. The war between Lenburg and Masin will be difficult to end in the short term."
"Our strategic department expects that Intis and Feysac will be able to capture Backlund by the first half of next year at the latest. If we don't have any significant achievements before then, we will be very passive during future negotiations."
Politicians are well aware of this, and Hobert is also very clear about the current situation of the Feynapotter Kingdom, but it is different when Ethel says it. This is a political statement and a gesture of seeking help.
Hobert pondered for a moment, then got up and took out a map of the Northern Continent from a bookshelf next to him and spread it on the table.
He pointed to the map and said, "I suggest you occupy the southwest of the Desi County and Desi Bay."
The location Hobert was talking about is in the southwest of Loen. The geographical location of these places is not very important. The Loen army did not dare to station too many troops here when they retreated.
Because the Intis Republic will definitely occupy the eastern part of Desi County and the coastal city of Conant. At that time, the garrison here will become an isolated force.
Intis doesn't pay much attention to this area either. It belongs to the kind of area that doesn't matter whether it is occupied or not.
So this area nominally still belongs to the Loen Kingdom, but it has become an exclave and there is almost no military force here.
Coincidentally, this place borders the Feynapotter Kingdom.
Ethel sighed and said, "We have also made this assumption, but these areas do not pose a threat to the Intis Republic, and they do not border the Feysac Empire."
"It can only threaten the Loen Kingdom, and it is difficult to become our bargaining chip in negotiations with Intis and Feysac."
The hilly area in the southwest of Desi County has always been the front line for Loen to block the Feynapotter Kingdom. After occupying this area, what lies in front of the Feynapotter Kingdom is the vast Tucker Plain.
Hobert smiled and said, "Trust me, occupy this place first, and the Feynapotter Kingdom will definitely benefit from it in the future."
He is very willing to help Feynapotter, because he does not want the Loen Kingdom to become the sole victor in this world war in the future.
Even if Feynapotter immediately defects after Loen starts its counterattack, it will not be able to share much of the spoils of victory.
But it is different to occupy the southwest of Desi County. If Loen wants to take it back, it will have to exchange a lot of spoils of victory.
It doesn't matter whether the Feynapotter Kingdom occupies Lenburg and Masin, it can still attend the post-war negotiations as a victor.
Ethel pondered for a moment before asking, "Do you think the Loen Kingdom still has hope? Or is the 'Creator's' power going to do everything possible to help Loen?"
Hobert seemed to answer Ethel, and seemed not to answer, "That's right, we will send a large number of forces to participate in the Backlund battle at the right time."
Originally, Hobert estimated that the war against the Highland Kingdom would not end until August at the earliest. At that time, after a short rest, they would enter the Northern Continent to participate in the war.
However, under Medici's command, the war against the Highland Kingdom ended cleanly.
This gave Hobert a chance to be promoted calmly, and gave him enough time to ask for a high price, but he would still choose to participate in the war in October at the earliest, when Backlund was at its most critical.
Ethel immediately nodded, "I understand."
In her opinion, if the Duchy of Southern Balam participated in the war, although it would not be able to change the overall situation, the Battle of Backlund would definitely become a protracted war, which would be enough to bring Intis and Feysac back to the negotiating table.
Then the pattern of the four major powers in the Northern Continent would still not change much. The only change might be that Intis would seize Loen's hegemonic position.
With Hobert's words, Ethel felt a lot more at ease.
Then the two people talked about the mutual trade between the two countries. Previously, the Duchy of Southern Balam had opened the South Kerrson area to the Feynapotter Kingdom. Now, Hobert has opened Longtail Island and Angers to Feynapotter.
Other cities still need a series of constructions, and the political and economic systems are not yet sound, so they will not be open to the outside world for the time being.
Ethel was also the first foreign dignitary to visit the Longtail Island Industrial Zone and the Southern Balam Industrial Zone. Ethel always felt a little incredible about these two large-scale industrial parks.
All along, colonies and industrial zones seem to have nothing to do with each other, so when she saw so many industrial zones in the colony, her first feeling was a bit magical.
After a more detailed understanding, Ethel discovered that the industrial system of the Duchy of Southern Balam was even more complete than that of the Feynapotter Kingdom!
This is also the reason why Hobert let her visit the industrial zone, because Feynapotter's industry is the worst among the four major countries, so it is very stable in fourth place.
After visiting the industrial zone, Ethel found that many industrial products could be imported from the Duchy of Southern Balam to avoid industrial dependence on the other three countries.
So, on the fourth day of the delegation's visit, they signed a series of economic cooperation agreements with the Duchy of Southern Balam. Ethel's visit was a fruitful one.
After seeing Ethel off, Hobert began to "wander around" the Duchy of Southern Balam again.
Currently, three mausoleums have been built almost completely. After the Highland Kingdom was destroyed, a new batch of labor was obtained on the construction site, and the first mausoleum will be completed soon.
So Hobert began to look for new places to build mausoleums. Hobert planned to build one of the mausoleums in a pharaoh's pyramid.
The king of the Highland Kingdom called himself a pharaoh, but their pyramids were not the triangular pyramids that Hobert remembered, but segmented trapezoids.
Generally, their pyramids will have the protection of spiritual barriers. Without corresponding clues, even angels will find it difficult to find their location.
Because everyone in Yason City instantly turned into monsters, the royal family of the Highland Kingdom did not have time to destroy the corresponding information. The "Dawn Army" and "Temperance Faction" stationed here have found several pharaoh's tombs.
And they dug out a lot of gold and sealed items!
For the "Temperance Faction", the pharaoh's body is of the greatest use to them. For a long time in the future, the "Temperance Faction" will not have to worry about the ritual of advancing to a demigod.
Hobert chose the largest one with the most comprehensive protection facilities to build... or rather, to transform it into his own mausoleum.
Hobert decided to build the fifth mausoleum on the seabed. When he was in school in the Modern Era, he heard his mentor talk about "undersea tombs".
First, build the tomb chamber on a large ship on the sea surface, and then sink the ship, and the tomb chamber sinks to the seabed.
The air inside the tomb chamber will isolate the seawater, forming a very closed environment.
One of the benefits of this type of tomb is that unless by chance, you can't find it on the sea surface where you can't pinpoint the location based on clues.
In the extraordinary world, Hobert will carry out sufficient anti-divination and spiritual barrier settings to make it difficult for Beyonders to find it.
As for the construction site of the sixth mausoleum, Hobert set his sights on Antarctica.
When he "tampered" with the climate before, Hobert once saw Antarctica from afar and determined that at least a large part of the continent existed in the real world.
So, after Hobert had nothing to deal with, he went to Antarctica alone to explore.
When Hobert saw the massive ice wall from afar, he felt the magnificence of this continent. During the Modern Era, he had only seen some introductions about this continent in documentaries, but after coming here, he realized how beautiful the scenery was.
It was a kind of tranquil beauty, far from the hustle and bustle of humanity, as if it were a pure land for the soul.
Regardless of whether there were extraordinary powers or not, this continent was very peaceful, appearing as if it had never been disturbed by the outside world.
Hobert had heard that the Loen Kingdom and the Intis Republic had both sent survey ships to this continent, but because icebreaking technology was not very mature, they had only landed on the continent and had not established observation stations or research stations.
It was said that the Feysac Empire had corresponding icebreaking technology, but this country was too far away, and there were no colonies nearby, so they had never sent survey ships here.
Looking towards the sky, this continent was still in the polar night, and the cosmos was very beautiful.
But Hobert didn't dare to look too much, fearing the dangers hidden within.
With Hobert's current eyesight, he could see very far even under such starlight.
Even with the obstruction of wind and snow, Hobert could see the tall mountains in the distance. After arriving at the top of the mountain by 'distorting' space, Hobert was somewhat disappointed with the scenery here.
Looking down from here, there was only a white desert, as if there was no life at all.
So Hobert began to look for a place on the mountain to build a mausoleum. Soon, he found a cave in the mountains.
Hobert's spirituality also sensed that there was a weak life form in the cave. He guessed that it was some Antarctic animal hibernating in the cave.
Because he didn't sense any danger, he didn't pay much attention to it. He took a step forward and 'tampered' with his position to inside the cave.
Although there was no howling cold wind, the cave was also very cold. After all, it was the polar night in Antarctica, and there would be no warm places on the entire continent.
Just as Hobert was pondering how to use Beyonder abilities to hollow out the inside of the mountain and create a space to build a mausoleum, he sensed that the weak life form was at the corner in front of him.
Hobert remembered that penguins didn't seem to hibernate. He was a little curious about what kind of creature it would be there? Could it be a polar bear?
He joked in his heart as he passed the bend ahead, and then he got an even more absurd answer than a polar bear: there was actually a person there!
To be precise, it was an ice sculpture standing there. Even though Hobert had become Sequence 1, seeing a person frozen into an ice sculpture in such a dimly lit environment still made his scalp tingle.
Immediately afterwards, he realized two strange things. First of all, this person seemed to still have some vital signs.
Originally, Hobert thought that this should be a Beyonder, and at least a demigod-level Beyonder, otherwise it would be impossible to be frozen into an ice sculpture and still not be dead.
But soon he realized another strange thing. This person was stark naked, but he was holding a water bottle in his hand, and there was a pile of clothes beside him.
After seeing those clothes, Hobert's eyes narrowed. Among them, there was actually a parka!
Yes, it was a polar parka!
This made Hobert's scalp tingle even more, because he was very sure that there were no parkas in the entire Northern and Southern continents!
Hobert had a bold idea: could this be a 'prehistoric' human?
But the question was, why was he still alive?
With these questions in mind, Hobert carefully looked at the appearance of the ice sculpture. It was actually an Asian face.
Before the transmigration, Hobert faced such faces every day, but now he felt a little unfamiliar with such facial features.
Because the people of the Northern and Southern continents have some differences in facial features compared to Asians!
Hobert had never seen a living elf, and didn't know if they had Asian facial features, but Alger, a half-elf and half-human, didn't have any Asian features at all.
He took a deep breath, calmed down, and then realized another strange thing about this ice sculpture.
Judging from the clothes on the ground, his equipment was very complete. If he hadn't taken off his clothes himself, he wouldn't have been frozen to death even in the polar night.
If he had gotten lost in Antarctica and had to wait for rescue here, and died in the process, he should have died wearing clothes, not frozen to death like this.
Hobert swallowed and said, "Who are you? Why are you here?"
Then he smiled: "It would be terrifying if you could talk."
The cold wind outside continued to howl, and the surrounding light was still very dim.
Hobert considered it for a while, and finally decided that since he had encountered it, he should investigate what was going on.
But if he directly thawed this ice sculpture brother, Hobert felt it would be a bit dangerous, so he looked at the clothes at the ice sculpture's feet. There seemed to be a bag in there.
Hobert was about to use the method of 'tampered' with the position to take one of the clothes over and search it, but for some reason, he always felt that if he touched the ice sculpture's things, this guy could suddenly move and stop him.
He sighed to himself: "Having too much humanity is not a good thing."
So Hobert first used the method of 'distorting' space to transfer the ice sculpture to the deeper, invisible part of the cave. Only then did he pick up a piece of clothing.
But the moment he touched the clothing, the clothing seemed to collapse, turning into pieces of cloth.
Even in a cold place like Antarctica, but after thousands of years, or perhaps longer, these clothes could only maintain their current shape.
So Hobert 'tampered' with the flexibility of these items, making them stronger, and then picked up one of the parkas.
First, he saw a few Chinese characters on the parka: Great Wall Station, Sun Zhilin.
Hobert smiled and sighed: "Chinese characters that have nothing to do with the Roselle diary!"
Immediately afterwards, he looked at the small, bright five-star red flag on it, and was stunned for a long time.
Taking another deep breath, Hobert recalled that he remembered that the Great Wall Station was a Chinese Antarctic research station. He wasn't very clear about the specific location, but he knew there was such a research station.
This name tag confirmed the 'prehistoric human' identity of the ice sculpture!
Next, Hobert found some electronic products in the only bag, but when he saw the mobile phone, Hobert was about to put it in his pocket, intending to give it to the researchers for research when the time was right.
But then he thought that without a satellite, having a mobile phone was useless.
After hesitating for a while, he finally put it away, in case he might need it in the future.
Fortunately, there was also a paper notebook in the bag. Hobert opened it and looked at it. They were all some very scattered things recorded randomly, including meeting minutes and some data that Hobert didn't know what they were.
It wasn't until he turned to the last page that Hobert saw something of value: "My phone is out of power, so I have to record the voices in my head in this way.
That voice said: Everyone will die, but they will also usher in a new life.
That voice said: He came from a very far place, but he was frozen under Antarctica.
That voice said: The ice and snow of Antarctica have an abstract meaning.
That voice said: He wants to take advantage of this opportunity to...revive inside me."
When Hobert saw these words, he felt a little disturbed. He knew that 'that voice' was definitely not simple. If he wasn't an angel, he might have already been corrupted by the unknown.
There were two more sentences at the end: "Everything, everything, starts with the abnormality of Kunlun Station!"
"I'm dead...but I don't seem to be dead!"
Closing the notebook, Hobert's first thought was: Is there also an entrance to the 'Chaos Sea' in Antarctica? The staff of the research station were corrupted by the origin. But who is 'that voice'? Could it be the awakened 'Original Creator'?
Hobert also thought: 'That voice' said, 'He came from a very far place,' where did he come from?
Also, what does 'The ice and snow of Antarctica have an abstract meaning' mean?
Hobert shook his head and made some speculations using some of the knowledge he knew: This should be the influence of the Original Creator on the researchers here after waking up.
Perhaps that 'ice sculpture' that has existed for thousands of years is a special case? Is the Original Creator preparing to revive in his body? But no matter what, his current state is already a monster.
Taking a deep breath, Hobert continued to search and found a map of Antarctica in the bag, with the locations of research stations from various countries on the map.
Among them, Hobert found the Great Wall Station, Zhongshan Station, Taishan Station, Kunlun Station, and Qinling Station with the five-star red flag logo. According to the approximate locations, the Great Wall Station didn't seem too far from here.
And Kunlun Station is located in the more central part of Antarctica, quite far from here.
Hobert pondered for a while and decided to go to the Great Wall Station first.
Hobert didn't recognize these electronic products except for the mobile phone, but he still put them away, in case he could use them in the future.
Hobert restored the flexibility of these clothes and destroyed them.
He didn't want that prehistoric civilization to be presented to more people.
As for that 'ice sculpture', Hobert originally wanted to crush him, but just as he was about to take action, he suddenly thought of the name 'Sun Zhilin' and silently left the cave after all.
He explained to himself: Perhaps in the process of investigation, he still needs to obtain more clues from him.
In the vast ice and snow, Hobert relied on the guidance of his spirituality to come to the foot of a hillside.
Logically speaking, it should be the location of the Great Wall Station, but there was nothing here.

chapters.title: Chapter 708 - 704: Messages Left Behind by Prehistoric Civilization
chapters.content:
join the Church of MissRaven and become a Sequence 9: Reader p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Hobert looked around, suddenly realizing that it was normal for there to be nothing here.
After all, so much time had passed, and judging from the changes in the terrain of the Northern and Southern continents, the several wars between gods in history had a huge impact on the entire world's landmass.
This vast continent in the south most point of Earth should have also experienced disasters such as earthquakes. The research station might have been buried underground long ago, or it might have suffered severe damage in natural disasters and been blown away by the strong winds.
Besides, some gods should have come to explore this place before. Other gods might not be interested in this place, but the Evernight Goddess or Roselle would probably take a look after becoming a High-Sequence, right?
I haven't heard of Roselle finding a research station here in his diary.
"Huh!" Just as Hobert was about to use his spirituality to sense whether there was any buried space underground, he suddenly saw a corner of a man-made object in the ice and snow.
The next second, He had already used the method of "distorting" space to come to the front of the ice and snow. It was indeed a corner of an iron building.
Hobert used his spirituality to sense it. There were no signs of life inside, but there was a considerable space.
Similarly, not sensing any danger, Hobert took out the "Sun Scepter" and used the method of "tampering" with position to enter the space inside.
Under the light emitted by the "Sun Scepter," Hobert saw that this was a slightly inclined rectangular space. As far as the eye could see, there was a thick layer of dust, but there were no "ice sculptures" or any humanoid creatures here.
Regardless of the howling sea breeze outside, the enclosed space inside was very quiet.
Taking a closer look at the furnishings here, Hobert found that they were very well preserved, greatly exceeding His expectations. If it had experienced several major earthquakes, these buildings should have collapsed long ago.
After simply glancing around, Hobert noticed that there seemed to be some dirt-like things on the largest white wall. They seemed to be some words, but they were too old to see clearly.
Hobert pondered for a moment and increased the refractive index of these "dirt," and they became clearly visible.
Those were two lines of bright red characters: "The crying of children has attracted some terrifying things…"
"But, there are no children in the research station…"
Hobert scratched his head. These words should have been written in blood. He felt that the more he investigated this matter, the more terrifying it became.
But He knew that this was also very likely some illusory sounds or hallucinations that the researchers heard after the "Original Creator" began to exert influence on the entire real world.
It looked quite terrifying, but the matter did not seem to exceed Hobert's previous guess.
Continuing to search inside, Hobert found a few scattered documents on a table in an archive room.
These documents seemed to have been repeatedly reviewed by the researchers.
Hobert first "tampered" with the toughness of these documents to prevent them from turning into paper scraps with a slight touch.
He waved his hand gently, and after the dust on them floated away, only a piece of paper that was almost blank was left.
Hobert looked at it carefully. It should have been printed text, but after a long time, the ink had almost disappeared.
This was not difficult for Hobert. He "tampered" with the brightness of the dye in the ink, and soon the contents of these documents reappeared.
Hobert picked up the documents and quickly glanced at them.
These documents were divided into two parts. One part was the paper archives of the Great Wall Station's contact with the outside world, and the other folder was the archives of communication between the Great Wall Station and the Kunlun Station.
The contact between the research station and the outside world was normal at first, but about "a month ago," there seemed to be some huge changes in the outside world.
First of all, oil resources dried up in a matter of days, and the whole world was plunged into panic. Oil was already an indispensable thing in that world, and it was hard to imagine how the human world would regress without oil.
Then, the research station received a retreat order, but the icebreaker that was supposed to pick them up never appeared.
Finally, the outside world began to send a lot of messy things here, including mythological stories, some unintelligible descriptions, and some incomprehensible but terrifying descriptions.
For example: "The sun suddenly fell to the ground…"
"A group of elaborately dressed rats invited me to be their food…"
"A strange smiling face appeared in the air…"
"The seawater did not freeze, but it suddenly turned into a solid, ah… that doesn't seem to be a solid, but a huge monster…"
The last message from the outside world was: "The monsters want to rush in here very much, but they are not monsters. Just now they were all human beings. Many of us have heard some strange murmurs and turned into monsters. Hehe, actually, I am also a monster… Hello, I will find you…"
There was also a line of pen writing: What exactly happened outside? Who made that huge roar? Why are sunrise and sunset no longer regular? Why is there no response from the outside world?
Based on some information previously released by Klein, Hobert roughly sorted out this catastrophe.
First of all, some anomalies occurred in Chernobyl. To be precise, the only "Chaos Sea" with an entrance in the real world created some supernatural phenomena. These anomalies lasted for a period of time, at least enough time to build a research institute there.
At the same time, the two personalities, Celestial Worthy and God, created by the tendency of the "Original Creator" to split during sleep, further affected the real world. Especially Celestial Worthy, who began to "recruit people."
As the connection between the "Chaos Sea" and the real world became deeper and deeper, oil was quickly assimilated by the expanding "Chaos Sea."
The manifestation of the Sephirot and the power of Celestial Worthy and God turned many people into monsters and caused huge changes in this world.
Finally, the "Original Creator" woke up. The moment He woke up, this world was destroyed. Just the awakening of His consciousness was enough to turn all the creatures on this planet into monsters.
Thinking of these things, Hobert looked at the line of pen writing again: The destruction here… seems to be a beat slower?
At least when the people outside were all crazy, unable to get any replies, and the laws of nature became chaotic, there were still people here who maintained their sanity.
Hobert guessed that when sunrise and sunset were disrupted, it should have been very close to the time when the "Original Creator" woke up. At that time, no one in the whole world should have been able to leave a few lines of pen writing.
After thinking for a while, Hobert felt that he could not grasp the key points, so he took a deep breath and went to look at the communication archives with the Kunlun Station.
There was only one folder for the communication with the Kunlun Station, because the Kunlun Station was in another direction of Antarctica, deep inside the Antarctic continent. That research station basically obtained supplies from the Zhongshan Station, so there was not much contact with the Great Wall Station.
Most of the time, the contact between the two research stations was for joint observation of the climate or the cosmos.
After seeing some of their observations of the cosmos, Hobert instinctively felt a little resistance, but then he thought that the cosmos at that time seemed to be safe, so he continued to look down.
The anomaly of the Kunlun Station appeared "two months ago." At that time, the two research stations had a text message conversation. The content in the archive is as follows:
Great Wall Station: Why not use video calls or voice calls?
Kunlun Station: Can't use them?
Great Wall Station: Is there a fault in the communication system?
Kunlun Station: No, a strange thing happened here. When we were about to report the recent findings to the superiors, the outside world couldn't hear or see anything.
Great Wall Station: Sorry, this… this is a bit difficult to understand.
Kunlun Station: For example, when I have a video call with Beijing, it is clear that the video has been connected, and we confirm that there is no problem with the communication when we greet each other, but when it comes to work content, Beijing cannot hear my voice or see the samples I am showing.
Great Wall Station: There must be a problem with the communication system.
Kunlun Station: We have checked it many times. This time we are contacting you for an experiment. We found that describing it in words can convey some information to the outside, but it is incomplete. So, we want to try in the Antarctic continent, in the form of text, whether you can receive the content we need to report.
Great Wall Station: Suggest checking the communication system again.
Kunlun Station: We found a biological-like tissue structure in the ice layer of Area 3. Two biologists who observed it through a microscope suddenly had serious mental problems. They kept saying: "He has lived for a long, long time, he is still alive… he is still alive…"
Kunlun Station: Please forward the information I sent you earlier.
Great Wall Station: Brother, how long have you been in Antarctica? Isn't it time to go back to your country for a rest?
Kunlun Station: Send it to me quickly, this is very important to me!
Great Wall Station: Okay, since you insist. We are in Area 3…
This was the first abnormal message sent by the Kunlun Station, but unfortunately, there was no description of the investigation results of this matter.
Hobert pinched his chin. He guessed: Could it be that at the same time as the anomaly appeared in Chernobyl, an anomaly was also discovered in Antarctica?
The "biological tissue structure" they discovered was obviously corrupted with a high level corruption, and the scientists who directly observed it with a microscope were corrupted.
But it is not known whether the words they kept repeating were some kind of illusion or some murmurs.
If it is the former, it is just nonsense after the spirit body basically collapses.
If it is the latter, in essence, that extraordinary corruption have established some kind of connection between the two scientists and the source of corruption, and the scientists' spirit bodies have obtained some information from the source of corruption.
If it is the latter, these words can be used as a reference to a certain extent.
Hobert reread the words that the two scientists were constantly repeating: Could the "biological tissue structure" they discovered be the body of the original Creator? Or was it the Celestial Worthy or God Almighty? Or was it their shared body?
They have always been on Earth, but it is difficult to determine what state they exist in.
Hobert and Klein had once speculated whether the original Creator might have been sleeping in the "Chaos Sea" at the Earth's core? But whether He had His own body was unknown.
The Celestial Worthy and God Almighty should have structures similar to bodies. God Almighty's body even formed the first "Blasphemy Slate." So, the question is, did the Celestial Worthy or God Almighty sleep in Antarctica back then?
This thought made Hobert smile and think: This is indeed a good place for "hibernation."
Another place worth noting is that any information sent by Kunlun Station outside of Antarctica is blocked by a strange force.
This kind of thing happening in the extraordinary world wouldn't feel like much.
But if it happens in the real world, it's quite terrifying. For example, during work communication, no matter how you describe a certain task, others can't understand or hear it.
Hobert realized that this seemed a bit like the authority of "Concealment"!
Then Hobert thought: If it's not God Almighty or the Celestial Worthy, could there be another being on Earth before the Original Creator awoke?
Combining the information previously discovered in the cave, Hobert felt that it was not impossible: He has been sleeping in Antarctica, and influenced by the awakening of the original Creator, He is also preparing to revive, or rather, awaken?
With this question, Hobert continued to read on. More than a month later, the two research stations had another contact. This time, the content was very short:
Kunlun Station: We must stop him! We must stop him! If we don't succeed, you must take over our mission!
Changcheng Station: Stop who? What mission?
Kunlun Station: We must stop him! We must stop him!
Hobert withdrew his gaze. Obviously, during this communication, Kunlun Station's abnormality was already very obvious.
He boldly guessed: Could it be that there is a being who has been sleeping in Antarctica, and when the "Original Creator" is about to awaken, He regained a part of his consciousness, affecting the scientists at Kunlun Station?
And after the researchers at Kunlun Station were corrupted by Him, they understood that if He continued to be active, it would definitely be a disaster!
So the scientists want to stop him! Or rather, Him.
Then, Hobert thought of another possibility: Maybe there were some high-level Beyonder characteristics near Kunlun Station at that time. With the gradual awakening of the "Original Creator", those Beyonder characteristics began to become active, ready to gather with the "Original Creator", thus affecting the researchers at Kunlun Station?
Hobert continued to read on. The following was the last contact between the two sides:
Kunlun Station: We shouldn't have dug that place open!
Changcheng Station: Where?
Kunlun Station: Area 3! Antarctica is different from other continents… different…
Changcheng Station: How is it different?
Kunlun Station: A week later, if we don't contact you, please come immediately. We have organized all the information. To prevent electronic equipment from malfunctioning, we have made paper backups, all in folder number 155. Goodbye everyone, now that we know the truth, we cannot sit idly by… cannot sit idly by…
The other party's last message suddenly made Hobert feel a bit tragic.
How could the power of ordinary people stop the awakening of the "Original Creator"?
But… Hobert re-examined this space buried under the ice and snow. Except for the blood writing on the wall, this place is basically neat, which means that after some strange things started happening here, the researchers most likely left in an orderly manner.
If the people here had all turned into monsters, this place couldn't be so neat, and it couldn't be as simple as leaving two lines of blood writing.
Since the ship that was supposed to pick them up never came, they should have gone to Kunlun Station.
"Cannot sit idly by…"
Hobert glanced at this sentence again. He felt it was necessary to take a look at Kunlun Station.
He knew that in the end, the "Original Creator" still awakened, and the scientists at Changcheng Station of course also failed, but if their bodies were still exposed in the wilderness, Hobert felt that he should bury them.
There is a detailed map of Antarctica in Changcheng Station. After identifying the direction and calculating the distance, Hobert directly entered the "Spirit World" to go to Kunlun Station.
Just after entering the Spirit World, Hobert realized that the Spirit World corresponding to Antarctica seemed a bit deserted.
Generally, after entering the Spirit World, there would be many Spirit World creatures wandering around, but in the Spirit World here, there were no signs of any Spirit World creature activity as far as the eye could see.
This made Hobert more cautious, but he didn't retreat. After all, he was already Sequence 1, so there was no need to be as timid as before.
A dozen seconds later, Hobert arrived at the location of Kunlun Station. In the Spirit World, he seemed to see several blurry giant figures around, but no matter how carefully he looked, he couldn't see them clearly.
Because his spirituality did not sense danger, he entered the real world.
But to Hobert's surprise, Kunlun Station in the darkness actually looked quite complete!
Some cuboid-like buildings, like containers, still stood there! On the left were some structures like large oil pipes, and on the right were some large snowmobiles.
Some of these large snowmobiles had nameplates with the words "Changcheng Station", "Zhongshan Station", etc.
The researchers from Changcheng Station did come here. Not only did they come, but people from other research stations also came.
In front of these buildings, there was a dark stone engraved with the words "Chinese Antarctic Kunlun Station"!
This is indeed Kunlun Station, but the fact that the buildings here are so well preserved made Hobert realize that something was wrong here.
Since this place is so well preserved, why didn't any gods discover it before? Or did some gods discover this place, but didn't announce the relevant information?
Hobert's spirituality still didn't detect any danger, nor did he detect any signs of living beings in the research station.
This time, Hobert didn't use extraordinary powers to enter the research station, but went to open the door to check the situation inside first.
Everything inside seemed like a long-sealed history. So many years have passed, but everything inside is still undamaged.
Hobert cautiously entered the house. First, in a room that was similar to a combination of an activity room and a conference room, he saw a circle of teacups placed around the table.
This should have been left by the people from Changcheng Station. He didn't know if they had a short meeting here, or just rested here.
Towards the inside, the door of the archive room was open.
Hobert cautiously went in. First, he saw a thick folder on the table, and the walls of the archive room were covered with dirt.
Hobert was very familiar with these "dirt." After he "tampered" with it, he saw some incoherent words written on it:
"He said he was a god, hehe, I told him I was an atheist…"
"Strange, how do their voices reach our ears? Why is there still that terrifying effect? Are they directly talking to our brains?"
"The things underground are unsettling…"
"I seem to have seen a rainbow…"
"Their bodies are too big, too big…"
Hobert took a deep breath. These words were obviously also written in blood. The handwriting was full of frenzy, but there also seemed to be some rationality in the frenzy.
Such messy words basically wouldn't yield much useful information, so Hobert simply went to look at the thick folder.
At this moment, Hobert seemed to understand: Even if some gods discovered this place, they wouldn't think it was a prehistoric ruin, but would think it was the residence of some ancient god. Unless They knew Chinese characters.
In that case, only "Roselle" would understand what this place was if he discovered it.
But thinking about it carefully, if that guy had time, he would go find noble ladies and witches to play with. Would he go deep into the interior of Antarctica to explore?
If it weren't for accidentally finding relevant clues, it would actually be difficult to discover this place.
Thinking of this, Hobert looked at the furnishings outside again. The biggest question appeared in his mind again: This place is preserved too well.
With questions, Hobert also "tampered" with the brightness of the dye. He saw that the folder's number was indeed 155.
The first page of the document only had one sentence: After you finish reading the following content, your mind will irreversibly have problems. Be sure to be prepared to fight against that voice!
Hobert slowly nodded. Just knowing some indescribable existences would also be corrupted.
The second page of the document began to describe the entire process in detail. Initially, Kunlun Station discovered a strange ice layer in Area 3. There seemed to be an invisible barrier there. No matter how big the wind and snow were, they would be blocked by the barrier, forming a spectacle of ice and snow colliding with air.
After peeling off the snow layer, the researchers found a black, very regular square under the ice layer, and began to drill down to extract ice.
But what they didn't expect was that they drilled hundreds of meters down before obtaining the black sample that made up the square.
All the abnormalities started with this sample. Initially, people thought they were minerals, but after cutting them, they found that they seemed to be the tissue structure of some living organisms.
Then the incident happened where the two biologists had mental problems. After such an accident, Kunlun Station immediately stopped the research and waited for further orders from above.
During this stage, they made many guesses, one of which was very close to the truth: Could the black substance be a virus that spreads through sight? A virus frozen under the Antarctic ice?
Using the term 'virus' to describe the Beyonder characteristic's corruption was actually quite fitting.
It was at this moment that the two biologists rushed towards Area 3 without wearing sufficient equipment. Only then did people discover that a descending ice staircase had appeared at the location of the black cube!
And the black cube was now gone.
Because they were unable to report everything here to the outside world in a timely manner, Kunlun Station had no choice but to organize an expedition to explore down the staircase.
Below was a huge underground structure. Here are some photos; it was so vast that the boundaries couldn't be seen!
After several explorations, they roughly determined the general structure of the entire underground space.
During the last exploration, people saw six huge, blurry shadows in the ice layer further down.
It was unknown what those things were. Strangely, all the cameras were unable to photograph them; only human vision could see them.
Following this are six hand-drawn sketches. Some of those blurry shadows seemed to have human-like shapes, some were like regular geometric figures, and some were strangely shaped.
Another strange thing was that everyone who saw these shadows went mad after returning to the research station!
