chapters.title: Chapter 774 - 767 Extra 5: Chaos Sea Appears
chapters.content:
join the Church of MissRaven and become a Sequence 9: Reader p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
The Modern Era, before the depletion of oil resources.
Grisha, who worked at the Academy of Sciences, was suddenly invited to the Kremlin to attend a very high-level meeting.
He originally thought it was another meeting to discuss revitalizing the national industrial chain, but unexpectedly, as soon as he entered the Kremlin, he was led to a small conference room.
The people sitting in the conference room surprised him. They were all top figures in the global scientific community, and their names were almost household names.
Another thing that puzzled Grisha was that, although there had been no international scientific gatherings in Moscow recently, the attendees included Chinese, Americans, and people from the European Union.
The appearance of Chinese scientists in the Kremlin was not unusual, but the presence of American and European Union scientists here was somewhat strange.
After all, the war was still ongoing, and the sanctions from Europe and the America were still in effect.
Grisha greeted everyone briefly and then sat down in an empty seat. At this moment, a tall colonel with distinct facial features came in with a folder and walked to the podium: "Gentlemen, the reason we have invited you here today is because we have made a major geological discovery that requires your knowledge for further research."
The colonel spoke in English, so no translation was needed.
He continued: "Especially for foreign nationals, since you are here, you should be informed of the urgency of this matter, which also proves your countries' concerns and attention to it.
"Therefore, you must first sign a confidentiality agreement before I can describe the truth of the matter to you."
An American scientist joked: "Did you discover dinosaurs underground?"
Several scholars around him echoed with laughter, but only laughed for a moment, because the colonel's expression was serious, as if dinosaurs had really been discovered.
The American scientist cleared his throat awkwardly and made a "please continue" gesture.
The colonel continued: "If you do not intend to sign the confidentiality agreement, you may leave now."
He waited for more than ten seconds, and seeing that no one left, he opened the folder and distributed the confidentiality agreement to everyone.
After everyone signed the agreement, the colonel began to speak: "Ten years ago, the nuclear radiation at Chernobyl suddenly disappeared. At that time, the war between us and Ukraine had not yet broken out.
"At the invitation of Ukraine, we sent a research team to investigate."
At that time, Ukraine had already suffered a significant brain drain, and they investigated for a long time without finding out the reason for the sudden disappearance of radiation.
Therefore, they had no choice but to invite scientists from other countries to investigate. Inviting scientists from Moscow was also a last resort, because Europe and America did not pay much attention to this matter and were very perfunctory about it.
In the subsequent investigation, Moscow gradually took the initiative. Until the war, the investigation was mainly led by Ukraine.
After the war began, the Ukrainen side took away a large amount of research data, so when the investigation was restarted recently, they had to invite the Ukrainen side to participate.
"We found a deep pit in Chernobyl," the colonel continued. "The deep pit seemed to appear suddenly, and the reason for its formation has not been investigated clearly to this day.
"From the bottom of the pit, a strange sound occasionally comes. After a period of monitoring, we found that this sound is regular.
"Initially, we thought there might be some unknown geological activity underground, but we soon discovered that this sound seemed to possess a certain intelligence.
"So, a research institute was gradually built there to conduct long-term research, but we used many methods and failed to reach the very bottom of the pit.
"To this day, it is not clear what geological activity is down there.
"Several scientists have claimed that they have been affected by something from the depths, and their bodies have undergone some changes, but we have not detected any harmful substances such as radiation.
"Strangely, their psychological activities have indeed undergone some changes.
"However, due to the arrival of the war, this round of investigation had to be ended."
Speaking of this, the colonel turned on the computer and projector and continued: "Last year, a Ukrainian army brigade disappeared suddenly while passing through Pripyat.
"The subsequent search troops found them in the previously built research institute. They were constantly sending soldiers towards the deep pit.
"At that time, a video like this was left behind."
The colonel began to play a video. The person in the video appeared to be a regimental commander based on his shoulder insignia. His eyes were blank, and his expression was somewhat unnatural.
Through his narration, everyone understood that this was an officer from the missing unit. He said that the entire brigade had heard a voice from underground.
That voice made them suddenly realize that the current direction of technological development was wrong. There was a substance, or rather a force, that had been neglected by the scientific community for a long time, and that force was the key to constructing this world, this universe.
As long as they entered the very bottom of the deep pit, they could find this force and figure out all the operating rules of this universe.
Therefore, the soldiers scrambled to explore downwards with crude ropes, but so far, no soldier has returned.
The video ended, and the colonel continued: "In addition to the exploration team tying up some officers and soldiers, all the other people in the entire brigade entered the underground.
"And those officers and soldiers who were tied up did the same thing within a month after being sent to the rear for recuperation: they returned to the research institute and continued to explore the deep pit.
"So, the research on the deep pit was restarted…"
In fact, this research was restarted by Europe and America, but in order to obtain the previous research data from Ukraine, they brought in the Eastern power to study together.
Under the coordination of the Eastern power, the war was still ongoing, but the secret research on the deep pit was restarted.
The colonel finally said: "What we can currently confirm is that there is an unknown mysterious force hidden in the underground of the deep pit.
"Currently, the frequency of this force's external influence is increasing, and the scope is widening. Experts predict that in the future, that force may affect the entire human race, so now we urgently need to summarize the rules of this force in order to avoid the destructive power that this force may produce in the future!
"This will be your future mission."
The scientists raised their hands one after another, wanting to ask some detailed questions, but the colonel replied that he didn't know either, and told them to take a break. In an hour, a special plane would be arranged to take them to Chernobyl.
Grisha remained silent throughout, but he was very interested in everything that happened in Chernobyl.
When he went to the toilet, he met Academician Zhang Hongwen from Beijing. He was very familiar with this fifty-year-old academician wearing glasses. The two smiled and chatted for a few words and went to wash their hands together.
Just as he turned on the faucet, Academician Zhang Hongwen suddenly said softly in Mandarin: "This is your last chance to give up.
"I know more than you. Several of us came here after writing our wills."
After speaking, Zhang Hongwen turned off the faucet and left quickly.
Grisha understood Chinese, but he didn't speak it very fluently. He was stunned for a few seconds, but ultimately did not choose to give up.
One reason was because of his curiosity, and the other was a kind of helplessness. He was one of the few "young" people in the Academy of Sciences.
The National Academy of Sciences was no longer as prosperous as it used to be. Except for the relatively good situation of the Institute of Mathematics, most of the other institutes were filled with old people in their seventies.
They couldn't send these old men and women, could they?
Half an hour later, Grisha boarded the plane to Chernobyl. Zhang Hongwen didn't say anything after seeing him, as if he had never reminded him in the toilet.
They first landed at a military airport, and then took a helicopter to Chernobyl.
Everyone was stunned after arriving here, because it looked very desolate and did not look like there was a research institute at all.
But under the leadership of the previous colonel, they came to an abandoned command room and opened a secret door here. There was a long downward staircase, as if leading to the underground.
Grisha glanced at the huge building built of layers of concrete, which was the No. 4 reactor where the accident happened that year. At this time, their location was not far from that reactor.
Later, Grisha learned that the place where they worked was almost next to the No. 4 reactor, and there were several similar small secret doors connecting to the outside world, as well as a larger secret door responsible for receiving supplies.
After walking for a few minutes in the underground section, they arrived at a wide road where several cars picked them up and took them to the research institute. Only then did they realize that this was no ordinary research institute.
It was clearly built as a secret research institute from the start, capable of meeting the needs of at least several hundred researchers for work and living, and there was also a company of soldiers maintaining order.
There were already some scientists here, but they were not as prestigious or highly regarded as Grisha's group.
After entering the research institute, the first requirement was far beyond Grisha's expectations: they had to wear clerical attire and carry a cross or corresponding religious artifact.
At this point, Grisha was very certain that Zhang Hongwen really knew more, because he and several Chinese scientists had brought Taoist robes, peach wood swords, and Three Purities Bells.
On the first day, they rested for a while. The next day, someone explained the research projects and progress to them.
However, someone raised their hand first and asked, "Excuse me, why do we have to wear clerical clothes? Are we going to study demons here?"
"To be honest, our research subject is really a bit like a demon." The explainer suddenly smiled: "There is a mysterious force here, and we can clearly feel it expanding every ten days.
"Each expansion causes people to go crazy, but just a few months ago, we discovered that the priests here were hardly affected. We have experimented and found that as long as you wear clerical clothes and carry the corresponding religious artifacts, you will hardly be affected."
Everyone was stunned, suddenly feeling like they had entered the wrong door. Was this really a research institute?
Immediately afterwards, the person who asked the question earlier reacted: "You said there are priests here?"
Besides a theological research institute, what research institute would have priests?
"Because the discoveries here are too astonishing, and many problems cannot be explained by science." The explainer said: "Let us get to the main topic.
"But before that, I would like to take you to a place first."
So, under their leadership, a group of scientists walked through the corridor to a large glass viewing platform.
Outside the glass viewing platform, it was pitch black, and only the stone walls on both sides could be vaguely seen, as if it was connected to the dark space outside.
The explainer used the button on the wall to turn on the outside lights. Under the illumination of the giant searchlights, a huge pit was revealed in front of everyone.
This gave people the illusion that the pit led to another world!
Below the pit, it was pitch black, causing the scientists to take a step back involuntarily, feeling that some dangerous monsters would crawl out of it.
In other parts of the glass viewing platform, there were many downward-facing devices, some were steel cables leading to the bottom, and some were platforms for launching drones or exploration robots.
Amid everyone's surprise, the explainer said: "So far, we have not had any instruments that can detect the existence of that mysterious force, we can only rely on our human bodies to feel it.
"But when that mysterious force expands, our body functions, or rather, our metabolism, will accelerate, and this we can detect with instruments.
"In addition, all possible methods have been used, but no matter what method we use, we have not detected the bottom of this pit."
One scientist asked: "Have you used the latest seismic survey instrument?"
"We have used it, but it didn't detect the bottom."
Another scientist asked: "What about the latest electromagnetic prospecting equipment?"
"We have also used it, but it didn't detect the bottom."
The scientists were silent, which meant that this pit was at least ten thousand meters deep!
The explainer continued: "So far, the only person who has seen the bottom of the pit clearly is a devout Catholic believer, um… he was also one of the earliest researchers.
"At that time, the top of this pit had not yet been covered with steel frames. According to the description of those present, at noon, the devout believer held a cross and said: Almighty, omniscient, and all-good God, please shine sunlight into the pit and let me see clearly what is at the bottom!
"It is said that the sunlight suddenly became very dazzling at that time, and the devout believer really saw the bottom of the pit. He described it as: a beautiful and illusory ocean!"
Everyone continued to be silent, because they didn't know how to evaluate this event that seemed like a story from the "Bible."
After a while, someone asked: "What happened to that devout believer now?"
The explainer said: "After he described what he saw, he turned into a monster."
"Turned into a monster?"
"Okay, we can go back now." The explainer did not immediately answer everyone's questions, and first returned to the conference room just now, and projected a blurry photo on the projector.
Although the figure in the photo still had human structure, it did look like a monster in a movie: covered in blood red, as if the skin had been stretched and burst, with flesh exposed. There was also a large mouth with sharp teeth on his stomach, and this mouth was slightly open, and you could even see the internal organs inside.
Everyone understood one after another that this was the devout believer.
The explainer continued: "Later, we replicated the situation at that time many times, but we never saw the sunlight that could see the bottom of the pit again.
"However, we soon discovered that when the sunlight was at its harshest, or when there was thunder and rain, some researchers were prone to mental breakdown.
"Occasionally, some pitch-black monsters would suddenly appear. People who were scratched by those monsters would have rust-like spots on their bodies, and die in great pain, with all their organs failing.
"Currently, we have not found any drugs that can treat or delay this process.
"These monsters are not afraid of bullets, bombs, or even the attacks of electromagnetic and ultrasonic weapons.
"We can only wait for the sunlight to no longer directly shine into the pit, or for the lightning to no longer be in the sky above the pit, and then those monsters will disappear on their own.
"This situation no longer occurred until we completely covered the top of the giant pit with a steel frame structure."
After everyone was silent for a while, someone finally asked: "Then, what exactly did you call us here to study? I mean, I study quantum mechanics, how can I help?"
The explainer said: "What we can say for sure now is that there is an unknown force existing underground here, and now we urgently need a theory that can provide a reasonable explanation for this force.
"However, we don't know where to start, so we can only widely invite experts from various fields to see if everyone can use their own theories to explain the current situation.
"Perhaps in the process of discussion, everyone can have a clear explanation for this phenomenon."
Then he waved to the two soldiers at the door, and several soldiers each carried in a stack of thick documents: "These are all of our research processes and results so far, and everyone can learn about them first.
"If there are any research needs, please design your own experiments, and we will try our best to cooperate with your actions."
Although everyone had some complaints, they still carefully read the materials.
The first day was spent reading, and from the second day onwards, everyone gradually had some discussions.
Geologists believe that this may be an unknown phenomenon of the Earth's magnetic field. There are unknown drastic changes in the magnetic field here, which affect the emotions of the researchers.
However, this statement does not make sense in many places, such as why there is a pit? Why do monsters appear? And so on.
More importantly, changes in the magnetic field are relatively easy to detect. After several rounds of experiments, it was proved that there were no obvious drastic changes in the nearby magnetic field.
Some biologists also speculated that there may be unknown microorganisms underground, and people infected with microorganisms will undergo drastic changes in their bodies.
However, after multiple and multi-directional sampling on the stone walls of the pit, no unknown microorganisms were found.
Just as everyone was continuing to guess, suddenly, they all looked in the direction of the pit, and as if they had received some kind of order, they all came to the glass viewing platform.
At this time, it was already crowded with people, and everyone looked at the pit together, all feeling that something seemed to be emerging from it.
Immediately afterwards, everyone seemed to feel very terrified and took a step back.
They could clearly feel that a mysterious force was surging towards the surface from the ground. The veins on everyone's foreheads bulged, as if the blood in their bodies had rushed to their heads.
Beep— Beep— Beep!
The instrument that detected everyone's metabolism suddenly sounded, but everyone entered a dreamlike state. They did not look at the bottom of the pit, but everyone seemed to have a picture in front of them: a phantom stream was surging upwards from the bottom of the pit.
Only after several minutes did everyone awaken as if from a dream, hearing the "beep beep" sounds of the instruments.
Another ten-odd seconds passed before the director announced: "This is the most turbulent surge of that mysterious power to date."
"Ladies and gentlemen, if it were a sealed demon, then it is now not far from being unsealed."
Grisha and the others returned to the conference room somewhat dispiritedly, only now having a true feeling for that mysterious power.
The guesses they were just discussing seemed very pale in comparison.
More than an hour later, astonishing news came from the outside world: at the same time as that power surged, all the world's oil deposits disappeared.
… …
In the evening, after work.
Grisha, carrying two bottles of vodka, knocked on Zhang Hongwen's door.
After opening the door, Grisha said in somewhat broken Mandarin: "Old Zhang, looking for you to have a couple of drinks."
Zhang Hongwen smiled slightly, gestured "please come in", and took out some spiced peanuts and jerky from his suitcase.
The two drank and chatted, starting with their previous cooperation, then talking about their recent situations. By the time they talked about their current research, they had already drunk a bottle of wine.
Grisha chewed on a peanut, looking at Zhang Hongwen: "You must have some ideas, right? I remember you used to be like this; the more silent you are, the more you have your own opinions."
Zhang Hongwen adjusted his glasses, smiling helplessly: "I'm afraid I'll disappoint you this time, I really don't have any decent ideas."
"But you do have some ideas, right? Old Zhang, tell me, you felt that atmosphere today too. We don't have much time left, your ideas might be key."
Zhang Hongwen looked at Grisha for a second or two before saying: "My ideas might make you even more confused."
"Then I want to hear them."
"Alright, alright." Zhang Hongwen took a sip of wine, paused for a second or two, and then said: "Do you believe in science?"
"I do."
"Do you blindly believe in science?"
Grisha was stunned for a moment before saying: "Are you saying that everything that happened today is really related to theology?"
Zhang Hongwen did not answer this question, but instead said: "There is a huge gap between the cultural cores of you and me. We believe that the appearance of many things cannot be explained by a single way of thinking."
"Because both the universe and human society are complex. If you only use a single way of thinking to explain it, it is easy to not explain it comprehensively enough."
Grisha seemed to have thought of something, but was unable to connect the fragments in his mind: "Old Zhang, can you explain in more detail?"
"That is to say, we Orientals believe that many things are not black and white. Perhaps they are both black and white, both right and wrong. Hmm, it sounds similar to Schrödinger's cat, but it's still a bit different." Zhang Hongwen smiled as he looked at Grisha's blank expression: "I told you, you would be more confused after hearing my thoughts."
"Okay, I'll just say my conclusion."
"I think that the problems we are encountering now cannot be solved by either science or theology."
"Sometimes I have this idea that science, which is regarded as truth by modern people, always has a limit, right? There are always things that it cannot explain, right? So you can believe in science, but you can't blindly believe in it."
"And theology is 'human theology'. Those disciplines are all imagined by humans. Rather than using theology to solve problems, it is better to say that we are using human imagination to solve problems."
Grisha felt that these ideas were in a field that his thinking had never touched: "Then what kind of thinking should be used to solve the problem?"
"I don't know." Zhang Hongwen spread his hands: "Maybe this is a discipline that mankind has never touched."
Grisha seemed to suddenly realize something: "Double-slit experiment! Wave-particle duality!"
The former is an experiment to observe light. Under the same preconditions, there are completely different observation results under two different conditions: with and without an observer.
The latter means that microscopic particles sometimes have "wave-like" properties and sometimes have "particle-like" properties.
Zhang Hongwen said seriously: "I don't know if there is any connection between them. I'm just saying that we should break away from our original way of thinking now, and maybe then there will be a breakthrough."
Grisha was silent. Just as Zhang Hongwen said before, after knowing his thoughts, he really became more and more confused.
At the same time, it was like opening a new door, with many new ideas.
For a period of time after this conversation, the two remained silent. They were both very clear that at this time they should think like ascetic monks, and it was best not to announce their ideas to others before they were sure, otherwise it would only complicate the problem.
About a week later, various countries sent representatives to Moscow, wanting to hear if the scientists had any new ideas about the Chernobyl research.
So Grisha and others returned to Moscow together to participate in a large-scale seminar held there.
It was also at this time that Grisha received a call from his old classmate Augustine Farbauti. The conversation with this old classmate gave Grisha some inspiration.
That night, he excitedly brought two bottles of vodka and knocked on Zhang Hongwen's door.
Zhang Hongwen had dried tofu and vacuum-packed soy-stewed pig trotters, which his family had just sent from China.
The two were still eating and chatting, but this time they quickly got to the point.
Grisha smiled and said: "Old Zhang, I have a very good idea today."
"First, let me talk about a discussion I had with a classmate about humanity when I was in college."
"At that time, we were very strange. Why is the ability of the human body so limited, but it has a brain with a very vast thinking space?"
"I initially studied biology and was very clear that although the human body is very precise, its limit is there, but the upper limit of human imagination is very high."
"Of course, I mean under sufficient cognition."
"Just like Einstein, many of our current studies are only gradually proving that Einstein's theory was correct."
"This is a concrete expression of our idea. Taking the scientific community as an example, when a person has a very good idea, there is no way to immediately verify this idea."
"Even decades later, we can prove some of the theories of top scientists."
"This is a manifestation of human action not keeping up with ideas."
Zhang Hongwen nodded repeatedly, indicating that he understood.
"So, is there such a phenomenon?" Grisha asked: "Actually, our bodies were originally very strong? Or rather, they could match our thinking?"
"For example, if we want to go to the moon and have a look, we can jump to the moon."
"But I don't know why, the ability of our bodies has been weakened, but some of the characteristics before the weakening are still hidden in our genes."
Grisha stared at Zhang Hongwen. He had expressed his thoughts very clearly, so he didn't continue.
Zhang Hongwen held his wine glass and paused for a full minute before saying: "This is a very constructive idea."
He took a sip of wine before saying: "That is to say, the illusory ocean at the bottom of the pit may be the key to our bodies being weakened!"
"Now that illusory ocean is emerging to the ground, it will make our bodies strong again."
Grisha nodded seriously.
Zhang Hongwen looked at his Ukrainen friend for a second or two before finishing the wine in his glass and saying: "We can announce our ideas, and the sooner the better."
With the announcement of their idea, the direction of research immediately began to unfold towards this conjecture.
But at this time, people discovered a paradox: if that illusory ocean would make human bodies stronger, why have so many people gone down to the bottom of the pit, but no one has returned?
At this time, Zhang Hongwen gave an explanation: humans have been weak for too long, and their current bodies cannot withstand such power at all. It's like a person who has been hungry for several days, if you give him a lot of meat, he will die from diarrhea instead.
The only thing that cannot be explained now may be why those illusory water currents devour oil?

chapters.title: Chapter 775 - 768 Extra 6: The Awakening of the Ancient Sun God
chapters.content:
join the Church of MissRaven and become a Sequence 9: Reader p atreon.com/KeyofStars for more chapters
Following up on Extra 5:
A massive pit and a mysterious force suddenly appeared in Chernobyl, leading to the secret construction of a research institute. The world's top scientists gathered to study this mysterious force!
With the sudden disappearance of oil worldwide, the research task became even more urgent.
At this time, Zhang Hongwen from China and Grisha from Ukraine put forward a relatively reliable hypothesis.
So, an experiment was immediately designed. Two white mice in similar conditions were lowered into the 500-meter and 1000-meter deep pits using steel cables, and then retrieved after one hour for observation.
Soon after the two white mice were retrieved, it was discovered that the one placed in the 1000-meter pit had a significantly increased appetite and was emotionally unstable.
Three days later, the white mouse placed in the 1000-meter pit was noticeably larger than the one in the 500-meter pit, and its emotions were even more volatile.
The white mouse placed at 15,000 meters turned into a monster shortly after being retrieved.
All the white mice placed below 15,000 meters could not be retrieved. For some reason, the steel cables snapped, and the boxes containing the white mice disappeared.
By studying the cross-sections of the broken steel cables, it was discovered that some seemed to be burned by high-voltage electricity, some by high temperature, and some were corroded.
At this point, everyone roughly understood that the illusory ocean should be located about 15,000 meters underground.
After multiple, multi-faceted experiments, it was proven that Zhang Hongwen and Grisha's hypothesis was basically reasonable: the illusory ocean could make creatures stronger, but current creatures could not withstand such powerful forces.
Now that there was a hypothesis to explain the illusory ocean, the next step was to further understand or utilize it.
The first problem facing everyone was sampling. It was difficult to perform any operations at a depth of 15 kilometers underground, and it was clear that all currently known materials were insufficient to collect the illusory water.
However, after discussions, a solution was quickly found. At this time, China's 'artificial sun' project had made some progress. Scientists believed that the force field controlling nuclear fusion could be used to try to control the illusory water.
Moreover, sampling could be done during 'high tide'! This would shorten the sampling distance.
This experiment began in full swing. The first problem to be solved was the huge power demand of the force field, which could not be sustained by a large diesel engine.
So, after inspecting the No. 1 and No. 2 reactors of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant, these two reactors were restarted.
In fact, after the Chernobyl disaster, the other reactors continued to operate normally for some time, some even for about 20 years.
The nuclear power plant was completely shut down only when Ukraine could no longer maintain the nuclear reactors.
Restarting the reactors by adding nuclear fuel at this time posed huge safety risks, but there was no better solution at present.
So, with intensive preparation, everything was ready for sampling in just about ten days.
At the moment of another 'high tide,' the instrument generating the force field at a depth of 3 kilometers underground immediately began to work, but soon, contact with the instrument was lost.
It took a full ten minutes before the signal between the control room and the instrument was re-established.
Because there was no time to establish a relevant triggering device, it was not clear whether the sampling was successful.
Subsequent operations were handed over to the intelligent computer, because according to previous information, people could not directly look at the illusory water.
The extremely large device for the force field, under the control of the intelligent computer, was sent into a specially vacated laboratory using pre-laid tracks, and a sealed space was formed after the metal door was closed.
Soon, according to the computer's analysis, there was a liquid-like structure in the force field.
Everyone in the institute cheered. The sampling was successful!
Subsequent research was carried out intensively. The first research was on the sample's weight, density, basic structure, and so on.
Unexpectedly, the weight of the sample was very unstable. Sometimes the weight was 0, and more often the weight was constantly changing, from 1 gram to 326 grams.
People exclaimed: 'These are truly amazing materials!'
...
Russia, Second Baku Oilfield.
After the disappearance of oil deposits, the oil workers here left one after another.
For more than half a month, only a few gatekeepers remained in the vast oil field area.
Rumble~
Suddenly, a huge sound came from underground, as if a behemoth was about to break out of the ground.
The several gatekeepers of the oil field area came out of the rooms in their respective areas, looking for the source of the sound.
Old Galey, one of the gatekeepers, saw an oil pump not far from him trembling, as if a force was about to push it forward.
Old Galey cautiously checked from a distance and called his superior to report the situation here.
Bang~
At the moment of making the call, a stream of black liquid erupted near the oil pump!
"My God!" Old Galey exclaimed: "That's oil! It's just spraying out like this!"
But soon he realized something was wrong. The oil was getting bigger and bigger, forming a huge fountain!
Moreover, there was obviously something wrong with this oil. There were objects with strange lights flashing in the black liquid.
Old Galey sensed a huge danger. He turned and ran, but he was quickly caught up.
The oil wrapped him up as if it had a life of its own. In Old Galey's screams, he turned into a black liquid and continued to flow forward with the oil.
...
One hour later, the Chernobyl Research Institute learned everything that happened at the Second Baku Oilfield.
Five hours later, samples of the ejected oil, as well as samples of objects with strange lights, were sent to the Chernobyl Research Institute.
Along with these samples came a preliminary investigation report.
According to eyewitnesses, at first, the oil seemed to have life, killing living things. All creatures wrapped in oil also turned into black oil.
But after coming to the ground for about a minute, the oil lost its 'life'.
As for those objects with strange lights, they were more terrifying than radioactive materials.
Although no radiation or harmful substances could be detected, if you were within ten meters of them, your emotions would be significantly affected. If you were within one meter of them, you would go crazy in just three seconds and turn into a twisted monster!
So, they were collected with a mechanical arm more than ten meters long, put into boxes, and during subsequent transportation, personnel kept more than ten meters away from the boxes.
This sudden event completely disrupted the institute's research plan. All the researchers were very clear that this meant the illusory ocean underground had begun to overflow in small amounts on the ground, and many people must have been affected.
So, more scholars and scientists were invited here, and some routine experiments were skipped to start live experiments directly.
White mice were brought into contact with the ejected oil, the substances with strange lights, and the samples collected from the illusory ocean, respectively.
Because the white mice would definitely turn into monsters, the experiment was carried out in a steel-structured sealed space. There were offensive weapons in the laboratory, as well as an observation window made of bulletproof glass for easy observation.
Through several rounds of experiments, it was confirmed that the ejected oil no longer had many harmful substances, and the white mice did not have any severe adverse reactions after coming into contact with it.
Soon, further experiments were carried out with war refugees, further proving that the oil no longer possessed bizarre destructiveness after coming to the surface for a period of time.
However, those substances with strange lights still made the white mice go crazy and turn into irrational monsters.
Further experiments with war refugees also proved this point, and the monsters that these refugees turned into possessed some wonderful abilities. Some could make their bodies emit light, and some could create lightning out of thin air.
Fortunately, the experimental site was strong enough, and these lights and lightning failed to break through the barrier of the steel frame structure and were burned to ashes by the electromagnetic weapons prepared inside.
After multiple rounds of experiments, researchers could even determine that those strange lights could give the experimental subjects the ability to emit sunlight, and those could give the experimental subjects the ability to generate lightning.
As more strange substances gushed out from underground and were sent here, experiments continued to be used to determine their capabilities.
Experiments on those illusory water currents were the most thrilling. White mice that came into contact with the light-emitting substances would at most turn into monsters that were a circle larger than their bodies.
But contact with these illusory water currents could instantly turn them into monsters the length of an adult's arm with strong attack power.
Everyone dared not conduct further experiments, fearing that they would create uncontrollable monsters.
As experiments continued to unfold, there were finally means to detect these strange forces. Only by monitoring the activity of microscopic particles could the existence of this force be monitored.
In the monitoring equipment, it could be seen that those strange light-emitting substances formed a small twisted vortex, while the collected illusory water flow was a huge twisted vortex.
But the experiment had to continue, because their ultimate goal was to utilize these strange substances.
...
Late at night, Grisha had just finished a video conference. According to official information from Russia, there had been multiple monster attacks in the country, and the situation was getting more and more urgent. The institute had to achieve results as soon as possible.
Holding materials such as 'Research on Re-oiling of Dried-up Oil Fields,' he left the conference room somewhat tired. He had seen too many human experiments in the past two days and was physically and mentally exhausted.
At the end of the corridor was a huge glass grandstand. Grisha saw Zhang Hongwen standing alone on the grandstand, looking down.
He quickly came to Zhang Hongwen's side: 'Continuing human experiments is not a good idea.'
Zhang Hongwen gave an 'um' and said, 'Everyone knows this.'
His eyes were fixed on the deep pit: 'Do you feel it? There seems to be a voice from the ground.'
Grisha nodded: 'Many people have mentioned this. In dreams, unintentionally, there seems to be a voice from the ground hoping to communicate with us.'
'Perhaps, we still lack a channel,' Zhang Hongwen retracted his gaze.
Grisha immediately said: 'Friend, I know what you want to do, but that's useless. You'll instantly become a madman.'
Zhang Hongwen shook his head: 'These days, I have been carefully studying the reactions of those whose minds have been affected. I have found that their initially incoherent words are not meaningless.
'It's just that they are limited by their own knowledge and don't understand what they are experiencing, so they seem incoherent.'
He looked at the Russian friend in front of him: 'Actually, many people have thought of this, right?'
Grisha took a deep breath: 'But no one is willing to say it.'
'The higher-ups don't seem to care about human experiments at all.'
'Buddy, I know you've always been against human experiments.' Grisha suddenly felt a little uneasy: 'But... but... okay, most people know that human experiments are meaningless.'
Zhang Hongwen took off his glasses and said, 'No, you don't understand. If there is a chance, I will invite you to the Northeast to visit the evidence exhibition hall of the Japanese invaders in China.
'We are different from you. We still remember that painful history.'
He wiped his glasses and put them back on: 'In my opinion, it is a little nobler to volunteer to be a test subject than to let others be test subjects.'
Grisha's eyes were red as he grabbed Zhang Hongwen's arm: 'Friend, you... maybe, maybe we can also teach those refugees some theoretical knowledge...'
'There's no time.' Zhang Hongwen smiled: 'In this unknown disaster, we are too weak. If we want to know the truth, we must pay some price.
'If we don't try, how can we know if it is because of limited knowledge and information that we have not been able to obtain too much useful information.'
He paused and said seriously: 'This may be our last chance.'
Grisha was silent, not knowing what to say for a moment.
Zhang Hongwen's experiment was immediately approved, which also made everyone realize how serious the situation had become.
After multiple awards and commendations, Zhang Hongwen was sent to the laboratory. He chose to directly contact the illusory water flow taken from the ground.
However, the contact distance was determined by himself, so there were communication microphones inside and outside the laboratory.
The illusory water flow was still under the control of the force field and was approaching the laboratory using the track. When it was thirty meters away, even with several thick steel plates in between, Zhang Hongwen said that he had heard some strange whispers.
When it was twenty meters away, Zhang Hongwen's emotions were obviously more irritable. He seemed very angry, why couldn't he still hear those whispers clearly?
As the illusory water flow came to the laboratory where he was, he suddenly said, 'Stop.'
At this time, Zhang Hongwen already looked a little abnormal. With every movement he made, layers of hair fell off, his skin turned gray for a while, then white again, and his eyes were bloodshot red.
'It comes from the distant past.' Zhang Hongwen said with a painful face, 'Very, very distant, it existed before the formation of the universe!'
The institute director immediately asked, "What exactly is it? What is its purpose?"
Zhang Hongwen seemed not to hear the director's question and continued, "It doesn't seem to like me very much."
"It gave me too much information; I can only describe the useful parts!"
This was the difference between him and the other test subjects; he knew which information might be useful.
Grisha snatched the microphone from the director, "Old Zhang, just relay everything it 'says' to us."
"It prefers those who wear crosses." Zhang Hongwen's bloodshot eyes were somewhat blurred; as his hair fell out, his skin began to peel off in patches. "What we captured wasn't that illusory ocean.
"That illusory ocean is indivisible; these are just some oil deposits that have undergone qualitative changes because of the illusory ocean.
"This is a substance we've never discovered before, existing between reality and illusion. There are six portions of such a substance on Earth, and only this illusory ocean has an entrance in the real world.
"The illusory water flow is different in nature from the luminous substance. These illusory water flows are difficult to tame with human will, but humans can utilize the luminous substance relatively easily.
"But this path will inevitably be very tortuous. We have to do many experiments, and there will be many sacrifices."
Zhang Hongwen's flesh was twisted at this point, making him tall and thin, with the monster component being excessively human-like.
He continued in a hoarse voice, "A great being is about to awaken. I see, humanity still has some hope. Yes, as long as we are not destroyed, there is still hope.
"It, it says, it doesn't like the Taoist robe on me. It prefers you people who wear crosses.
"The only, the only, no, not the only hope, the hope to control that illusory ocean, is at the bottom of the pit.
"We can do it, yes, we can do it.
"Heh, what a wonderful ocean... an ocean..."
Zhang Hongwen suddenly looked outside the laboratory. At this point, all his skin had peeled off, his whole body was blood red, his muscles were wriggling, he was fully three meters tall, and his eyes were more like those of a beast.
The moment they saw these eyes, everyone was stunned, their eyes blank, as if they didn't know why they were there.
Suddenly, the scientist closest to the laboratory door seemed to receive some kind of order, and with dazed eyes, he pressed the button, and the laboratory door was opened just like that.
"Zhang Hongwen" immediately came out of the door, and with a slight wave of his hand, the observation room was filled with dark clouds.
Crack~
Several thunderclaps sounded, and six people were struck dead on the spot, and many others were paralyzed by the lightning.
The remaining people woke up as if from a dream and fled, but they were all jammed at the door for a while.
"Zhang Hongwen" opened his arms, as if embracing the sun.
Blazing sunlight appeared in the sky above the doorway, and a scorching sunbeam was about to shine into the crowd, burning most of them to death.
"Old Zhang!" Grisha, whose body was numb from the lightning strike, struggled to get up and shouted.
Zhang Hongwen suddenly froze, and the sunlight above everyone's heads gradually disappeared.
The whole world seemed to be quiet for a second or two. At this moment, Zhang Hongwen suddenly rushed to the door, and several researchers who couldn't dodge were knocked away.
Grisha struggled to chase after him. When he came to the corridor, he saw Zhang Hongwen smashing the glass of the grandstand and then jumping onto the windowsill.
He turned his head, showed Grisha a smile, and then leaped down.
Grisha shouted with a cry, "Old Zhang!"
The director limped over at this time and said, "Zhang Hongwen was very brave, but our research must continue, who will be the next..."
Rumble~
At this moment, the institute suddenly shook, and everyone looked at the flickering lights above their heads, and for a moment, they had a bad feeling.
More than half a minute later, the company commander in charge of maintaining order came over and said, "Retreat quickly! Reactor No. 1 has exploded violently!"
These devices from more than half a century ago finally couldn't bear the burden and suffered a serious failure.
The first thing Grisha and others thought of was not to escape, but to look at the device carrying the illusory water flow.
Buzz~ Buzz~ Buzz~~ Buzz~
The force field stopped working, and the metal wall outside the force field immediately turned black and liquefied at a speed visible to the naked eye.
Grisha quickly turned his head away. He knew he couldn't look directly at the illusory water flow.
The company commander realized the seriousness of the problem and immediately ran to the button with the glass cover not far away, smashed the glass with a punch, and then pressed the button hard.
An urgent alarm sounded immediately. At this moment, all the exits of the institute were automatically closed, and an engineering company outside would completely seal all the exits with concrete after receiving the corresponding notification.
This was an emergency plan determined long ago to prevent the monsters in the institute from escaping to the outside world.
At this time, the illusory water flow had successfully "escaped" from the container. For a time, some people turned into pools of oil, and some people turned into monsters similar to Zhang Hongwen.
More people were fleeing in a panic.
Grisha followed the director and others to the institute's emergency shelter.
This place even had nuclear protection functions, temporarily blocking the monsters.
The monsters obviously had limited intelligence and were chasing the researchers who had failed to escape here, so it was still safe here.
After the director reported the experimental results and the current situation here to Moscow using the emergency communication system, he took out a pistol and committed suicide.
Despair filled the crowd. Everyone knew they couldn't get out.
Grisha sat in the corner, not speaking, not drinking water, and not eating anything.
About a day or two later, he said with bloodshot eyes, "You must wear a cross, you must have enough determination, to be able to use that illusory ocean."
An Englishman next to him said, "It's useless, there's no hope, we have no hope."
"Yes!" Grisha said firmly, "Zhang Hongwen has found hope for us!"
He glanced at the Englishman, only to see despair in his eyes. Looking down, he saw the Englishman writing some disordered words in his notebook:
"What exactly happened? The doctor turned into a pool of black oil in front of me!
The outside has sealed off this institute... no one can leave, no one can leave...
Only we are still normal, but our food is running out.
I seem to be hallucinating. There seems to be a sound coming from underground. It's calling me, He's calling me..."
Grisha suddenly smiled, struggled to get up, and walked out, saying, "The matter is actually very simple. It's a substance that makes humans stronger, but the price is that they will become crazy.
"It is different from all the elements we have discovered so far, even without substance, even not in the real world..."
As he spoke, he opened the door of the shelter.
No one stopped him, but after he went out, someone quickly closed the door again.
Grisha saw that the emergency lights outside were still on, but it was a mess. There were clumps of oil on the ground and on the walls.
It seemed that all the monsters had eventually turned into oil.
Grisha continued as he walked, "In the future, we will definitely be able to control this power, yes, we will..."
Although there were no listeners, he continued, "But before that, we must have enough determination! We must believe that we can do it."
As he spoke, he came to the glass grandstand.
Whoosh~
Without the obstruction of the glass, the wind from the deep pit blew up, making him feel colder than ever before.
Grisha looked down with his upper body, the deep pit was dark and the bottom could not be seen.
He slowly climbed onto the windowsill, "Old Zhang, you have the determination, and so do I!"
After speaking, Grisha jumped down, he knew that this jump was likely to be fatal, but his eyes were firm, and Zhang Hongwen's smile when he jumped into the deep pit seemed to Blink before his eyes again.
Rumble~
At this moment, the surrounding area vibrated violently.
Grisha saw that the deep pit had collapsed on a large scale, and the institute had also collapsed in half, part of it falling into the ground with him.
The illusory ocean expanded at this time, more violently than ever before!
Grisha saw what seemed to be an infinite number of colors in the infinite ocean, "What a beautiful ocean..."
He fell into it silently, losing consciousness.
Time seemed to become eternal. Grisha had a very long dream. He dreamed that the outside world was badly damaged by the sudden extraordinary power.
But humans really survived. They underwent serious mutations. Some became blood clans, some became elves, some became werewolves, and some became giants.
One day, he finally woke up.
In a void, he looked at his hands and instantly understood many things.
Next to Grisha was an ancient stone slab with 22 potion formulas on it.
He realized that as long as these formulas were spread more widely, humans could better control the extraordinary.
So he took the stone slab, turned into a stream of light, and returned from the ground to the location of the laboratory.
This place had long been turned into ruins. After feeling a little emotional, he passed through the thick concrete wall by stealing space and came to the outside world.
It was pitch black outside, and he wanted to see what kind of changes had taken place outside.
So he said, "Let there be light!"

One day in the Modern Era.
Doctor Borlag met a very strange patient who was convinced that he could enter other people's dreams.
Of course, the reason he found this patient strange wasn't just because the patient had such a strange idea.
After all, as a well-known psychiatrist and a leading professor in the field of psychiatry, Borlag had seen patients with all sorts of strange ideas.
It was that the moment he saw the patient, he could tell that he knew the young man in front of him: "Have we, where have we met before?"
As Borlag spoke, he opened the medical record, which didn't have a photo, only a resume and the previous doctors' notes.
The patient's name was Flegrea, he was 26 years old, and he had already received treatment for a period of time, but the previous treatment plan obviously hadn't worked.
Flegrea, who had thick eyebrows and a sunny smile, smiled and said, "Maybe, but I don't remember you."
He didn't look like a mental patient at all.
Borlag shook his head slightly, feeling that his words had been somewhat rash, and thought that this patient was a bit strange, of course, all his patients were a bit strange.
He cleared his throat and said, "Let's chat casually."
In Borlag's view, an important part of treating mental illness was to find the cause, and only by finding the cause could effective treatment be carried out.
His way of finding the cause was to chat with the patient, and as they chatted, he could often judge the cause of the patient's mental abnormality.
Because of this special way of asking questions, he didn't even look at the medical records written by previous doctors.
"When did you start feeling that you could enter other people's dreams?" Borlag asked.
Flegrea replied without thinking, "From the moment I was born."
He went on to explain, "That's what my father told me, he said that that night, he and my mother had the same dream.
"They dreamed that I was born, and the next morning I really was born.
"My father said that at the moment of my birth, all the animals around our house felt uneasy.
"And I often dream about that scene."
Borlag asked curiously, "Which scene?"
"The scene of my own birth."
"Oh." Borlag casually wrote on the medical record: suspected mild delusion.
He continued to ask, "The ability to enter other people's dreams must have brought you a lot of trouble, right?"
"That's right." Flegrea immediately sat up straight: "You're a competent doctor, unlike those other bastards who just classify my thoughts as delusions."
Borlag smiled and glanced at what he had just written.
Flegrea continued, "When I was little, I couldn't tell which places in the dream were safe and which were dangerous, and because I occasionally encountered danger, I was very mentally unstable.
"And more often, I couldn't tell which times were the real thoughts of the person who was dreaming and which were his fantasies, so I often offended people."
He spread his hands with a helpless smile: "Can you imagine? A four or five-year-old child asking my father's good friend why he wanted to be intimate with my mother so much?"
Borlag smiled and said, "I often said the wrong thing when I was a kid too."
Then he asked, "So you didn't have any friends at that time?"
"Yes." Flegrea said, "I have a friend named Allen."
"How did you meet?"
"At home." Flegrea enthusiastically introduced, "Oh, right, Allen is a border collie.
"He and I were born on the same day, and we're good friends who can talk about anything."
Speaking of this, he gradually became a little sad, and sighed before saying, "Unfortunately, when I was 12 years old, Allen got lost.
"Many people say that he must have realized that he was about to die, so he chose to find a place to face death alone."
Borlag wrote on the medical record again: Allen, border collie.
After writing this, he drew a triangle behind it, indicating that this was important information.
"You must be very sad, right?" Borlag asked.
Flegrea took a deep breath: "It's okay, I can often see him in my dreams."
Borlag smiled slightly: "I almost forgot about your ability.
"What changes have there been in your life after Allen was gone?"
His experience told him that this dog should be the initial reflection of Flegrea's symptoms, so he planned to ask a few more questions about Allen.
"There have indeed been some changes." Flegrea replied, "As I got older, I gradually became able to distinguish which places in the dream were safe and which were dangerous.
"I also understood what was imagined by the dreamer, or what he didn't want others to know, so I tried not to mention it.
"So my mental state got much better, and I gradually stopped being annoyed by others."
This change surprised Borlag somewhat: "Now, are there new problems bothering you?"
In theory, if the patient's logic has a certain degree of self-consistency, the symptoms can be improved, at least most of the time they look relatively normal.
And this patient obviously had a tendency to self-heal after the age of 12. It must be that the condition has worsened again recently for some reason, so he came to see a doctor again.
"That's right." Flegrea seemed to habitually take a deep breath: "Recently I encountered a very strange problem, sometimes I dream that I will appear in a strange world.
"At first, I would only stay in that world for three or four days, then it was a week, and now I can stay in a strange place for a month at a time.
"Every time I fall asleep and wake up, I have a strong sense of separation.
"Can you imagine? When I lie down it's June 1st, and when I wake up it's clearly June 2nd, but I have a feeling that it's July 1st."
Borlag wrote on the medical record: Condition worsened?
He asked, "Can you tell me in detail, what kind of world is that?"
"It's just a normal modern human society." Flegrea replied, "But not in the United States, but in an Asian country.
"I don't know why I'm so familiar with the living habits there, I had a pretty good time there."
Borlag asked again, "Have you had similar situations before?"
"Yes, but only for a few hours, or even a few minutes, before I could figure out what was going on, the dream ended."
"What do you think that was about?"
"What do I think?"
"Yes, what you think." Borlag said, "Because I don't have the ability to enter other people's dreams, so I lack the corresponding professional knowledge."
Flegrea praised again: "You're a competent doctor."
Then he paused before saying, "I've had some ideas, thinking whether I've connected someone's dream with reality.
"But I'm not sure if that's the case, so I want to find a professional to confirm it."
Speaking of this, he shook his head, somewhat helplessly: "But, people think those are illusory things.
"I saw that you had published several papers on dreams before, and I got a lot of inspiration, so I wanted to hear your thoughts."
Borlag touched his hair and smiled, "That was a long time ago, but I did some research on dreams, and I think dreams should be used to treat mental illnesses.
"Unfortunately, we have no way to manipulate dreams."
He continued to ask, "Have you tried to find the area where your dream appeared?"
"I've looked for it." Borlag said, "I also found my 'role' in the dream."
Speaking of this, he suddenly became serious: "But, when I found that person, he was already dead!
"And the time of death was probably when I woke up."
Borlag understood: "In other words, you lived for a month from the perspective of a stranger, and then when you woke up, he died?"
"Probably like that."
Borlag couldn't help frowning, and then wrote "delusion" on the medical record, but then, he drew a question mark behind it.
At this time, Flegrea asked, "Doctor, do you have any suggestions?"
Borlag was stunned for a few seconds, then suddenly crossed out everything he had written on the medical record, and then said, "To be honest, I don't think dreams are connected to the real world.
"The reason you have the feeling of being connected is because you are connecting to another person's dream, and through the dream you are connecting to another real world.
"As for the problem of this time difference, I can't figure it out either."
He put the medical record and pen on the table and said, "But as a doctor, I want to tell you that you may also have severe delusions.
"I suggest that you go to the scene in your dream again with your family, if it's the same as the result you found alone before, then it's beyond my understanding.
"If you don't find the places you dreamed of, I suggest you come to me for inpatient treatment."
Flegrea nodded and said, "So far, the advice you have given is the most pertinent.
"Thank you very much for your advice, I can be sure that I don't have delusions."
Then he asked, "Doctor, if it doesn't delay your work and life, would you be willing to continue doing research on dreams?"
Borlag smiled and shook his head: "I can't continue to study dreams just because I want to, it requires a lot of high-end, professional equipment.
"The key is that I have to design some of the equipment myself, after all, there is no very professional instrument for dream research at present."
Flegrea smiled and said, "These are not problems, I just want to ask if you are willing?
"Well, I will try my best to provide you with the conditions you need, all the research results are yours, I just want to figure out some problems."
Borlag was somewhat tempted, as if he had regained the ideal of his youth to find new ways to treat mental illnesses: "I'll think about it."
Flegrea nodded: "I'll come again tomorrow."
Borlag was slightly stunned, and just watched the patient in front of him get up and leave.
Just as he was about to organize the patient's file and rewrite the medical record, Borlag suddenly opened his eyes.
He woke up!
...
Looking at the bright curtains, Borlag was slightly dazed, the treatment process just now was actually a dream!
But... it was too realistic!
Borlag couldn't tell whether the previous one was reality or the current one.
When eating breakfast, Borlag saw his three-year-old daughter looking out the window at the street, and he sternly told his daughter to eat seriously.
But the daughter suddenly asked, "Dad, can I have a puppy?"
Borlag casually said, "Don't we already have Bick in our house?"
Bick is the poodle they keep at home.
"That's different." The daughter said in a childish voice, "There's a puppy on the road outside, it's very obedient, and we talked very happily."
Borlag was slightly stunned: "Talked very happily?"
This reminded him of the description of the patient Flegrea he met in his dream last night.
At this time, the eldest son smiled while eating breakfast: "When did you learn the language of dogs?"
The daughter said seriously, "It can talk."
Borlag asked again, "What did it say? When did you meet it? What breed is that puppy?"
"It said it was waiting for a friend, and that friend is receiving your treatment." The little girl thought for a while and then said, "It seems like yesterday, and it seems like today."
Finally, she shook her head: "I don't know what breed it is."
Borlag's expression gradually became serious, at this time the daughter was not very clear about the difference between yesterday and the day before yesterday, so she was not very clear about which day it was.
So he took out his mobile phone and searched for a few photos of border collies for his daughter to identify, and finally the daughter pointed to a black and white dog: "It's similar to this one."
Borlag immediately fell into contemplation, and didn't even bother to eat, he immediately drove to the hospital, and contacted several of his classmates and friends, wanting to learn about the latest information on dream research.
But then he found that humans have too little research on dreams, and these friends he was looking for were all scientists with cutting-edge research topics, but they didn't get much useful information.
This made him unable to work all day, and he even suffered from insomnia at night, but in that moment he immediately fell into a deep sleep.
...
When Borlag came back to his senses, he found that he was already sitting in the office again, and at this time Flegrea pushed the door in: "Doctor, what have you considered?"
Borlag suddenly got up: "You, you really have the ability to enter other people's dreams!"
Flegrea pursed his lips and smiled: "You finally believe it?"
Borlag sat back in his chair and asked, "So the border collie waiting outside last night, no, was it Allen last night?"
"Yes."
Borlag asked again, "So, you and Allen 'talk about everything', do you talk about everything in your dreams?"
"Yes."
Borlag sat there motionless, thinking for more than half a minute before asking, "How do you plan to fund my research?"
"As long as it's the instrument you've used, I can present it to you in my dream." Flegrea said, "It doesn't matter if you don't understand the principle.
"If you've only heard of it but never seen it, and you know where it is, I can help you bring it to life."
"As for the instruments that need to be designed, I will enter the dreams of the relevant designers and have them design it for you."
"All research will be conducted in dreams, so it won't interfere with your life and work."
Borag nodded. "Okay, I'm willing to do the corresponding research. Can I go directly out of here to study the dreams outside?"
"It's best not to leave the hospital," Fregera said. "Because there are many unknown dangers outside."
"I've thought about this idea a long time ago, but it's not a good idea because your research on the outside world is like researching the entire universe in the real world. It's difficult to achieve great results."
"I will simulate a laboratory for you in the hospital so that you can use instruments to study the second layer of dreams. The research results there are the same as researching the current dreams in the real world."
Borag indicated that he understood. "In other words, the experimental results here are universal to the experimental results in the real world."
Fregera nodded.
Finally, Borag asked, "What do you want to know?"
"I really want to know why the recent dreams have become so unstable?" Fregera said. "I don't know why, but some changes suddenly appeared in the dream world some time ago."
"It was also from that time that I began to uncontrollably enter unfamiliar environments and stay there for a month or two."
"Well, I took a nap during the day and ended up staying on another planet for two months!"
"I think, as time goes by, my time in the dream may become longer and longer."
"I think finding the reason for the instability of the dream will help me understand the current situation."
Borag nodded and said, "I need several test subjects, preferably those related to the recent instability of the dream."
"For example, people affected by the instability of the dream."
"No problem," Fregera said. "I will provide them for you."
Borag asked again, "You went to an alien planet this time?"
"Yes," Fregera took a deep breath and said, "I originally thought that the changes in the dream world would at most make me appear somewhere on Earth, but now it seems that I may visit any planet with intelligent creatures that can produce dreams."
Then, they began to plan the laboratory. After obtaining the corresponding instruments and test subjects in an instant, Borag's research immediately began.
In the blink of an eye, a week in the real world had passed. When Borag was doing research in the dream laboratory, Fregera suddenly pushed the door open.
He looked very tired, and the previous sunny and cheerful look had disappeared.
"There are some results!" Borag immediately said, "I found that the instability of the dream has a source. This source is probably in Europe, but the specific location cannot be determined yet."
"I need you to bring a test subject from each European country, and we should be able to find the source of the instability soon."
"Okay," Fregera pinched his forehead and asked, "How many more days will it take?"
"One week." Then Borag said, "You look very tired."
"Yeah," Fregera took a deep breath. "I spent five whole years in a dream yesterday and almost mistook my life in the real world for a dream."
He touched his face and said helplessly, "This feeling is really amazing. When I woke up, I almost forgot to ask you to do the research."
Borag was stunned for a while. It was hard to imagine what it would be like to sleep for five years.
He paused before saying, "My suggestion is that you prepare some sticky notes on your bedside table to avoid forgetting some important things."
Fregera smiled helplessly again. "I will."
At this time, Borag saw a border collie at the door. "Is that Allen?"
"Yes."
Borag asked curiously, "Is it... did you 'create' it in the dream?"
Fregera was suddenly stunned. "I... I seem... seem... to be with it in the real world too?"
He pinched his forehead and found that he really couldn't distinguish between dream and reality!
Seeing that the other party's mental state was not good, Borag suggested, "You'd better go out for a walk and relax."
Fregera nodded. "I will... I will..."
As he spoke, he left in a daze. The border collie took a deep look at Borag and followed him away.
Another week passed. Fregera came to the hospital while drinking and looking very haggard. He asked Borag, who was sitting in the office, in a hoarse voice, "Are there any results yet?"
This time the border collie also came in, closer to Fregera than last time.
"Yes!" Borag said. "But before I tell you the specific location, I need you to promise me that I can continue my research in the dream afterwards."
Fregera gulped down a few mouthfuls of wine. "Okay, tell me."
Borag then said, "In Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine, probably in Pripyat."
Fregera was stunned. "Pripyat?"
"You might know it better by another name," Borag said. "Chernobyl."
Fregera nodded. "Okay, I know."
Then he reached out, and Borag suddenly felt a throbbing pain in his chest, followed by weakness in his legs, and he fell to the ground.
Amid Borag's surprised expression, Fregera took another sip of wine and laughed with some madness. "Sorry, I have no patience for this world anymore."
"You may not know, but the day before yesterday, I stayed in a strange world for a hundred years!"
"From the birth of a creature, to growing up, to adulthood, and then to death."
"Hehehe, you can't imagine that kind of pain."
He walked out step by step with the wine bottle in his hand. The border collie looked at Borag with some regret, and then followed him out.
Tomorrow morning, Dr. Borag will be found by his family, having died of a heart attack in the night.
…
Fregera woke up suddenly. He first reached for the wine on the bedside table.
At this time, his eyes were bloodshot and his face was pale. He hadn't slept for two days and two nights.
Fregera had been wandering in the dream just now, actively entering the dream, which could not be considered sleep at all. He would be even more tired each time he woke up.
It wasn't that he didn't want to sleep, but that he didn't dare to sleep.
According to the previous overlapping pattern of the dream world, he estimated that if he entered the dream again through normal sleep, he would stay there for at least 200 years. When he returned to this world, he would definitely be driven mad.
Gulp, gulp~
Fregera took a few sips of wine and looked at the border collie not far away. "Hey, buddy, a lot of times I suspect that I really have delusions. Why are you always by my side?"
Silence fell in the dim room.
"I'm really crazy," Fregera took another sip of wine before starting to pack his luggage and head to the airport.
After buying the corresponding ticket, Fregera was preparing to go through security and enter the waiting hall. While queuing, he suddenly noticed a strange instrument at the security checkpoint. It had a huge base and the middle looked like a giant printer. There was also a soldier operating the instrument.
Fregera suddenly had a bad feeling.
The next second, the soldier who was looking at the computer suddenly looked up and looked in Fregera's direction.
Fregera immediately put the soldier to sleep and learned from his dream that this instrument came from research at the Chernobyl Institute and could actually detect the fluctuations of supernatural power!
Chernobyl!
Fregera sneered and immediately left the queue waiting for security.
At this moment, he suddenly looked at the top of the opposite high-rise building.
Bang~
A sniper rifle rang out, and the sniper on the roof of the opposite building fired at Fregera, who had left the queue.
The sniper immediately reported into his headset, "Target eliminated!"
But there was no reply from the other end of the headset. The sniper was slightly stunned.
At this time, the space in front of him suddenly cracked like a broken mirror. His hand was still on the trigger, and he hadn't fired at all!
And the target had already fled the scene.
This surprised the sniper. Did he just have a hallucination?
The soldiers at the security checkpoint were also surprised that the enemy had escaped in the blink of an eye.
However, the target definitely couldn't run far, and his whereabouts could be found quickly through surveillance.
At this time, Fregera was hiding in a narrow street not far from the airport, surrounded by garbage and excrement.
But he was too sleepy to move.
Fregera had just consumed a lot of energy. If he maintained the dream for too long, he was afraid that he would fall asleep. Therefore, both the sniper and the soldiers woke up from the dream very quickly.
He had already cut a deep wound in his palm, relying on the pain to maintain his last bit of consciousness.
At this time, sirens rang out around him, as if the surrounding streets were full of police cars.
Fregera struggled to get up and continued to run with the border collie.
He suddenly turned his head and put several chasing soldiers to sleep.
Bang, bang~
But soldiers from another direction rushed over and fired two shots at Fregera, one of which hit him in the chest, knocking him to the ground.
Fregera was immediately in a daze, not knowing whether he was about to fall asleep or die.
Then he felt that everything around him seemed to become unreal. Was he still in a dream?
At this time, the border collie stepped forward at a leisurely pace. An invisible ripple spread out, and all the surrounding soldiers fell asleep.
The shepherd dog looked at Fregera and suddenly said, "Let me tell you a story."
"Once upon a time, a shepherd dog and a little boy were born on the same day, almost at the same time. The birth of the shepherd dog made the surrounding creatures aware of the anomaly, and there were some signs of chaos."
"At that time, people thought that those anomalies were caused by the birth of the little boy."
"The shepherd dog and the little boy grew up together, and became good friends whether in dreams or in the real world."
"Later, the little boy showed some amazing abilities, and his figure would appear in almost everyone's dreams."
"But people ignored the shepherd dog that appeared with the little boy."
"People thought that the little boy had the ability to enter other people's dreams, but in fact, it was the shepherd dog that had these abilities."
"Until the little boy was 12 years old, one of his classmates, jealous of his abilities, tricked the little boy into the wild and then shot him to death with a pistol."
Fregera's eyes narrowed, and he looked at the shepherd dog in front of him in disbelief. He seemed to suddenly recall many things!
The soldiers who came to support wave after wave fell asleep, but the shepherd dog still looked very calm. It continued to tell the story: "When the shepherd dog learned of all this, it often entered the murderer's dreams, gradually changing some of his subconscious thoughts."
"Under the accumulation of changes, the murderer gradually believed that he was the little boy! Until today, until now!"
"Heh heh heh heh~" "Fregera" tried hard to say something, but he couldn't say anything at this time. He tried hard to raise his hand, but he didn't grab anything.
The shepherd dog finally said: "The little boy's name is Allen, and the shepherd dog's name is Fregera."
"That's right, my name is actually Fregera."
"After the little boy died, I explored the dream world more deeply and found that my appearance was more like a mutation in the dream world, and my situation was actually very dangerous."
"So, I gave you some abilities to manipulate dreams and called you by my name."
"More than ten years later, this approach finally paid off. After the dream world became suddenly unstable, you finally replaced me and were affected by the distortion and madness of the dream world, falling into a long dream."
"And I, on the other hand, have hardly been affected."
As he spoke, his body became larger and larger, and four more legs grew out. In the end, it looked more like a wolf than a shepherd dog.
This was the gradual mutation of its body under the influence of the dream world recently.
"I can feel that huge changes are about to happen in this world, and my changes are the best evidence," the eight-legged demon wolf said. "So I took back my name and became Fregera again!"
"In this way, I will re-establish a close connection with the dream and can use the dream world to resist the drastic changes that will occur in the world in the near future."
After speaking, its eight legs gently moved, and it had already run a long distance.
The man on the ground looked at Fregera's back and swallowed his last breath.
